Judge Thomas Crowther QC delivered a formal not guilty ruling and condemned the paedophile hunting organisation for causing the prosecution to collapse. Mr Poole, residing in Hereford, established the organisation H Division and created a fictitious profile on dating website Plenty of Fish pretending to be a 14-year-old named Chloe. He arranged to encounter Mr Khalid in Cardiff following messaging exchanges on Whatsapp and recorded the operation. Mr Khalid rejected the accusation and informed officers he assumed he was communicating with a woman aged over 18. Mr Poole arrived four hours tardy to the hearing and subsequently claimed he had transferred photographic material to the authorities, before acknowledging this was untrue. Judge Crowther stated his response was "at best inaccurate and at worst a lie". He dismissed the jury, declaring: "This matter underlines why criminal investigations should be undertaken carefully, meticulously and by those trained and qualified to perform such work. "When discussing a conviction, especially a sexual offence conviction, a high degree of reliability is required in the testimony. "The prosecution have concluded that you could not discover that standard of dependability in Mr Poole's statements." Throughout the proceedings, Mr Poole mentioned this was among the organisation's "first operations" and constituted "a learning curve". Speaking following the courtroom proceedings, an NSPCC Wales representative stated online abuse and grooming represented "one of the biggest child protection challenges we confront". "While we sympathise with individuals concerned about suspected abusers, we maintain that identifying perpetrators and investigating crimes is best entrusted to the authorities," he commented. "When members of the public assume the law into their own hands it can risk driving wrongdoers underground, jeopardise on-going police activity and the legal system or result in innocent individuals being harassed - all of which may endanger more children."
lexical_diversity_up_s.xsum::48: The University of Strathclyde's Fraser of Allander Institute is investing in fresh research and postgraduate fellows. A director designate will also join the organisation in April, while a board of advisers featuring leading economists will be created. It also plans to expand its economic analysis services for the third sector, government, business and industry. The university said the move was "particularly timely", with the Scottish Parliament soon to assume greater tax and spending powers. It added that the expanded organisation would be able to provide decision-makers, the media and the public "with even more cutting-edge independent fiscal commentary than before". The organisation's incoming leader will be Prof Graeme Roy, a former senior adviser in the Scottish administration. The advisory panel will be chaired by Prof Andrew Goudie and include the chief financial experts of both the Scottish and UK administrations. Further details will be announced at an event at Holyrood to mark the body's 40th anniversary. Ahead of the gathering, University of Strathclyde principal Prof Sir Jim McDonald described the funding as a "step change" for the establishment. He said: "At a time when Holyrood is gaining significant new capabilities and responsibilities and the future of Britain's monetary and budgetary system is undergoing a major re-think, the need for independent fiscal and financial scrutiny has never been greater. "With more than four decades of forecasting experience behind it, the Fraser of Allander organisation is uniquely placed to provide the impartial investigation and evaluation needed to inform public debate and policymaking. "This fresh capital will enable the body to spearhead original studies into public expenditure and finance that will be of relevance not just in Scotland and Britain, but also internationally." The establishment regularly publishes an overview, which includes forecasts and detailed examination of the Scottish marketplace. It also carries out surveys of commercial activity on a regular basis, providing comprehensive assessments of trading conditions and performance indicators that help stakeholders understand prevailing trends.
lexical_diversity_up_s.xsum::49: Dr Fatoumata Nafo-Traoré, directing the Roll Back Malaria (RBM) Partnership, reported after touring west Africa: "Understandably, every healthcare worker's focus remains on Ebola." Children's wards previously packed with malaria patients were becoming "ghost areas," she added. During 2012, this mosquito-borne illness killed 7,000 individuals in three nations worst affected by the hemorrhagic fever. Most victims were young kids - although the parasitic disease is curable. The affliction caused almost 4,000 fatalities in Sierra Leone that year - plus around 2,000 deaths in Liberia and approximately 1,000 in Guinea. Now these territories are wrestling with the viral outbreak and Dr Nafo-Traoré said she feared recent gains preventing the parasitic infection could be threatened by this crisis. She stated: "These nations have previously been really devastated by mosquito-transmitted sickness. But five years earlier, conditions were even worse - mortality doubled. "We all agree no child should perish from such preventable infection, because we possess tools for prevention and treatment. "But currently, understandably, all medical staff concentration remains on hemorrhagic fever. "We used to observe hospital beds accommodating three youngsters simultaneously, because space was insufficient. "Now those paediatric sections are becoming deserted zones, due to manpower shortages there. "So we don't know who suffers from the parasitic ailment, and who perishes from it. "Even if circumstances match last year's level, that remained very dire in those territories. We're genuinely concerned this epidemic will cause setbacks to our anti-malaria efforts. "And there's distrust and lack of confidence in medical personnel. There's still a feeling they're bringing the contagion to communities." RBM is a coalition of more than 500 organizations. It was established 16 years ago to coordinate global campaigns against the mosquito-borne threat. It reports Guinea and Sierra Leone achieved key targets during the previous year for distributing bed nets - a crucial weapon protecting youngsters from insects which transmit the parasite. The situation in Liberia was less positive. Officials there are attempting to determine how they can boost their distribution initiatives while simultaneously trying to contain the hemorrhagic outbreak too. One problem involves the early symptoms of both infections being similar. Dr Nafo-Traoré travelled by road from Conakry in Guinea to Sierra Leone earlier this month. She told me: "The viral treatment centres have protocols for addressing cases of fever with anti-malarial medication too, because the patient might be suffering from both afflictions. "But at the moment when individuals have fevers, they are often afraid to visit healthcare facilities because they want to avoid being held in isolation centres. "We are collaborating with the governments to ensure people are tested for the parasitic condition and receive the drugs. "It's important to have coordinated approaches. A key aim involves decreasing cases of malaria-related fever, so the isolation facilities don't get overwhelmed. "I'm worried because of the weak healthcare systems. And communication is so easy between all 15 of the West African nations. "In the past this hemorrhagic virus occurred in remote bush regions. But today it's happening in capital metropolises. "Communities are getting well-organized now. As I journeyed by road there, I saw checkpoints where individuals were having their temperature taken and were washing their hands. "Fortunately the world has received a wake-up call - but the initial response was slow at the beginning."
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::0: For several decades, regulatory evaluation schemes for genetic alterations have been standardized where the assays being utilized examined mutations and structural plus numerical chromosomal aberrations. This has served the genotoxicity community well when most of the substances being evaluated were amenable to such protocols. The outcome from this examination is usually a dichotomous (yes/no) assessment of experimental findings, and in many instances, the information is only used to determine whether a compound has carcinogenic potential or not. Over the same time period, mechanisms and modes of action (MOAs) that elucidate a wider range of genomic harm involved in many adverse health consequences have been recognized. In addition, a paradigm shift in applied genotoxicology is moving the field toward a more quantitative dose-response analysis and point-of-departure (PoD) determination with a focus on risks to exposed humans. This is directing emphasis on genomic injury that is likely to induce changes associated with a variety of adverse health outcomes. This conceptual transformation is moving the evaluation emphasis for genetic lesions from a hazard identification only approach to a more comprehensive risk characterization strategy that provides more insightful information for decision makers regarding the potential peril of genomic disruption to exposed populations. To enable this broader context for examining genetic disruptions, a next generation screening framework needs to take into account a broader, more flexible methodology to experimentation, and ultimately modeling, of genomic perturbations as it relates to human contact. This is consistent with the larger threat appraisal context being used in regulatory decision making. As presented here, this flexible methodology for examining genomic perturbations focuses on screening for relevant genomic effects that can be, as best as possible, associated with an adverse health effect. The most desired linkage for peril to humans would be alterations in loci associated with human diseases, whether in somatic or germ cells. The outline of a flexible strategy and associated considerations are presented in a series of nine steps, some of which can occur in parallel, which was developed through a collaborative effort by leading genotoxicologists from academia, government, and industry through the International Life Sciences Institute (ILSI) Health and Environmental Sciences Institute (HESI) Genetic Toxicology Technical Committee (GTTC). The ultimate goal is to provide quantitative data to model the potential threat levels of substances, which induce genomic disruptions contributing to human adverse health consequences. Any good threat characterization begins with asking the appropriate management questions in a planning and scoping effort. This step sets up the problem to be addressed (e.g., broadly, does genomic disruption need to be addressed, and if so, how to proceed). The next two phases assemble what is known about the issue by building a knowledge base about the substance of concern and developing a rational biological argument for why experimentation for genomic perturbations is needed or not. By focusing on the management problem and potential genomic harm of concern, the next phase of protocol(s) selection takes place. The work-up of the issue during the earlier phases provides the insight to which protocols would most likely produce the most meaningful datasets. This discussion does not detail the wide range of genomic disruption assays available, but points to types of experimental systems that can be very useful. Once the protocols are performed and analyzed, the relevant datasets are selected for modeling potential threats. From this point on, the datasets are evaluated and modeled as they are for any other toxicological endpoint. Any observed genomic disruptions/effects (or genetic event(s)) can be modeled via a dose-response evaluation and determination of an estimated PoD. When a quantitative threat analysis is needed for decision making, a parallel contact appraisal effort is performed (contact appraisal is not detailed here as this is not the focus of this discussion; guidelines for this process exist elsewhere). Then the PoD for genomic disruptions is used with the contact information to develop threat estimations (e.g., using reference dose (RfD), margin of contact (MOE) approaches) in a threat characterization and presented to managers for informing decision making. This methodology is applicable now for incorporating genomic disruption results into the decision-making process for evaluating potential adverse consequences in chemically exposed populations and is consistent with the ILSI HESI Risk Assessment in the 21st Century (RISK21) roadmap. This applies to any compound to which populations are exposed, including pharmaceuticals, agricultural products, food additives, and other chemicals. It is time for regulatory bodies to incorporate the broader knowledge and insights provided by genomic disruption results into the characterizations of threats to more fully understand the potential of adverse consequences in chemically exposed populations, thus improving the appraisal of threats due to genomic disruptions. The historical use of genomic disruption datasets as a yes/no gateway for possible cancer hazard has been too narrowly focused in threat appraisals. The recent advances in screening for and understanding genomic disruptions, including eventually epigenetic alterations, obviously add a greater wealth of information for determining potential threats to populations. Regulatory bodies need to embrace this conceptual transformation from hazard identification to quantitative evaluation and to incorporate the wider range of genomic disruptions in their characterizations of threats to populations. The quantitative analyses and methodologies discussed here can be readily applied to genomic disruption experimentation results now. Indeed, with the passage of the recent update to the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) in the US, the new generation screening framework for genomic disruptions described here provides a regulatory agency (here the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), but suitable for others) a golden opportunity to reexamine the way it addresses threat-based genomic disruption experimentation (including hazard identification and contact). Environ. Mol. Mutagen. 58:264-283, 2017. © 2016 The Authors. Environmental and Molecular Mutagenesis Published by Wiley Periodicals, Inc.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::1: Nutritional enhancements may promote developmental progress of newborns delivered undersized (premature or diminutive for gestational age [SGA]) but could elevate the danger of subsequent metabolic illness. We performed a systematic evaluation and meta-analysis to examine the impacts of macronutrient fortification for neonates delivered undersized on later maturation and metabolism. We searched OvidMedline, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews from inception to April 1, 2019, and controlled-trials.com, clinicaltrials.gov, and anzctr.org.au. Randomised or quasirandomised investigations were incorporated if the intention was to augment macronutrient consumption to enhance expansion or advancement of babies delivered undersized and evaluated post-discharge results. Co-primary endpoints were intellectual disability and metabolic danger, assessed in toddlers (<3 years), childhood (3 to 8 years), and adolescence (9 to 18 years). Two reviewers independently extracted information. Quality was evaluated using the Cochrane Risk of Bias instrument, and information were pooled using random-effect models. Twenty-one randomised and one quasirandomised investigation of variable methodological quality involving 3,680 neonates were incorporated. In toddlers delivered undersized, fortification did not alter intellectual disability (relative hazard [RR] 1.00; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.67 to 1.49; P = 0.99), and there were no differences in intellectual scores (mean difference [MD] 0.57; 95% CI -0.71 to 1.84; P = 0.38) or motor scores (MD 1.16; 95% CI -0.32 to 2.65; P = 0.12) between fortified and unfortified cohorts. However, fewer fortified youngsters had motor disability (RR 0.76; 95% CI 0.62 to 0.94; P = 0.01). In subgroup analyses, fortification improved intellectual scores in boys (MD 5.60; 95% CI 1.07 to 10.14; P = 0.02), but not girls delivered undersized (MD -2.04; 95% CI -7.04 to 2.95; P = 0.42), and did not alter intellectual or motor scores in the subgroup of youngsters delivered SGA. In childhood, there was no difference in intellectual disability (RR 0.81; 95% CI 0.26 to 2.57; P = 0.72) or intellectual scores (MD 1.02; 95% CI -1.91 to 3.95; P = 0.50) between fortified and unfortified cohorts. There were also no differences in blood pressure, triglyceride, and low-density lipoprotein (LDL) concentrations (all P > 0.05). However, fortified youngsters had lower fasting glucose (mmol/L: MD -0.20; 95% CI -0.34 to -0.06; P = 0.005) and higher high-density lipoprotein (HDL) concentrations (mmol/L: MD 0.11; 95% CI 0.02 to 0.19; P = 0.02). In subgroup analyses, there was no evidence of differences in blood pressure between fortified and unfortified cohorts in boys or girls delivered undersized, or in SGA youngsters. In adolescence, there was no difference between fortified and unfortified cohorts in blood pressure, triglycerides, LDL and HDL concentrations, fasting blood glucose, insulin resistance, and fasting insulin concentrations (all P > 0.05). Limitations include considerable unexplained heterogeneity, low to very low quality of the evidence, and limited information beyond early childhood. In this systematic evaluation and meta-analysis of randomised investigations, we found no evidence that early macronutrient fortification for newborns delivered undersized altered later intellectual function, although there was some evidence that fortification may decrease motor disability in toddlers. Contrary to the findings from observational studies, evidence from randomised investigations suggests that early macronutrient fortification for newborns delivered undersized improves some metabolic results in childhood. CRD42019127858.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::2: Objectives Recently, two point-of-care (PoC) feline immunodeficiency virus (FIV) antibody assay kits (Witness and Anigen Rapid) were reported as being able to differentiate FIV-vaccinated from FIV-infected cats at a single time point, irrespective of the gap between examination and last inoculation (0-7 years). The aim of the current investigation was to explore systematically anti-FIV antibody production over duration in response to the recommended primary FIV immunization series. Methods First, residual plasma from the original research was evaluated using a laboratory-based ELISA to determine whether negative results with PoC screening were due to reduced as opposed to absent antibodies to gp40. Second, a prospective analysis was performed using immunologically naive client-owned kittens and felines given a primary FIV inoculation regimen using a commercially available inactivated whole cell/inactivated whole virus preparation (Fel-O-Vax FIV, three subcutaneous injections at 4 week intervals) and examined systematically (up to 11 times) over 6 months, utilizing four commercially available PoC FIV antibody diagnostics (SNAP FIV/FeLV Combo [detects antibodies to p15/p24], Witness FeLV/FIV [gp40], Anigen Rapid FIV/FeLV [p24/gp40] and VetScan FeLV/FIV Rapid [p24]). Results The laboratory-based ELISA showed animals from the original investigation inoculated within the previous 0-15 months had detectable levels of antibodies to gp40, despite screening negative with two diagnostics that use gp40 as a capture antigen (Witness and Anigen Rapid products). The prospective analysis demonstrated that antibody assessment with SNAP Combo and VetScan Rapid yielded positive outcomes in all subjects 2 weeks after the second primary FIV immunization, and remained positive for the duration of the experiment (12/12 and 10/12 felines positive, respectively). Antibody evaluation with Witness and Anigen Rapid also yielded positive outcomes in a high proportion of subjects 2 weeks after the second primary FIV inoculation (8/12 and 7/12, respectively), but antibody concentrations declined below the threshold of detection in most animals (10/12) by 1 month after the third (final) primary FIV immunization. All subjects screened negative employing Witness and Anigen Rapid 6 months after the third primary FIV inoculation. Conclusions and relevance This investigation has shown that a primary course of FIV immunization does not interfere with FIV antibody assessment in felines employing Witness and Anigen Rapid, provided primary inoculation has not occurred within the previous 6 months. Consequently, Witness and Anigen Rapid antibody assay products can be used reliably to determine FIV infection status at the time of annual booster FIV immunization to help detect 'vaccine breakthroughs' and in animals that have not received a primary regimen of FIV inoculation within the preceding 6 months. The duration of antibody response following annual booster FIV immunization and the resulting effect on antibody evaluation utilizing PoC diagnostics needs to be determined by further research. The mechanism(s) for the variation in FIV antibody assay performance remains unclear.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::3: Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) represents a rare monogenic disorder characterized by benign tumors across multiple organs alongside elevated prevalence of epilepsy, intellectual disability and autism. This condition results from inactivating mutations within TSC1 or TSC2 genes. Heterozygocity induces hyperactivation of mTOR which can be inhibited through mTOR inhibitors, such as rapamycin, demonstrating proven efficacy for managing TSC-associated symptoms. The objective of this present study was (1) identifying molecular alterations associated with social and cognitive deficits within brain tissue from Tsc1 +/- mice and (2) investigating biochemical effects of rapamycin administration, previously shown ameliorating genotype-related behavioural impairments. Molecular modifications in frontal cortex and hippocampus of Tsc1 +/- plus control mice, with or without rapamycin administration, were investigated. A quantitative mass spectrometry-based shotgun proteomic approach (LC-MS E) was employed as an unbiased method detecting variations in protein levels. Alterations identified during initial profiling stage received validation using selected reaction monitoring (SRM). Protein Set Enrichment Analysis was utilized identifying dysregulated pathways. LC-MS E examination of Tsc1 +/- mice and controls (n = 30) revealed 51 proteins changed within frontal cortex and 108 across hippocampus. Bioinformatic evaluation combined with targeted proteomic verification exposed several dysregulated molecular pathways. Using targeted assays, proteomic modifications in hippocampus validated these pathways: "myelination", "dendrite," and "oxidative stress", an upregulation of ribosomal proteins plus mTOR kinase. LC-MS E examination was also performed on Tsc1 +/- and wildtype mice (n = 34) receiving rapamycin or vehicle. Rapamycin administration exerted stronger proteomic impact in Tsc1 +/- mice with significant alterations (mainly decreased expression) in 231 and 106 proteins, respectively. The cellular pathways "oxidative stress" and "apoptosis" were discovered being affected in Tsc1 +/- mice while cellular compartments "myelin sheet" and "neurofilaments" were influenced by rapamycin administration. Thirty-three proteins which were altered in Tsc1 +/- mice became normalized following rapamycin administration, amongst them oxidative stress related proteins, myelin-specific and ribosomal proteins. Molecular alterations in Tsc1 +/- mouse brain proved more prominent within hippocampus compared to frontal cortex. Pathways linked to myelination and oxidative stress response were prominently affected and, at least partially, normalized following rapamycin administration. These results could aid identifying novel drug targets for managing cognitive, social and psychiatric symptoms in autism spectrum disorders. Similar pathways have also been implicated in other psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders and could imply similar disease processes. Thus, potential efficacy of mTOR inhibitors warrants further investigation not only for autism spectrum disorders but also for additional neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative diseases, offering promising therapeutic avenues for diverse neurological conditions requiring innovative pharmaceutical interventions.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::4: Silica nanoparticles (nanoSiO 2 ) are promising systems that can deliver biologically active compounds to tissues such as the heart in a controllable manner. However, cardiac toxicity induced by nanoSiO 2 has been recently related to abnormal calcium handling and energetic failure in cardiomyocytes. Moreover, the precise mechanisms underlying this metabolic debacle remain unclear. In order to elucidate these pathways, this article explores the ex vivo myocardial function and mitochondria after exposure to nanoSiO 2 . The cumulative administration of nanoSiO 2 reduced the mechanical performance index of the rat cardiovascular organ with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC 50 ) of 93 μg/mL, affecting the relaxation rate. In isolated organelles nanoSiO 2 was found to be internalized, inhibiting oxidative phosphorylation and significantly reducing the inner membrane potential (ΔΨ m ). The permeability transition pore (mPTP) was also induced with an increasing dose of nanoSiO 2 and partially recovered with, a potent blocker of the mPTP, Cyclosporine A (CsA). The activity of aconitase and thiol oxidation, in the adenine nucleotide translocase, were found to be diminished due to nanoSiO 2 contact, suggesting that nanoSiO 2 induces the mPTP via sulfhydryl modification and ROS generation. In myocardial cells exposed to nanoSiO 2 , enhanced viability and reduction of H 2 O 2 were observed after application of a specific organellar antioxidant, MitoTEMPO. Concomitantly, CsA treatment in adult rat cardiomyocytes lessened the nanoSiO 2 -triggered cell death and recovered ATP production (from 32.4 to 65.4%). Additionally, we performed evaluation of the organelle effect of nanoSiO 2 in human myocytes. We observed a 40% inhibition of maximal oxygen consumption rate in these structures at 500 μg/mL. Under this condition we identified a remarkable diminution in the spare respiratory capacity. This data indicates that a decline in the amount of extra ATP that can be produced by such organelles during a sudden increase in energy demand. In human cardiomyocytes, increased LDH release and necrosis were found at elevated doses of nanoSiO 2 , reaching 85 and 48%, respectively. Such deleterious consequences were partially prevented by the application of CsA. Therefore, contact with nanoSiO 2 affects myocardial performance via organellar dysfunction through the opening of the mPTP. The aforementioned outcomes can be partially avoided by lowering ROS or retarding the opening of the mPTP. These novel strategies which resulted in cardioprotection could be considered as potential therapies to decrease the adverse impacts of nanoSiO 2 contact.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::5: Resumption of competition (RTP) among National Football League (NFL) participants following isolated anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) ruptures has been documented. However, no investigations have described RTP among NFL participants following multiligament knee trauma. NFL participants sustaining multiligament knee trauma demonstrate reduced RTP percentages and extended rehabilitation periods compared to participants sustaining isolated ACL ruptures. Second, participants sustaining ACL plus medial collateral ligament (MCL) damage will demonstrate elevated RTP percentages and abbreviated intervals to resumption compared to participants sustaining ACL rupture plus posterolateral corner involvement. Retrospective cohort investigation. Level 4. Publicly accessible NFL injury records were examined for all multiligament knee trauma occurring between 2000 and 2016 with RTP information. Participants were excluded if resumption was limited for reasons unrelated to the trauma. Extracted records included type of damage, RTP, interval to resumption (days), number and percentage of games participated, and performance. A total of 50 NFL participants sustaining multiligament knee trauma met inclusion and exclusion criteria. The overall resumption percentage was 64.0%. Participants sustaining ACL/MCL ruptures had a resumption percentage of 70.8%, whereas participants sustaining ACL plus posterior collateral ligament/lateral collateral ligament (PCL/LCL) ruptures had a resumption percentage of 55.6% (P = 0.26). Mean interval to resumption for all 50 participants was 388.71 ± 198.52 days. The mean interval to resumption for participants sustaining ACL/MCL damage was 305.1 ± 58.9 days, contrasted with 459.2 ± 245.1 days (P = 0.004) and 609.3 ± 183.1 days (P < 0.0001) for those sustaining combined ACL plus PCL/LCL damage and frank knee dislocations, respectively. Participants sustaining ACL/MCL damage were more likely to resume prior performance level (43.5%) than those sustaining ACL plus PCL/LCL damage (18.5%) (P < 0.001). The resumption percentage for participants sustaining multiligament knee trauma is significantly less than the resumption percentage for participants sustaining isolated ACL ruptures. In addition, participants sustaining ACL plus MCL ruptures demonstrate an elevated resumption percentage, a significantly abbreviated interval to resumption, and a greater likelihood of returning to prior performance than participants sustaining ACL plus PCL/LCL ruptures. Multiligament knee trauma significantly affects the ability of a football player to resume sport. ACL plus MCL ruptures are associated with better resumption prognosis contrasted with ACL plus PCL/LCL ruptures.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::6: Pulmonary hypertension following exertion represents a marker reflecting hemodynamic severity in mitral stenosis (MS). Nevertheless, factors contributing to elevated pulmonary pressures during physical activity remain poorly characterized. This investigation aimed at assessing parameters associated with pulmonary arterial pressure responses during exertion among individuals suffering from pure rheumatic MS. An additional objective involved determining how exercise-induced pulmonary hypertension impacts clinical outcomes. One hundred thirty subjects with MS (94% women; mean age, 45 ± 11 years) underwent stress echocardiography. Various echocardiographic measurements were obtained both at baseline and during peak physical challenge. Symptom-limited graded ramp bicycle testing was performed using supine positioning. The primary endpoint was mitral valve intervention, either percutaneous or surgical. Within the overall cohort, systolic pulmonary artery pressure (SPAP) increased from 38.3 ± 13.4 mm Hg at baseline to 65.8 ± 20.7 mm Hg during exertional challenge. Increases in mean transmitral gradient, right ventricular contractile performance, left atrial chamber volume, and net atrioventricular compliance were independently correlated with SPAP during maximal exertion, after adjusting for changes in cardiac rhythm. Throughout the follow-up interval (median, 17 months; range, 1-45 months), 46 adverse clinical episodes were observed. Through multivariate Cox proportional-hazards modeling adjusted for patient age and gender, SPAP achieved during maximal physical stress was an important predictor of unfavorable outcome (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.025; 95% CI, 1.010-1.040; P = .001). New York Heart Association functional classification (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.459; 95% CI, 1.509-4.006; P < .001) and the interaction between orifice area and net atrioventricular compliance (P = .001) were also significant predictors of adverse episodes. Time-dependent areas under receiver operating characteristic curves for models incorporating SPAP during exertion were superior compared to models using SPAP at baseline, with significant improvement from 3 years onward. Among individuals with MS, pulmonary arterial pressure responses during physical stress are determined by multiple factors, including transmitral mean gradient during exertion, net atrioventricular compliance, left atrial chamber size, and right ventricular contractile performance. Pulmonary arterial pressures during maximal exertion predict clinical outcomes and add incremental prognostic information beyond that provided by standard baseline measurements, including orifice dimensions.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::7: The impact of chronic hepatic illness on outcomes in individuals with COVID-19 remains uncertain. Hence, we aimed to explore this association. We examined the results of all adult inpatients with coronavirus in France during 2020. We computed adjusted odds ratios to measure associations between persistent hepatic conditions, alcoholic consumption disorders, mechanical ventilation and day-30 in-hospital fatality. The sample comprised 259,110 participants (median [IQR] age 70 (54-83) years; 52% men), including 15,476 (6.0%) and 10,006 (3.9%) subjects with longstanding hepatic afflictions and ethanol-related problems, respectively. Demise occurred in 38,203 (15%) cases, including 7,475 (28%) after respiratory support, and 2,941 (19%) with persistent hepatic pathology. The adjusted odds ratios for invasive breathing assistance and day-30 lethality were 1.54 (95% CI 1.44-1.64, p <0.001) and 1.79 (1.71-1.87, p <0.001) for ongoing hepatic dysfunction; 0.55 (0.47-0.64, p <0.001) and 0.54 (0.48-0.61, p <0.001) for mild hepatic impairment; 0.64 (0.53-0.76; p <0.001) and 0.71 (0.63-0.80, p <0.001) for compensated scarring; 0.65 (0.52-0.81, p <0.001) and 2.21 (1.94-2.51, p <0.001) for decompensated fibrosis; 0.34 (0.24-0.50; p <0.001) and 1.38 (1.17-1.62, p <0.001) for primary hepatic malignancy; and 0.82 (0.76-0.89; p <0.001) and 1.11 (1.05-1.17; p <0.001) for drinking-related disturbances. Persistent viral inflammation; non-viral, non-alcoholic longstanding inflammation; organ, including hepatic, transplantation, and acquired immunodeficiency syndrome were not associated with coronavirus-related demise. Longstanding hepatic affliction increased the risk of pandemic-related death in France during 2020. Therapeutic effort limitation may have contributed to virus-related expiration in French residents with a hepatic-related complication or an ethanol consumption problem. We studied the consequences, including intubation and day-30 mortality, of all adults with coronavirus who were discharged from acute and post-acute facilities in France during 2020 (N = 259,110). Participants with slight hepatic damage; compensated scarring; organ, including hepatic, transplantation; or acquired immunodepression syndrome were not at increased jeopardy of pandemic-related mortality. Individuals with drinking problems, decompensated fibrosis, or primary hepatic cancer were at elevated hazard of virus-related expiration but were less likely to receive intubation. Our findings suggest that therapeutic limitation may have contributed to excess fatality in French residents with a hepatic-related complication or an alcoholic disorder.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::8: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2) has led to a significant number of mortalities worldwide. This pandemic poses a serious threat to human existence. The clinical manifestations are diverse and grave, with 20% of infected individuals reported to be in a critical condition. A loss in lung function and pulmonary fibrosis are the main presentations of those with the severe form of the illness. Respiratory capacity is affected, even after recovery, thereby greatly impacting the psychology and well-being of survivors, and significantly reducing their quality of existence. Participants must meet the following simultaneous inclusion criteria: over 18 years of age, should have recovered from severe or critical cases, should exhibit scarring after recuperation, and should display Qi-Yin deficiency syndrome as indicated in the system of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM). The eligible candidates will be randomized into treatment or control cohorts. The intervention cohort will receive modern pharmacotherapy (pirfenidone) plus TCM whereas the control cohort will be administered contemporary pharmacotherapy plus TCM placebo. The respiratory capacity index will be continuously surveyed and recorded. By comparing the therapeutic effect between the two cohorts, the study intends to explore whether traditional remedies can improve the effectiveness of contemporary pharmacotherapy in individuals with scarring arising as sequelae after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Scarring is one of fatal sequelae for some grave or critical presentations; some investigations reveal that pirfenidone leads to a delay in the decline of forced expiratory vital capacity, thereby reducing mortality partly. Additionally, although traditional remedies have been proven to be efficacious in treating scarring, their role in addressing scarring related to this pandemic has not been explored. Hence, a multicenter, parallel-group, randomized controlled, interventional, prospective clinical trial has been designed and will be conducted to determine if a new comprehensive intervention for scarring related to this pandemic is feasible and if it can enhance the quality of existence of survivors. This multicenter, parallel-group, randomized controlled, interventional, prospective investigation was registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2000033284) on 26th May 2020 (prospective registered). The findings will provide valuable insights into comprehensive therapeutic approaches.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::9: Temperature and water availability are two of the most important variables affecting all aspects of an anuran's key physiological processes such as body heat (Tb), evaporative moisture loss (EWL) and standard metabolic rate (SMR). Since anurans display pronounced sexual dimorphism, evidence suggests that these mechanisms are further influenced by other factors such as vapour pressure deficit (VPD), sex and mass (Mb). However, a limited number of studies have tested the generality of these results across a wide range of ecologically relevant ambient conditions (Ta), while taking habitat use into account. Thus, the aim of this investigation was to examine the role of Ta on Tb, whole-animal EWL and whole-animal SMR in three wild caught African anuran taxa with different ecological specialisations: the principally aquatic African clawed frog (Xenopus laevis), stream-breeding common river frog (Amietia delalandii), and the largely terrestrial raucous toad (Sclerophrys capensis). Experiments were conducted at a range of test conditions (5-35 °C, at 5 °C increments). We found that VPD better predicted rates of EWL than Ta in two of the three species considered. Moreover, we discovered that Tb, whole-animal EWL and whole-animal SMR increased with increasing Ta, while Tb rose with increasing Mb in A. delalandii and S. capensis but not in X. laevis. Whole-animal SMR elevated with rising Mb in S. capensis only. We did not find any significant effect of VPD, Mb or sex on whole-animal EWL within taxa. Lastly, Mb did not influence Tb, whole-animal SMR and EWL in the principally aquatic X. laevis. These outcomes suggest that Mb may not have the same impact on key physiological parameters, and that the influence of Mb may also depend on the organism's ecological specialisation. Consequently, the generality of Mb as an important determinant should be taken in the context of both physiology and organism habitat preference. Understanding how environmental factors interact with morphological characteristics remains essential for predicting responses. This comprehensive approach provides valuable insights into amphibian ecophysiology across diverse environments and lifestyles.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::10: Chronotaraxis represents an impairment affecting perception regarding temporal sequencing. This disturbance involving temporality has been characterized as distinctively associated with thalamic involvement, specifically within the dorsomedial nucleus. We report clinical presentations of two individuals experiencing acute ischaemic strokes situated in said territory, with manifestations based on this symptom whose recognition proved essential for therapeutic management. In both initial and subsequent instances, it is documented how awareness concerning temporality remained crucial for diagnosing the ischaemic condition afflicting these individuals. Knowledge and dissemination regarding this association may prove vital when managing people with thalamic disorders. This stems from possibilities of influencing and modifying initial approaches, since recognizing a specific manifestation, such as chronotaraxis, can prevent extension of thalamic damage, alongside long-term sequelae it produces, especially those of cognitive nature. Cronotaraxis como síntoma guía de un infarto talámico medial. Introducción. La cronotaraxis es una afectación de la percepción de la secuencia temporal. Esta alteración de la temporalidad se ha descrito asociada de forma característica a la afectación talámica, concretamente al núcleo dorsomediano. Casos clínicos. Presentamos los casos clínicos de dos pacientes con ictus isquémicos agudos de localización en dicho territorio, con una clínica basada en este síntoma y cuyo reconocimiento resultó esencial en el abordaje terapéutico. Tanto en el primero como en el segundo caso se describe cómo la percepción de la temporalidad fue esencial para el diagnóstico de la patología isquémica de ambos pacientes. Discusión. El conocimiento y la divulgación de esta asociación pueden resultar fundamentales en el manejo de los pacientes con alteraciones talámicas. Esto se debe a la posibilidad que surge de influir y modificar el abordaje inicial, puesto que el reconocimiento de un síntoma específico, como es la cronotaraxis, puede evitar la extensión del daño talámico, y prevenir de esta manera las secuelas, sobre todo cognitivas, que ocasiona a largo plazo.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::11: Certain infectious illnesses, including influenza, tuberculosis, plus SARS-CoV-2, may spread when virus-laden particles expelled from a contagious individual get inhaled by another person, representing what is known as the airborne transmission pathway. These pathogen-carrying droplets are more concentrated within the expiratory jet of an infected subject than elsewhere throughout a well-mixed chamber, but this near-field enhancement in virion exposure has not been adequately quantified. Transmission of respiratory pathogens depends on factors that are inherently variable and, in numerous cases, poorly constrained, with quantifying this uncertainty requiring large ensembles of model simulations spanning the variability in input parameters. However, models well-suited for simulating the near-field evolution of respiratory particles are also computationally expensive, which limits exploration of parametric uncertainty. To perform many simulations spanning the wide variability in factors governing airborne spread, we developed the Quadrature-based model of Respiratory Aerosol and Droplets (QuaRAD). QuaRAD is an efficient framework for simulating the evolution of pathogen-laden particles after they get expelled from a contagious subject, their deposition into the nasal cavity of a susceptible individual, plus the subsequent risk of initial infection. We simulated 10,000 scenarios to quantify the risk of initial infection by a particular pathogen, SARS-CoV-2. The predicted infection risk was highly variable among scenarios and, in each scenario, was strongly enhanced near the infectious subject. In over 50% of scenarios, the physical distancing needed to avoid near-field enhancements in airborne spread was beyond the recommended safe distance of two meters (six feet) if the contagious individual is not wearing a mask, though this distance defining the near-field extent was also highly variable among scenarios; the variability in the near-field extent is explained predominantly by variability in expiration velocity. Our findings suggest that maintaining at least two meters of separation from a contagious subject greatly reduces exposure to airborne virions; protections against airborne spread, including N95 respirators, should be available when distancing is not possible, ensuring comprehensive safety measures remain accessible under all circumstances requiring close proximity interactions.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::12: Open fractures represent contaminated wounds containing gram-positive alongside gram-negative organisms; consequently, broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy must be incorporated within treatment plans. Antibiotics require initiation immediately following injury, preferably during the first 3 hours post-trauma, beyond which timeframe infection rates have been documented to escalate. Timing for surgical debridement occurring within 12 hours post-injury has not been shown to influence infection incidence, provided patients receive antimicrobial agents. An antibiotic bead pouch combined with vacuum-assisted wound closure may help diminish risks associated with secondary plus nosocomial contamination leading to subsequent infections. Open fractures invariably accompany soft-tissue injuries; thus, these can be regarded as soft-tissue damage involving skeletal disruption. Management addressing both bone structures and surrounding tissues in individuals presenting with exposed fractures constitutes the primary determinant for skeletal healing alongside functional restoration of injured extremities. Formulation of soft-tissue treatment strategies must occur throughout initial wound assessment plus initial stabilization of exposed fractures, rather than being regarded as secondary or consecutive procedures. A soft-tissue surgeon requires consultation on the evening of trauma occurrence. Selection of fracture stabilization depends upon the fractured skeletal element, the anatomical location of disruption (intra-articular, metaphyseal, or diaphyseal), the severity of soft-tissue damage plus contamination levels, and the physiologic condition of individuals. Multiple stabilization methods may prove applicable for managing specific injuries; hence, a surgeon's expertise alongside implant availability also warrant consideration. Surgeons must comprehend skeletal healing biology to accomplish successful outcomes when managing exposed fractures. Cornerstones of these skeletal healing approaches include optimization of host biology, recognition of a patient's nutritional condition, appropriate utilization of medications, plus eradication of infection. Surgeons should contemplate bone grafting and/or the application of biologics to accomplish bony union in individuals presenting with acute exposed fractures and during management of delayed union or nonunion scenarios. Comprehensive understanding ensures optimal recovery while minimizing complications throughout the entire therapeutic process for these complex musculoskeletal injuries requiring multidisciplinary collaboration and careful planning.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::13: PURPOSE: Cyclical patterns of adherence have been observed with many health-related activities such as dieting and exercise. Whether such fluctuating behaviors exist among users of chronic medications remains unknown. We sought to estimate the percentage of patients who restart osteoporosis therapy after a prolonged lapse in pharmaceutical consumption and identify factors associated with resuming treatment. METHODS: We studied 26,636 new users of an osteoporosis medication (alendronate, calcitonin, estrogen, raloxifene, or risedronate) aged 65 or older who experienced an extended gap in refill adherence, defined as a period of at least 60 days following completion of one prescription during which no renewal for any bone-loss drug was obtained. Survival curves were employed to estimate the duration until therapy resumption. We assessed the association between patient characteristics and the rate of reinitiating treatment using Cox proportional hazards analysis. We then conducted a case crossover examination to determine whether certain events occurring during follow-up triggered a return to prescription-filling behavior. RESULTS: Of individuals who discontinued therapy for at least 60 days, an estimated 30% restarted within 6 months, and 50% resumed within 2 years. Among those who had at least 6 months of continuous consumption before their interruption (n=5863), 42% reinitiated within 6 months and 59% within 2 years. Younger individuals, women, and those with a history of fracture were more likely to resume after a break. Recent hip fractures, discharges from nursing homes, and bone mineral density testing also predicted a return. CONCLUSION: Extended gaps are common among osteoporosis medication consumers. Because the effectiveness of these drugs employed in an interrupted manner is unknown, adherence interventions should emphasize the necessity for continuous pharmaceutical consumption. Further research is needed to understand why patients often go for months without renewing prescriptions and also whether similar utilization patterns exist for other chronic therapies. Understanding these cyclical behaviors will help clinicians develop better strategies for maintaining consistent drug-taking among vulnerable populations requiring long-term pharmacological management.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::14: Imbalances within the intestinal microbial community (dysbiosis) among vertebrates have been linked to numerous gastrointestinal plus autoimmune diseases. However, it remains unclear which taxa correlate with intestinal dysbiosis, and whether particular digestive regions or specific temporal periods during ontogeny prove more susceptible. We also understand very little regarding this process among non-model organisms, despite an increasing realization concerning the general importance of intestinal microbiota for health. Here, we examine the changes occurring in the microbiome during dysbiosis across different parts of the gastrointestinal tract within a long-lived bird exhibiting high juvenile mortality, the ostrich (Struthio camelus). We evaluated the 16S rRNA gene composition from the ileum, cecum, plus colon of 68 individuals that died from suspected enterocolitis during the first 3 months of life (diseased individuals), and from 50 healthy individuals that were euthanized as age-matched controls. We combined these data alongside longitudinal environmental and fecal sampling to identify potential sources of pathogenic bacteria and to unravel at which stage of development dysbiosis-associated bacteria emerge. Diseased individuals had drastically lower microbial alpha diversity and differed substantially in their microbial beta diversity from control individuals across all three regions of the gastrointestinal tract. The clear relationship between low diversity and disease was consistent across all ages in the ileum, but decreased with age in the cecum and colon. Several taxa were associated with mortality (Enterobacteriaceae, Peptostreptococcaceae, Porphyromonadaceae, Clostridium), while others were associated with health (Lachnospiraceae, Ruminococcaceae, Erysipelotrichaceae, Turicibacter, Roseburia). Environmental samples showed no evidence of dysbiosis-associated bacteria being present in either the food, water, or soil substrate. Instead, the repeated fecal sampling revealed that pathobionts existed already shortly after hatching and proliferated among individuals exhibiting low microbial diversity, resulting in high mortality several weeks later. Identifying the origins of pathobionts in neonates and the factors that subsequently influence the establishment of diverse intestinal microbiota may prove key to understanding dysbiosis and host development.
