lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::15: We investigate the reason for quantum speedup -- algorithms requiring fewer computation steps than classical counterparts. We extend their representation to the process of establishing the challenge. The initial measurement selects a configuration at random, Bob (the challenge setter) unitarily transforms it into the desired one. This representation is available to Bob and any external observer, it cannot be accessible to Alice (the challenge solver). It would reveal to her the function computed by the oracle, which should remain hidden inside it. We resort to relational mechanics. To Alice, the projection of the state due to the initial measurement is retarded at the end of her solving action. To her, the input remains one of complete ignorance regarding the configuration. By oracle computations, she unitarily sends it into the output encoding, for each possible configuration, the corresponding answer, acquired through the final measurement. We show that we can ascribe to the final measurement the selection of any part -- say the R-th portion -- of the random outcome produced by the initial measurement. This projects the input available to Alice onto a condition of lower entropy where she knows a corresponding fragment of the challenge configuration. The algorithm becomes a sum over classical histories in each of which Alice, knowing in advance one of the R-th portions of the configuration, performs the oracle computations still required to identify the answer. Given an oracle challenge and a value of R, this retrocausality model provides the number of oracle operations required to solve it. Conversely, given a known algorithm, it yields the value of R that explains its speedup. R = 1/2 always yields the number of oracle operations required by an existing algorithm and the order of magnitude needed by optimal ones. This framework demonstrates how temporal correlations between measurements enable computational advantages previously attributed solely to superposition and entanglement phenomena.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::16: Cardiac disease and clinical intervention may both lead to an elevated risk for thrombosis events due to modified blood flow in the heart, thereby altering the mechanical stimuli of cells passing through the chambers. Specifically, the degree of platelet activation is influenced by the level and type of mechanical stresses within circulation. Here we analyze circulation within the left ventricle through a computational model constructed from patient-specific data. Circulation in this chamber is modeled by the Navier-Stokes equations, while movement through the mitral valve employs a parameterized representation of the projected opening. A finite element method solves these equations, from which a simulation of velocity and pressure is constructed. A triple decomposition of the velocity gradient tensor then distinguishes between rigid body rotational circulation, irrotational straining circulation, and shearing circulation. This triple decomposition enables separation of three fundamentally different structures, each generating a distinct type of mechanical stimulus on cells within circulation. We compare results to simulations where a mitral valve clip intervention is modelled, which leads to significant modification of ventricular circulation patterns. It was found that shearing in simulation cases treated with clips increased more compared to untreated cases than rotation and strain did. A decrease in valve opening area of 64 % in one case led to a 90 % increase in rotation and strain, but a 150 % elevation in shearing. The computational analysis suggests a process for patient-specific simulation of clinical interventions within cardiac chambers with detailed analysis of resulting circulation dynamics, which could support clinical risk assessment with respect to platelet activation and thrombotic events. This approach provides comprehensive evaluation of hemodynamic changes following therapeutic procedures, enabling physicians to better predict potential complications related to altered circulation patterns and associated cellular responses within treated patients.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::17: The diffuse very high-energy (VHE, > 100 GeV) gamma-ray emission observed in the central 200 pc of the Milky Way by H.E.S.S. was found to follow the dense matter distribution in the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) up to a longitudinal distance of about 130 pc to the Galactic Centre (GC), where the flux rapidly decreases. Recent sensitive H.E.S.S. analysis revealed that the cosmic-ray (CR) density profile drops with increasing separation from the centre, making observations compatible with a steady cosmic PeVatron at the GC. In this paper, we extend this investigation to obtain for the first time a detailed characterisation of the correlation with material and to search for additional features and individual gamma-ray sources in the inner 200 pc region. Taking advantage of 250 hours of H.E.S.S. observations and improved analytical techniques we perform a detailed morphology study of the diffuse VHE radiation detected from the GC ridge and reconstruct its total spectrum. We show that the signal correlated with dense substance covers the full CMZ and that its intensity is about half the total diffuse photon intensity. We also detect some radiation at higher latitude likely produced by hadronic collisions of CRs in less concentrated regions of the GC interstellar medium. We identify an additional component centred on the GC and extending over about 15 pc that is consistent with the existence of a strong CR concentration gradient and confirms the presence of a CR accelerator at the very heart of our Galaxy. We demonstrate that the spectral characteristics of the full ridge diffuse energy distribution is compatible with the one previously derived from the central areas, suggesting that a single population of particles fills the entire CMZ structure. Finally, we report the discovery of a VHE gamma-ray object near the GC radio arc and argue that it is generated by the pulsar wind nebula candidate G0.13-0.11.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::18: These international clinical practice recommendations (CPR) for developmental coordination disorder (DCD), initiated by the European Academy of Childhood Disability (EACD), aim to address key questions on definition, diagnosis, assessment, intervention, and psychosocial aspects relevant for clinical work. Key questions in five areas were considered through literature reviews and formal expert consensus. For recommendations based on evidence, literature searches on 'mechanisms', 'assessment', and 'intervention' were updated since the last guidance in 2012. New searches were conducted for 'psychosocial issues' and 'adolescents/adults'. Evidence was rated according to the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine (level of proof [LOE] 1-4) and transferred into recommendations. For suggestions based on formal consensus, two meetings of an international, multidisciplinary expert panel were conducted with a further five Delphi rounds to develop good clinical practice (GCP) recommendations. Thirty-five recommendations were made. Eight were derived from the research literature (three on 'evaluation', five on 'treatment'). Twenty-two were updated from the 2012 guidance. Novel recommendations relate to diagnosis and evaluation (two GCPs) and psychosocial matters (three GCPs). Additionally, one new recommendation (LOE) reflects active video games as adjuncts to more traditional activity-oriented and participation-oriented interventions, and two new suggestions (one GCP, one LOE) were made for adolescents and adults with DCD. The CPR-DCD is a comprehensive overview of current understanding based on research findings and expert agreement. It reflects the state of the art for clinicians and scientists of varied disciplines. The international CPR-DCD may serve as a foundation for national guidelines. Updated global clinical practice standards on developmental coordination disorder. Refined and extended recommendations on clinical evaluation and treatment. A critical synopsis of current research on mechanisms. A critical review of psychosocial matters, with implications for clinical work. The first international guidance to consider adolescents and adults experiencing motor difficulties characteristic of this condition.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::19: Hypertension can trigger mood disturbances that may deteriorate or improve depending on the category of antihypertensive medication prescribed. Depression is linked with alterations in basal cerebral asymmetry particularly that of the frontal lobe, which participates in blood pressure regulation. Furthermore, different vasoactive medications may modify the cerebrum's lateralization in a manner that influences cognition performance. We investigated the bilateral functioning of several neuropeptidases in frontal cortical tissue as a reflection of the operational condition of certain neuropeptides implicated in affective states. Using arylamide compounds as substrates, we fluorometrically examined the enzymatic performance of these catalysts in the left and right frontal regions of control untreated Wistar-Kyoto (WKY) and spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs) and compared their responses with WKY or SHR receiving the antihypertensive pharmaceuticals captopril (CAP) and propranolol (PRO) or with the hypertensive N (G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester. SBP was also measured in all WKY and SHR cohorts. Untreated WKY, WKY receiving CAP or PRO and SHR receiving CAP exhibited normotensive readings of SBP. However, WKY receiving N (G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester as well as untreated SHR and SHR receiving PRO and N(G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester demonstrated elevated readings of SBP. Variations in the bilateral distribution of neuropeptidases were contingent on the strain, the catalyst examined and the pharmaceutical utilized. Normotensive WKY cohorts (WKY, CAP, PRO) revealed intrahemispheric associations mainly in the left hemisphere. In contrast, WKY receiving N(G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester and SHR cohorts demonstrated intrahemispheric associations mainly in the right hemisphere. Interhemispheric associations were mostly observed in WKY as well as in SHR cohorts with antihypertensive interventions (CAP, PRO). Our findings suggest specific cerebral bilateral patterns of neuropeptidase responsiveness in WKY that shift in SHR. This observation may be connected to the cognitive impairments that have been documented in these animals and that shift under antihypertensive or hypertensive pharmaceutical interventions.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::20: The objective of this investigation is to assess the utility and effectiveness of rapid response teams (RRTs) for various triggering circumstances in total hip arthroplasty (THA) individuals. A retrospective analysis of all RRT activations at a single, tertiary referral institution from 2014 to 2016 was conducted. Inclusion parameters were established as subjects >18 years old who underwent primary or revision THA. Data queried included demographics, principal reason for RRT, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), underlying cause, whether any modifications in treatment occurred, and whether the individual was uptriaged. In total, 168 RRTs were summoned on 153 hip replacement recipients (mean age 65.2 ± 14.1 years; mean body mass index 32.3 ± 4.8, 66% female). Duration of hospitalization in RRT for initial and repeat THA was 3.4 and 6.2 days, respectively. This was significantly longer than the duration of hospitalization for initial THA recipients (2.4 days, P < .001) and repeat THA recipients (4.6 days, P = .005) who did not require an RRT. There were no mortalities. RRTs for hypotension/presyncope (11%) and for syncope (11%) resulted in significantly fewer alterations in care (P < .01) than tachycardia (77%), hypoxia (57%), AMS (79%), and other (47%). RRTs for hypotension/presyncope (28%), syncope (15%), and hypoxia (30%) resulted in significantly fewer individuals being uptriaged (P < .001) than tachycardia (81%). Hypotension/presyncope was found to be significantly more commonly attributable to volume depletion (67%) (P < .001) than other causes. Hypoxia was significantly more commonly attributable to atelectasis (57%) and opioids/oversedation (30.4%) (P = .037). AMS/delirium was also significantly more commonly caused by opioids/over-sedation (71%) (P < .001). In subjects undergoing THA, RRTs for hypotension/presyncopal manifestations and syncope were significantly less likely to produce alterations in treatment or uptriaging compared to tachycardia. The most common causes were potentially preventable, including fluid deficit and opioid administration.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::21: Emergency medical services constitute a vital component of acute cerebrovascular event management. We developed a prehospital assessment instrument, the TOYOTA preliminary evaluation tool for tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) intravenous therapy (TOPSPIN) for triaging individuals with occlusive cerebrovascular events and particular indications for intravenous thrombolytic treatment in December 2006; this instrument comprises five elements including consciousness level, cardiac rhythm abnormality, verbal impairment, dysfunction of upper limbs, and dysfunction of lower limbs. The objective of this investigation was to analyze outcomes from a decade of implementation and distinguish occlusive cerebrovascular events from bleeding-related episodes in actual clinical practice. We prospectively enrolled consecutive individuals who were transported to our facility and assessed by Toyota city ambulance personnel utilizing this screening tool from December 2006 to January 2017. We examined definitive diagnoses at hospital discharge (occlusive cerebrovascular event, bleeding-related episode, or mimic), positive-predictive value of cerebrovascular events, recanalization procedure rate, and clinical differentiation among individuals with bleeding-related episodes, occlusive cerebrovascular events, and mimics. A total of 1,482 consecutive individuals were enrolled; 1,134 (76.5%) had confirmed cerebrovascular events (628 occlusive-type, 34 transient occlusive attack-type, and 472 bleeding-type) and 348 (23.5%) without cerebrovascular events (80 with seizure activity, 42 with syncope episodes, 27 with hypoglycemia, and 199 other conditions). Among 628 individuals with occlusive cerebrovascular events, 130 (20.7%) received intravenous recombinant thrombolytic treatment, endovascular procedure, or both interventions. The presence of cardiac rhythm abnormality, older age, lower blood pressure readings, and lower total screening scores was more commonly associated with occlusive cerebrovascular events than bleeding-related episodes. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, cardiac rhythm abnormality presence was independently associated with occlusive cerebrovascular events (OR 2.33; 95% CI 1.61-3.40). TOPSPIN represents a simple preliminary assessment instrument that includes cardiac rhythm abnormality evaluation. Detection of cardiac rhythm abnormalities during preliminary assessment may indicate higher probability of occlusive cerebrovascular events.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::22: We aim at determining the distance indicator for GDS-1408, representing the strongest z~7 stellar system nominee situated within the Hubble Ultra Deep Field. We employed every VLT observation of GDS-1408 gathered by our team plus two additional collaborations using FORS2 on VLT during the past five years, totaling 52hr exposure duration. The merged observation constitutes the most profound ever acquired for any stellar assembly during the Reionization era. We fail to identify emission features or continua across the entire wavelength span, extending to 10100A. Relying on precise simulation sets, we establish a rigorous upper boundary of f(Lya)<3x10^(-18) erg/s/cm2 at 3-9 sigma within the examined wavelength interval, matching a rest-frame equivalent width EW<9A. Merging this boundary with SED modeling allows us to refine the distance parameter to z=6.82+/- 0.1 (1-sigma). Identical SED fitting reveals that GDS-1408 exhibits relatively substantial extinction (A1600~1) alongside a dust-corrected stellar formation velocity of approximately 20 Msol/yr. Comparing the unattenuated equivalent width anticipated by case-B recombination theory against the observed boundary yields a constraint on the effective Lya escape proportion of f_(esc)^(eff)(Lya)<8%. Although we cannot exclude major contributions from the inter/circum galactic environment in suppressing the feature, a reasonable interpretation suggests that GDS-1408 appears moderately evolved and harbors adequate gas plus particulate matter to attenuate the Lya radiation before reaching the intergalactic environment. Distance confirmation for even the premier z~7 nominees proves extremely difficult to accomplish (unless the Lya or unusually powerful rest-UV nebular radiation features appear) with current generations of 8-10m class instruments. We demonstrate that both JWST and E-ELT will prove necessary to achieve decisive progress. Presently, the enhanced distance precision obtained through this kind of methodology renders ALMA an intriguing alternative for distance verification.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::23: The persistence of Salmonella species as pathogenic indicators during composting underwent investigation. The inoculation technique provided known quantities of these bacteria involved in decomposition processes. Bacterial suspension was introduced directly into organic waste materials. Direct introduction underwent comparison with vial-based inoculation methods. Salmonella solution was placed inside containers and inserted into the central portion of decomposing matter before initiating the breakdown procedure. The conventional approach utilized for enumerating these microorganisms is serial dilution followed by standard membrane filtration as recommended in quality standards PAS 100 and British regulations (BS EN ISO 6579:2002). This investigation was designed to examine relationships between heat levels and substrate contact that may influence pathogenic activation specifically for these enterobacteria. Exposure to average thermal conditions during decomposition of approximately 55-60°C was maintained for no less than three days as previously reported to sufficiently eliminate the vast majority of intestinal pathogens (Deportes et al., 1995). Bacterial quantities and thermal measurements for both specimens served as indicators to determine persistence in direct versus indirect inoculation scenarios. This research provides figures regarding die-off rates for these organisms throughout the decomposition period. Differentiation between immediate substrate contact (Specimen A) and non-contact with organic matter (Specimen B) during breakdown was also revealed. Results from laboratory-scale decomposition experiments demonstrated that after eight days (which included exposure to at least 66°C) bacterial numbers in Specimen A fell below limits specified in UK standards (designated as PAS 100)(BSI, 2005) which mandated finished humus be free of these enterobacteria. Meanwhile, Specimen B continued yielding elevated bacterial counts even following twenty days of processing. The findings clearly demonstrate that physical contact with decomposing substrates significantly accelerates pathogen elimination compared to protected inoculation within sealed containers, suggesting substrate interaction plays a crucial role in microbial inactivation beyond thermal effects alone.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::24: BACKGROUND: Although ethnicity is associated with prostate malignancy progression in early stage illness, once patients have advanced conditions, it remains unclear whether racial background continues to predict poor outcomes. The investigators hypothesized that, in an equal-access setting among individuals with castration-resistant prostatic carcinoma (CRPC) and no known metastases (M0/Mx), African American males would receive imaging tests at similar rates as non-African American males (ie, there would be equivalent opportunity to detect spreading) but would have higher risk of metastatic spread. METHODS: In total, 837 patients who were diagnosed with M0/Mx CRPC during 2000 through 2014 from 5 Veterans Affairs medical centers in the SEARCH (Shared Equal Access Regional Cancer Hospital) database were analyzed. Information on all diagnostic imaging after CRPC identification was collected, including date, modality, and result. Multivariable Cox models were used to test associations between racial background and the interval to first metastasis, initial osseous metastasis, first bone scan, second skeletal scan among subjects who had negative initial skeletal imaging, and overall survival. RESULTS: African American participants (n = 306) were equally as likely as non-African American participants (n = 531) to receive primary and secondary skeletal scans after a diagnosis of CRPC. There were no significant differences in the likelihood of developing any spreading, osseous spreading, interval to skeletal imaging, or overall mortality between African American subjects and non-African American subjects (all P > .2). CONCLUSIONS: The lack of ethnic differences in the development of metastases and scanning practices observed in this investigation suggests that, once individuals have a diagnosis of M0/Mx CRPC, ethnicity may not be a prognostic factor. Efforts to understand prostatic malignancy ethnic disparities may derive greater benefit by focusing on the likelihood of developing prostatic carcinoma and on the outcomes of patients who have early stage illness. Cancer 2016;122:3848-3855. © 2016 American Cancer Society.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::25: We present deep Hubble Space Telescope single-star photometry of Leo A in B, V, and I. Our new field of view is offset from the centrally located region observed by Tolstoy et al. (1998) in order to expose the halo population of this dwarf system. We report the detection of metal-poor red horizontal branch objects, which demonstrate that Leo A is not a young entity. In fact, this galaxy proves at least as old as metal-deficient Galactic Globular Clusters which exhibit crimson horizontal branches, and are considered to have a minimum age of about 9 Gyr. We discuss the distance to Leo A, and perform an extensive comparison of the observations with stellar isochrones. For a modulus of 24.5, the measurements are better than 50% complete down to absolute magnitudes of 2 or more. We can easily identify luminous sources with metallicities between 0.0001 and 0.0004, and ages between approximately 5 and 10 Gyr, in their post-main-sequence phases, but lack the discovery of main-sequence turnoffs which would provide unambiguous proof of ancient (>10 Gyr) generations. Blue horizontal branch objects are above the detection limits, but difficult to distinguish from youthful sources with similar colors and brightnesses. Synthetic color-magnitude diagrams show it is possible to populate the azure horizontal branch in the halo of Leo A. The models also suggest roughly 50% of the total astrated mass in our pointing to be attributed to an ancient (>10 Gyr) component. We conclude that Leo A started forming luminous matter at least about 9 Gyr ago. This dwarf exhibits an extremely low oxygen abundance, of only 3% of Solar, in its ionized interstellar medium. The existence of elderly material in this very oxygen-deficient system illustrates that a low oxygen content does not preclude a history of early formation activity involving such celestial bodies.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::26: One objective of neuromorphic engineering involves creating 'realistic' robotic apparatus that interacts with the physical environment by adopting neuromechanical principles from biology. Critical to this aim is the methodology for implementing spinal circuitry responsible for afferented muscular behavior. At its core, muscle afferentation constitutes closed-loop activity arising from interactions among populations of spindle proprioceptors, alpha and gamma motoneurons, plus fibers enabling useful actions. We used programmable very-large-scale-circuit (VLSI) hardware for implementing simple spiking neuronal models, skeletal musculature, proprioceptive sensors, alpha-motoneuronal recruitment, gamma-motoneuronal sensitivity control, and monosynaptic connectivity linking them together. This multi-scale assembly of spiking cellular populations emulated physiological properties characterizing a pair of antagonistic afferented mammalian muscles—each simulated by 1024 alpha- and gamma-motoneurones—acting on a joint via long tendons. This integrated configuration maintained joint angles successfully, and reproduced stretch reflex responses even when driving nonlinear biomechanics of an actual cadaveric finger. Moreover, this arrangement allowed exploration of numerous values and combinations of gamma-static plus gamma-dynamic gains when operating a robotic digit, some replicating certain human pathological conditions. Lastly, we explored behavioral consequences of adopting three alternative formulations of isometric force production. We found that dynamic responses to rate-coded spike trains produce ramps that can be very sensitive to tendon elasticity, especially at high output. Our methodology produced, to our knowledge, the first example of an autonomous, multi-scale, neuromorphic, neuromechanical apparatus capable of creating realistic reflex activity in cadaveric digits. This research platform allows exploration of mechanisms behind healthy and pathological sensorimotor function in the physical environment by building them from first principles, and it serves as a precursor to neuromorphic robotic apparatus. Such systems promise to advance our understanding of biological motor control through hardware implementations that faithfully capture essential features of natural neuromuscular organization.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::27: Introduction and Objective: Individuals presenting with urinary tract infections alongside kidney or ureteral stones represent a urologic emergency often achieving early clinical stability but remaining hospitalized while awaiting results from urine antibiotic sensitivity analyses. We aimed to identify clinical predictors of antimicrobial resistance in those who underwent urgent decompression for sepsis and obstructive urolithiasis to facilitate early discharge on empiric oral therapy. Methods: Subjects who required emergent drainage for infection and an obstructing calculus from 2014 to 2018 at two academic medical centers were identified. Emergency stent placement was performed and individuals received broad-spectrum intravenous antimicrobials. We assessed the association between parameters at presentation and susceptibility to at least one drug from culture using the Wilcoxon test and Fisher exact test for continuous and categorical variables, respectively. Multivariate logistic regression was then conducted using all significant factors from univariate evaluation. Results: Out of 134 enrolled, 84 subjects (62.7%) had cultures demonstrating reduced susceptibility to at least one agent. On univariate evaluation, those with resistant isolates were significantly more likely to have had previous ureteroscopy, require postoperative intensive care unit-level management, have bacteremia, and a longer hospitalization duration. In multivariate modeling using significant factors from univariate evaluation, only prior ureteroscopy was significantly associated with antimicrobial resistance with an increased odds of 6.95 (p = 0.011). Conclusions: In this investigation, we demonstrate that a background of ureteroscopy is significantly correlated with reduced drug susceptibility in both univariate and multivariate evaluations. Our findings suggest that individuals with a background of prior endoscopic intervention should await culture sensitivity outcomes, while those without such surgical history may be released early on empiric oral therapy. However, future investigations are necessary to determine the effectiveness of this predictor for guiding discharge decisions and optimizing patient management strategies.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::28: Evidence details how cannabis can influence consumption patterns of other psychoactive substances, including prescription medications, alcohol, tobacco and illicit drugs, but very little research has examined factors associated with these modifications in usage behaviors. This paper explores self-reported utilization of marijuana as a replacement for drinking among a Canadian medical cannabis patient population. Data was derived from a survey of 2102 people enrolled in the national therapeutic marijuana program. We included 973 (44%) respondents who reported consuming alcoholic beverages on at least 10 occasions over a 12 month period prior to initiating treatment, and then used retrospective information on frequency and amount of drinking pre-and post treatment initiation to determine which participant characteristics and other variables were associated with reductions and/or cessation. Overall, 419 (44%) participants reported decreases in beverage consumption over 30 days, 323 (34%) diminished the number of standard servings they had per week, and 76 (8%) reported no drinking at all in the 30 days prior to completing the questionnaire. Being below 55 years of age and reporting higher rates in the pre-period were both associated with greater odds of reducing intake, and an intention to utilize therapeutic marijuana to curtail drinking was associated with significantly greater odds of both reducing and ceasing consumption altogether. Our findings suggest that treatment initiation may be associated with self-reported reductions and cessation among patients. Since alcoholic beverages are the most prevalent recreational substance in North America, and their consumption results in significant rates of criminality, morbidity and mortality, these findings may result in improved health outcomes for therapeutic marijuana patients, as well as overall improvements in public health and safety. The relationship between marijuana treatment and decreased drinking warrants further investigation to better understand mechanisms underlying substitution effects.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::29: The delicate balance among spin-orbit coupling, Coulomb repulsion and crystalline electric field interactions observed in Ir-based oxides is usually manifested as exotic magnetic behavior. Here we investigate the evolution of exchange coupling between Co and Ir for partial La substitution by Ca in La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$. A great advantage of using Ca$^{2+}$ as replacement for La$^{3+}$ is the similarity of its ionic radii. Thus, the observed magnetic changes can more easily be associated with electronic variations. A thorough investigation of structural, electronic and magnetic properties of the La$_{2-x}$Ca$_{x}$CoIrO$_6$ system was carried out by means of synchrotron x-ray powder diffraction, muon spin rotation and relaxation ($\mu$SR), AC and DC magnetization, XAS, XMCD, Raman spectroscopy, electrical resistivity and dielectric permittivity. Our XAS results show that up to 25% of Ca substitution at the La site results in emergence of Co$^{3+}$, possibly in high spin state, while introduction of larger amounts of Ca leads to increase of Ir valence. The competing magnetic interactions resulting from mixed valences lead to coexistence of a magnetically ordered phase and an emerging spin glass (SG) state for doped samples. Our $\mu$SR findings indicate that for La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$ a nearly constant fraction of a paramagnetic (PM) phase persists down to low temperature, possibly related to presence of a small amount of Ir$^{3+}$ and to anti-site disorder at Co/Ir sites. For doped compounds the PM phase freezes below 30 K, but there remains some dynamics associated with the SG. The dielectric data obtained for parent compound and one with 25% of Ca-doping indicate a possible magnetodielectric effect, which is discussed in terms of electron hopping between TM ions, anti-site disorder and distorted crystalline structure. These observations collectively demonstrate how controlled cation substitution modifies competing exchange pathways within double perovskite materials.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::30: With stringent requirements introduced by novel sixth-generation (6G) internet-of-things (IoT) scenarios, traditional approaches toward multiple access control have started revealing their limitations. A fresh wave of grant-free (GF) methods has been therefore proposed as viable alternatives. However, definitive solutions remain to be accomplished. In our work, we propose an innovative semi-GF coordinated random entry (RA) protocol, denoted partial-information multiple connectivity (PIMA), to reduce packet loss plus latency, particularly when sporadic activations occur. We consider machine-type communications (MTC) environments, wherein devices need transmitting data packets via uplink toward base stations (BS). When using PIMA, BSs can acquire partial information regarding instantaneous traffic conditions and, utilizing compute-over-the-air techniques, estimate quantities of devices with packets awaiting transmission within their queues. Based on this knowledge, BSs assign each device single slots for transmissions. However, since individual slots may still be allocated to several users, collisions might occur. Both total quantities of allocated slots plus user assignments are optimized, based upon estimated quantities of active users, reducing collisions while improving efficiency of multiple connectivity schemes. To prove validity of our solution, we compare PIMA against time-division multiple-entry (TDMA) alongside slotted ALOHA (SALOHA) schemes, ideal solutions for orthogonal multiple connectivity (OMA) in temporal domains under cases of low versus high traffic conditions, respectively. We demonstrate that PIMA can not only adapt toward different traffic circumstances and provide fewer packet drops regardless of intensity of packet generations, but also merge advantages of both TDMA alongside SALOHA schemes, thus providing performance improvements concerning packet loss probability plus latency metrics. Our findings establish PIMA's capability to dynamically adjust operational parameters while maintaining superior throughput characteristics across varying network load scenarios.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::31: Background and purpose — Skeletal remodeling as a response to osseous trauma, postoperative immobilization, and device-related reactions can lead to loss of stock and increase the risk of periprosthetic fracture and aseptic loosening. This study investigates adaptive changes in the proximal tibia after uncemented total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Patients and methods — We performed a 2-year follow-up of 53 individuals (mean age 62 (38–70) years, 27 of whom were men, who received an uncemented TKA in a randomized controlled trial with mineral density (BMD) as secondary endpoint. Participants were randomized to 2 groups of either monoblock (A) or modular (B) polyethylene design. The procedures were performed using the Zimmer Nexgen trabecular metal prosthesis. Measurements of BMD were done postoperatively and after 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. Density was measured in 3 regions of interest (ROI). Results and interpretation — In cohort A statistically significant alterations in BMD were seen after 24 months in both the medial and lateral ROI. Values decreased medially by 15% (p = 0.004) and laterally by 13% (p = 0.01). In cohort B the changes were limited and after 24 months returned to the preoperative baseline. The differences in change between cohorts were statistically significant in both the medial (p = 0.03) and lateral (p = 0.02) ROI. In the distal area we found no significant alteration in either cohort. A significantly different remodeling pattern of the proximal tibia was observed in the 2 cohorts with a higher degree of loss in the knees that received the monoblock polyethylene configuration, indicating that the flexible implant configuration, previously shown to improve fixation, does not decrease the skeletal loss of the proximal tibia despite expectations otherwise.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::32: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) are bio-inspired models of computational processing that have proven highly effective. Still, ANNs lack a natural notion of temporality, and processing elements in ANNs exchange analog values through frame-based transmission, a computationally and energetically inefficient form of communication. This contrasts sharply with biological neurons that communicate sparingly and efficiently using binary action potentials. While artificial Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) can be constructed by replacing the components of an ANN with pulsing neuron units, the current performance remains far from that achieved by deep ANNs on challenging benchmarks and these SNNs utilize much higher discharge frequencies compared to their biological counterparts, limiting their efficiency. Here we demonstrate how pulsing neurons employing an efficient form of information representation can be used to construct SNNs that match high-performance ANNs and exceed state-of-the-art results in SNNs on important benchmarks, while requiring much lower average emission frequencies. For this purpose, we use spike-time encoding based on the discharge limitation adaptation phenomenon observed in biological pulsing neurons. This phenomenon can be captured in adapting neuron models, for which we derive the effective transfer function. Processing elements in ANNs trained with this transformation function can be substituted directly with adaptive pulsing neurons, and the resulting Adaptive SNNs (AdSNNs) can carry out inference in deep networks using up to an order of magnitude fewer pulses compared to previous SNNs. Adaptive spike-time encoding additionally allows for dynamic control of information representation precision: we demonstrate how a simple arousal model in AdSNNs further halves the average required emission frequency and this concept naturally extends to other forms of attention. AdSNNs thus hold promise as a novel and efficient framework for computational processing that naturally fits temporally continuous and asynchronous applications.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::33: Context. LQ Hya represents one of the most frequently investigated young solar analogue objects. Recently, observations have revealed intriguing behaviour through analysing extended-term photometry: during 2003--2009, a coherent spot configuration migrating within the rotational reference frame was reported by various researchers, but since that period the stellar body entered a disordered state where organized structures appear to have vanished and rapid phase jumps of photometric minima occur irregularly over time. Aims. LQ Hya is among the objects included in the SOFIN/FIES extended-term monitoring campaign spanning 25 years. Here we publish new temperature charts for this target during 2006--2017, covering the disordered condition of the system. Methods. We employ a Doppler imaging technique to derive surface temperature distributions from high-resolution spectra. Results. From mean temperatures of these reconstructed maps we observe a weak but systematic increase in the photospheric temperature of the target. This finding is consistent with simultaneously increasing photometric magnitude. During nearly all observing seasons we detect a high-latitude spot configuration which is clearly nonaxisymmetric. The phase behaviour of this feature is very erratic but agrees reasonably well with photometry. Equatorial spots are also frequently detected, but many of these we interpret to be artefacts due to poor to moderate phase coverage. Conclusions. Even during the disordered episode of the object, the spot topology has remained very similar to higher activity epochs with more organized and long-lived configurations: we observe high-latitude and equatorial activity, the mid-latitude range still being most often void of features. We interpret the erratic jumps and drifts in phase of photometric minima to be caused by changes in high-latitude configurations rather than equatorial ones. This interpretation suggests that variations in polar regions dominate the observed photometric evolution throughout the monitoring period.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::34: Context: Hydrogenation processes are expected to be among the most important surface transformations on interstellar frozen materials. However, solid state astrochemical laboratory data on transformations of hydrogen atoms with common cosmic ice constituents are largely lacking. Aims: The goal of our experimental work is to determine whether and how carbon dioxide (CO2), formic acid (HCOOH) and acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) undergo reactions with atomic hydrogen in the solid phase at low temperatures and to derive destruction rates and production yields. Methods: Pure CO2, HCOOH and CH3CHO interstellar frozen analogues are bombarded by H-atoms in an ultra-high vacuum experiment. The samples are monitored by reflection absorption infrared spectroscopy and the resulting products are detected in the gas stage through temperature programmed desorption to determine the destruction and formation amounts as well as the corresponding transformation speeds. Results: Within the sensitivity of our set-up we conclude that hydrogen atom bombardment of pure CO2 and HCOOH specimens does not result in detectable products. The upper limits on the destruction speeds are less or equal to 7e(-17) cm^2/s which make it unlikely that these species play a major role in the creation of more complex organics in interstellar frozen materials due to processes with atomic hydrogen. In contrast, CH3CHO does undergo transformations with H-atoms. At most 20% is hydrogenated to ethanol (C2H5OH) and a second pathway leads to the break-up of the carbon-carbon bond to form solid methane (~20%) as well as H2CO and CH3OH (15-50%). The methane generation amount is expected to be equal to the summed quantity of H2CO and CH3OH and therefore CH4 most likely evaporates partly after creation due to the high exothermicity of the process. The destruction speeds for CH3CHO depend on specimen temperature and not on sample thickness.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::35: The methodology of funnel regulation was introduced during the early 2000s, developing since then across numerous respects while achieving mathematical maturity balanced through practical implementations. Its fundamental tenet involves attainment of prescribed transient plus asymptotic behaviour for continuous-time regulated dynamical processes encompassing linear alongside nonlinear structures described via functional differential equations, differential-algebraic frameworks, and partial differential formulations. Considered are classes of configurations specified through structural properties - such as relative degree combined with stable internal dynamics - belonging to these arrangements only; precise data remain generally unknown, reflecting that any model representing a dynamical process lacks precision. Prespecified are: a funnel shaped by choosing a smooth function freely selected by designers, fairly large collections of smooth reference trajectories, and a configuration class satisfying certain structural characteristics. The aim involves designing, based on structural assumptions plus input-output information exclusively, a single 'simple' regulation strategy -- termed the funnel regulator -- so its application to any arrangement within the given collection and to any reference trajectory results in feasibility of the funnel regulation objective: solutions of closed-loop arrangements avoid blow-up in finite time, all variables remain bounded, and -- most importantly -- evolution of error between the arrangement's output and the reference trajectory remains within prespecified funnels. In the Introduction, we describe genesis of funnel regulation. Afterward, we investigate diverse configuration classes amenable to funnel regulation. Funnel regulation is demonstrated for configurations with arbitrary relative degree and arrangements described through partial differential formulations. Finally, we discuss input limitations and implementations, exploring how these constraints affect performance and examining various practical scenarios where this approach proves beneficial for achieving desired tracking objectives.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::36: With the growing variety of Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks, designing a completely protected network becomes extremely challenging. For instance, Stealthy Link Flooding Attack (SLFA) represents a variant that strives to block access toward target areas by overwhelming small sets of connections, bypassing traditional defensive mechanisms. One potential solution for tackling such threats involves applying Moving Target Defense (MTD) techniques where configurations are dynamically altered to confuse and deceive adversaries, thus making successful campaigns highly expensive to launch. However, since this approach comes with certain overhead costs, finding optimal strategies—specifically when and to what extent implementation should occur—has been a major challenge. Such strategic decisions are significantly influenced by adversary behavior patterns that remain difficult to predict. In our work, we address obtaining superior tactical approaches that effectively mitigate these flooding assaults while incurring minimal operational burdens. We formulate the problem as signaling game theory, considering system defenders and hostile actors as participants. A belief function is established throughout engagements during campaigns, which gets utilized for picking best responses and actions for each participant. We analyze this theoretical model and derive protective measures based on equilibria within the framework. We evaluate our technique on Mininet-based environments where adversaries perform stealthy link-flooding operations and defenders apply moving-target defenses based on equilibrium principles. The results demonstrate that our signaling-game-based dynamic protective methodology can provide similar levels of security against such assaults like extensive implementations, however, causing significantly reduced operational expenses. This methodology proves effective through empirical validation, showing that intelligent application of countermeasures outperforms continuous deployment while maintaining comparable effectiveness. The framework balances protection requirements with resource constraints, offering practical advantages for real-world deployment scenarios where computational and bandwidth limitations must be carefully managed.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::37: Multi-fidelity (MF) techniques are gaining popularity for enhancing surrogate modeling and design optimization by incorporating data from various low-fidelity (LF) sources. While most existing MF approaches assume a fixed dataset, adaptive sampling strategies that dynamically allocate resources among different accuracy levels can achieve higher efficiency in exploring and exploiting the parameter space. However, most current MF procedures rely on hierarchical assumptions regarding precision tiers or fail to capture intercorrelations between multiple accuracy gradations and utilize them to quantify the value of future observations and navigate the sequential selection process. To address this hurdle, we propose a framework hinged on latent embedding for distinct accuracy representations and associated pre-posterior analysis to explicitly leverage their correlation for adaptive observation selection. In this methodology, each infill iteration includes two steps: We first identify the location of interest with greatest potential improvement using high-fidelity (HF) evaluations, then we search for the next observation across all precision tiers that maximize enhancement per unit expenditure at the position identified in the first stage. This is made possible by a single Latent Variable Gaussian Process (LVGP) formulation that maps distinct accuracy representations into an interpretable hidden dimension to capture their correlations without assuming hierarchical precision structures. The LVGP enables us to assess how LF candidates will affect HF response through pre-posterior examination and determine the subsequent observation with optimal benefit-to-cost ratio. Through test scenarios, we demonstrate that the proposed technique outperforms benchmark approaches in both MF global fitting (GF) and Bayesian Optimization (BO) problems in convergence speed and robustness. Moreover, the methodology offers flexibility to switch between GF and BO by simply changing the acquisition criterion.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::38: Cytotoxic lesions affecting the corpus callosum represent secondary damage induced by substantial elevations in cytokine concentrations within cerebral tissue and are associated with subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). However, their clinical significance for individuals suffering from SAH remains unclear. We retrospectively examined patients experiencing SAH who received treatment at our hospital and evaluated between-group differences regarding backgrounds, clinical findings, and outcomes comparing those developing cytotoxic damage to the corpus callosum versus individuals who did not. We further contrasted subjects achieving favorable results with those experiencing unfavorable prognoses. Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified risk factors predicting adverse clinical results. We studied 159 SAH sufferers; 17 subjects (10.7%) exhibited cytotoxic damage affecting the corpus callosum. Individuals manifesting such cytotoxic injury were more likely presenting severe conditions (World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies grading IV-V: odds ratio [OR], 4.53; 95% confidence interval [95% CI]: 1.60-12.84; p = 0.0042) and displaying intraventricular (OR, 5.98; 95% CI: 1.32-27.13; p = 0.0054) or intraparenchymal hematoma (OR, 3.62; 95% CI: 1.25-10.45; p = 0.023). Subjects showing cytotoxic injury demonstrated greater propensity toward unfavorable prognosis 3 months following onset (modified Rankin Scale score 0-2: OR, 0.22; 95% CI: 0.07-0.66; p = 0.0043). Multivariate analysis confirmed such cytotoxic damage increased risk for adverse prognosis (OR, 4.39; 95% CI: 1.06-18.1; p = 0.037). Development of these cytotoxic injuries may relate to hematoma extent among SAH sufferers. Although typically reversible pathology, emergence of cytotoxic damage involving the corpus callosum might serve as a predictor signaling poor outcomes for individuals experiencing SAH, suggesting important prognostic implications warranting clinical attention.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::39: Data regarding suitable protocols for sedating Nordestino donkeys remains limited. To assess the calming and cardiovascular-respiratory impacts of reduced dosages of intravenous (i.v.) xylazine combined with or without acepromazine in 'Nordestino' donkeys. Seven healthy female animals (150 ± 18 kg) participated in this blinded, randomised, crossover investigation. Four regimens were administered, comprising two i.v. injections, at baseline (T0, 1st administration) and 15 minutes later (T15, 2nd administration). Regimens included acepromazine 0.05 mg/kg bodyweight plus saline (AS), saline plus xylazine 0.5 mg/kg bodyweight (SX0.5), acepromazine plus xylazine 0.25 mg/kg bodyweight (AX0.25) or acepromazine plus xylazine 0.5 mg/kg bodyweight (AX0.5). Sedative and cardiovascular-respiratory variables were assessed before T0 and 15, 20, 30, 45, 60, 75 and 90 minutes following treatment. Degree [height of head above ground (HHAG)] and quality of sedation [ataxia, responses to stimuli and visual analogue scale (VAS) scoring] and respiratory frequency were evaluated by the principal researcher in situ, while heart rhythm was measured by an assistant researcher. Three experienced evaluators examined videos for ataxia and responses to stimuli. Normal distributions were analysed using repeated measures ANOVA, and non-normal distributions by Kruskal-Wallis (P<0.05). HHAG was reduced compared to baseline for 15 minutes following xylazine injection in AX0.25 and for 30 minutes in SX0.5 and AX0.5 cohorts. All regimens containing xylazine elevated VAS and ataxia scores in situ for 15 minutes post-xylazine injection, with no distinctions between cohorts. Ataxia scores in situ were greater in SX0.5 and AX0.5 cohorts than AS for 15 and 30 minutes post-xylazine injection, respectively. Absence of a negative control cohort (saline-saline). Acepromazine combined with xylazine at 0.25 mg/kg bodyweight yielded shorter and gentler sedation compared to xylazine at 0.5 mg/kg bodyweight.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::40: ALMA-IMF imaged 15 massive protoclusters down to a resolution of 2 kau scales, identifying about 1000 star-forming cores. The mass and luminosity of these condensations, which are fundamental physical characteristics, remain difficult to determine, a problem greatly exacerbated at the distances >2 kpc of ALMA-IMF regions. We combined new datasets and radiative transfer modeling to characterize these objects. We estimated their mass-averaged temperature and the resulting values these calculations imply. For 1/6 of the sample, we measured the bolometric output, implementing deblending corrections when necessary. We used spectral energy distribution (SED) analysis obtained with the PPMAP Bayesian procedure, which aims to preserve the best angular sharpness of the input information. We extrapolated the brightness and dust warmth images provided by PPMAP at 2.5" clarity to estimate those of individual condensations, which were identified at higher spatial precision. To accomplish this, we applied approximate radiative exchange relationships between the output of a protostar and the warmth of its surrounding envelope and between the external heating of prestellar structures and their thermal properties. For the first time, we provide data-informed assessments of grain warmth for 883 condensations identified with ALMA-IMF: 17-31 K and 28-79 K (5th and 95th percentiles, up to 127 K) for the 617 prestellar and 266 protostellar entities, respectively. We also measured embryonic stellar brightness spanning 20-80 000 Lsun. For hot structures, we obtained systematically lower thermal values than studies based on complex organic molecules. We established a mass-brightness evolutionary diagram, for the first time at the condensation spatial scale and for a large collection of high-mass embryonic stellar objects. The ALMA-IMF observations favor a scenario in which protostars accrete their material from a larger reservoir than their host condensations.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::41: The objective of this investigation was examining the function of microRNA (miR)-27a-3p in osteoarthritis (OA). Reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction plus western blotting were performed determining levels of miR-27a-3p alongside aggrecanase-2 (ADAMTS5) within cartilage specimens from patients suffering OA versus healthy controls, additionally within interleukin (IL)-1beta-treated primary human chondrocytes. Primary human chondrocytes underwent transfection utilizing miR-27a-3p. A luciferase reporter assay validated direct contact between miR-27a-3p alongside its putative binding location within the 3'-untranslated region ADAMTS5 mRNA. Furthermore, impacts of IL-1beta-induced activation regarding mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) plus nuclear factor (NF)-kappaB on miR-27a-3p were evaluated employing specific inhibitors. Results revealed that concentrations of miR-27a-3p were diminished in OA cartilage specimens compared against those from normal controls. Additionally, decreased miR-27a-3p alongside increased ADAMTS5 was observed in a time- plus dose-dependent manner within chondrocytes treated utilizing IL-1beta. Furthermore, overexpression regarding miR-27a-3p suppressed levels regarding ADAMTS5 in human chondrocytes induced by IL-1beta. miR-27a-3p overexpression also decreased luciferase activity regarding the wild-type ADAMTS5 reporter plasmid. Mutation regarding the miR-27a-3p binding location within the 3'-untranslated region regarding ADAMTS5 mRNA abolished the miR-27a-3p-mediated repression regarding reporter activity. Furthermore, utilization regarding specific inhibitors demonstrated that IL-1beta may regulate miR-27a-3p via NF-kappaB alongside MAPK signaling routes in chondrocytes. This investigation concluded that miR-27a-3p was downregulated in human OA and was suppressed by IL-1beta, functioning as a crucial regulator regarding ADAMTS5 in OA chondrocytes. Additionally, IL-1beta-mediated suppression regarding miR-27a-3p activity may occur through the MAPK alongside NF-kappaB routes. This investigation may provide a novel strategy for clinical intervention regarding OA caused by upregulation regarding miR-27a-3p, offering potential therapeutic implications for managing this degenerative joint disease.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::42: Space weathering represents a phenomenon transforming surfaces of airless planetary bodies. Primary agents include solar wind irradiation and micrometeoroid bombardment. These mechanisms alter planetary reflectance spectra and frequently modify compositional diagnostic features. In this investigation we concentrated on simulating and comparing spectral modifications caused by solar wind exposure and micrometeoroid impacts to gain improved understanding of individual processes. We utilized olivine and pyroxene pellets as proxies for planetary materials. To replicate solar wind conditions we employed hydrogen, helium, and argon ions with energies ranging from 5 to 40 keV and fluences reaching $10^{18}$ particles/cm$^2$. To mimic micrometeoroid bombardment we applied individual femtosecond laser pulses. We analyzed corresponding evolution of different spectral parameters, determined by applying Modified Gaussian Model methodology, and conducted principal component analysis. Original mineralogy influences spectral development more than the weathering mechanism, as demonstrated by diverse evolution of slope in olivine versus pyroxene upon exposure. Slope modifications observed in olivine remain consistent with observations of A-type asteroids, while moderate to absent slope alterations detected in pyroxene align with asteroid (4) Vesta characteristics. We also noticed some distinctions in effects induced by the two agents. Ions replicating solar wind exert smaller influence on longer wavelengths compared to laser treatment representing micrometeoroid collisions. This difference most likely stems from distinct penetration depths of ions versus laser pulses. Our findings suggest that in certain instances distinguishing between contributions of the two mechanisms on a weathered terrain might be achievable. The investigation demonstrates how original composition plays a critical role in determining final spectral characteristics after exposure to space weathering phenomena, whether through particle bombardment or electromagnetic radiation interactions with mineral surfaces.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::43: HEALPix by G\'orski et. al. (2005) represents the de-facto standard for Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) information storage plus analysis, finding widespread adoption in contemporary and forthcoming CMB experiments. Nearly every dataset within the Legacy Archive for Microwave Background Data Analysis (LAMBDA) employs HEALPix as its preferred format. Visualizing such information plays a crucial role in research, prompting development of several toolsets designed to accomplish this with HEALPix maps, most notably original Fortran facilities alongside Python integration via healpy. Given current GPU performance capabilities, visualizing extremely large maps in real time on laptops or tablets has become feasible. The HEALPix Viewer described here was developed for macOS, taking full advantage of GPU acceleration to handle massive datasets interactively. It compiles natively on Intel and Arm64 architectures, utilizing Metal framework for high-performance GPU computations. This project aims to reduce effort required for interactive exploration while minimizing time overhead when producing publication-quality cartographic representations. Drag-and-drop integration with Keynote and PowerPoint simplifies presentation creation. The main codebase is written in Swift, a modern and efficient compiled language, with high-performance computing tasks delegated entirely to GPUs, plus several inserts in C interfacing to cfitsio library for input/output operations. The graphical user interface utilizes SwiftUI, a novel declarative UI framework based on Swift. Most common spherical projections and colormaps are supported out of the box, and available source code simplifies customization of the application and addition of new features if desired. Overall performance improves upon existing Python software stack by a factor ranging from 3 to 180x depending on the specific task at hand.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::44: To compare cervical shear wave elastography (SWE) utilizing transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) between twin and singleton pregnant women. This prospective cohort investigation involved expectant mothers carrying twins or singletons attending antenatal care at Ramathibodi Hospital, Bangkok, Thailand. Participants meeting inclusion criteria underwent serial measurements of shear wave speed (SWS) via TVS during early, mid-, and third trimesters. Changes in SWS with advancing gestational age among twin versus singleton gestations were evaluated. Delivery timing and spontaneous preterm birth rates were also analyzed. A total of 36 twin gestations and 38 singleton gestations were examined. No significant differences in baseline characteristics emerged, except maternal age (twin group 33.1±4.6 years, singleton group 29.9±5.4 years, p-value = 0.006). Cervical SWS declined with advancing gestation in both groups, but a statistically significant variation in cervical SWS at the lower location during mid-gestation appeared (twin cohort 2.27±0.4, singleton cohort 2.71±0.6 m/s, p-value = 0.001). However, no significant variations in cervical SWS at upper or lower locations during early or third periods were demonstrated. Although delivery timing revealed significant disparities between groups (twin cohort 35.9±2.8, singleton cohort 37.6±2.9 wk., p-value = 0.008), spontaneous preterm birth rates did not differ significantly (twin cohort 22.2%, singleton cohort 15.8%, p-value = 0.483). Mid-gestation cervical SWS assessment at the lower location detects disparities in cervical softness between twin versus singleton gestations. Cervical SWS might represent an additional option for monitoring alterations in cervical softness among twin gestations, providing valuable information for clinical management and risk stratification purposes in obstetric practice.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::45: Chromosomal count represents a crucial characteristic of higher-order genomic organization, and alterations in chromosomal quantity play a fundamental role in evolutionary processes. Dysploid gains plus losses in chromosomal tallies, alongside polyploidization occurrences, may drive reproductive isolation and lineage diversification. Recent development of probabilistic frameworks for chromosomal numerical shifts in groundbreaking work by Mayrose et al. (2010, ChromEvol) have enabled inference of ancestral karyotypes over molecular phylogenies and generated novel interest in studying the contribution of karyotypic modifications to evolutionary dynamics. However, the ChromEvol approach assumes all transformations occur anagenetically (along branches), without modeling specifically cladogenetic phenomena. Cladogenetic transitions may be expected if karyotypic rearrangements result in reproductive isolation. Here we present a new class of frameworks for chromosomal numerical shifts (called ChromoSSE) that incorporate both anagenetic plus cladogenetic variation. The ChromoSSE framework allows us to determine the mode of karyotypic transformation; is such variation occurring primarily within lineages, predominantly at splitting events, or in taxon-specific combinations of both? Furthermore, we can estimate the location and timing of possible speciation through chromosomal restructuring across the phylogeny. We implemented ChromoSSE in a Bayesian statistical paradigm, specifically in the software RevBayes, to accommodate uncertainty in parameter estimates while leveraging the full power of likelihood-based methods. We tested ChromoSSE's accuracy with simulations and re-examined karyotypic diversification in Aristolochia, Carex section Spirostachyae, Helianthus, Mimulus sensu lato (s.l.), and Primula section Aleuritia, finding evidence for taxon-specific combinations of anagenetic and cladogenetic dysploid plus polyploid patterns of chromosomal diversification. [Anagenetic; Bayes factors; chromosome evolution; chromosome speciation; chromoSSE; cladogenetic; dysploidy; phylogenetic models; polyploidy; reversible-jump Markov chain Monte Carlo; whole genome duplication.].
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::46: We present outcomes of our temporal variability investigations of Mg II and Al III absorption features in a sample comprising 22 Low Ionization Broad Absorption Line QSOs (LoBAL quasars) at 0.2 <= zem <= 2.1 utilizing the 2m instrument at IUCAA Girawali Observatory across a time-scale spanning 10 days to 7.69 years within the quasar's rest frame. Spectra are analyzed in conjunction with photometric brightness curves from Catalina Real-Time Transient Survey. Extended time-scale (i.e >= 1 year) absorption feature variability is observed in 8 instances (36% objects) while only 4 of them (i.e 18% sources) exhibit variability across brief time-scales (i.e < 1 year). We notice a tendency of highly variable LoBAL quasars to possess high ejection velocity, low equivalent width and low redshift. The detection rate of variability in LoBAL QSOs displaying Fe fine-structure features (FeLoBAL targets) is less than that observed in non-Fe LoBAL candidates. Absorption characteristic variability is more frequently detected in quasars having continuum dominated by Fe emission characteristics compared to remaining QSOs. Confirming these trends with a larger dataset will provide vital clues for understanding the physical distinction between different BAL subclasses. We correlate the absorption profile variability with various parameters derived from continuum brightness measurements and find no clear correlation between flux and absorption characteristic variabilities. However, targets with large absorption profile variability also display large fluctuations in their brightness measurements. We also observe appearance/disappearance of absorption components in 2 instances and clear indications for profile variations in 4 examples. The observed variability can be best explained by a combination of processes driven by continuum fluctuations and clouds transiting across the viewing direction.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::47: The H{\alpha} nebular emission feature represents an optimal tracer for recent stellar genesis within galaxies. With the advent of JWST, this spectral signature has recently become observable at z>3 for the first time. We present a catalog of 1013 H{\alpha} emitters at 3.7<z<6.7 in the GOODS fields obtained from a blind search in JWST NIRCam/grism data. We make use of the FRESCO survey's 124 arcmin^2 of observations in GOODS-North and GOODS-South with the F444W filter, probing H{\alpha} at 4.9<z<6.7; and the CONGRESS survey's 62 arcmin^2 in GOODS-North with F356W, tracing H{\alpha} at 3.8<z<5.1. We identify an overdensity containing 97 sources at z~4.4 in GOODS-N and confirm previously reported overdensities at $z\sim5.2$ in GOODS-N and at z~5.4 plus z~5.9 in GOODS-S. We compute the observed H{\alpha} luminosity functions (LFs) in three bins centered at z~4.45, 5.30, and 6.15, which are the first such measurements at z>3 obtained based purely on spectroscopic information, robustly characterizing galaxy star formation rates (SFRs) beyond the peak of the cosmic stellar genesis history. We compare our results with theoretical predictions from three different simulations and discover good agreement at z~4-6. The UV LFs of this spectroscopically-confirmed sample match well with pre-JWST determinations obtained using photometrically-selected objects. Finally, we derive SFR functions and integrate these to calculate the evolution of the cosmic star-formation rate densities across z~4-6, yielding values in excellent concordance with recent UV estimates from Lyman-break systems, which imply a continuous decrease in SFR density by a factor of 3x over z~4 to z~6. Our investigation demonstrates the power of NIRCam grism observations to efficiently provide novel tests for early system formation models based on emission feature statistics.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::48: Multiple investigations have demonstrated that oxidative damage correlates strongly with depression's emergence and progression. Xiaoyao Pills (XYW) appear in China's Pharmacopoeia and are commonly employed for managing anxiety and melancholic disorders by harmonizing hepatic function, fortifying splenic activity, and enriching blood quality. Nevertheless, XYW's mood-elevating properties remain inadequately explored. Our research aimed to examine these antidepressant-like actions and their underlying molecular mechanisms using olfactory bulbectomized (OB) rodents as experimental subjects, evaluated through open field testing (OFT), sucrose preference assessment (SPT), splash examination (ST), and novelty suppressed feeding evaluation (NSFT). Findings revealed that XYW administration (0.93 and 1.86 g·kg -1 ) substantially ameliorated depressive-like conduct in animals, evidenced by enhanced sugar solution preference during SPT, extended grooming duration in ST, diminished horizontal locomotion in OFT, and reduced feeding latency throughout NSFT. Additionally, XYW intervention markedly reversed declining superoxide dismutase activity and glutathione concentrations, while simultaneously reducing malondialdehyde amounts, inflammatory mediators (nitric oxide), and pro-inflammatory cytokines (interleukin-6 and 1β) within serum and cortical tissue of OB animals. Regarding mechanisms, XYW prompted notable upregulation of messenger RNA and protein expression regarding NFE2L2, KEAP1, GPX3, HMOX1, SOD1, NQO1, OGG1, PIK3CA, p-AKT1/AKT1, NTRK2, and BDNF, alongside downregulation of reactive oxygen species in cortical and hippocampal regions via activating NFE2L2/KEAP1, PIK3CA/AKT1, and NTRK2/BDNF cascades. These discoveries indicate that XYW produces antidepressant-like outcomes in OB rodents exhibiting depressive manifestations, with such benefits mediated through alleviating oxidative damage and enhancing neuroprotective capabilities by activating PIK3CA-AKT1-NFE2L2/BDNF signaling networks. This comprehensive evidence supports XYW's therapeutic potential for addressing mood disorders through multiple biological pathways.
lexical_diversity_up_s.academic_abstracts::49: We report discovering 16 detached M-dwarf eclipsing binaries with J<16 mag and provide detailed characterisation of three systems, using high-precision infrared light curves from WFCAM Transit Survey (WTS). Such configurations offer the most accurate and model-independent method for measuring fundamental parameters of these poorly understood yet numerous stars, which currently lack sufficient observations to precisely calibrate stellar evolution models. We fully solve for masses and radii of three configurations, finding orbital periods spanning 1.5<P<4.9 days, with masses ranging 0.35-0.50 Msun and radii between 0.38-0.50 Rsun, with uncertainties of ~3.5-6.4% in mass and ~2.7-5.5% in radius. Close-companions in short-period binaries are expected to be tidally-locked into fast rotational velocities, resulting in high levels of magnetic activity. This is predicted to inflate their radii by inhibiting convective flow and increasing star spot coverage. The radii of WTS configurations are inflated above model predictions by ~3-12%, in agreement with observed trends, despite an expected lower systematic contribution from star spot signals at infrared wavelengths. We searched for correlation between orbital period and radius inflation by combining our results with all existing M-dwarf radius measurements of comparable precision, but we found no statistically significant evidence for a decrease in radius inflation for longer period, less active configurations. Radius inflation continues to exist in non-synchronised arrangements indicating that the problem remains even for very low activity M-dwarfs. Resolving this issue is vital not only for understanding the most populous stars in the Universe, but also for characterising their planetary companions, which hold the best prospects for finding Earth-like worlds in the traditional habitable zone. Understanding such astrophysical objects remains crucial for exoplanet science advancement.

The squared corner on this timber utensil makes it simple to scrape the bottom of your saucepan or skillet, and not miss areas, when you're stirring something that scorches readily. I really love it for preparing caramel ice cream, because the caramelized sugar forms a clump and adheres to the base of the vessel after I add cool cream. With this "flat-edged" implement, it's effortless to combine the hardened mass and dairy into a smooth caramel sauce without burning any of the browned sweetener.

This featherweight tool is crafted of beechwood, and is beautifully shaped and balanced. It's extremely comfortable to pick up, and to hold when you're mixing a condiment or gravy. The grip has a slight curvature, unlike the traditional timber cooking instrument with round, ramrod-straight shaft that you're likely to find at the grocery store (for example, [[ASIN:B0019R9QKI HIC Harold Import Beechwood Spoon 12-Inch]]).

Timber utensils are not dishwasher safe: they will quickly dry out and crack if washed in a dishwasher. Even if they are hand cleaned, they should be treated with mineral lubricant from time to time, to prevent splitting and prolong their useful lifespan. One reasonably priced petroleum product sold for this purpose is [[ASIN:B00280MY7M Snow River 7V03401 32-Ounce Wood Oil]].

This HAMILTON BEACH DIGITAL RICE COOKER (37518, Stainless Steel, 6-¾ cup yield for white rice) prepares perfect fluffy grains every time, and is a suitable family-sized appliance (enough servings for 4 persons). It has the same capacity as the [[ASIN:B071KPXVJ7 Hamilton Beach 37506 Model]], but features a hinged cover (with rubber gasket, an elaborate steam vent, an exterior condensation collector, and a top liner).

The elaborate cover of this Model 37518 causes steamed foods to finish in one-third to one-half of the duration required by the simpler Model 37506, but the fancy top has NO effect on grain or cereal preparation times. The Model 37518 has a condensation collector that must be emptied, as needed, during operation. The top liner is a component that must be removed each session for washing. (The instructions don't explain how to detach the cover liner, but it pulls straight off the post that holds it.)

The Model 37518 allows you to set custom intervals for Hot Cereal or Steam. This isn't really necessary, because the Model 37506 prepares both oatmeal and grains automatically, and steams food with the aid of a timer.

Most grain appliances do a satisfactory job of preparing rice—they have a thermostat that contacts the underside of the vessel and turns the device off automatically when the water evaporates and the pot temperature rises. Some grain devices—like this one—prepare rice to greater perfection than others, but such appliances mostly differ in their controls (ranging from simple on/off to extra-fancy multi-button digital displays), and in the quantity of their finished yield.

This appliance is sort of in the middle, regarding both controls and output. It will prepare different kinds of grains (there is a chart for correct amounts of rice and water for long grain brown or white, jasmine, basmati, etc.). It will handle different cereals and seeds (barley, oatmeal, Cream of Wheat, etc.). It will steam food (vegetables, poultry, seafood); and it will steam meals and rice together.

The size of this device is suitable if you're making rice for a household of four, or if you're steaming foods for a household of two. I love it for the way it produces fluffy grains and automatically keeps the results warm for up to 12 hours. I also appreciate it for handling Cream of Wheat automatically without burning it on the bottom.

Preparation in a rice appliance takes longer than working on a stovetop or in a microwave. For example, 3 cups of uncooked white rice will require up to 45 minutes; 1-½ cups of Cream of Wheat, up to 37 minutes. But it's easy to start the device and let it work while you're assembling the rest of your meal.

The appliance comes with a standard measuring cup (about ¾ cup U.S.), a rinsing/steamer insert, and a nylon spoon. The vessel has an excellent nonstick surface. The removable pieces are all hand washable in warm, soapy water; handwashing is very straightforward and convenient.

In choosing between this Model 37518 and the Model 37506, I prefer the latter (with a simple, vented glass top, no condensation collector, longer steaming durations, and no ability to set custom intervals). Both versions are very satisfactory, but sometimes simpler is superior. Each delivers reliable performance for typical household needs.
