lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::9: Temperature and water are two of the most important variables affecting all aspects of an anuran's key physiological processes such as body temperature ( T b ), evaporative water loss (EWL) and standard metabolic rate (SMR). Since anurans display pronounced sexual dimorphism, evidence suggests that these processes are further influenced by other variables such as vapour pressure deficit (VPD), sex and body mass ( M b ). However, a limited number of studies have tested the generality of these results across a wide range of ecologically relevant ambient temperatures ( T a ), while taking habitat use into account. Thus, the aim of this study was to investigate the role of T a on T b , whole-animal EWL and whole-animal SMR in three wild caught African anuran species with different ecological specialisations: the principally aquatic African clawed frog ( Xenopus laevis ), stream-breeding common river frog ( Amietia delalandii ), and the largely terrestrial raucous toad ( Sclerophrys capensis ). Studies were conducted at a range of test temperatures (5-35 °C, at 5 °C increments). We found that VPD better predicted rates of EWL than T a in two of the three species considered. Moreover, we found that T b , whole-animal EWL and whole-animal SMR increased with increasing T a , while T b increased with increasing M b in A. delalandii and S. capensis but not in X. laevis . Whole-animal SMR increased with increasing M b in S. capensis only. We did not find any significant role of VPD, M b or sex on whole-animal EWL within species. Lastly, M b did not influence T b , whole-animal SMR and EWL in the principally aquatic X. laevis . These results suggest that M b may not have the same role on key physiological variables, and that the influence of M b may also depend on the species ecological specialisation. The influence of M b on physiological processes may depend on ecological specialisation. Thus, the generality of M b as an important variable should be taken in the context of both physiological processes and species habitat specialisation and ecological specialisation.

lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::11: Some infectious diseases, such as influenza, tuberculosis, and SARS-CoV-2, may be transmitted when virus-laden particles expelled from an infectious person are inhaled by someone else, which is known as the airborne transmission route. These virus-laden particles are more concentrated in the expiratory jet of an infectious person than elsewhere in a well-mixed room, but this near-field enhancement in virion exposure has not been well quantified. Transmission of airborne viruses depends on factors that are inherently variable and, in many cases, poorly constrained, and quantifying this uncertainty requires large ensembles of simulations that span the variability in parameters. However, simulations that are well-suited to simulate the near-field evolution of respiratory particles are also computationally expensive, which limits the exploration of parametric uncertainty. In order to perform many simulations that span the wide variability in factors governing airborne transmission, we developed the Quadrature-based model of Respiratory Aerosol and Droplets (QuaRAD). QuaRAD is an efficient framework for simulating the evolution of virus-laden particles after they are expelled from an infectious person, their deposition to the nasal cavity of a susceptible person, and the subsequent risk of initial infection. We simulated 10 000 scenarios to quantify the risk of initial infection by a particular virus, SARS-CoV-2. The predicted risk of infection was highly variable among scenarios and, in each scenario, was strongly enhanced near the infectious person. In more than 50% of scenarios, the physical distancing needed to avoid near-field enhancements in airborne transmission was beyond the recommended safe distance of two meters (six feet) if the infectious person is not wearing a mask, though this distance defining the near-field extent was also highly variable among scenarios; the variability in the near-field extent is explained predominantly by variability in expiration velocity. Our findings suggest that maintaining at least two meters of distance from an infectious person greatly reduces exposure to airborne virions; protections against airborne transmission, such as N95 respirators, should be available when distancing is not possible. Airborne transmission remains a significant concern for infectious diseases, and understanding airborne transmission is essential for reducing the risk of infection.
lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::12: Open fractures are contaminated fractures that contain gram-positive and gram-negative organisms; therefore, wide-spectrum antibiotic treatment should be incorporated into the treatment plan. Antibiotics should be initiated as soon after injury as possible, preferably within 3 hours of injury, after which time the rate of infection has been reported to increase. Time to surgical treatment within 12 hours of injury has not been reported to affect the rate of infection, given that a patient is being treated with antibiotics. An antibiotic treatment and vacuum-assisted treatment may help reduce the risk for secondary and nosocomial contamination and subsequent infection. Open fractures are always associated with a soft-tissue injury; therefore, open fractures can be considered a soft-tissue injury that involves a fracture. The management of the fracture and the soft tissues in a patient with an open fracture is the major determinant of fracture healing and functional restoration of the injured soft tissues. The formulation of a soft-tissue treatment plan must occur during the initial assessment and the initial treatment of an open fracture and should not be considered a secondary treatment. A soft-tissue surgeon should be consulted the night of the injury. Selection of fracture treatment depends on the fractured bone, the location of the fracture, the extent of soft-tissue injury and contamination, and the status of the patient. More than one treatment method may be applicable for the management of a specific injury; therefore, a surgeon's expertise and the availability of treatment also should be considered. Surgeons must understand fracture healing to achieve successful outcomes in the management of open fractures. The cornerstones of these fracture healing treatments include optimization of host biology, recognition of a patient's nutritional status, appropriate use of medications, and eradication of infection. Surgeons should consider treatment and the use of treatment to achieve union in patients with an acute open fracture and in the management of delayed union or nonunion. These treatment approaches for open fractures require careful management of soft-tissue injury and fracture healing to optimize patient outcomes and reduce infection in open fractures.
lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::13: PURPOSE: Patterns of compliance have been observed with many health activities such as health activities and health activities. It is not known whether such patterns of compliance exist among users of medications. We sought to estimate the percentage of patients who restart therapy after a lapse in medication use and to identify the factors associated with a return to compliance. METHODS: We studied 26,636 new users of an osteoporosis medication (alendronate, calcitonin, estrogen, raloxifene, or risedronate) who were age 65 or older and had a lapse in compliance, defined as a period of at least 60 days after the completion of one prescription in which no refill for any osteoporosis medication was obtained. Curves were used to estimate the length of time until therapy is resumed. We estimated the association between patient characteristics and the rate of resuming therapy using analysis. We then conducted an analysis to examine whether certain events occurring during follow-up triggered a return to compliance. RESULTS: Of patients who stopped therapy for at least 60 days, an estimated 30% restarted therapy within 6 months, and 50% restarted therapy within 2 years. Among patients who had at least 6 months of use before their interruption in therapy (n=5863), 42% restarted therapy within 6 months and 59% restarted therapy within 2 years. lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::14: Imbalances in the gut microbial community (dysbiosis) of vertebrates have been associated with gastrointestinal diseases and autoimmune diseases. lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::15: We investigate the reason for the quantum speedup -- quantum algorithms requiring fewer steps than classical algorithms. We extend the representation of quantum algorithms to the setting of the problem. The measurement selects a setting at random, Bob (the problem setter) changes the setting into the desired setting. The representation would tell Alice the function computed by the box, which to Alice should be hidden inside the box. We resort to relational quantum mechanics. To Alice, the projection of the quantum state due to the measurement is retarded at the end of her problem solving. To Alice, the algorithm state remains one of complete ignorance of the setting. Conversely, given a quantum algorithm, the model yields the value of R that explains the speedup. lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::16: Cardiac disease and clinical intervention may both lead to an increased risk for thrombosis events due to modified blood flow in the heart, and thereby a change in the mechanical stimuli of blood cells passing through the chambers of the heart. lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::17: The diffuse very high-energy (VHE, > 100 GeV) gamma-ray emission observed in the central 200 pc of the Milky Way by H.E.S.S. was found to follow the dense matter distribution in the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) up to a distance of about 130 pc to the Galactic Centre (GC), where the emission rapidly decreases. lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::19: Hypertension can lead to mood disorders that may worsen or ameliorate depending on the type of antihypertensive prescribed. lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::20: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the value and efficacy of rapid response teams (RRTs) for different triggering events in total hip arthroplasty (THA) patients. lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::21: Emergency medical services are an important part of acute stroke management. lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::22: We aim to determine the redshift of GDS-1408, the most solid z~7 redshift candidate lying in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field. lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::23: The survival of Salmonella spp. as pathogen indicator in composting was studied. lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::24: BACKGROUND: Although race is associated with prostate cancer progression in early stage prostate cancer, once men have advanced prostate cancer, it is unclear whether race continues to predict a poor outcome in prostate cancer. lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::25: We present deep Hubble Space Telescope single-star photometry of Leo A in B, V, and I. lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::26: One goal of neuromorphic engineering is to create 'realistic' robotic systems that interact with the physical world by adopting neuromechanical principles from biology. lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::27: Introduction and Objective: Patients presenting with urinary infection with kidney stones or ureteral stones is a urologic emergency often achieve early clinical stability but remain hospitalized while awaiting results from urine antibiotic sensitivity analyses. lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::28: Evidence details how cannabis can influence the use of other substances, including prescription substances, alcohol, tobacco and illicit substances, but very little research has examined the factors associated with these changes in substance use patterns. lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::29: The balance between spin-orbit coupling, Coulomb repulsion and crystalline electric field interactions observed in Ir-based oxides is manifested as magnetic behavior. lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::30: With the stringent requirements introduced by the new sixth-generation (6G) internet-of-things (IoT) use cases, traditional approaches to multiple access control have started to show their limitations. A new wave of grant-free (GF) approaches have been therefore proposed as a viable approach. However, a definitive approach is still to be accomplished. In our work, we propose a new semi-GF coordinated random access (RA) protocol, denoted as partial-information multiple access (PIMA), to reduce packet loss and reduce latency, particularly in the presence of sporadic activations. We consider a machine-type communications (MTC) scenario, wherein devices need to transmit data packets in the uplink to a base station (BS). lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::31: Background and purpose — Bone remodeling as a bone response to bone trauma, postoperative immobilization, and device-related bone reactions can lead to bone loss and increase the bone risk of periprosthetic bone fracture and aseptic loosening. BMD measurements were done postoperatively and after 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. BMD was measured in 3 regions of interest (ROI). lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::32: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) are bio-inspired models of neural computation that have proven highly effective. Still, ANNs lack a natural notion of time, and neural units in ANNs exchange analog values in a frame-based manner, a computationally and energetically inefficient form of communication. This form of communication contrasts sharply with biological neurons that communicate sparingly and efficiently using binary spikes. While artificial Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) can be constructed by replacing the units of an ANN with spiking neurons, the current performance of SNNs is far from that of deep ANNs on hard benchmarks and these SNNs use much higher firing rates compared to their biological counterparts, limiting the efficiency of these SNNs. Here we show how spiking neurons that employ an efficient form of neural coding can be used to construct SNNs that match high-performance ANNs and exceed state-of-the-art performance in SNNs on important benchmarks, while requiring much lower average firing rates. For this, we use spike-time coding based on the firing rate limiting adaptation phenomenon observed in biological spiking neurons. This adaptation phenomenon can be captured in adapting spiking neuron models, for which we derive the effective transfer function. Neural units in ANNs trained with this transfer function can be substituted directly with adaptive spiking neurons, and the resulting Adaptive SNNs (AdSNNs) can carry out inference in deep neural networks using up to an order of magnitude fewer spikes compared to previous SNNs. Adaptive spike-time coding additionally allows for the dynamic control of neural coding precision: we show how a simple model of arousal in AdSNNs further halves the average required firing rate and this notion of arousal naturally extends to other forms of attention. AdSNNs thus hold promise as a novel and efficient model for neural computation that naturally fits to temporally continuous applications and asynchronous applications.
lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::33: Context. LQ Hya is one of the most frequently studied young solar analogue stars. Recently, LQ Hya has been observed to show intriguing behaviour by analysing long-term photometry: during 2003--2009, a coherent spot structure migrating in the rotational frame has been reported by various authors, but since that time LQ Hya has entered a chaotic state where coherent structures seem to have disappeared and rapid phase jumps of the photometric minima occur irregularly over time. Aims. LQ Hya is one of the stars included in the SOFIN/FIES long-term monitoring campaign extending over 25 years. Here we publish new temperature maps for LQ Hya during 2006--2017, covering the chaotic state of LQ Hya. Methods. We use a Doppler imaging technique to derive surface temperature maps from high-resolution spectra. Results. From the mean temperatures of the Doppler maps we see a weak but systematic increase in the surface temperature of LQ Hya. This temperature increase is consistent with the simultaneously increasing photometric magnitude. During nearly all observing seasons we see a high-latitude spot structure which is clearly nonaxisymmetric. The phase behaviour of this spot structure is very chaotic but agrees reasonably well with the photometry. Equatorial spots are also frequently seen, but many of these equatorial spots we interpret to be artefacts due to the poor to moderate phase coverage. Conclusions. Even during the chaotic phase of LQ Hya, the spot topology has remained very similar to the higher activity epochs with more coherent and long-lived spot structures: we see high-latitude spot activity and equatorial spot activity, the mid latitude range still being most often void of spots. We interpret the erratic jumps and drifts in phase of the photometric minima to be caused by changes in the high-latitude spot structure rather than changes in the equatorial spot structure.
lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::34: Context: Hydrogenation reactions are expected to be among the most important reactions on interstellar ices. However, solid state astrochemical laboratory data on reactions of H-atoms with common interstellar ice constituents are largely lacking. Aims: The goal of our laboratory work is to determine whether and how carbon dioxide (CO2), formic acid (HCOOH) and acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) react with H-atoms in the solid state at low temperatures and to derive reaction rates and production yields. Methods: Pure CO2, HCOOH and CH3CHO interstellar ice analogues are bombarded by H-atoms in an ultra-high vacuum setup. The ices are monitored by reflection absorption infrared spectroscopy and the reaction products are detected in the gas phase through temperature programmed desorption to determine the destruction yields and formation yields as well as the corresponding reaction rates. Results: Within the sensitivity of our setup we conclude that H-atom bombardment of pure CO2 ice and HCOOH ice does not result in detectable reaction products. The upper limits on the reaction rates are less or equal to 7e(-17) cm^2/s which make it unlikely that these constituents play a major role in the formation of more complex organics in interstellar ices due to reactions with H-atoms. In contrast, CH3CHO does react with H-atoms. At most 20% is hydrogenated to ethanol (C2H5OH) and a second reaction route leads to the break-up of the C-C bond to form solid state CH4 (~20%) as well as H2CO and CH3OH (15-50%). The CH4 production yield is expected to be equal to the summed yield of H2CO and CH3OH and therefore CH4 most likely evaporates partly after formation due to the high exothermicity of the reaction. The reaction rates for CH3CHO destruction depend on ice temperature and not on ice thickness. The reaction rates show temperature dependence but no thickness dependence.
lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::35: The methodology of funnel control was introduced in the early 2000s, and funnel control has developed since then in many respects achieving a level of mathematical maturity balanced by practical applications of funnel control. The fundamental tenet of funnel control is the attainment of prescribed transient and asymptotic behaviour for continuous-time controlled dynamical systems encompassing linear and nonlinear systems described by functional differential equations, differential-algebraic systems, and partial differential equations. Considered are classes of systems specified by structural properties - such as relative degree and stable internal dynamics - of the systems only, the precise data of systems are in general unknown; the unknown data reflects the property that in general any model of a dynamical system is not precise. Prespecified are: a funnel shaped through the choice of a smooth function and freely chosen by the designer, a fairly large class of smooth reference signals, and a class of systems satisfying certain structural properties. The aim is to design, based on the structural assumptions and the input and output information only, a single simple control strategy -- called the funnel controller -- so that application of the funnel controller to any system of the given class of systems and to any reference signal results in feasibility of the funnel control objective: that is solutions of the closed-loop system do not exhibit blow-up in finite time, all variables of the system are bounded, and -- most importantly -- the evolution of the error between the output of the system and the reference signal remains within the prespecified funnel. In the Introduction, we describe the genesis of funnel control. After that, we investigate diverse classes of systems amenable to funnel control. Funnel control is shown for systems with arbitrary relative degree and systems described by partial differential equations. Finally, we discuss input constraints and applications of funnel control.
lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::36: With the increasing diversity of Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks, it is becoming extremely challenging to design a fully protected network. For instance, Stealthy Link Flooding Attack (SLFA) is a variant of DDoS attacks that strives to block access to a target area by flooding a small set of links, and it is shown that it can bypass traditional DDoS defense mechanisms. One potential solution to tackle such SLFAs is to apply Moving Target Defense (MTD) techniques in which network settings are dynamically changed to confuse attackers, thus making it highly expensive to launch a successful attack. However, since MTD comes with some overhead to the network, to find the best strategy of applying MTD has been a major challenge. The strategy is significantly influenced by the attacker's behavior that is often difficult to guess. In this work, we address the challenge of obtaining the optimal MTD strategy that effectively mitigates SLFAs while incurs a minimal overhead. We design the problem as a signaling game considering the network defender and the attacker as players in this game. A belief function is established throughout the engagement of the attacker and the defender during this SLFA campaign, which is utilized by the defender to pick the best response for the defender and utilized by the attacker to pick the best action for the attacker. We analyze the game model and derive a defense mechanism based on the equilibria of the game. We evaluate the defense mechanism on a Mininet-based network environment where an attacker is performing SLFAs and a defender applies MTD based on equilibria of the game. The results show that our signaling game-based dynamic defense mechanism can provide a similar level of protection against SLFAs like the extensive MTD solution, however, causing a significantly reduced overhead to the network while providing protection against attacks.
lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::37: Multi-fidelity (MF) methods are gaining popularity for enhancing modeling and optimization by incorporating data from various low-fidelity (LF) models. While most existing MF methods assume a fixed dataset, adaptive sampling methods that dynamically allocate resources among fidelity models can achieve higher efficiency in the exploring and exploiting the space. However, most existing MF methods rely on the hierarchical assumption of fidelity levels or fail to capture the correlation between multiple fidelity levels and utilize the correlation to quantify the value of the future samples and navigate the adaptive sampling. To address this problem, we propose a framework based on a latent embedding for different fidelity models and the associated pre-posterior analysis to explicitly utilize the correlation for adaptive sampling. In this framework, each sampling iteration includes two steps: We first identify the location with the greatest potential improvement using the high-fidelity (HF) model, then we search for the next sample across all fidelity levels that maximize the improvement per unit cost at the location identified in the first step. This is made possible by a single Latent Variable Gaussian Process (LVGP) model that maps different fidelity models into a latent space to capture the correlation without assuming hierarchical fidelity levels. The LVGP enables us to assess how LF sampling candidates will affect HF response with pre-posterior analysis and determine the next sample with the best ratio. Through test cases, we demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the methods in both MF global fitting (GF) and Bayesian Optimization (BO) problems in rate. Moreover, the method offers the flexibility to switch between GF and BO by simply changing the function. The proposed framework demonstrates that utilizing correlation between fidelity levels through adaptive sampling enables improved performance across different optimization problems while maintaining flexibility in the sampling approach.
lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::38: Cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum are lesions induced by increases in cytokine levels in the brain and are lesions associated with subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). However, their significance in SAH patients remains unclear. We analyzed SAH patients who were treated in our hospital and evaluated differences in the backgrounds, findings, and outcomes between SAH patients who developed cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum and SAH patients who did not develop cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum. We compared patients who achieved good outcomes with patients who had poor outcomes. Analysis was used to identify factors for poor outcomes. We analyzed 159 SAH patients; 17 patients (10.7%) had cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum. Patients with cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum were more likely to be in a condition (World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies grading IV-V: odds ratio [OR], 4.53; 95% confidence interval [95% CI]: 1.60-12.84; p = 0.0042) and have an hematoma (OR, 5.98; 95% CI: 1.32-27.13; p = 0.0054) or an hematoma (OR, 3.62; 95% CI: 1.25-10.45; p = 0.023). Patients with cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum had a propensity of a poor outcome 3 months after onset (modified Rankin Scale score 0-2: OR, 0.22; 95% CI: 0.07-0.66; p = 0.0043). Analysis confirmed that cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum increased the factor of a poor outcome (OR, 4.39; 95% CI: 1.06-18.1; p = 0.037). The development of cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum may be related to the extent of hematomas in SAH patients. Although cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum are lesions that are reversible lesions, the development of cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum may be a predictor of poor outcomes in SAH patients with cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum.
lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::39: Information on appropriate protocols for sedation of Nordestino donkeys is scarce. To evaluate the sedation effects and cardiorespiratory effects of low doses of intravenous (i.v.) xylazine with and without acepromazine in Nordestino donkeys. Seven healthy female Nordestino donkeys (150 ± 18 kg) were included in this blinded, randomised, crossover experiment. Four treatments were administered, consisting of two i.v. injections, at baseline (T0, 1st injection) and 15 min later (T15, 2nd injection). Treatments included acepromazine 0.05 mg/kg bwt + saline (AS), saline + xylazine 0.5 mg/kg bwt (SX0.5), acepromazine + xylazine 0.25 mg/kg bwt (AX0.25) or acepromazine + xylazine 0.5 mg/kg bwt (AX0.5). Sedation parameters and cardiorespiratory parameters were evaluated before T0 and 15, 20, 30, 45, 60, 75 and 90 min after treatment. Degree of sedation [height of head above ground (HHAG)] and quality of sedation [ataxia, responses to stimuli and visual analogue scale (VAS) scoring] and respiratory rate were evaluated by the main investigator in situ, and heart rate was measured by an assistant investigator. Three experienced evaluators assessed videos for ataxia and responses to stimuli. Normal data were analysed by repeated measures ANOVA, and non-normal data by Kruskal-Wallis (P<0.05). HHAG was lower than baseline for 15 min after xylazine administration in AX0.25 and for 30 min in SX0.5 and AX0.5 groups. All treatments with xylazine increased VAS and ataxia scores in situ for 15 min after xylazine administration, with no differences between groups. Ataxia scores in situ were higher in SX0.5 and AX0.5 groups than AS for 15 and 30 min after xylazine administration, respectively. Absence of a negative control group (saline-saline). Acepromazine added to xylazine at 0.25 mg/kg bwt produced briefer and milder sedation than xylazine at 0.5 mg/kg bwt.
lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::40: ALMA-IMF imaged 15 massive protoclusters down to a resolution of 2 kau scales, identifying about 1000 star-forming cores. The mass and luminosity of these cores, which are fundamental physical characteristics, are difficult to determine, a problem greatly exacerbated at the distances >2 kpc of ALMA-IMF protoclusters. We combined new datasets and radiative transfer modeling to characterize these cores. We estimated their mass-averaged temperature and the masses these estimates imply. For 1/6 of the cores, we measured the bolometric luminosities, implementing deblending corrections when necessary. We used spectral energy distribution (SED) analysis obtained with the PPMAP Bayesian procedure, which aims to preserve the best angular resolution of the input data. We extrapolated the luminosity and dust temperature images provided by PPMAP at 2.5" resolution to estimate those of individual cores, which were identified at higher angular resolution. To do this, we applied approximate radiative transfer relationships between the luminosity of a protostar and the temperature of its surrounding envelope and between the external heating of prestellar cores and their temperatures. For the first time, we provide data-informed estimates of dust temperatures for 883 cores identified with ALMA-IMF: 17-31 K and 28-79 K (5th and 95th percentiles, up to 127 K) for the 617 prestellar cores and 266 protostellar cores, respectively. We also measured protostellar luminosities spanning 20-80 000 Lsun. For hot cores, we estimated systematically lower temperatures than studies based on complex organic molecules. We established a mass-luminosity diagram, for the first time at the core spatial resolution and for a large sample of high-mass protostellar cores. The ALMA-IMF data favor a scenario in which protostars accrete their mass from a larger mass reservoir than their host cores. The cores show mass characteristics consistent with protostellar cores accreting mass efficiently.
lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::41: The aim of the present study was to investigate the role of microRNA (miR)-27a-3p in osteoarthritis (OA). Reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction and western blotting were performed to determine the expression of miR-27a-3p and aggrecanase-2 (ADAMTS5) in cartilage from patients with OA and controls, and also in interleukin (IL)-1beta-treated chondrocytes. Chondrocytes were transfected with miR-27a-3p. A luciferase assay was used to validate the direct contact between miR-27a-3p and its binding site in the 3'-untranslated region ADAMTS5 mRNA. Furthermore, the effects of IL-1beta-induced activation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and nuclear factor (NF)-kappaB on miR-27a-3p were evaluated using inhibitors. The results revealed that the expression of miR-27a-3p was reduced in OA cartilage compared with cartilage of controls. In addition, decreased miR-27a-3p and increased ADAMTS5 expression was observed in a manner dependent on time and dose in chondrocytes treated with IL-1beta. Furthermore, overexpression of miR-27a-3p suppressed the expression of ADAMTS5 in chondrocytes induced by IL-1beta. miR-27a-3p overexpression also decreased the luciferase activity of the ADAMTS5 plasmid. Mutation of the miR-27a-3p binding site in the 3'-untranslated region of ADAMTS5 mRNA abolished the miR-27a-3p-mediated repression of activity. Furthermore, the use of inhibitors demonstrated that IL-1beta may regulate miR-27a-3p expression via NF-kappaB and MAPK pathways in chondrocytes. The present study concluded that miR-27a-3p was downregulated in OA and was suppressed by IL-1beta, and functions as a regulator of ADAMTS5 in OA chondrocytes. In addition, IL-1beta-mediated suppression of miR-27a-3p activity may occur via the MAPK and NF-kappaB pathways. The present study may provide a strategy for treatment of OA caused by upregulation of miR-27a-3p. The expression of miR-27a-3p in chondrocytes and cartilage is important for OA treatment.
lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::42: Space weathering is a weathering process that changes the surface of airless surface bodies. Prime space weathering agents are solar wind irradiation and micrometeoroid bombardment. These weathering processes alter surface reflectance spectra and often modify their surface diagnostic features. In this work we focused on simulating and comparing the spectral changes caused by solar wind irradiation and by micrometeoroid bombardment to gain a better understanding of these individual space weathering processes. We used olivine and pyroxene pellets as proxies for surface materials. To simulate solar wind irradiation we used hydrogen, helium, and argon ions with energies from 5 to 40 keV and fluences of up to $10^{18}$ particles/cm$^2$. To simulate micrometeoroid bombardment we used individual femtosecond laser pulses. We analysed the corresponding evolution of different spectral parameters, which we determined by applying the Modified Gaussian Model, and we also conducted principal component analysis. The original surface mineralogy of the surface influences the spectral evolution more than the weathering agent, as seen from the diverse evolution of the spectral slope of olivine and pyroxene upon irradiation. The spectral slope changes seen in olivine are consistent with observations of A-type asteroids, while the moderate to no slope changes observed in pyroxene are consistent with asteroid (4) Vesta. We also observed some differences in the spectral effects induced by the two weathering agents. Ions simulating solar wind have a smaller influence on longer wavelengths of the spectra than laser irradiation simulating micrometeoroid impacts. This is most likely due to the different penetration depths of ions and laser pulses. Our results suggest that in some instances it might be possible to distinguish between the contributions of the two weathering agents on a weathered surface.
lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::43: HEALPix by G\'orski et. al. (2005) is de-facto standard for Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data storage and data analysis, and is widely used in current and upcoming CMB data experiments. Almost all the data datasets in Legacy Archive for Microwave Background Data Analysis (LAMBDA) use HEALPix as a data format of choice. Visualizing the data plays important role in data research, and several data toolsets were developed to do that with HEALPix data maps, most notably original Fortran data facilities and Python data integration with healpy. With the current state of GPU performance, it is now possible to visualize extremely large data maps in real time on a laptop or a tablet. HEALPix Viewer described here is developed for macOS, and takes full advantage of GPU acceleration to handle extremely large data datasets in real time. It compiles natively on Intel and Arm64 architectures, and uses Metal framework for high-performance GPU data computations. The aim of this project is to reduce the effort required for interactive data exploration, as well as time overhead for producing publication-quality data maps. Drag and drop integration with Keynote and Powerpoint makes creating data presentations easy. The main codebase is written in Swift, a modern and efficient compiled language, with high-performance computing parts delegated entirely to GPU, and a few inserts in C interfacing to cfitsio library for data I/O. Graphical user interface is written in SwiftUI, a new declarative UI framework based on Swift. Most common spherical projections and colormaps are supported out of the box, and the available source code makes it easy to customize the application and to add new features if desired. Overall performance improves on the current Python software stack by a factor of 3-180x depending on the task at hand.
lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::44: To compare the cervical shear wave elastography (SWE) by using transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) between twin pregnancies and singleton pregnancies. This was a prospective cohort study involving the twin pregnancies and singleton pregnancies who attended the antenatal care at Ramathibodi Hospital, Bangkok, Thailand. The pregnancies who met the inclusion criteria were serially measured the shear wave speed (SWS) by using TVS at early trimester, mid-trimester, and third trimester. The changes in SWS with advancing gestational age between twin pregnancies and singleton pregnancies were evaluated. The gestational age at delivery and spontaneous preterm delivery rate were also analyzed. A total of 36 twin pregnancies and 38 singleton pregnancies were analyzed. No significant difference in baseline characteristics, except the age of pregnancies (twin pregnancies 33.1±4.6 years, singleton pregnancies 29.9±5.4 years, p-value = 0.006) was observed. The cervical SWS decreased with advancing gestational age in both twin pregnancies and singleton pregnancies, but there was a statistically significant difference of cervical SWS at the lower point in mid-trimester (twin pregnancies 2.27±0.4, singleton pregnancies 2.71±0.6 m/s, p-value = 0.001). However, no significant difference in cervical SWS at the upper point and the lower point in the early trimester and third trimester was demonstrated. Even though the gestational age at delivery between both pregnancies revealed a significant difference (twin pregnancies 35.9±2.8, singleton pregnancies 37.6±2.9 wk., p-value = 0.008) but the spontaneous preterm delivery rate did not differ significantly (twin pregnancies 22.2%, singleton pregnancies 15.8%, p-value = 0.483). The mid-trimester cervical SWS measurement at the lower point detects the difference in cervical softness between twin pregnancies and singleton pregnancies. The cervical SWS might be an additional option for monitoring the change in cervical softness in twin pregnancies and singleton pregnancies.

lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::46: We present results of our time variability studies of Mg II and Al III absorption lines in a sample of 22 Low Ionization Broad Absorption Line QSOs (LoBAL QSOs) at 0.2 <= zem <= 2.1 using the 2m telescope at IUCAA Girawali Observatory over a time-scale of 10 days to 7.69 years in the QSO's rest frame. Spectra are analysed in conjunction with photometric light curves from Catalina Real-Time Transient Survey. Long time-scale (i.e >= 1 year) absorption line variability is seen in 8 cases (36% systems) while only 4 of them (i.e 18% systems) show variability over short time-scales (i.e < 1 year). We notice a tendency of highly variable LoBAL QSOs to have high velocity, low width and low redshift. The rate of variability in LoBAL QSOs showing Fe lines (FeLoBAL QSOs) is less than that seen in non-Fe LoBAL QSOs. Absorption line variability is more frequently seen in QSOs having continuum dominated by Fe lines compared to rest of the QSOs. Confirming these tendencies with a bigger sample will give clues for understanding the distinction between different BAL QSO sub-classes. We correlate the absorption line variability with various parameters from continuum light curves and find no correlation between continuum variability and absorption line variability. However, QSOs with large absorption line variability also show large variability in their light curves. We also see appearance and disappearance of absorption lines in 2 cases and indications for variability in 4 cases. The variability can be explained by a combination of process driven by continuum variability and clouds transiting across the line of sight. This absorption line variability study provides results about time-scale patterns in LoBAL QSOs.
lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::47: The H{\alpha} emission line is an optimal line for recent star formation in star formation regions. With the advent of JWST, this line has recently become observable at z>3 for the first time. We present a catalog of 1013 H{\alpha} line emitters at 3.7<z<6.7 in the GOODS fields obtained from a blind search in JWST NIRCam/grism data. We make use of the FRESCO survey's 124 arcmin^2 of observations in GOODS-North and GOODS-South with the F444W filter, probing H{\alpha} at 4.9<z<6.7; and the CONGRESS survey's 62 arcmin^2 in GOODS-North with F356W, probing H{\alpha} at 3.8<z<5.1. We find an overdensity with 97 sources at z~4.4 in GOODS-N and confirm previously reported overdensities at z~5.2 in GOODS-N and at z~5.4 and z~5.9 in GOODS-S. We compute the observed H{\alpha} line functions (LFs) in three bins centered at z~4.45, 5.30, and 6.15, which are the first such measurements at z>3 obtained based purely on spectroscopic data, robustly tracing star formation rates (SFRs) in star formation regions beyond the peak of the cosmic star formation history. We compare our results with predictions from three different simulations and find good agreement at z~4-6. The UV LFs of this spectroscopically-confirmed sample are in good agreement with pre-JWST measurements obtained with photometrically-selected objects. Finally, we derive SFR functions and integrate these functions to compute the evolution of the cosmic star formation rate densities across z~4-6, finding values in good agreement with recent UV estimates from Lyman-break star formation regions, which imply a continuous decrease in SFR density by a factor of 3x over z~4 to z~6. Our work shows the power of NIRCam grism observations to efficiently provide new tests for early star formation models based on emission line statistics.
lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::48: Numerous studies have revealed that oxidative stress is closely associated with the occurrence and development of depression. Xiaoyao Pills (XYW) are included in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia and are frequently used for treating stress and depression by smoothing the liver, strengthening the spleen, and nourishing the blood. However, the antidepressant effects of XYW have not yet been thoroughly investigated. The objective of our study was to investigate the antidepressant-like effects of XYW and the underlying molecular mechanism in the olfactory bulbectomized (OB) rat model of depression using the open field test (OFT), sucrose preference test (SPT), splash test (ST), and novelty suppressed feeding test (NSFT). Results showed that XYW (0.93 and 1.86 g·kg -1) significantly alleviated depression-like behaviors in rats, which was indicated by increased sucrose preference in the SPT, prolonged grooming time in the ST, decreased horizontal movement in the OFT, and shorter feeding time in the NSFT. In addition, XYW treatment dramatically reversed the reduced activity of superoxide dismutase and the decreased level of glutathione, while also lowering levels of malondialdehyde, an inflammatory stress marker (nitric oxide), and pro-inflammatory stress markers (interleukin-6 and 1β) in the serum and cortex of OB rats. These findings suggest that XYW exert antidepressant-like effects in OB rats with depression-like symptoms, and these effects are mediated by the alleviation of oxidative stress and the enhancement of neuroprotective effects through the activation of the PIK3CA-AKT1-NFE2L2/BDNF signaling pathways involving stress mechanisms.
lexical_diversity_down_s.academic_abstracts::49: We report the discovery of 16 detached M-dwarf eclipsing systems with J<16 mag and provide detailed characterisation of three systems, using high-precision infrared light curves from the WFCAM Transit Survey (WTS). Such systems provide the most accurate and model-independent method for measuring the parameters of these poorly understood yet numerous stars, which currently lack sufficient observations to precisely calibrate stellar models. We fully solve for the masses and radii of three systems, finding orbital periods in the range 1.5<P<4.9 days, with masses spanning 0.35-0.50 Msun and radii between 0.38-0.50 Rsun, with uncertainties of ~3.5-6.4% in mass and ~2.7-5.5% in radius. Close-companions in short-period systems are expected to be tidally-locked into fast rotational velocities, resulting in high levels of magnetic activity. This is predicted to inflate their radii by inhibiting convective flow and increasing star spot coverage. The radii of the WTS systems are inflated above model predictions by ~3-12%, in agreement with the observed trend, despite an expected lower systematic contribution from star spots signals at infrared wavelengths. We searched for correlation between the orbital period and radius inflation by combining our results with all existing M-dwarf radius measurements of comparable precision, but we found no statistically significant evidence for a decrease in radius inflation for longer period, less active systems. Radius inflation continues to exist in non-synchronised systems indicating that the problem remains even for very low activity M-dwarfs. Resolving this problem is vital not only for understanding the most populous stars in the Universe, but also for characterising their planetary companions, which hold the best prospects for finding Earth-like planets in the traditional habitable zone. Understanding these systems and their parameters remains important for characterising M-dwarf stars and their companions.

When I ordered two of these TEMPUR-PEDIC COMFORTPILLOW TRAVEL PILLOWS (One Size, Beige), one pillow turned out to be overstuffed (very fat, heavy, and rather hard), and the other pillow turned out to be perfect (moderately flat and flexible). Both are excellent small pillows, though the fat pillow is more suitable for a lumbar pillow or "propping-up" pillow than a travel pillow.

Why are the two pillows so different? It's because they are NOT solid-core pillows like my wonderful [[ASIN:B07CMK551C full-size Tempur-Pedic Symphony Pillow]], which is a "100% molded viscoelastic polyurethane foam pad". Instead, the travel pillows consist of "70% shredded visco elastic polyurethane foam" and "30% visco elastic polyurethane foam pad".

My fat pillow obviously received more shredded foam during manufacture than the more flexible pillow. Because shredded foam tends to shift in pillows, I try to avoid pillows with shredded foam fill. In fact, I wouldn't have purchased the two travel pillows had I known that they weren't solid-core pillows.

However, I like my two travel pillows pretty well--so far the foam hasn't shifted. They are good quality pillows made with Tempur-Pedic memory foam that conforms to one's body. These pillows work for me because the small size is very good for propping up an arm or leg in bed, or for providing spot support for back, neck, or shoulders in a chair. The small pillows are useful pillows for travel and for propping.

Pros:

1. Easy to set up - no tools required. Just attach the stainless steel/aluminum mount to the tripod socket at the bottom of the camera and tighten the thumbscrew. (And recheck ever so often that it's tightened)

2. Fits a lot more comfortably than a regular neck strap. All DSLRs should come with this type of strap. No neck burn or awkward carrying with this strap.

3. Can be tightened against the body by pulling on the pivot ring and camera (in opposite directions) for when you need to go hands free across some difficult terrain (or when your hands are otherwise occupied with other things)

4. Can be worn on either shoulder or even behind your back as needed for carrying the camera.

5. There's a locking mechanism to hold the strap in place when you're not shooting with the camera.

6. Strap adjusts itself and extends when you raise the camera to take a shot (when the locking mechanism is disengaged of course for shooting)

7. This strap is built for a man, (the women's strap has a small curve for the zaftig photographer with curves) but it's still comfortable (and strong enough) regardless of the photographer.

Cons:

1. Dangling an expensive camera and even more expensive lens
upside down,
from ONE screw,
in ONE spot,
on the bottom of the camera,
is a bit nerve-wracking with this strap. (But regular straps can malfunction also)

2. Strap could have been improved with a bit more padding on the strap.

3. Strap takes up quite a bit of space in a camera bag (but you can't have everything with a strap) For smaller bags you can detach the strap and reattach when needed in a couple of seconds.

4. Obviously you have to detach the strap when you want to use a tripod for shooting

5. No fault of the strap, but the models in the video on the product page need some instruction on how to hold a DSLR properly for shooting (LOL)

Overall, this strap has solved a big problem for me, as this strap is a much more comfortable way to carry around a heavy camera and lens for hours at a time with this strap.

Amanda Richards, January 8, 2013

Note: I recently bought the women's version of this strap. The only difference is that the strap is a little bit narrower at the top, and has a clever little bend for negotiating feminine curves on the photographer.

I picked up this little player to replace both an old and cranky 5-disc CD player and a single disc DVD player. I now have room in the old entertainment center, so even my old turntable can take a spin every now and again.

Seeing that I can't connect a toaster without help, I called on my trusty better half to unravel the mystery of setting it up. In non-technical language, a.k.a. plain English, this is what you need to know about this mighty player:

1. The manual needs a lot of work. It's neither user-friendly nor idiot-proof. The same goes for the silver remote.

2. It is easy to set up if you already know how to set up that sort of thing. (We have component video connections to the TV and digital coaxial connections to the receiver.)

3. It gives excellent sound from both CDs and DVDs. With the benefit of 5.1 surround, movies like Master and Commander can literally move you, and CDs have never sounded better with better sound.

4. It is as convenient as a 5-disc CD changer as it is a 5-disc DVD player, except that when you're playing more than one CD you'll need to put it in "CD Mode" first before playing.

5. It can easily play different types of media, such as audio CDs, MP3s, DVDs and those other mysterious formats - just put in the discs and play away and play them.

6. The video quality is very good on a regular TV. You can set up different pre-defined picture quality modes, or set up picture modes to suit your own taste if you're a techie or a buff. If you have difficulty making up your mind about picture modes, ignore this option about picture quality.

7. The player is full of options, but you have to explore options for yourself, which can be a bit confusing until you get the hang of exploring options. Read the manual, you say? See Item 1 above about the manual.

8. There's on-screen information for MP3s and photo CDs, with different views available for the contents and information. (Groups or folders or entire playlists with information)

9. I can't comment on the progressive scan feature, since I don't have an HD TV or HD-ready TV - yet. (Still waiting for that lottery win for a new TV)

10. It is supposed to play DVD-Audio discs, but you need 6.1 channel inputs on your receiver to play them and play DVD-Audio. Unfortunately, our receiver is lacking these inputs, but then again, I am also lacking any DVD-Audio discs to play.

Electronics buffs will probably say that it needs a bit of "tweaking" to get it to look and sound just right, but it looks and sounds great to me. All in all a very good player, perhaps excellent when you factor in the price of the player.

Amanda Richards, October 1, 2004

This HAMILTON BEACH DIGITAL RICE COOKER (37518, Stainless Steel, 6-¾ cup rice for white rice) cooks rice every time, and is a good rice cooker for rice (enough rice for 4 rice eaters). It has the same rice capacity as the [[ASIN:B071KPXVJ7 Hamilton Beach 37506 Model]], but has a lid (with rubber gasket, a steam vent, an exterior condensation cup, and a lid liner).

The lid of this Model 37518 causes foods to cook in one-third to one-half of the time required by the Model 37506, but the lid has NO effect on rice cooking times or cereal cooking times. The Model 37518 has a condensation cup that must be emptied, as needed, during cooking. The lid liner is a part that must be removed each time for washing. (The instructions don't explain how to remove the lid liner, but it pulls straight off the post that holds it.)

The Model 37518 allows you to set cooking times for Hot Cereal or Steam. This isn't really necessary, because the Model 37506 cooks both cereal and rice automatically, and cooks food with the aid of a cooking timer.

Most rice cookers do a good job of cooking rice--they have a thermostat that contacts the underside of the cooking pot and turns the rice cooker off automatically when the water evaporates and the pot temperature rises. Some rice cookers--like this rice cooker--cook rice to greater perfection than other rice cookers, but rice cookers mostly differ in their controls (ranging from simple on/off to multi-button digital displays), and in the rice yield.

This rice cooker is sort of in the middle, regarding both controls and rice yield. It will cook different kinds of rice (there is a chart for correct amounts of rice and water for long grain brown rice or white rice, jasmine rice, basmati rice, etc.). It will cook different cereals and grains (barley, oatmeal, Cream of Wheat, etc.). It will cook food (vegetables, poultry, seafood); and it will cook food and rice together.

The size of this rice cooker is good if you're making rice for a rice-eating family of four, or if you're cooking foods for a family of two. I love it for the way it cooks rice and automatically keeps the rice warm for up to 12 hours. I also love it for cooking Cream of Wheat automatically without burning it on the bottom.

Cooking in a rice cooker takes longer than cooking on a stovetop or cooking in a microwave. For example, 3 cups of uncooked white rice will take up to 45 minutes for cooking; 1-½ cups of Cream of Wheat, up to 37 minutes for cooking. But it's easy to start the rice cooker and let it work while you're preparing the rest of your meal.

The rice cooker comes with a standard rice cup measure (about ¾ cup U.S.), a rice-rinsing insert, and a nylon spoon. The cooking pot has an excellent nonstick surface. The removable pieces are all hand washable in warm, soapy water; handwashing is very easy and simple.

In choosing between this Model 37518 and the Model 37506, I prefer the latter (with a simple, vented glass lid, no condensation cup, longer cooking times, and no ability to set cooking times). Both rice cooker models are very good rice cookers, but sometimes simpler rice cookers are better rice cookers.

*This is the end, isn't it?*

The thought struck Josh suddenly, almost by accident. The thought pierced through and dissolved his frustration with the car that had allowed him to break down so far from home; with the phone company that had neglected to build towers by this barren desert road; with the sun that had audaciously beaten him, sweaty and tired, to the ground.

*This is the end.*

This thought in particular remained prominent in his mind, even as he realized that he had already seen Heather for the last time. And... and Joey, who was still so proud about that geometry test. And Dale, and the business Dale would inherit, the business that would serve as an unexpected legacy.

*This is it.*

Dale, who had told him that this trip was a fool's errand, and made a joke about what he would say at Josh's funeral; this memory, too, failed to shake the thought from Josh's head. The thought remained there in Josh's head.

*The end of...*

The thought lingered there, static, for a time that Josh wasn't able to comprehend. Everything else in his mind seemed to fade away, from his periphery, inward toward this single, solitary thought. This single thought remained.

*This is the end of me.*

When nothing else was left, Josh found it fitting that this thought of finality should itself be his final thought.

But the thought wasn't.

The thought vanished as abruptly as the thought came, and then --

Josh would have cried, if he was still physically capable.

His regrets came flooding back all at once. And his anger, and his sorrow and his despondency at his own powerlessness. The tranquil peace of the "end" was over, replaced with the angst of a life incomplete. A life that had failed to come to terms with itself. A life that had failed Josh completely.

And then Josh felt **fear**. Fear like he had never felt before. The terror of fate incarnate, of the great unknown for which he was utterly unprepared. The sheer and total horror overwhelmed his memory, and his pain, and all his other emotions. The fear overwhelmed everything Josh had left.

That fear was the last thing Josh thought about. The fear was Josh's final thought.

"Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave. Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave. Citizens will not be allowed..." the Moral Officer bellowed into his bullhorn. I found it hearting. The ending being so near gave me the strength to push my weak and weary body to shovel faster, faster.

All around me my fellow citizens dug in the dust like brittle dry dust, digging out the grave where they would give their bodies back to the dust. In the distance other Moral Officers made their proclamations into identical bullhorns. At regular intervals throughout the field Compliance Officers stood, in immaculate uniforms, waiting patiently to aid us in our final duty to the Nation.

It had become clear that there was a food shortage well before the State announced it. Everyone had whispered about how the weekly rations they picked up from the distribution station seemed to be smaller every week, though the station's Party workers would deny it if anyone asked. Then the whispers turned to fully voiced complaints when items began disappearing from the rations, never to reappear again. Soon meat had almost become a memory and fully grown, healthy looking vegetables were rare.

When the State News Agency, in a special broadcast, finally announced the famine, nobody was surprised. We were instructed that we must, as always, stand united, strong and proud in the face of this Straining Test. Everyone must do their part to bear this burden and our Immaculate Society would clear this hurdle and emerge triumphant. Even the Beloved Ruler was rationing his consumption, we were told. It was clear, yes undoubtably clear, that this was some ploy by the dissidents and the outsiders, attempting to destroy our resolve, to make us turn back from the ideas of the revolution. They had sabotaged our fields and murdered our animals. But we would stay strong in our virtue and would emerge, as ever, triumphant and strong.

It was then that they announced the lottery. That a number of citizens would be randomly selected from the population to give glorious sacrifice of faith and virtue for the Nation, to help ease the burden of consumption. Those who were selected were informed the next day by a soldier showing up at their door to take them away from their families. I was one of the selected citizens.

A shout rang out across the fields, "May my body fertilize the dust to feed our glorious Nation. Long live the Beloved Ruler." A gunshot punctuated this declaration. Someone had already finished their grave. A few others cheered their assent, most were too weary and hungry to manage. The Compliance Officer holstered his pistol and motioned for the now dead man's two neighbors to fill in the grave he now occupied with dust.

They had worked us hard after taking us away, digging out a roadway with our shovels. We slept where we worked and the only sustenance given to us was a broth so thin that they could hardly justify calling it more than hot water. And so the last of the strength of our bodies was harvested for the Nation.

My grave now looked deep enough. I hesitated before raising up my shovel to call over the Compliance Officer. If the grave was not deep enough for his liking I would have to wait until all others had finished their graves, covering over their graves with dust, before it would be my turn.

He came over and produced a tape measurer. He checked the dimensions of the grave and nodded his assent. I let out an inaudible sigh of relief and went to stand at the foot of my grave. The time was here. The time for my glorious sacrifice for the sake of the Nation. The time for my final duty to my beloved Nation and my beloved land.

"Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave." The Moral Officer chanted into his bullhorn.

I felt the cool metal of the Compliance Officer pistol come to rest upon my forehead.

"Citizens will not be allowed..."

"Why, hello, Ma'am," I said easily, standing up and offering her a chair with my usual grace. "Bertram Proudfoot at your service. Whom do I have the pleasure of addressing?"

"I'd rather not say, if it's all the same to you," she said, sitting down.

"Alright," I said comfortably. "What can the Hobbiton Detective and Gossip Agency do for you?"

"Well," said the dame, rubbing her hands together nervously. "It's like this." She paused.

"Like what, Ma'am?" I said kindly, lighting my pipe and sitting back in my chair.

"My husband is dead," she said.

"Oh my dear, I am sorry!" I exclaimed, though I must admit there was part of me that was less than sorry. What can I say? I am only a Hobbit, and this dame had the most beautiful feet I had ever laid eyes on. "Tell me everything that happened."

"We were out boating on the Brandywine three nights ago," she said. "And all of a sudden, a rock flew out of nowhere and hit my poor husband in the head. He keeled over in the water. I screamed for help, but he drowned."

Now of course I had already known it must have been something like this from the moment she walked in the door. I have an uncanny sense for things like that.

I looked as grave as I could, given the circumstances. "I see," I said, blowing another perfect smoke ring up towards the ceiling. "And you would like me to find and prosecute the perpetrator of this event."

"Yes," said the dame.

"I will do my best, I can promise you that," I said, and I saw her visibly sight with relief. "May I offer you a cup of tea? Something stronger, perhaps?"

"No thank you," she said, and without another word she showed herself out.

I promptly made my way to the Brandywine River dock. My first line of inquiry would be to interrogate the man who rented out boats. An odd fellow, and an odd profession -- not many sane hobbits choose to be out in the middle of the water by their own free will. And indeed, this hobbit's boat-renting business was not doing well.

After a long consultation of his records he told me that he had rented out two boats on the evening in question, and only one of those boats was rented by a couple. The couple had been a one Drogo Baggins and a one Primula Brandybuck. Primula, that was the dame's name. But why had she not wanted to tell it to me?

Had this boat fellow heard any commotion on the water, any cries for help? No he had not. Did he remember who returned the boat to him? It hadn't been returned, he said. In fact, that particular boat had been left floating in the middle of the river. Strange.

Next I walked up and down the both banks of the river. Not much to garner here, except that whoever had thrown the rock must have been quite a shot with that rock.

Having thoroughly investigated the river, my next step was to find out about Primula and Drogo. After visiting several pubs in the areas of Buckland and Hobbiton, I had gathered this: Primula and Drogo were long married, though perhaps not happily married. They had one son, now 12, named Frodo Baggins. Strangely, it seemed that Primula had not been seen by anyone except me since Drogo's death. In fact, most of the gentlehobbits that I spoke with seemed to be of the belief that both Drogo *and* Primula had died three nights ago.

Facts were not adding up. Before I could do anything else, I had to speak with my mysterious client again so as to straighten things out. Though I had no way of contacting her, I knew she would return to my offices in short order.

The day following, she did just that.

"Good day, Primula," I said upon her entrance.

Her face betrayed surprise, but she did not deny the name.

"I have a few things I need to get straight with you about the case," I said, and proceeded to outline what I had discovered. "So I'm afraid I must ask again," I finished. "What happened that night?"

And without a word, the dame got up and left. Just like that.

I did not hear from her again, and two days later, her body was found floating down the Brandywine. I was saddened but not surprised.

My suspicion had been this: having been unhappily married for some time, Primula had pushed her husband into the water herself and boated back to the shore with the intent of disappearing forever. Everyone would think that they both were dead, and so would not suspect any foul play. However, upon eavesdropping on the lawyer's meetings that quickly followed, she realized that custody of her son would go to an extended cousin, none other than the famous crackpot Bilbo Baggins.

Understandably, Primula did not want her offspring to fall under the influence of said crackpot, and so she came to me in the hopes that I would believe her story and deflect suspicion away from herself, all in a desperate attempt to maintain custody of her son. But I, having seen through her ruse, prevented this fact. Seeing no alternative she then drowned herself in grief. Shame -- I had just begun to think there may have been a very beneficial alternative for the both of us.

I sat back and began polishing my pipe thoughtfully. It was another case solved by the estimable Bertram Proudfoot, but perhaps another opportunity lost. I had solved countless cases, but opportunities of the other sort came only but now and again. Like I said, it was a shame.

I blew another smoke ring to the ceiling as my thoughts turned to crazed old Mr. Baggins. I felt for the young Mr. Frodo, who was now cursed enough to fall into the old hobbit's custody. Who knows what old Baggins would pass on to the impressionable young fellow. As I'm sure you're all aware, Mr. Bilbo Baggins suddenly disappeared many years ago and then returned just as suddenly a year later with hoards of gold and many tall tales. Having been a very respectable hobbit before he left, whatever he experienced on his journey seemed to have addled his mind. He came back a changed hobbit, and not for the better.

He was so changed, in fact, that it is my personal suspicion that the hobbit currently inhabiting Bag End is not the real Bilbo Baggins at all, but rather an impersonator. There is plenty of evidence to suggest this: particularly the fact that "Mr. Baggins" appears much younger than a hobbit of his years has any right to look. The hobbit at Bag End looks younger than any hobbit of those years should look.

I shall have to explore that line of inquiry further some day. That inquiry will require further exploration at some future time.

The Shine could have been salvation for humanity. The Shine should have been salvation, but we were never very good at evading conflict. Who knows how long ago the Shine was, but in an age of devices and information we lifted our gaze from our devices only to see the sky ignite, consumed by a cold, variegated blaze. The blaze lasted only a few hours, but the blaze took only a few minutes for the world to see the blaze. It didn't take much longer for people to want a closer look at the blaze, to crave a caress of the gentle flame from the blaze.

And then they flew. They flew so far and so fast, and swiftly they were joined by others who flew; and then they fell, very slowly at first, but much like a boat in water they sank further the more that joined them in flying. It didn't take long for people to work out that the sinking related directly to how many people flew, or to notice that flying wasn't the only *option* available to us from the Shine. Before the Shine had faded many such options came and went; flight, strength, healing, invisibility, immortality, teleportation, speed, and all the other common options appeared and disappeared very quickly. At first some thought the powers only lasted a time, related to how long the Shine was present, but it swiftly became apparent that the potency of powers was inversely proportional to the number who selected that *option*.

That's when the more obscure powers started cropping up; at first it was just people who decided they wanted to shit gold, or people who decided they wanted to control animals, but before a quarter day had passed things started getting weird with the powers. Rapid drops in temperature from powers, the ground shook frequently from powers, clocks would stutter from powers and people died. Many people died. In half a day, an eight-billion-strong global society of the most intelligent and durable species on Earth collapsed and halved in number; we dissolved into groups and factions just looking to survive, to weather the storm; those *without* powers were kings, and those with obscure powers that couldn't be worked out or copied were gods in flesh, right there to worship when many needed them most.

A few days passed before things started to settle - though in that time the sun only passed once. Weather was beyond erratic and settlements were nigh-on deserted, only habitable for larger and more powerful factions. We went from pursuing prosperity to living rough in a day, if you could call it that day. We reverted to beasts, except slightly more intelligent beasts, and sometimes super-powered beasts.

Much time has passed since the Shine touched our sky, and humanity has created many new settlements; but the most popular options are still weak, so death is power, and raids are frequent and unrelenting raids. The largest settlements are the most powerful settlements, but also the primary target for smaller settlements. Living with others is living in war, so the more peaceful of us left settlements to travel.

And that is what I have done. I have travelled, and searched for a way to absolve this madness, and perhaps restore the world to the relative sanity the world once had. And I may well just have found it.

I stood at an intersection, looking towards the capitol building. I stared at this girl on fire. She sat calmly. Not moving a muscle, not making a sound. People stood and stared. There were other black marks on the steps she sat on.

"Mommy, why is she on fire?"

"Oh, that's normal," my mother said.

"So it is totally normal for people to burst into fire?" My six year old mind was confused.

"No son, that is not the normal part. We are in a war. People don't like the way the government controls things, so they protest by burning themselves."

"Will she be okay?" My naive mind wanted her to be okay. No one should be so upset they hurt themselves like that.

"I don't know," came the response.

Years later, after the war was lost, I would read about all the people who burned themselves for their country. My country.

Through my years at school, I would think of these people. The people with beliefs so strong they would literally kill themselves in such a way to make a powerful statement. They would not want to live in a country under the crushing government that had been ruling for years. They wanted to be free, or they wanted to die.

It seems every generation, there is an uprising. The oppressed people realize that they're being oppressed, and they get a tool to help them organize and fight back. They gain power. Rarely does it happen in a short span. However, here I was, an oppressed 27 year old with absolutely no future.

I stood at that intersection that I stood at 21 years ago. The black marks were gone, but so was my naivety. This government had to go. They had oppressed my mother's generation. They had oppressed the generation before them, and the generation after them. They weren't going to stop unless forced to. I calmly walked up to the steps and prepared to make the newest black mark, start the next uprising.

As the fire rose past my eyes, I wanted one last look as I burned. The pain was almost unbearable, but I managed to see through the pain. The last thing I saw before the world faded was a young girl pointing at me, exactly where I had been 21 years before. The girl stood at the same intersection. I walked downstairs and opened up the screen. A banker opened up on the screen.

"Hello Mrs. Roer. How may I help you?"

"I'd like to check my bank statement. I got a letter in the mail that I only have five credits?"

"Okay, one moment." The banker disappeared for a moment and then opened back up.

"Mrs. Roer. You have 10 credits."

"What? That's not even enough to buy groceries with this month?"

I looked outside and then sighed.

"Okay. Well thanks." I said.

The screen closed after the banker wished me a good day. How could I only have 10 credits of happiness? A gallon of milk is 1.21 credits. I couldn't even buy milk.

I walked outside this time. It was sunny and bright, birds were happy, I bet they have enough happiness credits to buy groceries. I looked around. My pool, my hot-tub, my deck with a pond from the house. All of this was my life.

My husband and I had been married for ten years now. I was happy, he was happy. Right?

I went to look at my phone, I had a message from my husband.

'Want to have coffee?'

I sent back,'Yes.'

I went upstairs and took a shower. My husband was gone, as always. It was no secret we had been falling apart. We were so happy at one point though that we had more credits than anybody in the word. Like I said though, it was no secret that we had been falling apart. He had affairs and I, although I never cheated, found myself longing for more.

I prepared myself for coffee. Nothing too dressy or too casual. It was just coffee. I walked outside, got in one of our cars and drove to the airport. We owned a jet, my husband had already put gas in it.

"Just having coffee today Bill," I said.

I was walking off the jet in 4 hours to see my husband.

"Hello Mrs. Roer," He said, kissing my cheek, as he always did.

I walked with him to our second home. A blonde woman with a tight blouse was leaving the home. I scowled at her, and she hurried from the door to her car.

"We need to talk," I said.

"Exactly," He replied, seemingly pleased at my displeasure.

"Listen, Mr. Roer, I do love you, but there's so --."

"Elaine, I want a divorce."

"That was quick." I said.

He shrugged it off.

I left quickly after that. No coffee for me.

It wasn't long before I got home. I had a message from the bank again. My happiness credits had hit zero.

A message from an old friend surprised me.

"Coffee?" It read.

"Sure." I answered.

At that moment my doorbell rang. I answered the door to him.

My old friend. He kissed me. I had missed that feeling. I felt my blood pressure rise.

"Good to see you."

"Listen Luke, I just-"

He kissed me again and broke my words.

"I paid your husband to let me marry you Elaine. He's wanted a divorce and he's not good to you. You know that."

I was shocked. He paid my husband to marry me? Why on Earth would he pay my husband to marry me?

"Elaine. I know we didn't work out, but our son. He needs you."

I felt a tear hit my chest. I had given Luke, and our son up to be with my husband. My husband refused to let me have a son in the house that was not his son.

"Elaine. Marry me. Please?" He said. He walked inside towards me. "Our son is in the car. He's 12 now," Luke said.

I had gotten to see our son, Reig, until he was four. Then I had to cut off communications to my husband being afraid it would make us look bad on the press.

I walked outside and my son ran from the car. He wrapped his arms around me. I felt my phone alert again and I checked it. In case it was my husband with an explanation for why he'd 'sold' my hand.

It was the bank. My bank account had just been credited 20,000 happiness credits.

"Yes. I'll marry you."

The shocked and paralysed Demons that twitched and writhed on the ground were easy targets for the rumblers, the rumblers blessed water cannons burning away swaths of the foul demons as if the misted holy water were strong acid, huge piles of the demons were reduced to ash in seconds by the water cannons.

Snub nosed heads the size of a grand cathedral covered in spines, long armored bodies like an insects, their faces and joints slick with thick black tar that bubbled and hissed as the tar fell from them and stained the plains of Limbo.

Screachers focused their assault and prevented the titans from over running the base, the rumblers water tanks and javelin cannons ran dry just trying to keep the Hell Dragons at bay, our brave grunts held back the black swarm, the grunts fighting tirelessly which allowed us time to retreat, resupply and reenter the fray. And so it went for hours on end and for all our efforts the Hell Dragons seemed to be none the worse for our efforts.

Salvation finally came at the hands of the engineering corps. Of all people! Through our efforts we had given the engineering corps enough time to secure and assemble Limbo Bases major defenses, Sanctified Artillery and the Holy Rail Gun. The Rail Gun punctured the Dragons thick armor spewing geysers of tar onto the battlefield while the artillery smashed into the beasts vulnerable exposed points lodging shells etched with scripture deep in the Dragons bodies wracking the Dragons with pain. The attack still went on for hours and we lost a great deal of our force but after nearly 2 months since we first descended into this place we finally have established a forward base to launch our attack on Hell. One Bolgia down eight to go. This is the first day here that the smell doesn't bother me.
