I was five years old at the time and entertained mostly by the colours, the beautiful blue and green were like nothing on the Ark. We had water- sure, but not water large enough to give that blue colour. We had plants too, but the conditions were far from optimal and made the plants a dirty green rather than lush green. I wanted to see the planet closer- touch the planet- feel the planet.

That was probably when I decided to join the recruitment for the first journey. The first journey was- as the name implies, the first journey back down to the planet. A lot of people wanted to go back down as soon as the storms ended, there were protests- riots even. People wanted the Ark to head straight back down to the planet- Idiots.

23 years may have been a long time to wait, but waiting was important... We were the last people after all- if we landed on the planet and something went wrong? We couldn't risk the planet. Years of planet scans, and low atmosphere scouting gave us the perfect landing spot on the planet. Minimal damage to local planet environment, enough space to develop a community on the planet, plenty of food- water- and importantly a lot of natural protection taking the form of storm-formed mountain ranges, and deep trenches filled with the darkest blue water.

Of course something as large as the Ark couldn't simply just land on the planet though... No- that was where the first journey came into the picture. We were the first people to go to the planet- and live on the planet permanently in over seven generations. "Hey, check out that chickadees over in the birdbath." Kylo whooped and puffed out his chest, nearly toppling off his perch.

"Don't be a troglodyte, bro," Atticus groused, pecking at his seeds, "You're a wren. That isn't even the same family."

"I don't care. I'm gonna go talk to them." Kylo took off, swerving through the air like a leaf trapped in a gust. Atticus sighed and took off after him. He'd have to keep close tabs on Kylo or else they'd get kicked out again.

Kylo crashed into the water with a mighty splash. Water flew in every direction, drenching the birds of the birdbath. They squawked with indignation as Kylo emerged from beneath the water, shaking the water from his head. He trotted up to a group of soaked finches and gave his wings a shake. "Hey, birds. Nice tits."

"We're not tits." A purple finch stepped forward from the group, and she launched into a tirade on how overused that line was. Atticus alighted on the rim of the bath and began to walk around, apologizing to everyone for Kylo's behavior and pleading with them not to call the bouncer over.

"Okay, sorry," Kylo interrupted, "let me make it up to you: how about you and I head over there—" He motioned to the feeder. "—and I share my seeds with you?" If birds had lips, Kylo would be smirking right now.

The finches began to flap their wings angrily, splashing Kylo with water. "You're such a boor. Get out of here!" Many of the birds chirped in agreement, and some of the bigger birds began to puff their chests threateningly. Atticus shoved Kylo to the side and raised his wings. "On behalf of my friend here, I apologize. He's clearly had too much nectar; we'll just be going now..."

"Oh, you think we're going to fall for that?" The purple finch spat a nut shell at his feet. "He's just trying to play wingbird for you, isn't he? Let him take the fall for you, and swoop in to look better by comparison." The other birds chorused in agreement. The birds were angry. The birds wanted action.

"I think these two need to be taught a lesson." A blue jay fluttered over to Atticus, towering a full inch above him. He spread his wings menacingly, blocking Atticus from taking off. "Why don't you peck on someone your own size?" The birds broke into cheers, shouting for a fight.

"Well, you're kind of bigger than me." Atticus took a step back into the bath. He felt feathers ruffle against him as the birds pressed around him, urged him back towards the jay. "That wouldn't be my own size now, would it?"

Kylo staggered in front of him and began to hop around. "Don't worry, Atticus; we got this."

"Hey, this is a one-on-one fight." The jay looked around. "If you get back-up, then—"

"Who on earth placed all this here?" A door opened, and the birds began to scatter, screaming, "Human!" Atticus grabbed Kylo and urged him into the air, and the two lost themselves amongst the cloud of fleeing birds. Out of the corner of his eye, he saw the human scratching his head in front of the birdbath. The human looked confused. The human examined the birdbath closely.

"Make sure to thank that human for bailing you out of yet another mess," Atticus said.

Kylo scoffed. "We could've totally taken that guy." As the two flew over the car in the driveway, he let loose a dropping that landed right in the center of the windshield.

He used to hit me so much.

I'd never even had a drink, and he hit me until he hit cracked ribs into me, hit bruised kidneys into me and hit loose teeth into me. To make sure I never became what he was.

Once when he was sober he told me he drank because of how he grew up. He said it like he wanted me to empathise with him, to forgive him. Like he couldn't see that my arm was broken from him protecting me from drink the week before. Like he couldn't see himself standing over me crying blood and snot and tears, jeering. Like he couldn't remember what was so bad about how he grew up, couldn't remember why he needed it to let him sleep at night, to stop waking up screaming in the night, to stop pissing himself when he had a bad dream.

He made me sick, my dad. My breath catches sometimes, and one of my wrists never set right, leaving me half crippled in that hand. I have eleven false teeth. At twenty three, all this.

I didn't go to his funeral, I celebrated it though. I didn't take a drink though, I could never do that. I cry myself to sleep most nights, I can't help myself screaming if someone comes up to me suddenly. Lately I've noticed a lot of blood coming up when I cough. I won't let him hit me though, I won't give him this little victory.

When my son was born it was the happiest day of my life. For the first time in my life, someone wanted me and needed me. His mother left soon after that, saying she didn't want to be trapped in a lifestyle she didn't choose after carrying a child for nine months, she leaves it in three weeks. Never in those nine months did she not choose that lifestyle.

Honestly, after she left it all got too much for me. I left my son with my mother for the night, and went and had a drink. It was perfect. It was the best I've felt in my whole life. For a few hours, I wasn't scared or self-loathing or on edge. Just calm and ok, I could deal with everything a little better. I think I'll probably have a few more drinks now, just to keep the buzz going. Sobriety now scares me even more, now that I know that there's such an easy alternative, which is so much better.

When I picked my son up in the morning mom looked at me funny, but I blew her off. I was in a bit of a rush, I'd heard good things about whisky, and was eager to try it. I was eager to try whisky and see if whisky was as good as I'd heard.

But don't worry, I won't let my son grow up like I did, I'll make sure he knows drink is evil. I won't expose him to that pain, to that fear. I'll make sure he hates me for as long as possible as much as possible. He'll associate drink with me, and I'm bad, so he'll break the cycle. I'm not strong enough, but he will be strong enough. I know he'll be strong enough. I'll make him calloused enough outside, and cold enough and hard enough inside. He'll be able to beat it. Like I can't beat it.

Craig was walking home from the shops when he met God. He wasn't expecting to meet God, people rarely do. In fact he didn't really ever think about God. He didn't believe in God, but he also didn't think about God not existing. God and God weren't really things he thought about.

A thing he thought deeply about was that of Caramels. If you don't know Caramels are a rather delicious chocolatey thing composed of several things of wafer encased in chocolate, and Craig was crazy about them. He may not have thought about God, but his thoughts on Caramels came close. The reason behind his shops trip was to buy more Caramels, and his mind was full of Caramels thoughts as he headed back home.

He was about two minutes away from his home, and Caramel satisfaction when God first spoke to him.

"Hey! Craig!"

His Caramel thoughts interrupted, Craig turned round to see who had spoken to him. Behind him stood a tall person in a loose fitting suit. Craig wasn't really sure of the person's gender, they were pretty androgynous, looking not dissimilar to Diamond Dogs era David Bowie. They looked familiar to Craig, but he couldn't quite put his finger on where he might have seen them before. He realised he'd been staring, and sought something to say.

"Hi," he began hesitantly. "Do I know you?"

"In a way," replied the Bowie lookalike. "I'm God."

"Well good for you. I've got to get going now. Bye." Said Craig before starting back towards his home. He had Caramels in his bag, and didn't want to be wasting time on a crazy person.

"Wait, don't go yet. Please." Called out the person. "What would it take for you to believe me?"

Craig sighed and turned back, deciding that humouring the person would probably get him to his Caramels faster.

"I don't know," said Craig, exasperated. "A miracle or something. Some extraordinary thing which couldn't just be done by any old person. Something more than just saying that you're god."

"Hmm. How about....*this*!" God pointed at a bush which burst into flames. The flames shaped themselves into a dragon which roared at the two of them. Then, with a snap of God's fingers, the flames were extinguished leaving the bush singed but intact. God turned back to Craig with arms spread wide as if to say'Tada!'

Craig, looking mildly impressed, turned back to God.

"Yeah, that was pretty good. Looked very impressive. I have to admit I have no idea how you did it. A hologram maybe? It worked for Tupac, so I can see it working for a dragon."

God stared at him for a few seconds before responding.

"I did it by being God. You asked for a miracle. I showed you one. What more do you want from me?"

"Don't get me wrong, it's very good. But the whole God thing probably isn't going to fly. Maybe people would be more likely to believe you're a wizard."

"But I'm not a damn wizard!" Shouted God. "I'm God. Why would I say I'm a wizard?"

Craig backed off a few meters, holding his hands up in front of him in the international gesture of'I don't want any trouble, let's all just calm down'.

"Hey calm down buddy. I'm sorry if I came across as harsh, but it's just constructive criticism. This is for a T.V. show or YouTube thing right? You're not going to get anyone with the whole'God' thing."

God, visably seething by this point, held Craig's gaze for a few more seconds before letting out an angry sigh and storming off.

Craig watched them leave, then shook his head and returned to his journey home. He considered checking out the bush to see if he could get any clues as to how the thing had been done, but decided against it. Whoever had been recording the thing was probably still watching, waiting for Craig to do exactly that. So he pushed it out of his mind, and set off home. After all, there were Caramels waiting for him. Caramels were what mattered. Caramels were what Craig thought about. Caramels were waiting at home for Craig.

The subway stopped abruptly. Laurentius awoke with a gasp. He struggled to take in his surroundings: It was cold, that was certain. He examined his armour: His hands were covered with gloves that appeared to be made of cow hide. His boots were black, fur-lined and warm. Underneath a thick black coat was a soft white shirt, with clasps holding the shirt together in the front. A red strip of fabric reached around his neck and made its way to just past his stomach. "*What is this, *" he thought. "*Is that how I died? Do we wear tokens of our death? *" His eyes met those of a rotund darker-skinned woman, who was reading a curious layered-parchment device on her lap. He looked around her neck: a cross. He looked at the woman sympathetically. "*I suppose so. *"

Tubes of light illuminated the metal chamber he was in. A smooth ding announced itself, and the doors closed shut. To Laurentius' surprise, the metal chamber began to move again. He stood, and made his way to a man he assumed was in charge. The man, covered in what seemed to be traditional dress for the era, with the exception of a large silver wig, and glasses that read "2015" across the front of the glasses.

"*Salve*," Laurentius began.

The man returned a confused look, then returned to gazing out the window. The man smelled of wine.

"*Aut ubi sum? Quis hic locus? *"

The metal chamber shook once again, slightly, disrupting Laurentius' balance. A voice rang out over the loudspeaker, but Laurentius couldn't make out what the voice had said. The metal chamber made another stop, but Laurentius wasn't prepared. He fell onto the floor below as a wave of people exited. He got up and followed the crowd, which weaved through tunnels. He struggled to take everything in: Musicians lined the enclosed street. Few vendors, from what he understood. He continued until he reached a flight of stairs. He ascended the stairs, and was astounded by what he saw.

Bright lights flashed around him, in all directions. What was the steady hum of voices, interrupted occasionally by an outburst, had now turned into an onslaught of voices and action. To his left and right, the streets were lined with people all moving towards a central location, where a large spire reached into the heavens. Atop this spire was a sphere. He looked into the sky.

No stars?

No stars. He pondered. Suddenly, a realization came to him, and with the realization, a wave of happiness and relief. There were no stars, for he was above the stars all: Might these be the plains of Asphodel? The plains were more beautiful than he'd ever imagined.

Suddenly, a man in a similar outfit – a black coat, black pants, white shirt – ran up to him. Black metal covered his eyes, and frost came out of his mouth when the man spoke.

"Dick!" the man said, grabbing Laurentius by the arm. So overwhelmed, Laurentius had no expectation of arguing. He followed this man.

"Dick, where have you been? We've been looking all over – the crowd's waiting, and they ain't happy. Kathy's been doing what she can, but..."

Laurentius paused. Clearly, he must learn the language of the afterlife. He noticed some of the crowd had begun to direct their attention towards him. He returned the same greeting he was offered.

"Dick," he said, nodding his head at the passers-by as he was carried off by the man he had met.

"Dick," he said once more, this time at a young girl. Her ears were covered immediately by her mother, who left a scathing glare in her wake.

A few minutes of navigating the bustling streets passed, and Laurentius passed by other similarly-dressed gentlemen who padded him down. After greeting both of the gentlemen formally, he was ushered up steep metal stairs, and onto a platform which overlooked the massive crowd below. The platform held a woman, red-haired, who was holding a microphone. "Dick!" the woman said, "Where have you been? We're on in 2."

"Dick," Laurentius smiled.

"Well, you know what I like."

Someone handed Laurentius a plastic cord with a bud on the end of the cord. He looked at the woman, who had the cord placed in her ear, and did the same. Perhaps this was part of the welcoming ceremony.

He heard the woman speak with the man behind a larger metal contraption, one with a folded glass mirror in the centre of the contraption.

"Live in 30."

"Alright. You ready?" the woman said, looking directly at Laurentius. He nodded. The woman handed him another metal stick with fur at the end of the stick, much like the stick she was holding. The woman stared into the contraption. Her lips formed a smile, and Laurentius couldn't help but smile himself.

A small red light went on in the corner of the metal-glass contraption. There was a brief pause. The woman nudged Laurentius expectantly.

Laurentius smiled and inhaled deeply. "Dick," Laurentius said, and looked expectantly once again at the woman to his right.

*** 
 The Author 
 *** 
 
 I can't shake the feeling. You know, that feeling creeping along your spine waiting to take up residence in the base of your skull like some kind of parasite. It's an indeterminable feeling you're being watched. I can't shake the feeling off. I am sure I know what the feeling is, but I'm not ready to admit I know. The... *author* let's call him. The author is watching, waiting, building. Even as I think this, the author is scratching it down in his chicken-scratch scrawl, touching the pen against his teeth in thought. I can feel it; I can see it in my mind's eye. The author is trying to figure out how to kill me. 
 
 I suppose it is my own fault. See I kept asking, I needed to understand the feeling. I had to find out if there was some directing hand to life. If mankind had a purpose, a reason, I needed to appreciate what purpose we worked toward. There's a moment, one moment of particular realization, which caught me and held fast. Like my apprehension regarding an observer; only, this feeling was deeper, more primal. I *knew*, I mean really *understood*; all of it is a narrative. Life is a story. Which inevitably led me to the conclusion -- there needs to be an architect, an *author*. 
 
 The car narrowly missed me. I had an inkling of a feeling pressing against my chest verging on the edge of panic. I didn't cross when the green man displayed on the crossing signal, instead I took a step back. My *spidey-sense* tingled. The taxi-cab driver never saw me, I hadn't seen the driver either. His drunken sprawling car slammed into the same traffic signal post I had been, until recently, standing by. Can I tell you how fucked up that feeling is, I have this realization, followed by a sudden feeling of fear. If I hadn't heeded my gutless compulsion, I might have been splattered between the cabbie's car and the hard place which was the traffic signal pole. I turned my gaze upward, burning eyes and clenching jaw notwithstanding, and decried whoever worked at compiling this narrative. 
 
 "What the actual fuck was that?" I said. 
 
 Okay, so I realize my choice of words probably did not fall into the definition of circumspect, but hell we're talking about some kind of god-figure deciding on my time to die. 
 
 *Are you sure? * My logical brain asked. 
 
 I pondered my position, both in the physical sense and meta-physical sense. 
 
 *Yeah, I'm fucking sure, * I replied to myself internally. *How else do you explain the sudden epiphany and subsequently my almost immediate death. There's an* author *and the author doesn't want to be known. * 
 
 I'm not sure how I knew the *author* didn't want to be known, or the fact the author was a man, but I figured it was something in my general make-up granting me the knowledge. Oh don't get all high and mighty and preach at me now, I'm not talking religion or spirituality, I want to live damnit. I stood, still staring up at the sky, trying to impart my utter disgust and frustration when the signal pole creaked, unnaturally so. I adjusted my head so my eyes were level with the pole. 
 
 The metal appeared warped, and I realized that the car had burst into flames. 
 
 *When had that happened? * I thought. *Nevermind, run stupid. * 
 
 My internal dialog is not always the most kind; I'm a blunt sort. So, I ran. What I was running from, if Mr. Omniscient *author* was already in my head, the author could follow me anywhere. Hell, I could have an inopportune flashback, and the author could hit me with a mack truck. If this *author* decided I was going to die, why didn't the author do it already? 
 
 *Fuck me, * I thought. *It's about the drama; the story. * 
 
 "Sick fuck," I said. I knew the author would hear me, or the author would write that in his juvenile scrawl, knowing I intended it for the author. 
 
 *What if I stop? * 
 
 I looked up again, and said, "What are you going to do with a character who won't cooperate, huh?" 
 
 Naturally, the author didn't respond. It wasn't like I expected a voice from the sky, but I figured the author might strike me down with lightning or something, I mean the author potentially has that within his ability, right? The author might decide my knowledge of the plan labeled me as a liability. The author might decide the plan needed to change. The author might decide the plan was already working. 
 
 *What the hell is the plan anyway? * 
 
 I don't know, I guess the plan is for me to die. Perhaps, the author is not into the mundane. Maybe, just maybe, the author wants my death to be something significant, something of a show. I bet that's the plan. I got the feeling again; a gut punch to my stomach making my insides roil like they were leaking to the outside, and the rumbling feeling in my stomach suggested I take a step back. I did. Something pierced the skin in my back. It was a fluid, smooth motion that parted the skin. I felt the warm blood mixing with my sweat as it soaked the back of my flannel shirt. 
 
 A quiet voice whispered in my ear. "Hello protagonist," she said. "I'm your antagonist, the *author* says hello." 
 
 That was all she said. She didn't have a scent, like you would expect. She was a ghost from the shadows. I don't know who she was, or why her, but she'd made it clear... I was right. Take that fucker. I didn't have the strength to say it, but I know the author heard me. The author always hears me. The author always knows the feeling.

words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::2: Objectives Recently, two point-of-care (PoC) feline immunodeficiency virus (FIV) antibody examination kits (Witness and Anigen Rapid) were reported as being capable of differentiating FIV-vaccinated from FIV-infected cats at a solitary temporal point, irrespective of the interval between testing and ultimate vaccination (0-7 years). words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::3: Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) constitutes an uncommon monogenic malady characterized by benign neoplasms in multiple viscera as well as an elevated prevalence of epilepsy, intellectual disability and autism. Heterozygocity induces hyperactivation of mTOR which can be inhibited by mTOR inhibitors, such as rapamycin, which have demonstrated efficacy in the amelioration of TSC-associated manifestations. The objective of the present investigation was (1) to identify molecular alterations associated with social and cognitive deficits in the cerebral tissue of Tsc1 +/- mice and (2) to investigate the molecular consequences of rapamycin treatment, which has been demonstrated to ameliorate genotype-related behavioural deficits. Molecular alterations in the frontal cortex and hippocampus of Tsc1 +/- and control mice, with or without rapamycin treatment, were investigated. A quantitative mass spectrometry-based shotgun proteomic approach (LC-MS E ) was employed as an unbiased methodology to detect alterations in protein concentrations. Alterations identified in the initial profiling stage were validated utilizing selected reaction monitoring (SRM). Protein Set Enrichment Analysis was employed to identify dysregulated pathways. LC-MS E analysis of Tsc1 +/- mice and controls ( n = 30) identified 51 proteins altered in frontal cortex and 108 in the hippocampus. Bioinformatic analysis combined with targeted proteomic validation revealed several dysregulated molecular pathways. Utilizing targeted assays, proteomic alterations in the hippocampus validated the pathways "myelination", "dendrite," and "oxidative stress", an upregulation of ribosomal proteins and the mTOR kinase. LC-MS E analysis was also employed on Tsc1 +/- and wildtype mice ( n = 34) treated with rapamycin or vehicle. Rapamycin treatment exerted a more pronounced proteomic effect in Tsc1 +/- mice with significant alterations (predominantly decreased expression) in 231 and 106 proteins, respectively. words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::4: Silica nanoparticles (nanoSiO 2 ) are auspicious systems that can deliver biologically dynamic compounds to tissues such as the cardiac muscle in a governable manner. In order to elucidate these mechanisms, this article explores the ex vivo cardiac function and mitochondria after exposure to nanoSiO 2 . The cumulative administration of nanoSiO 2 diminished the mechanical performance index of the rodent cardiac muscle with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC 50 ) of 93 μg/mL, affecting the relaxation velocity. The aforementioned consequences can be partially circumvented diminishing ROS or retarding the aperture of the mPTP. words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::5: Reversion to participation (RTP) of National Football League (NFL) athletes following isolated anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) ruptures has been documented. Athletes were excluded if RTP was constrained for rationales unrelated to the injury. ACL and MCL ruptures are correlated with superior RTP prognosis juxtaposed with ACL and PCL/LCL ruptures.
words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::6: Pulmonary hypertension in response to exertion constitutes a marker of the hemodynamic severity of mitral stenosis (MS). Nevertheless, the factors correlated to elevated pulmonary pressure with exertion remain insufficiently delineated. The objective of this investigation was to assess the parameters associated with the pulmonary pressure response to exertion in patients with pure rheumatic MS. An additional objective was to ascertain the impact of exercise-induced pulmonary hypertension on clinical outcome. One hundred thirty patients with MS (94% women; mean age, 45 ± 11 years) underwent exertion echocardiography. A range of echocardiographic parameters were procured at repose and at peak exertion. Symptom-limited graded ramp bicycle exertion was performed in the supine position. The primary terminus was mitral valve intervention, either percutaneous or surgical. In the overall population, systolic pulmonary artery pressure (SPAP) increased from 38.3 ± 13.4 mm Hg at repose to 65.8 ± 20.7 mm Hg during exertion. New York Heart Association functional class (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.459; 95% CI, 1.509-4.006; P < .001) and the interaction between valve area and net atrioventricular compliance (P = .001) were also significant predictors of adverse events. Time-dependent areas beneath the receiver operating characteristic curve for the model with SPAP during exertion were superior than for the model with SPAP at repose, with a significant amelioration from 3 years onward. In patients with MS, the pulmonary artery pressure response to exertion is determined by a combination of factors, encompassing transmitral mean gradient at exertion, net atrioventricular compliance, left atrial volume, and right ventricular function. Pulmonary artery pressure at peak exertion constitutes a predictor of clinical outcomes and confers incremental prognostic value beyond that furnished by standard resting measurements, encompassing valve area.
words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::7: The ramifications of chronic hepatic affliction upon outcomes in patients with COVID-19 remain uncertain. Hence, we endeavoured to explore this association. words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::8: The coronavirus malady 2019 (COVID-19) instigated by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2) has precipitated a substantial quantity of mortalities globally. COVID-19 constitutes a grave menace to human existence. The clinical manifestations of COVID-19 are multifarious and grievous and 20% of infected individuals are documented to be in a critical circumstance. A diminution in pulmonary function and pulmonary fibrosis are the principal manifestations of individuals with the severe manifestation of the malady. The pulmonary function is compromised, even following convalescence, thereby tremendously affecting the psychological state and well-being of individuals, and substantially diminishing their quality of existence. Participants must satisfy the following simultaneous inclusion criteria: exceeding 18 years of age, should have recuperated from severe or critical COVID-19 cases, should exhibit pulmonary fibrosis following convalescence, and should exhibit Qi-Yin deficiency syndrome as delineated in the system of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM). The eligible candidates will be randomized into therapeutic or control cohorts. The therapeutic cohort will receive contemporary medicine (pirfenidone) plus TCM whereas the control cohort will be administered contemporary medicine plus TCM placebo. The pulmonary function index will be continuously surveyed and documented. By comparing the therapeutic efficacy between the two cohorts, the investigation intends to ascertain whether TCM can ameliorate the effectiveness of contemporary medicine in individuals with pulmonary fibrosis arising as a sequelae following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Pulmonary fibrosis is one of fatal sequelae for some severe or critical COVID-19 cases, some investigations disclose that pirfenidone precipitates a postponement in the declension of forced expiratory vital capacity, thereby diminishing the mortality partially. Additionally, although TCM has been demonstrated to be efficacious in treating pulmonary fibrosis, its role in treating pulmonary fibrosis related COVID-19 has not been investigated. Hence, a multicenter, parallel-group, randomized controlled, interventional, prospective clinical investigation has been devised and will be conducted to ascertain if a novel comprehensive therapeutic regimen for pulmonary fibrosis related to COVID-19 is practicable and if it can ameliorate the quality of existence of individuals. This multicenter, parallel-group, randomized controlled, interventional, prospective investigation was registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2000033284) on 26th May 2020 (prospective registered).
words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::9: Thermal conditions and aqueous availability constitute two of the most paramount variables influencing all facets of an anuran's cardinal physiological processes such as corporeal temperature ( T b ), evaporative aqueous loss (EWL) and standard metabolic rate (SMR). Since anurans display pronounced sexual dimorphism, evidence suggests that these processes are further influenced by other factors such as vapour pressure deficit (VPD), sex and corporeal mass ( M b ). However, a limited number of investigations have tested the generality of these results across a wide range of ecologically relevant ambient temperatures ( T a ), while taking habitat utilisation into account. Thus, the aim of this investigation was to examine the role of T a on T b , whole-animal EWL and whole-animal SMR in three wild caught African anuran species with different ecological specialisations: the principally aquatic African clawed frog ( Xenopus laevis ), stream-breeding common river frog ( Amietia delalandii ), and the largely terrestrial raucous toad ( Sclerophrys capensis ). Experiments were conducted at a range of test temperatures (5-35 °C, at 5 °C increments). We discovered that VPD better predicted rates of EWL than T a in two of the three species considered. Moreover, we discovered that T b , whole-animal EWL and whole-animal SMR increased with increasing T a , while T b increased with increasing M b in A. delalandii and S. capensis but not in X. laevis . Whole-animal SMR increased with increasing M b in S. capensis only. We did not discover any significant effect of VPD, M b or sex on whole-animal EWL within species. Lastly, M b did not influence T b , whole-animal SMR and EWL in the principally aquatic X. laevis . These results suggest that M b may not have the same effect on cardinal physiological variables, and that the influence of M b may also depend on the species ecological specialisation. Thus, the generality of M b as an paramount factor should be taken in the context of both physiology and species habitat specialisation.
words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::10: Chronotaraxis constitutes an impairment of the perception of the sequencing of temporality. This alteration of temporal consciousness has been delineated as being characteristically associated with thalamic involvement, specifically within the dorsomedial nucleus. We report the clinical cases of two patients with acute ischaemic strokes situated in said territory, with a clinical presentation predicated upon this symptom and the recognition of which proved essential in the therapeutic approach. In the first and second cases, it is delineated how the perception of temporality was essential for the diagnosis of the ischaemic condition in both patients. Awareness and dissemination of this association may be vital in the management of patients with thalamic disorders. This is attributable to the possibility of influencing and modifying the initial approach, since the recognition of a specific symptom, such as chronotaraxis, can prevent the propagation of thalamic damage, in addition to the long-term sequelae that it engenders, especially those of a cognitive nature. Cronotaraxis como síntoma guía de un infarto talámico medial. Introducción. La cronotaraxis es una afectación de la percepción de la secuencia temporal. Esta alteración de la temporalidad se ha descrito asociada de forma característica a la afectación talámica, concretamente al núcleo dorsomediano. Casos clínicos. Presentamos los casos clínicos de dos pacientes con ictus isquémicos agudos de localización en dicho territorio, con una clínica basada en este síntoma y cuyo reconocimiento resultó esencial en el abordaje terapéutico. Tanto en el primero como en el segundo caso se describe cómo la percepción de la temporalidad fue esencial para el diagnóstico de la patología isquémica de ambos pacientes. Discusión. El conocimiento y la divulgación de esta asociación pueden resultar fundamentales en el manejo de los pacientes con alteraciones talámicas. Esto se debe a la posibilidad que surge de influir y modificar el abordaje inicial, puesto que el reconocimiento de un síntoma específico, como es la cronotaraxis, puede evitar la extensión del daño talámico, y prevenir de esta manera las secuelas, sobre todo cognitivas, que ocasiona a largo plazo.
words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::11: Certain infectious maladies, such as influenza, tuberculosis, and SARS-CoV-2, may be transmitted when virus-laden particles expelled from an infectious individual are inhaled by another individual, which is denominated as the airborne transmission pathway. These virus-laden particles are more concentrated within the expiratory jet of an infectious individual than elsewhere within a well-mixed chamber, but this near-field enhancement in virion exposure has not been adequately quantified. Transmission of airborne viruses depends upon factors that are inherently variable and, in numerous cases, poorly constrained, and quantifying this uncertainty necessitates large ensembles of model simulations that span the variability in input parameters. However, models that are well-suited to simulate the near-field evolution of respiratory particles are also computationally expensive, which limits the exploration of parametric uncertainty. In order to perform numerous simulations that span the wide variability in factors governing airborne transmission, we developed the Quadrature-based model of Respiratory Aerosol and Droplets (QuaRAD). QuaRAD is an efficient framework for simulating the evolution of virus-laden particles after they are expelled from an infectious individual, their deposition to the nasal cavity of a susceptible individual, and the subsequent peril of initial infection. We simulated 10 000 scenarios to quantify the peril of initial infection by a particular virus, SARS-CoV-2. The predicted peril of infection was highly variable among scenarios and, in each scenario, was robustly enhanced near the infectious individual. In more than 50% of scenarios, the physical distancing requisite to avoid near-field enhancements in airborne transmission was beyond the recommended safe distance of two meters (six feet) if the infectious individual is not wearing a mask, though this distance defining the near-field extent was also highly variable among scenarios; the variability in the near-field extent is elucidated predominantly by variability in expiration velocity. Our findings suggest that maintaining at least two meters of distance from an infectious individual greatly diminishes exposure to airborne virions; protections against airborne transmission, such as N95 respirators, should be available when distancing is not feasible or practicable in various circumstances.
words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::12: Exposed fractures constitute contaminated lesions harboring gram-positive and gram-negative organisms; consequently, broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy should be incorporated into the therapeutic regimen. Antimicrobials should be initiated as expeditiously following trauma as feasible, preferably within 3 hours of trauma, after which interval the proportion of infection has been documented to escalate. Interval to surgical debridement within 12 hours of trauma has not been documented to influence the proportion of infection, provided that a patient is being administered antimicrobials. An antimicrobial bead pouch and vacuum-assisted wound closure may facilitate diminishing the jeopardy for secondary and nosocomial contamination and subsequent infection. Exposed fractures are invariably associated with a soft-tissue trauma; consequently, they can be regarded as a soft-tissue trauma that involves a fracture. The administration of the osseous structures and the soft tissues in a patient with an exposed fracture constitutes the principal determinant of fracture restoration and functional rehabilitation of the injured extremity. The formulation of a soft-tissue therapeutic regimen must transpire during the initial wound assessment and the initial stabilization of an exposed fracture and should not be regarded as a secondary or consecutive procedure. A soft-tissue surgeon should be consulted the nocturnal period of the trauma. Selection of fracture stabilization depends on the fractured osseous structure, the location of the fracture (intra-articular, metaphyseal, or diaphyseal), the magnitude of soft-tissue trauma and contamination, and the physiologic condition of the patient. More than one stabilization methodology may be applicable for the administration of a specific trauma; consequently, a surgeon's proficiency and the availability of implants also should be contemplated. Surgeons must comprehend osseous restoration biology to accomplish successful outcomes in the administration of exposed fractures. The cornerstones of these osseous restoration therapeutics include optimization of host biology, recognition of a patient's nutritional condition, appropriate utilization of medications, and eradication of infection. Surgeons should contemplate osseous grafting and/or the utilization of biologics to accomplish osseous union in patients with an acute exposed fracture and in the administration of delayed union or nonunion.
words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::13: PURPOSE: Cyclical configurations of adherence have been documented with numerous health-related endeavours such as dietary regimens and physical exertion. It remains uncertain whether such configurations of adherence exist among consumers of chronic pharmaceuticals. We endeavoured to estimate the percentage of individuals who reinitiate osteoporosis therapeutics after a protracted hiatus in pharmaceutical utilisation and to identify the determinants associated with a return to adherence. METHODS: We investigated 26,636 novel consumers of an osteoporosis pharmaceutical (alendronate, calcitonin, estrogen, raloxifene, or risedronate) who were age 65 or older and had an extended hiatus in refill adherence, defined as a duration of at least 60 days after the completion of one prescription in which no refill for any osteoporosis pharmaceutical was procured. Survival curves were employed to estimate the duration of time until therapeutics are resumed. We estimated the association between individual characteristics and the rate of resuming treatment utilising Cox proportional hazards analysis. We then conducted a case crossover analysis to examine whether certain occurrences transpiring during follow-up triggered a return to refill adherence. RESULTS: Of individuals who discontinued therapeutics for at least 60 days, an estimated 30% reinitiated treatment within 6 months, and 50% reinitiated within 2 years. Among individuals who had at least 6 months of continuous utilisation before their interruption in treatment (n=5863), 42% reinitiated therapeutics within 6 months and 59% within 2 years. Younger individuals, women, and those with a history of a fracture were more inclined to return after a hiatus in pharmaceutical utilisation. Recent hip fractures, discharges from nursing facilities, and bone mineral density testing also predicted a return to treatment. CONCLUSION: Extended lacunae in treatment are commonplace among consumers of osteoporosis pharmaceuticals. Because the efficacy of these pharmaceuticals employed in an interrupted manner is uncertain, adherence interventions should emphasise the necessity for continuous pharmaceutical utilisation. Further investigation is requisite to comprehend why individuals often proceed for months without refilling prescriptions and also whether analogous utilisation configurations exist for other chronic pharmaceuticals.
words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::14: Imbalances within the intestinal microbial consortium (dysbiosis) of vertebrates have been correlated with numerous gastrointestinal and autoimmune maladies. Nevertheless, it remains ambiguous which taxa are correlated with intestinal dysbiosis, and if particular intestinal regions or specific temporal periods during ontogeny are more susceptible. We also comprehend exceedingly little of this phenomenon in non-model organisms, despite an escalating realization of the general significance of intestinal microbiota for salubrity. Here, we examine the alterations that transpire in the microbiome during dysbiosis in different portions of the gastrointestinal tract in a long-lived avian species with elevated juvenile mortality, the ostrich (Struthio camelus). We evaluated the 16S rRNA gene composition of the ileum, cecum, and colon of 68 individuals that perished of suspected enterocolitis during the initial 3 months of existence (diseased individuals), and of 50 healthy individuals that were euthanized as age-matched controls. Several taxa were correlated with mortality (Enterobacteriaceae, Peptostreptococcaceae, Porphyromonadaceae, Clostridium), while others were correlated with salubrity (Lachnospiraceae, Ruminococcaceae, Erysipelotrichaceae, Turicibacter, Roseburia). Environmental specimens showed no evidence of dysbiosis-associated bacteria being present in either the sustenance, aqueous medium, or soil substrate. Instead, the repeated fecal sampling demonstrated that pathobionts were already present shortly after hatching and proliferated in individuals with diminished microbial diversity, resulting in elevated mortality several weeks subsequently. Identifying the origins of pathobionts in neonates and the factors that subsequently influence the establishment of diverse intestinal microbiota may be paramount to understanding dysbiosis and host development. words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::15: We investigate the rationale for the quantum speedup -- quantum algorithms necessitating fewer computation steps than their classical counterparts. We extend their representation to the process of establishing the problem. The initial measurement selects a configuration at random, Bob (the problem setter) unitarily transforms it into the desired one. This representation is accessible to Bob and any external observer, it cannot be accessible to Alice (the problem solver). It would reveal to her the function computed by the black box, which to her should be concealed inside it. We resort to relational quantum mechanics. To Alice, the projection of the quantum state due to the initial measurement is retarded at the termination of her problem solving action. To her, the algorithm input state remains one of complete ignorance of the configuration. By black box computations, she unitarily transmits it into the output state that, for each possible configuration, encodes the corresponding solution, acquired by the final measurement. We demonstrate that we can ascribe to the final measurement the selection of any portion -- say the R-th portion -- of the random outcome of the initial measurement. This projects the input state to Alice on a state of lower entropy where she knows a corresponding portion of the problem configuration. The quantum algorithm is a summation over classical histories in each of which Alice, knowing in advance one of the R-th portions of the configuration, performs the black box computations still required to identify the solution. Given an oracle problem and a value of R, this retrocausality model furnishes the number of black box computations required to solve it. Conversely, given a known quantum algorithm, it yields the value of R that elucidates its speed up. R equals one-half always yields the number of black box computations required by an existing quantum algorithm and the order of magnitude of the number required by optimal one.
words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::16: Cardiac pathology and clinical intervention may both engender an augmented risk for thrombosis events attributable to modified haemodynamic flow within the heart, and thereby an alteration in the mechanical stimuli of haematological cells traversing through the chambers of the heart. Here we analyze the haemodynamic flow within the left ventricle of the heart through a computational model constructed from patient-specific data. The haemodynamic flow within the ventricle is modeled by the Navier-Stokes equations, and the flow through the mitral valve by a parameterized model which represents the projected aperture of the valve. A finite element methodology is utilized to solve the equations, from which a simulation of the velocity and pressure of the haemodynamic flow is constructed. A triple decomposition of the velocity gradient tensor is subsequently utilized to distinguish between rigid body rotational flow, irrotational straining flow, and shear flow. The triple decomposition enables the separation of three fundamentally different flow structures, each generating a distinct type of mechanical stimulus upon the haematological cells within the flow. We compare the results to simulations where a mitral valve clip intervention is modelled, which engenders a significant modification of the ventricular flow. It was ascertained that the shear within the simulation cases treated with clips increased more compared to the untreated case than the rotation and strain did. A decrease in valve aperture area of sixty-four percent in one of the cases engendered a ninety percent increase in rotation and strain, but a one hundred fifty percent increase in shear. The computational analysis suggests a process for patient-specific simulation of clinical interventions within the heart with a detailed analysis of the resulting haemodynamic flow, which could support clinical risk assessment with respect to platelet activation and thrombosis events, thereby providing enhanced prognostic capabilities for therapeutic decision-making processes.
words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::17: The diffuse exceedingly elevated-energy (VHE, > 100 GeV) gamma-ray emanation observed within the central 200 pc of the Milky Way by H.E.S.S. was discovered to follow the dense matter distribution within the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) up to a longitudinal distance of approximately 130 pc to the Galactic Centre (GC), where the flux rapidly diminishes. Recent sensitive H.E.S.S. analysis revealed that the cosmic-ray (CR) density profile drops with the distance to the centre, rendering data compatible with a steady cosmic PeVatron at the GC. Within this paper, we extend this analysis to obtain for the initial time a detailed characterisation of the correlation with matter and to search for supplementary features and individual gamma-ray sources within the inner 200 pc. Taking advantage of 250 hours of H.E.S.S. data and improved analysis techniques we perform a detailed morphology study of the diffuse VHE emanation observed from the GC ridge and reconstruct its total spectrum. We demonstrate that the emanation correlated with dense matter encompasses the full CMZ and that its flux is approximately half the total diffuse emanation flux. We also detect some emanation at higher latitude likely produced by hadronic collisions of CRs within less dense regions of the GC interstellar medium. We detect an supplementary emanation component centred on the GC and extending over approximately 15 pc that is consistent with the existence of a robust CR density gradient and confirms the presence of a CR accelerator at the very centre of our Galaxy. We demonstrate that the spectrum of the full ridge diffuse emanation is compatible with the one previously derived from the central regions, suggesting that a single population of particles permeates the entire CMZ. Finally, we report the discovery of a VHE gamma-ray source near the GC radio arc and argue that it is produced by the pulsar wind nebula candidate G0.13-0.11, representing a significant astronomical finding worthy of further investigation and detailed scrutiny.
words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::18: These international clinical practice recommendations (CPR) for developmental coordination disorder (DCD), initiated by the European Academy of Childhood Disability (EACD), aim to address pivotal questions on the definition, diagnosis, assessment, intervention, and psychosocial aspects of DCD pertinent for clinical practice. Pivotal questions in five domains were considered through literature reviews and formal expert consensus. For recommendations predicated on evidence, literature searches on 'mechanisms', 'assessment', and 'intervention' were updated since the ultimate recommendations in 2012. Novel searches were conducted for 'psychosocial issues' and 'adolescents/adults'. Evidence was rated according to the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine (level of evidence [LOE] 1-4) and transferred into recommendations. For recommendations predicated on formal consensus, two assemblies of an international, multidisciplinary expert panel were conducted with a further five Delphi rounds to develop exemplary clinical practice (GCP) recommendations. Thirty-five recommendations were formulated. Eight were predicated on the evidence from literature reviews (three on 'assessment', five on 'intervention'). Twenty-two were updated from the 2012 recommendations. Novel recommendations relate to diagnosis and assessment (two GCPs) and psychosocial issues (three GCPs). Additionally, one novel recommendation (LOE) reflects active video games as adjuncts to more traditional activity-oriented and participation-oriented interventions, and two novel recommendations (one GCP, one LOE) were formulated for adolescents and adults with DCD. The CPR-DCD is a comprehensive overview of DCD and contemporary understanding predicated on research evidence and expert consensus. It reflects the state of the art for clinicians and scientists of varied disciplines. The international CPR-DCD may serve as a foundation for national guidelines. Updated international clinical practice guidelines on developmental coordination disorder (DCD). Refined and extended recommendations on clinical assessment and intervention for DCD. A critical synopsis of contemporary research on mechanisms of DCD. A critical synopsis of psychosocial issues in DCD, with implications for clinical practice. The inaugural international recommendations to consider adolescents and adults with DCD.
words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::19: Hypertension can precipitate mood disturbances that may deteriorate or ameliorate contingent upon the category of antihypertensive prescribed. Depression is correlated with modifications in basal cerebral asymmetry particularly that of the frontal cortex, which is implicated in sanguineous pressure regulation. We investigated the bilateral activity of numerous neuropeptidases in frontal cortex as a manifestation of the functional status of certain neuropeptides implicated in mood. Utilising arylamide derivatives as substrates, we fluorometrically analysed the activity of these enzymes in the sinistral and dextral frontal cortex of control untreated Wistar-Kyoto (WKY) and spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs) and compared their activities with WKY or SHR treated with the antihypertensive pharmaceuticals captopril (CAP) and propranolol (PRO) or with the hypertensive N (G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester. SBP was likewise measured in all WKY and SHR cohorts. Untreated WKY, WKY treated with CAP or PRO and SHR treated with CAP exhibited normotensive values of SBP. Our findings suggest specific cerebral bilateral patterns of neuropeptidase activities in WKY that transform in SHR. This observation may be correlated to the cognitive disturbances that have been delineated in these animals and that transform under antihypertensive or hypertensive pharmaceutical's treatments.
words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::20: The objective of this investigation is to appraise the merit and efficacy of rapid response teams (RRTs) for disparate triggering occurrences in total hip arthroplasty (THA) patients. Duration of sojourn in RRT for primary and revision THA was 3.4 and 6.2 days, respectively. words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::21: Emergency medical services constitute a crucial component of acute cerebrovascular accident management. words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::22: We aspire to ascertain the redshift of GDS-1408, the most robust z~7 galaxy candidate residing in the Hubble Ultra Profound Field. Currently, the augmented redshift precision procured with this kind of analysis renders ALMA an intriguing option for the redshift confirmation.
words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::23: The persistence of Salmonella spp. as pathogen indicator in composting was investigated. The quantity of Salmonella spp. and temperature for both specimens was established as indicator to ascertain the persistence of Salmonella spp. in direct and non-direct inoculums. The differentiation between direct contact (Sample A) and non-contact of Salmonella spp. with compost material (Sample B) during composting was also disclosed. The results from laboratory scale of composting investigation has been demonstrated that after 8 diurnal periods (which encompassed at least at 66{\deg}C) the numbers of Salmonella spp. in Sample A were beneath the limits in UK compost standard (designated as PAS 100)(BSI, 2005) which necessitated the compost to be devoid of Salmonella spp. Meanwhile, Sample B still furnishes elevated quantity of Salmonella spp. in even after composting for 20 diurnal periods.
words_rare_s.academic_abstracts::24: BACKGROUND: Although ethnicity is correlated with prostatic carcinoma progression in nascent stage malady, once gentlemen possess advanced pathology, it remains ambiguous whether ethnicity continues to prognosticate an unfavorable outcome. The investigators postulated that, in an equivalent-access milieu among patients with castration-resistant prostatic carcinoma (CRPC) and no documented metastases (M0/Mx), ebony gentlemen would obtain imaging examinations at comparable rates as nonebony gentlemen (ie, there would be an equivalent opportunity to detect metastases) but would possess an elevated peril of metastatic pathology. METHODS: In aggregate, 837 gentlemen who were diagnosed with M0/Mx CRPC during 2000 through 2014 from 5 Veterans Affairs hospitals in the SEARCH (Shared Equal Access Regional Cancer Hospital) database were scrutinized. RESULTS: Ebony gentlemen (n = 306) were equivalently as probable as nonebony gentlemen (n = 531) to obtain an initial and subsequent osseous scan after a diagnosis of CRPC. There were no substantial differences in the peril of developing any metastases, osseous metastases, duration to osseous scans, or comprehensive survival between ebony gentlemen and nonebony gentlemen (all P > .2). CONCLUSIONS: The absence of ethnic differences in the development of metastases and scanning practices observed in this investigation suggests that, once gentlemen possess a diagnosis of M0/Mx CRPC, ethnicity may not constitute a prognostic determinant. Endeavors to comprehend prostatic carcinoma ethnic disparities may derive superior benefit by concentrating on the peril of developing prostatic carcinoma and on the outcomes of gentlemen who possess nascent stage pathology.
