More than one fixing method may be suitable for the management of a specific injury; therefore, a surgeon's skill and the availability of materials also should be thought about. Surgeons must understand bone healing science to achieve successful outcomes in the management of open fractures. The basic principles of these bone healing treatments include making the best of host body processes, recognition of a patient's food intake condition, appropriate use of medicines, and removal of infection. Surgeons should think about bone grafting and the use of biological materials to achieve bony joining in patients with an acute open fracture and in the management of delayed joining or failure to join.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::13: PURPOSE: Repeating patterns of following treatment plans have been seen with many health-related activities such as dieting and exercise. It is not known whether such patterns of following treatment plans exist among users of long-term medications. We tried to figure out the percentage of patients who restart bone-weakness therapy after a long break in medication use and to identify the factors connected with a return to following treatment plans. METHODS: We studied 26,636 new users of a bone-weakness medication (alendronate, calcitonin, estrogen, raloxifene, or risedronate) who were age 65 or older and had a long break in refill following, defined as a period of at least 60 days after the completion of one prescription in which no refill for any bone-weakness medication was gotten. Survival curves were used to figure out the length of time until therapy is started again. We figured out the connection between patient features and the rate of starting treatment again using Cox proportional hazards analysis. We then did a case crossover analysis to look at whether certain events happening during follow-up caused a return to refill following. RESULTS: Of patients who stopped therapy for at least 60 days, a figured 30% restarted treatment within 6 months, and 50% restarted within 2 years. Among patients who had at least 6 months of continuous use before their break in treatment (n=5863), 42% restarted therapy within 6 months and 59% within 2 years. Younger patients, women, and those with a history of a broken bone were more likely to return after a break in medication use. Recent hip broken bones, releases from nursing homes, and bone mineral density testing also predicted a return to treatment. CONCLUSION: Long gaps in treatment are common among users of bone-weakness medications. Because the ability of these drugs to work when used in a stopped-and-started way is unknown, following treatment plans actions should stress the need for continuous medication use. Further research is needed to understand why patients often go for months without refilling prescriptions and also whether similar use patterns exist for other long-term medications.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::14: Imbalances in the gut bacterial community (dysbiosis) of animals with backbones have been linked with several stomach and intestinal diseases and immune system diseases. However, it is unclear which groups of bacteria are linked with gut dysbiosis, and if particular gut areas or specific time periods during growth and development are more likely to be affected. We also know very little of this process in animals that are not commonly studied in laboratories, despite an increasing understanding of the general importance of gut bacteria for health and wellbeing. Here, we examine the changes that occur in the bacterial community during dysbiosis in different parts of the stomach and intestinal system in a long-lived bird with high death rates in young birds, the ostrich (Struthio camelus). We measured the 16S rRNA gene makeup of the ileum, cecum, and colon of 68 birds that died of suspected intestinal inflammation during the first 3 months of life (diseased birds), and of 50 healthy birds that were killed as age-matched controls for comparison purposes. We combined these measurements with repeated environmental samples and fecal samples taken over time to identify possible sources of disease-causing bacteria and to discover at which stage of development dysbiosis-linked bacteria appear and become established. Diseased birds had much lower bacterial variety within samples and differed greatly in their bacterial variety between samples from control birds in all three areas of the stomach and intestinal system. The clear relationship between low variety and disease was steady across all ages in the ileum, but decreased with age in the cecum and colon areas. Several groups of bacteria were linked with death (Enterobacteriaceae, Peptostreptococcaceae, Porphyromonadaceae, Clostridium), while others were linked with health (Lachnospiraceae, Ruminococcaceae, Erysipelotrichaceae, Turicibacter, Roseburia). Environmental samples showed no sign of dysbiosis-linked bacteria being present in either the food, water, or soil material. Instead, the repeated fecal samples showed that harmful bacteria were already present shortly after hatching and grew rapidly in birds with low bacterial variety, resulting in high death rates several weeks later.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::15: We look into the reason for the quantum speedup -- quantum algorithms needing fewer calculation steps than their classical counterparts. We extend their representation to the process of setting the problem. The initial measurement selects a setting at random, Bob (the problem setter) changes it in a reversible way into the desired one. This representation is available to Bob and any external observer, it cannot be available to Alice (the problem solver). It would tell her the function calculated by the black box, which to her should be hidden inside it. We use relational quantum mechanics. To Alice, the collapse of the quantum state due to the initial measurement is delayed at the end of her problem solving action. To her, the algorithm input state remains one of complete lack of knowledge of the setting. By black box calculations, she reversibly sends it into the output state that, for each possible setting, holds the matching solution, gained by the final measurement. We show that we can assign to the final measurement the selection of any part -- say the R-th part -- of the random outcome of the initial measurement. This collapses the input state to Alice on a state of lower disorder where she knows a matching part of the problem setting. The quantum algorithm is a sum over classical histories in each of which Alice, knowing in advance one of the R-th parts of the setting, performs the black box calculations still needed to identify the solution. Given an oracle problem and a value of R, this backward causality model provides the number of black box calculations needed to solve it. In the other direction, given a known quantum algorithm, it yields the value of R that explains its speed up. R equals one half always yields the number of black box calculations needed by an existing quantum algorithm and the order of size of the number needed by the best one.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::16: Heart disease and medical treatment may both lead to a higher risk for blood clot events due to changed blood flow in the heart, and thereby a change in the physical forces on blood cells passing through the rooms of the heart. In particular, the degree of platelet activation is influenced by the level and type of physical stresses in the blood flow. Here we study the blood flow in the left lower chamber of the heart through a computer model built from individual patient data. The blood flow in the chamber is represented by the Navier-Stokes equations, and the flow through the mitral valve by a mathematical model which represents the expected opening of the valve. A finite element method is used to solve the equations, from which a computer recreation of the speed and pressure of the blood flow is built. A triple breaking down of the speed change measurement is then used to tell apart rigid body turning flow, flow without rotation that stretches, and sliding flow. The triple breaking down enables the separation of three basically different flow patterns, each creating a distinct type of physical force on the blood cells in the flow. We compare the results to computer recreations where a mitral valve clip treatment is represented, which leads to a large change of the chamber flow. It was found that the sliding in the computer recreation cases treated with clips increased more compared to the untreated case than the turning and stretching did. A decrease in valve opening area of sixty four percent in one of the cases led to a ninety percent increase in turning and stretching, but a one hundred fifty percent increase in sliding. The computer study suggests a process for individual patient computer recreation of medical treatments in the heart with a detailed study of the resulting blood flow, which could support medical risk evaluation with respect to platelet activation and blood clot events.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::17: The spread-out very high-energy (VHE, > 100 GeV) gamma-ray light seen in the central 200 pc of the Milky Way by H.E.S.S. was found to follow the thick matter spread in the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) up to a length-wise distance of about 130 pc to the Galactic Centre (GC), where the flow quickly gets smaller. Recent careful H.E.S.S. study showed that the cosmic-ray (CR) amount drops with the distance to the centre, making data fit with a steady cosmic PeVatron at the GC. In this paper, we extend this study to get for the first time a detailed description of the connection with matter and to search for more features and single gamma-ray sources in the inner 200 pc. Taking use of 250 hours of H.E.S.S. data and improved study methods we do a detailed shape study of the spread-out VHE light seen from the GC ridge and rebuild its total range of colors. We show that the light connected with thick matter covers the full CMZ and that its flow is about half the total spread-out light flow. We also find some light at higher up-down position likely made by collisions of CRs with atoms in less thick areas of the GC space between stars. We find an extra light part centered on the GC and reaching over about 15 pc that fits with the existence of a strong CR amount slope and proves the presence of a CR speed-up machine at the very centre of our Galaxy. We show that the range of colors of the full ridge spread-out light fits with the one before worked out from the central areas, pointing to the idea that a single group of tiny pieces fills the entire CMZ. Finally, we report the discovery of a VHE gamma-ray source near the GC radio arc and argue that it is made by the pulsar wind cloud candidate G0.13-0.11.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::18: These international medical practice advice papers (CPR) for developmental coordination disorder (DCD), started by the European Academy of Childhood Disability (EACD), aim to answer key questions on the meaning, finding, checking, treatment, and mental and social parts of DCD important for medical practice. Key questions in five areas were looked at through reading studies and formal expert agreement. For advice based on facts, reading studies on 'ways it works', 'checking', and 'treatment' were brought up to date since the last advice papers in 2012. New reading studies were done for 'mental and social problems' and 'teenagers and grown-ups'. Facts were scored according to the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine (level of facts [LOE] 1-4) and changed into advice. For advice based on formal agreement, two meetings of an international, many-subject expert group were done with a further five Delphi rounds to create good medical practice (GCP) advice. Thirty-five pieces of advice were made. Eight were based on the facts from reading studies (three on 'checking', five on 'treatment'). Twenty-two were brought up to date from the 2012 advice papers. New pieces of advice relate to finding and checking (two GCPs) and mental and social problems (three GCPs). Also, one new piece of advice (LOE) shows active video games as additions to more usual activity-focused and taking-part-focused treatments, and two new pieces of advice (one GCP, one LOE) were made for teenagers and grown-ups with DCD. The CPR-DCD is a complete view of DCD and current understanding based on research facts and expert agreement. It shows the best current knowledge for doctors and scientists of varied subjects. The international CPR-DCD may be used as a starting point for national guides. Brought up to date international medical practice guides on developmental coordination disorder (DCD). Improved and bigger advice on medical checking and treatment for DCD. A careful short review of current research on ways DCD works. A careful short review of mental and social problems in DCD, with meaning for medical practice. The first international advice to think about teenagers and grown-ups with DCD.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::19: High blood pressure can lead to mood problems that may get worse or get better depending on the type of blood pressure medicine given. Depression is linked with changes in basic brain balance especially that of the front brain area, which is involved in blood pressure control. Also, different blood vessel drugs may change the brain's balance in a way that affects thinking ability. We studied the two-sided activity of several brain chemicals that break down messengers in front brain area as a sign of the working condition of certain brain messengers involved in mood. Using special chemical compounds as starting materials, we measured with light the activity of these chemicals in the left and right front brain area of control untreated Wistar-Kyoto (WKY) and naturally high blood pressure rats (SHRs) and compared their activities with WKY or SHR treated with the blood pressure lowering drugs captopril (CAP) and propranolol (PRO) or with the blood pressure raising chemical compound. Blood pressure was also measured in all WKY and SHR groups. Untreated WKY, WKY treated with CAP or PRO and SHR treated with CAP showed normal values of blood pressure. However, WKY treated with the blood pressure raising chemical as well as untreated SHR and SHR treated with PRO and the blood pressure raising chemical showed high blood pressure values. Changes in the two-sided spread of brain chemicals that break down messengers were depending on the rat type, the chemical studied and the drug used. Normal blood pressure WKY groups (WKY, CAP, PRO) showed connections within the same side mainly in the left side of the brain. In contrast, WKY treated with the blood pressure raising chemical and SHR groups showed connections within the same side mainly in the right side of the brain. Connections between sides were mostly seen in WKY as well as in SHR groups with blood pressure lowering treatments (CAP, PRO). Our results suggest specific brain two-sided patterns of brain chemical activities in WKY that change in SHR. This finding may be related to the thinking problems that have been described in these animals and that change under blood pressure lowering or blood pressure raising drug treatments.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::20: The purpose of this study is to measure the value and usefulness of rapid response teams (RRTs) for different triggering events in total hip replacement (THA) patients. A backward-looking review of all RRT events at a single, advanced care hospital from 2014 to 2016 was performed. Patients included were defined as patients over 18 years old that had first-time or repeat THA. Information gathered included basic facts, main reason for RRT, Charlson Health Problems List (CCI), root cause, whether any changes in treatment occurred, and whether the patient was moved to higher care. In total, 168 RRTs were called on 153 hip replacement patients (average age 65.2 plus or minus 14.1 years; average body weight measure 32.3 plus or minus 4.8, 66% female). Length of stay in RRT for first-time and repeat THA was 3.4 and 6.2 days, in that order. This was much longer than the length of stay for first-time THA patients (2.4 days, P less than .001) and repeat THA patients (4.6 days, P equals .005) that did not need an RRT. There were no deaths. RRTs for low blood pressure or feeling faint (11%) and for fainting (11%) led to much fewer changes in treatment (P less than .01) than fast heartbeat (77%), low oxygen (57%), confused thinking (79%), and other (47%). RRTs for low blood pressure or feeling faint (28%), fainting (15%), and low oxygen (30%) led to much fewer patients being moved to higher care (P less than .001) than fast heartbeat (81%). Low blood pressure or feeling faint was found to be much more often due to lack of fluids (67%) (P less than .001) than other causes. Low oxygen was much more often due to lung collapse (57%) and pain medicine or too much calming medicine (30.4%) (P equals .037). Confused thinking was also much more often caused by pain medicine or too much calming medicine (71%) (P less than .001). In patients having THA, RRTs for low blood pressure or feeling faint and fainting were much less likely to lead to changes in treatment or moving to higher care compared to fast heartbeat. The most common causes were possibly preventable, including lack of fluids and pain medicine use.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::21: Emergency medical services are an important part of quick stroke care. We created a before-hospital stroke scale, the TOYOTA before-hospital stroke scale for tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) intravenous therapy (TOPSPIN) for sorting patients with blocked-vessel stroke and special reasons for intravenous t-PA therapy in December 2006; this scale has 5 items including awareness, irregular heartbeat, language problems, trouble with the upper arms and hands, and trouble with the lower legs and feet. The goal of this study was to look at the results of 10 years of TOPSPIN use and to tell apart blocked-vessel stroke from bleeding stroke in the real world. We signed up patients one after another who were brought to our hospital and checked by Toyota city ambulance services using the TOPSPIN from December 2006 to January 2017. We looked at final diagnosis at the time of hospital release (blocked-vessel stroke, bleeding stroke, or stroke lookalike), positive-guessing value of the stroke, the rate of the vessel-opening therapy, and medical differences among patients with bleeding stroke, blocked-vessel stroke, and stroke lookalikes. A total of 1,482 patients one after another were signed up; 1,134 (76.5%) were patients with stroke (628 blocked-vessel-type, 34 temporary blocked-vessel attack-type, and 472 bleeding-type) and 348 (23.5%) without stroke (80 with seizures, 42 with fainting, 27 with low blood sugar, and 199 other). Among 628 patients with blocked-vessel stroke, 130 (20.7%) received intravenous man-made t-PA treatment, inside-vessel therapy, or both. The presence of irregular heartbeat, older age, lower blood pressure, and lower total TOPSPIN score was more often linked with blocked-vessel stroke than with bleeding stroke. In multiple-variable thinking backward analysis, the presence of irregular heartbeat was separately linked with blocked-vessel stroke (OR 2.33; 95% CI 1.61-3.40). The TOPSPIN is a simple before-hospital stroke scale that includes a check of irregular heartbeat. Finding irregular heartbeat in the before-hospital stage may point to a higher chance of blocked-vessel stroke.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::22: We aim to find out the redshift of GDS-1408, the most solid z~7 galaxy candidate lying in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field. We have used all the VLT observations of GDS-1408 collected by us and two other groups with FORS2 at VLT in the last five years, for a total viewing time of 52hr. The combined observation is the deepest ever obtained of a galaxy in the Reionization time period. We do not detect any release line or continuum over the whole wavelength range, up to 10100A. Based on an accurate set of computer models, we are able to put a tight upper limit of f(Lya)<3x10^(-18) erg/s/cm2 at 3-9 sigma in the looked at wavelength range, matching to a rest-frame equal width EW<9A. Combining this limit with the SED modeling we improve the redshift to be z=6.82+/- 0.1 (1-sigma). The same SED fitting shows that GDS-1408 is fairly extinct (A1600~1) with a dust corrected star formation rate of ~ 20 Msol/yr. The comparison between the un-weakened equal width predicted by the case-B recombination theory and the observed upper limit, provides a limit on the effective Lya escape fraction of f_(esc)^(eff)(Lya)<8%. Even though we cannot rule out a major contribution of the inter/circum galactic medium in reducing the line, a reasonable understanding is that GDS-1408 is moderately evolved and contains enough gas and dust to weaken the Lya release, before it reaches the intergalactic medium. The redshift confirmation of even the best z~7 candidates is very hard to achieve (unless the Lya or unusually strong rest-UV cloud release lines are present) with the current generation of 8-10m class telescopes. We show that both JWST and E-ELT will be needed to make important progress. Currently, the increased redshift accuracy obtained with this kind of study makes ALMA an interesting option for the redshift confirmation.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::23: The survival of Salmonella spp. as disease-causing germ indicator in composting was studied. The adding method was used to give the known amounts of Salmonella spp. involved in composting. The added amount of Salmonella spp. liquid was put directly into the compost material. The direct adding was compared with adding in small bottle method. The Salmonella spp. liquid placed into a small bottle and pushed into the middle of compost material before starting the composting process. The usual method that is used for the counting of Salmonella spp. is step-by-step thinning followed by standard filter paper filtering as recommended in the compost quality standard method PAS 100 and the British Standard (BS EN ISO 6579:2002). This study was designed to look at the relationship of temperature and touching material that may also be involved in disease-causing germ activity specifically to Salmonella spp. The exposure to an average temperature during composting of about 55-60 degrees Celsius was kept for at least 3 days as it was reported well enough kills the very large majority of gut disease-causing germs (Deportes et al., 1995). The amount of Salmonella spp. and temperature for both samples was set as indicator to figure out the survival of Salmonella spp. in direct and non-direct adding. This study gives the numbers of death rate for Salmonella spp. during composting. The difference between direct touching (Sample A) and non-touching of Salmonella spp. with compost material (Sample B) during composting was also shown. The results from laboratory size of composting study has been showed that after 8 days (which included at least at 66 degrees Celsius) the numbers of Salmonella spp. in Sample A were below the limits in UK compost standard (known as PAS 100)(BSI, 2005) which required the compost to be free of Salmonella spp. Meanwhile, Sample B still gives high amount of Salmonella spp. in even after composting for 20 days.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::24: BACKGROUND: Although race is connected with prostate cancer getting worse in early stage disease, once men have advanced disease, it is unclear whether race continues to predict a poor outcome. The authors thought that, in an equal-access setting among patients with treatment-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) and no known spread (M0/Mx), black men would receive imaging tests at similar rates as nonblack men (that is, there would be an equal opportunity to find spread) but would have a higher risk of spreading disease. METHODS: In total, 837 men who were found to have M0/Mx CRPC during 2000 through 2014 from 5 Veterans Affairs hospitals in the SEARCH (Shared Equal Access Regional Cancer Hospital) database were looked at. Information on all imaging tests after CRPC finding were collected, including date, type, and outcome. Multiple-variable Cox models were used to test connections between race and the time to first spread, first bone spread, first bone scan, second bone scan among men who had a negative first bone scan, and overall survival. RESULTS: Black men (n = 306) were equally as likely as nonblack men (n = 531) to receive a first and second bone scan after a finding of CRPC. There were no meaningful differences in the risk of developing any spread, bone spread, time to bone scans, or overall survival between black men and nonblack men (all P > .2). CONCLUSIONS: The lack of racial differences in the development of spread and scanning practices observed in this study suggests that, once men have a finding of M0/Mx CRPC, race may not be a predicting factor. Efforts to understand prostate cancer racial differences may get greater benefit by focusing on the risk of developing prostate cancer and on the outcomes of men who have early stage disease. Cancer 2016;122:3848-3855. © 2016 American Cancer Society.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::25: We present deep Hubble Space Telescope single-star brightness measurements of Leo A in B, V, and I. Our new field of view is moved away from the centrally located field observed by Tolstoy et al. (1998) in order to show the outer region population of this galaxy. We report the finding of metal-poor red horizontal branch stars, which show that Leo A is not a young galaxy. In fact, Leo A is as least as old as metal-poor Galactic Globular Clusters which show red horizontal branches, and are thought to have a minimum age of about 9 Gyr. We discuss the distance to Leo A, and perform a wide-ranging comparison of the data with stellar age models. For a distance measure of 24.5, the data are better than 50% complete down to brightness levels of 2 or more. We can easily identify stars with metal contents between 0.0001 and 0.0004, and ages between about 5 and 10 Gyr, in their after-main-sequence stages, but lack the finding of main-sequence turnoffs which would provide clear proof of ancient (>10 Gyr) stellar groups. Blue horizontal branch stars are above the finding limits, but difficult to tell apart from young stars with similar colors and brightness levels. Computer-made color-brightness pictures show it is possible to fill the blue horizontal branch in the outer region of Leo A. The computer models also suggest around 50% of the total processed mass in our pointing to be connected to an ancient (>10 Gyr) stellar population. We reach the conclusion that Leo A started to form stars at least about 9 Gyr ago. Leo A shows an extremely low oxygen amount, of only 3% of Solar, in its charged gas between stars. The existence of old stars in this very oxygen-poor galaxy shows clearly that a low oxygen amount does not prevent a history of early star formation from occurring in such systems.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::26: One goal of brain-like engineering is to create 'realistic' robot systems that interact with the physical world by using nerve and muscle rules from biology. Important to this is the method to build the backbone circuits responsible for the behavior of muscles with feeling. At its core, muscle feeling is the closed-loop behavior coming from the interactions among groups of muscle spindle sensors, alpha and gamma nerve cells that control muscles, and muscle fibers to enable useful behaviors. We used programmable very-large-scale-circuit (VLSI) hardware to build simple models of firing nerve cells, body muscles, muscle spindle position sensors, alpha nerve cell recruitment, gamma nerve cell control of spindle awareness, and the direct circuits connecting them. This many-level system of groups of firing nerve cells copied the body properties of a pair of opposing muscles with feeling in mammals (each copied by 1024 alpha- and gamma nerve cells that control muscles) acting on a joint via long connecting tissues. This combined system was able to maintain a joint angle, and showed stretch reaction responses even when driving the non-straight body mechanics of an actual dead body finger. What is more, this system allowed us to explore many values and combinations of gamma-static and gamma-dynamic gains when driving a robot finger, some of which copied some human disease conditions. Finally, we looked at the behavioral results of using three different models of muscle force production when length stays the same. We found that the changing responses to rate-coded spike trains produce force increases that can be very affected by connecting tissue stretch, especially at high force output. Our method produced, to our knowledge, the first example of an independent, many-level, brain-like, nerve and muscle system capable of creating realistic reaction behavior in dead body fingers. This research platform allows us to explore the ways behind healthy and disease-related sense and movement function in the physical world by building them from first rules, and it is a step toward brain-like robot systems.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::27: Introduction and Goal: Patients coming in with a urinary tract infection with kidney or tube stones is a medical emergency often reach early health stability but remain in the hospital while waiting for results from urine drug sensitivity tests. We aimed to find health signs that predict drug resistance in patients who had urgent urinary tract relief for blood infection and blocked stones to help early release on trial mouth drugs. Methods: Patients who had emergency urinary tract relief for blood infection and a blocking tube stone from 2014 to 2018 at two teaching medical centers were found. Emergency tube placement was done and patients were treated with wide-range drugs given through the vein. We looked at the connection between health measures at the time of arrival and resistance to at least one drug from urine culture using the Wilcoxon test and Fisher exact test for number-based and group-based measures, one after the other. Multiple variable math analysis was then done using all important measures from single variable analysis. Results: Out of 134 patients, 84 patients (62.7%) had urine cultures resistant to at least one drug. On single variable analysis, patients with resistant cultures were much more likely to have had previous tube viewing procedure, need after-surgery critical care unit-level care, have blood infection, and a longer length of stay. In multiple variable analysis using important measures from single variable analysis, only previous tube viewing procedure was clearly connected with drug resistance with an increased chance of 6.95 ( p = 0.011). Conclusions: In this study, we show that a history of tube viewing procedure is clearly connected with drug resistance in both single variable and multiple variable tests. Our findings point out that patients with history of tube viewing procedure should wait for urine culture results, while those without a history of tube viewing procedure may be released early on trial mouth drugs. However, future studies are needed to decide the usefulness of this sign.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::28: Evidence shows how cannabis can affect the use of other mind-changing substances, including prescription medicines, alcohol, tobacco and illegal drugs, but very little research has looked at the reasons connected with these changes in substance use patterns. This paper looks at the self-reported use of cannabis as a replacement for alcohol among a Canadian medical cannabis patient population. Data was taken from a survey of 2102 people enrolled in the Canadian medical cannabis program. We included 973 (44%) people who reported using alcohol on at least 10 occasions over a 12 month period before starting medical cannabis, and then used backward-looking data on the frequency and amount of alcohol use before and after medical cannabis starting to determine which participant features and other variables were connected with reductions and stopping of alcohol use. Overall, 419 (44%) participants reported decreases in alcohol usage frequency over 30 days, 323 (34%) decreased the number of standard drinks they had per week, and 76 (8%) reported no alcohol use at all in the 30 days before the survey. Being below 55 years of age and reporting higher rates of alcohol use in the earlier period were both connected with greater odds of reducing alcohol use, and a plan to use medical cannabis to reduce alcohol drinking was connected with much greater odds of both reducing and stopping alcohol use altogether. Our findings suggest that medical cannabis starting may be connected with self-reported reductions and stopping of alcohol use among medical cannabis patients. Since alcohol is the most common fun substance in North America, and its use results in large rates of crime, sickness and death, these findings may result in improved health outcomes for medical cannabis patients, as well as overall improvements in public health and safety. The connection between medical cannabis use and reduced alcohol drinking deserves further study and attention from health workers.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::29: The delicate balance between spin-orbit coupling, Coulomb repulsion and crystal electric field interactions observed in Ir-based oxides is usually shown as unusual magnetic behavior. Here we investigate the changes of the exchange coupling between Co and Ir for partial La replacement by Ca in La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$. A great advantage of the use of Ca$^{2+}$ as replacement for La$^{3+}$ is the similarity of its ionic radii. Thus, the observed magnetic changes can more easily be linked to electronic changes. A thorough investigation of the structural, electronic and magnetic properties of the La$_{2-x}$Ca$_{x}$CoIrO$_6$ system was carried out by means of synchrotron x-ray powder diffraction, muon spin rotation and relaxation ($\mu$SR), AC and DC magnetization, XAS, XMCD, Raman spectroscopy, electrical resistivity and dielectric permittivity. Our XAS results show that up to 25% of Ca replacement at the La site results in the appearance of Co$^{3+}$, possibly in high spin state, while the introduction of larger amount of Ca leads to the increase of Ir valence. The competing magnetic interactions resulting from the mixed valences lead to a coexistence of a magnetically ordered and an appearing spin glass (SG) state for the doped samples. Our $\mu$SR results indicate that for La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$ a nearly constant fraction of a paramagnetic (PM) phase continues down to low temperature, possibly related to the presence of a small amount of Ir$^{3+}$ and to the anti-site disorder at Co/Ir sites. For the doped compounds the PM phase freezes below 30 K, but there is still some movement connected with the SG. The dielectric data obtained for the parent compound and the one with 25% of Ca-doping indicate a possible magnetodielectric effect, which is discussed in terms of the electron hopping between the TM ions, the anti-site disorder and the distorted crystal structure.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::30: With the strict requirements introduced by the new sixth-generation (6G) internet-of-things (IoT) use cases, traditional approaches to multiple access control have started to show their limits. A new wave of grant-free (GF) approaches have been therefore proposed as a workable alternative. However, a final solution is still to be reached. In our work, we propose a new semi-GF coordinated random access (RA) method, called partial-information multiple access (PIMA), to reduce packet loss and delay, particularly in the presence of occasional activity. We consider a machine-type communications (MTC) situation, wherein devices need to send data packets in the uplink to a base station (BS). When using PIMA, the BS can get partial information on the immediate traffic conditions and, using compute-over-the-air techniques, guess the number of devices with packets waiting for sending in their queue. Based on this knowledge, the BS gives to each device a single slot for sending. However, since each slot may still be given to multiple users, crashes may occur. Both the total number of given slots and the user assignments are made better, based on the guessed number of active users, to reduce crashes and improve the performance of the multiple access method. To prove the strength of our solution, we compare PIMA to time-division multiple-access (TDMA) and slotted ALOHA (SALOHA) methods, the perfect solutions for straight multiple access (OMA) in the time area in the case of low and high traffic conditions, in that order. We show that PIMA is able not only to adjust to different traffic conditions and to provide fewer packet drops no matter the strength of packet creations, but also able to bring together the good points of both TDMA and SALOHA methods, thus providing performance improvements in terms of packet loss chance and delay.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::31: Background and purpose — Bone rebuilding as a response to bone injury, after-surgery lack of movement, and device-related bone reactions can lead to loss of bone material and increase the risk of bone break around the replacement and non-infected loosening. This study looks at the changing bone rebuilding of the upper shin bone after uncemented total knee replacement surgery. Patients and methods — We did a 2-year follow up of 53 patients (average age 62, range 38 to 70 years, 27 of whom were men, who received an uncemented total knee replacement in a randomized controlled trial with bone mineral density as secondary goal. Patients were randomized to 2 groups of either single-piece (A) or multiple-piece (B) plastic liner design. The knee replacements were done using the uncemented Zimmer Nexgen trabecular metal. Measurements of bone mineral density were done after surgery and after 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. Bone mineral density was measured in 3 areas of interest. Results and understanding — In group A, numbers showed important changes in bone mineral density after 24 months in both the inner and outer areas of interest. Bone mineral density went down on the inner side by 15% (p = 0.004) and on the outer side by 13% (p = 0.01). In group B the bone mineral density changes were small and after 24 months returned to the before-surgery values. The differences in bone mineral density change between groups were numbers-wise important in both the inner (p = 0.03) and outer (p = 0.02) areas of interest. In the lower area of interest we found no important change in bone mineral density in either group. A clearly different bone rebuilding pattern of the upper shin bone was seen in the 2 groups with a higher amount of bone loss in the knees that received the single-piece plastic liner design, showing that the bendable single-piece replacement design, earlier shown to improve attachment, does not reduce the bone loss of the upper shin bone.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::32: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) are models of brain-based thinking that have proven highly effective. Still, ANNs lack a natural sense of time, and brain units in ANNs exchange number values in a frame-based manner, a thinking-wise and energy-wise wasteful form of communication. This stands in sharp difference with biological brain cells that communicate rarely and well using simple on-off spikes. While artificial Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) can be built by replacing the units of an ANN with spiking brain cells, the current performance is far from that of deep ANNs on hard tests and these SNNs use much higher firing rates compared to their biological matches, limiting their usefulness. Here we show how spiking brain cells that use an efficient form of brain coding can be used to build SNNs that match high-performance ANNs and go beyond the best results in SNNs on important tests, while needing much lower average firing rates. For this, we use spike-time coding based on the firing rate limiting change seen in biological spiking brain cells. This change can be captured in changing spiking brain cell models, for which we work out the working transfer function. Brain units in ANNs trained with this transfer function can be replaced directly with changing spiking brain cells, and the resulting Changing SNNs (AdSNNs) can carry out thinking in deep brain networks using up to ten times fewer spikes compared to earlier SNNs. Changing spike-time coding also allows for the moving control of brain coding exactness: we show how a simple model of alertness in AdSNNs further cuts in half the average needed firing rate and this idea naturally reaches to other forms of focus. AdSNNs thus hold promise as a new and efficient model for brain thinking that naturally fits to time-based continuous and non-synchronized uses.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::33: Background. LQ Hya is one of the most often studied young sun-like stars. Recently, it has been observed to show interesting behaviour by looking at long-term brightness measurements: during 2003--2009, a clear spot pattern moving in the spinning frame has been reported by different authors, but since that time the star has entered a messy state where clear patterns seem to have disappeared and sudden phase jumps of the brightness lows occur without pattern over time. Goals. LQ Hya is one of the stars included in the SOFIN/FIES long-term watching campaign covering more than 25 years. Here we publish new temperature maps for the star during 2006--2017, covering the messy state of the star. Methods. We use a Doppler imaging method to get surface temperature maps from high-detail light patterns. Results. From the average temperatures of the Doppler maps we see a weak but steady increase in the surface temperature of the star. This is in line with the at the same time increasing brightness level. During nearly all watching seasons we see a high-latitude spot pattern which is clearly not matching around the axis. The phase behaviour of this pattern is very messy but matches reasonably well with the brightness measurements. Spots near the middle are also often seen, but many of them we understand to be false images due to the poor to moderate phase coverage. Conclusions. Even during the messy phase of the star, the spot layout has remained very similar to the higher activity times with more clear and long-lasting spot patterns: we see high-latitude and middle spot activity, the mid latitude range still being most often empty of spots. We understand the random jumps and drifts in phase of the brightness lows to be caused by changes in the high-latitude spot pattern rather than the spots near the middle of the star.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::34: Context: Hydrogen-adding reactions are expected to be among the most important surface reactions on space ices. However, solid state space chemistry laboratory data on reactions of hydrogen atoms with common space ice parts are mostly missing. Aims: The goal of our laboratory work is to find out whether and how carbon dioxide (CO2), formic acid (HCOOH) and acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) react with hydrogen atoms in the solid state at low temperatures and to get reaction speeds and production amounts. Methods: Pure CO2, HCOOH and CH3CHO space ice copies are hit by hydrogen atoms in an extremely high empty space experiment. The ices are watched by reflection taking in light measurement and the reaction products are found in the gas state through temperature controlled removal to find out the destruction and formation amounts as well as the matching reaction speeds. Results: Within the ability to detect of our equipment we say that hydrogen atom hitting of pure CO2 and HCOOH ice does not give detectable reaction products. The upper limits on the reaction speeds are less or equal to seven times ten to the power of minus seventeen centimeters squared per second which make it unlikely that these materials play a major role in the formation of more complicated carbon-based molecules in space ices because of reactions with hydrogen atoms. In contrast, CH3CHO does react with hydrogen atoms. At most twenty percent is changed by adding hydrogen to ethanol (C2H5OH) and a second reaction path leads to the breaking up of the carbon-carbon bond to form solid state methane or CH4 (around twenty percent) as well as H2CO and CH3OH (fifteen to fifty percent). The methane production amount is expected to be equal to the added amount of H2CO and CH3OH and therefore methane most likely escapes as gas partly after formation because of the high heat release of the reaction. The reaction speeds for CH3CHO destruction depend on ice temperature and not on ice thickness.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::35: The method of funnel control was brought in during the early 2000s, and it has grown since then in many ways reaching a level of mathematical development balanced by real-world uses. Its main idea is the reaching of set temporary and long-term behaviour for continuous-time controlled changing processes including straight-line and curved systems described by functional differential equations, differential-algebraic systems, and partial differential equations. Looked at are groups of systems given by building properties - such as relative degree and stable internal workings - of the systems only, the exact systems' facts are in general unknown; the latter shows the property that in general any model of a changing process is not exact. Set ahead of time are: a funnel shaped through the choice of a smooth function and freely chosen by the person designing it, a fairly large group of smooth guide signals, and a system group meeting certain building properties. The goal is to design, based on the building guesses and the input and output information only, a single 'simple' control way of working -- called the funnel controller -- so that its use to any system of the given group and to any guide signal results in the ability to achieve the funnel control goal: that is answers of the closed-loop system do not show blow-up in limited time, all changing amounts are limited, and -- most importantly -- the movement of the error between the system's output and the guide signal stays within the set-ahead-of-time funnel. In the Introduction, we describe the beginning of funnel control. After that, we look at different system groups that work with funnel control. Funnel control is shown for systems with any relative degree and systems described by partial differential equations. Finally, we discuss input limits and uses.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::36: With the growing variety of Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks, it is becoming extremely difficult to design a fully protected network. For example, Stealthy Link Flooding Attack (SLFA) is a type of DDoS attacks that tries to block access to a target area by flooding a small set of links, and it is shown that it can get past traditional DDoS defense methods. One possible solution to deal with such SLFAs is to use Moving Target Defense (MTD) techniques in which network settings are constantly changed to confuse or trick attackers, thus making it very expensive to launch a successful attack. However, since MTD comes with some extra cost to the network, to find the best plan, meaning when and how much to use it, has been a major problem. The plan is greatly affected by the attacker's behavior that is often hard to predict. In this work, we address the problem of getting the best MTD plan that works well against SLFAs while causing a smallest possible extra cost. We design the problem as a signaling game considering the network defender and the attacker as players. A belief function is built throughout the interaction of the attacker and the defender during this SLFA campaign, which is used to pick the best response or action for each player. We look at the game model and work out a defense method based on the balance points of the game. We test the technique on a Mininet-based network environment where an attacker is performing SLFAs and a defender uses MTD based on balance points of the game. The results show that our signaling game-based changing defense method can provide a similar level of protection against SLFAs like the wide-reaching MTD solution, however, causing a much smaller extra cost to the network operations and performance overall.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::37: Multi-fidelity (MF) methods are becoming more popular for improving replacement modeling and design improvement by using data from different low-fidelity (LF) models. While most existing MF methods assume a fixed dataset, flexible sampling methods that actively distribute resources among fidelity models can achieve higher efficiency in the searching and using the design space. However, most existing MF methods depend on the step-by-step assumption of fidelity levels or fail to capture the relationship between multiple fidelity levels and use it to measure the value of the future samples and guide the flexible sampling. To address this problem, we propose a framework based on a hidden representation for different fidelity models and the related before-after analysis to clearly use their relationship for flexible sampling. In this framework, each added sampling round includes two steps: We first identify the location of interest with the greatest possible improvement using the high-fidelity (HF) model, then we search for the next sample across all fidelity levels that increase the improvement per unit cost at the location identified in the first step. This is made possible by a single Latent Variable Gaussian Process (LVGP) model that maps different fidelity models into an understandable hidden space to capture their relationships without assuming step-by-step fidelity levels. The LVGP enables us to judge how LF sampling choices will affect HF response with before-after analysis and determine the next sample with the best benefit-to-cost ratio. Through test cases, we show that the proposed method performs better than the comparison methods in both MF global fitting (GF) and Bayesian Optimization (BO) problems in speed of improvement and strength. Moreover, the method offers the ability to switch between GF and BO by simply changing the selection function. The approach demonstrates clear advantages in practical uses across different engineering fields.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::38: Cell-damaging injuries of the corpus callosum are secondary injuries caused by large increases in cytokine levels in the brain and are connected with subarachnoid bleeding (SAH). However, their medical importance in SAH patients remains unclear. We looked back at SAH patients who were treated in our hospital and studied between-group differences in the backgrounds, medical findings, and results between SAH patients who developed cell-damaging injuries of the corpus callosum and those who did not. We further compared patients who achieved good results with those who had poor results. Multiple variable analysis was used to identify risk factors for poor medical results. We studied 159 SAH patients; 17 patients (10.7%) had cell-damaging injuries of the corpus callosum. Patients with cell-damaging injuries of the corpus callosum were more likely to be in a serious condition (World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies grading IV-V: odds ratio [OR], 4.53; 95% confidence interval [95% CI]: 1.60-12.84; p = 0.0042) and have an intraventricular (OR, 5.98; 95% CI: 1.32-27.13; p = 0.0054) or an intraparenchymal blood clot (OR, 3.62; 95% CI: 1.25-10.45; p = 0.023). Patients with cell-damaging injuries of the corpus callosum had a greater tendency of a poor result 3 months after start (modified Rankin Scale score 0-2: OR, 0.22; 95% CI: 0.07-0.66; p = 0.0043). Multiple variable analysis showed that cell-damaging injuries of the corpus callosum increased the risk of a poor result (OR, 4.39; 95% CI: 1.06-18.1; p = 0.037). The development of cell-damaging injuries of the corpus callosum may be related to the extent of blood clots in SAH patients. Although they are usually reversible injuries, the development of cell-damaging injuries of the corpus callosum may be a sign of poor results in SAH patients.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::39: Information on proper methods for calming Nordestino donkeys is limited. To measure the calming and heart-breathing effects of low amounts of into-vein (i.v.) xylazine with and without acepromazine in 'Nordestino' donkeys. Seven healthy female Nordestino donkeys (150 ± 18 kg) were included in this hidden, mixed-order, switching experiment. Four treatments were given, made up of two i.v. injections, at starting point (T0, 1st injection) and 15 min later (T15, 2nd injection). Treatments included acepromazine 0.05 mg/kg body weight + salt water (AS), salt water + xylazine 0.5 mg/kg body weight (SX0.5), acepromazine + xylazine 0.25 mg/kg body weight (AX0.25) or acepromazine + xylazine 0.5 mg/kg body weight (AX0.5). Calming and heart-breathing measurements were checked before T0 and 15, 20, 30, 45, 60, 75 and 90 min after treatment. Amount [height of head above ground (HHAG)] and quality of calming [loss of balance, responses to outside actions and visual comparison scale (VAS) scoring] and breathing rate were checked by the main researcher on site, and heart rate was measured by a helper researcher. Three skilled checkers looked at videos for loss of balance and responses to outside actions. Normal data were studied by repeated measures ANOVA, and non-normal by Kruskal-Wallis (P<0.05). HHAG was lower than starting point for 15 min after xylazine use in AX0.25 and for 30 min in SX0.5 and AX0.5 groups. All treatments with xylazine increased VAS and loss of balance scores on site for 15 min after xylazine use, with no differences between groups. Loss of balance scores on site were higher in SX0.5 and AX0.5 groups than AS for 15 and 30 min after xylazine use, in that order. Lack of a negative control group (salt water-salt water). Acepromazine added to xylazine at 0.25 mg/kg body weight produced shorter and weaker calming than xylazine at 0.5 mg/kg body weight.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::40: ALMA-IMF took pictures of 15 huge star-forming groups down to a detail level of 2 kau sizes, finding about 1000 star-forming centers. The weight and brightness of these centers, which are basic physical features, are hard to figure out, a problem made much worse at the distances more than 2 kpc of ALMA-IMF star-forming groups. We put together new information sets and brightness movement modeling to describe these centers. We calculated their weight-averaged temperature and the weights these calculations suggest. For one sixth of the group, we measured the total brightness values, using separation corrections when needed. We used energy spread analysis obtained with the PPMAP mathematical method, which tries to keep the best angle detail of the starting information. We stretched out the brightness and dust temperature pictures provided by PPMAP at 2.5" detail to calculate those of individual centers, which were found at higher angle detail. To do this, we used rough brightness movement relationships between the brightness of a young star and the temperature of its surrounding layer and between the outside heating of early star centers and their temperatures. For the first time, we provide information-based calculations of dust temperatures for 883 centers found with ALMA-IMF: 17-31 K and 28-79 K (5th and 95th percentage points, up to 127 K) for the 617 early star and 266 young star centers, in that order. We also measured young star brightness values covering 20-80 000 sun brightness units. For hot centers, we calculated regularly lower temperatures than studies based on complicated carbon-based molecules. We created a weight-brightness development picture, for the first time at the center space detail and for a large group of heavy young star centers. The ALMA-IMF information supports a situation in which young stars gather their weight from a larger weight storage than their home centers.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::41: The goal of this study was to look at the role of microRNA (miR)-27a-3p in osteoarthritis (OA). Reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction and western blotting were done to find out the expression of miR-27a-3p and aggrecanase-2 (ADAMTS5) in cartilage tissues from patients with OA and healthy controls, and also in interleukin (IL)-1beta-treated primary human chondrocytes. Primary human chondrocytes were transfected with miR-27a-3p. A luciferase reporter test was used to check the direct contact between miR-27a-3p and its possible binding site in the 3'-untranslated region ADAMTS5 mRNA. Also, the effects of IL-1beta-caused activation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and nuclear factor (NF)-kappaB on miR-27a-3p were checked using specific blockers. The results showed that the level of miR-27a-3p was lower in OA cartilage tissues compared with those of normal controls. Also, lowered miR-27a-3p and increased ADAMTS5 expression was seen in a time- and dose-dependent way in chondrocytes treated with IL-1beta. Also, too much expression of miR-27a-3p held back the expression of ADAMTS5 in human chondrocytes caused by IL-1beta. miR-27a-3p too much expression also lowered the luciferase activity of the wild-type ADAMTS5 reporter plasmid. Change of the miR-27a-3p binding site in the 3'-untranslated region of ADAMTS5 mRNA stopped the miR-27a-3p-caused holding back of reporter activity. Also, the use of specific blockers showed that IL-1beta may control miR-27a-3p expression through NF-kappaB and MAPK signaling pathways in chondrocytes. This study ended by saying that miR-27a-3p was lowered in human OA and was held back by IL-1beta, and works as an important controller of ADAMTS5 in OA chondrocytes. Also, IL-1beta-caused holding back of miR-27a-3p activity may happen through the MAPK and NF-kappaB pathways. This study may give a new way for medical treatment of OA caused by increase of miR-27a-3p.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::42: Space weathering is a process that changes the surface of airless planetary bodies. Main space weathering causes are solar wind hitting the surface and tiny rock pieces hitting the surface. These processes change how planets reflect light and often change their makeup features. In this work we focused on copying and comparing the light changes caused by solar wind hitting the surface and by tiny rock pieces hitting the surface to gain a better understanding of these separate space weathering processes. We used olivine and pyroxene pressed pieces as stand-ins for planetary materials. To copy solar wind hitting the surface we used hydrogen, helium, and argon ions with energies from 5 to 40 keV and amounts of up to $10^{18}$ particles/cm$^2$. To copy tiny rock pieces hitting the surface we used single very short laser bursts. We looked at the matching changes of different light measurements, which we found by applying the Modified Gaussian Model, and we also did principal component analysis. The original rock type of the surface affects the light changes more than the weathering cause, as seen from the different changes of the light slope of olivine and pyroxene upon hitting with radiation. The light slope changes seen in olivine are the same as observations of A-type asteroids, while the small to no slope changes observed in pyroxene are the same as asteroid (4) Vesta. We also observed some differences in the light effects created by the two weathering causes. Ions copying solar wind have a smaller effect on longer wavelengths of the light than laser hitting copying tiny rock piece impacts. This is most likely due to the different depths that ions and laser bursts reach into the material. Our results suggest that in some cases it might be possible to tell apart the effects of the two causes on a weathered surface.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::43: HEALPix by Gorski et. al. (2005) is the accepted standard for Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data storage and study, and is widely used in current and coming CMB experiments. Almost all the datasets in Legacy Archive for Microwave Background Data Analysis (LAMBDA) use HEALPix as a format of choice. Showing the data in pictures plays an important role in research, and several toolsets were developed to do that with HEALPix maps, most notably original Fortran tools and Python connection with healpy. With the current state of GPU performance, it is now possible to show very large maps in real time on a laptop or a tablet. HEALPix Viewer described here is developed for macOS, and takes full advantage of GPU speed-up to handle very large datasets in real time. It builds naturally on Intel and Arm64 designs, and uses Metal framework for high-performance GPU calculations. The goal of this project is to reduce the effort needed for hands-on data exploration, as well as time overhead for producing publication-quality maps. Drag and drop connection with Keynote and Powerpoint makes creating presentations easy. The main codebase is written in Swift, a modern and effective built language, with high-performance computing parts given entirely to GPU, and a few inserts in C connecting to cfitsio library for input and output operations. Picture-based user interface is written in SwiftUI, a new clear UI framework based on Swift. Most common round ball projections and colormaps are supported out of the box, and the available source code makes it easy to change the application and to add new features if wanted. Overall performance improves on the current Python software stack by a factor of 3-180x depending on the task at hand.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::44: To compare the neck of the womb shear wave picture-making (SWE) by using through-the-vagina sound waves (TVS) between twin and single baby pregnant women. This was a forward-looking group study involving the twin and single baby pregnant women who came to the before-birth care at Ramathibodi Hospital, Bangkok, Thailand. The people in the study who met the requirements for joining were measured repeatedly for the shear wave speed (SWS) by using TVS at early, middle, and third three-month period. The changes in SWS with moving forward pregnancy age between twin and single baby pregnancies were looked at. The pregnancy age at birth and natural early birth rate were also studied. A total of 36 twin pregnancies and 38 single baby pregnancies were studied. No important difference in starting features, except the age of people in the study (twin pregnancies 33.1±4.6 years, single baby pregnancies 29.9±5.4 years, p-value = 0.006) was seen. The neck of the womb SWS went down with moving forward pregnancy age in both twin and single baby pregnancy, but there was a number-wise important difference of neck of the womb SWS at the lower point in middle three-month period (twin pregnancies 2.27±0.4, single baby pregnancies 2.71±0.6 m/s, p-value = 0.001). However, no important difference in neck of the womb SWS at the upper point and the lower point in the early and third three-month period was shown. Even though the pregnancy age at birth between both groups showed an important difference (twin pregnancies 35.9±2.8, single baby pregnancies 37.6±2.9 wk., p-value = 0.008) but the natural early birth rate did not differ in an important way (twin pregnancies 22.2%, single baby pregnancies 15.8%, p-value = 0.483). The middle three-month period neck of the womb SWS measurement at the lower point finds the difference in neck of the womb softness between twin pregnancies and single baby pregnancies. The neck of the womb SWS might be an added choice for watching the change in neck of the womb softness in twin pregnancies.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::45: Chromosome number is a key feature of the higher-order organization of the genome, and changes in chromosome number play a basic role in evolution. Dysploid gains and losses in chromosome number, as well as polyploidization events, may drive reproductive isolation and lineage diversification. The recent development of chance-based models of chromosome number evolution in the groundbreaking work by Mayrose et al. (2010, ChromEvol) have enabled the inference of ancestral chromosome numbers over molecular phylogenies and generated new interest in studying the role of chromosome changes in evolution. However, the ChromEvol approach assumes all changes occur anagenetically, which means along branches, and does not model events that are specifically cladogenetic. Cladogenetic changes may be expected if chromosome changes result in reproductive isolation. Here we present a new class of models of chromosome number evolution, which we call ChromoSSE, that put together both anagenetic and cladogenetic change. The ChromoSSE models allow us to determine the mode of chromosome number evolution; is chromosome evolution occurring mainly within lineages, mainly at lineage splitting, or in clade-specific combinations of both? Furthermore, we can estimate the location and timing of possible chromosome speciation events over the phylogeny. We put ChromoSSE into use in a Bayesian statistical framework, specifically in the software RevBayes, to accommodate uncertainty in parameter estimates while using the full power of likelihood based methods. We tested ChromoSSE's accuracy with simulations and re-examined chromosomal evolution in Aristolochia, Carex section Spirostachyae, Helianthus, Mimulus sensu lato (s.l.), and Primula section Aleuritia, finding evidence for clade-specific combinations of anagenetic and cladogenetic dysploid and polyploid modes of chromosome evolution. [Anagenetic; Bayes factors; chromosome evolution; chromosome speciation; chromoSSE; cladogenetic; dysploidy; phylogenetic models; polyploidy; reversible-jump Markov chain Monte Carlo; whole genome duplication.].
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::46: We present results of our time changes studies of Mg II and Al III taking-in lines in a group of 22 Low Ionization Broad Absorption Line QSOs (LoBAL QSOs) at 0.2 <= zem <= 2.1 using the 2m telescope at IUCAA Girawali Observatory over a time-length of 10 days to 7.69 years in the QSO's rest frame. Observations are looked at together with brightness measurement light curves from Catalina Real-Time Transient Survey. Long time-length (i.e >= 1 year) taking-in line changes are seen in 8 cases (36% systems) while only 4 of them (i.e 18% systems) show changes over short time-lengths (i.e < 1 year). We notice a pattern of highly changing LoBAL QSOs to have high throwing-out speed, low equal width and low redshift. The finding rate of changes in LoBAL QSOs showing Fe fine-structure lines (FeLoBAL QSOs) is less than that seen in non-Fe LoBAL QSOs. Taking-in line changes are more often found in QSOs having background controlled by Fe release lines compared to rest of the QSOs. Proving these patterns with a bigger group will give important hints for understanding the physical difference between different BAL QSO sub-groups. We compare the taking-in line changes with different measures taken from background light curves and find no clear connection between background brightness and taking-in line changes. However, sources with large taking-in line changes also show large changes in their light curves. We also see appearance or disappearance of taking-in parts in 2 cases and clear signs for shape changes in 4 cases. The seen changes can be best explained by a mix of process driven by background changes and clouds moving across the line of sight.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::47: The H{\alpha} cloud bright line is a perfect way to track recent star formation in galaxies. With the arrival of JWST, this line has recently become able to be seen at z>3 for the first time. We present a list of 1013 H{\alpha} light sources at 3.7<z<6.7 in the GOODS fields found from a blind search in JWST NIRCam/grism data. We make use of the FRESCO survey's 124 arcmin^2 of views in GOODS-North and GOODS-South with the F444W filter, checking H{\alpha} at 4.9<z<6.7; and the CONGRESS survey's 62 arcmin^2 in GOODS-North with F356W, checking H{\alpha} at 3.8<z<5.1. We find an area with too many objects with 97 sources at z~4.4 in GOODS-N and confirm earlier reported areas with too many objects at z~5.2 in GOODS-N and at z~5.4 and z~5.9 in GOODS-S. We figure out the seen H{\alpha} brightness functions (LFs) in three groups centered at z~4.45, 5.30, and 6.15, which are the first such measurements at z>3 found based purely on light-pattern data, strongly tracking galaxy star formation rates (SFRs) beyond the peak of the space-wide star formation history. We compare our results with thought-out predictions from three different computer models and find good agreement at z~4-6. The UV LFs of this light-pattern-confirmed sample are in good agreement with pre-JWST measurements found with brightness-selected objects. Finally, we figure out SFR functions and add these to figure out the change of the space-wide star-formation rate amounts across z~4-6, finding values in good agreement with recent UV guesses from Lyman-break galaxies, which suggest a continuous decrease in SFR amount by a factor of 3x over z~4 to z~6. Our work shows the power of NIRCam grism views to quickly provide new tests for early galaxy formation models based on bright line numbers.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::48: Many studies have shown that harmful stress on cells is closely connected with the start and growth of depression. Xiaoyao Pills (XYW) are included in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia and are often used for treating worry and depression by calming the liver, making the spleen stronger, and feeding the blood. However, the effects of XYW against depression have not yet been fully looked into. The goal of our study was to look into the effects of XYW against depression and the basic molecular process in the smell bulb removed (OB) rat model of depression using the open field test (OFT), sugar liking test (SPT), splash test (ST), and newness held back feeding test (NSFT). Results showed that XYW (0.93 and 1.86 g·kg -1 ) greatly reduced behaviors like depression in rats, which was shown by increased sugar liking in the SPT, longer cleaning time in the ST, reduced flat movement in the OFT, and shorter feeding delay in the NSFT. In addition, XYW treatment strongly reversed the reduced action of a protective substance and the lowered level of another protective substance, while also lowering levels of a harmful breakdown product, a swelling messenger (a reactive gas), and swelling-causing cell signals (two related proteins) in the blood and outer brain of OB rats. Looking at the process, XYW caused clear increases of messenger molecule and protein levels of multiple protective proteins and pathways, and lowering of harmful molecules in the outer brain and memory area through the turning on of several connected pathways. These findings suggest that XYW create effects against depression in OB rats with symptoms like depression, and these effects are brought about by the reduction of harmful cell stress and the improvement of brain-protecting effects through the turning on of the connected signaling pathways.
words_common_s.academic_abstracts::49: We report the discovery of 16 separate M-dwarf blocking binaries with J<16 mag and provide a detailed description of three of them, using very accurate infrared light curves from the WFCAM Transit Survey (WTS). Such systems provide the most accurate and model-free method for measuring the basic features of these poorly understood yet common stars, which currently lack enough observations to accurately adjust star development models. We fully solve for the masses and sizes of three of the systems, finding orbital periods in the range 1.5<P<4.9 days, with masses covering 0.35-0.50 Msun and sizes between 0.38-0.50 Rsun, with doubts of around 3.5-6.4% in mass and around 2.7-5.5% in size. Close-companions in short-period binaries are expected to be tidally-locked into fast turning speeds, resulting in high levels of magnetic activity. This is predicted to blow up their sizes by blocking movement flow and increasing star spot coverage. The sizes of the WTS systems are blown up above model predictions by around 3-12%, in agreement with the observed trend, despite an expected lower regular contribution from star spots signals at infrared wavelengths. We searched for connection between the orbital period and size increase by combining our results with all existing M-dwarf size measurements of similar accuracy, but we found no statistically important evidence for a decrease in size increase for longer period, less active systems. Size increase continues to exist in non-matched systems showing that the problem remains even for very low activity M-dwarfs. Solving this issue is vital not only for understanding the most common stars in the Universe, but also for describing their planetary companions, which hold the best chances for finding Earth-like planets in the traditional livable zone.

The square corner on this wooden spoon makes it easy to scrape the bottom of your pot or frying pan, and not miss spots, when you're stirring something that burns easily. I really love it for making caramel ice cream, because the caramel sugar forms a lump and sticks to the bottom of the pan after I add cool cream. With this "flat-edged" spoon, it's easy to mix the lump and cream into a smooth caramel sauce without burning any of the caramel sugar.

This very light spoon is made of beechwood, and is beautifully shaped and balanced. It's very comfortable to pick up, and to hold when you're stirring a sauce or gravy. The handle has a slight curve, unlike the usual wooden spoon with round, completely straight handle that you're likely to find at the food store (for example, [[ASIN:B0019R9QKI HIC Harold Import Beechwood Spoon 12-Inch]]).

Wooden spoons are not dishwasher safe: they will quickly dry out and split if washed in a dishwasher. Even if they are hand washed, they should be oiled with mineral oil from time to time, to stop splitting and make their useful life longer. One fairly priced mineral oil sold for this purpose is [[ASIN:B00280MY7M Snow River 7V03401 32-Ounce Wood Oil]]. This helps keep the wood in good condition for many years of cooking use.

I love this game but it's not a game to easily pick up and play with just anyone. My current regular playmate, despite having played several games, has me hold their hand through almost every single step for their own play and asks for my help to the point that I can't focus on my own play until they're done with theirs. When I ask for working together for just a small portion of my play, whether due to being a poor team player or not having the confidence with the rules, it's not given back and then I'm somehow a bother to them for "taking forever" because I'm finally able to set up my own play. The new cable ends are very tight fitting which I'm happy with, the old one was getting a little too easy to pop loose but it got a LOT of use so I really can't complain seeing as how much longer the six foot cable lasted. If this ten footer lasts that long I'll be quite happy with the purchase and will tell others about it.

Update 01/23/2018 - I bought this 10' cable based on the long life of the company's 6' cable of the same style. My 6' cable lasted nearly a year of many daily times plugging and unplugging my tablet. With no clear change in use or handling the 10' cable is now coming apart from the tablet at the lightest touch after less than three months. Very let down by this.

Update: 02/08/2018 - I contacted Anker about their promise to fix or replace this cable.
