words_common_s.amazon_reviews::17:
When I ordered two of these TEMPUR-PEDIC COMFORTPILLOW TRAVEL PILLOWS (One Size, Beige), one pillow turned out to be overstuffed (very fat, heavy, and rather hard), and the other turned out to be perfect (reasonably flat and bendable). Both are excellent small pillows, though the fat one is more right for a lower back pillow or "propping-up" pillow than a travel pillow.

Why are the two pillows so different? It's because they are NOT solid-core pillows like my wonderful [[ASIN:B07CMK551C full-size Tempur-Pedic Symphony Pillow]], which is a "100% shaped memory foam pad". Instead, the travel pillows are made of "70% torn-up memory foam" and "30% memory foam pad".

My fat pillow clearly received more torn-up foam during making than the more bendable pillow. Because torn-up foam tends to move around in pillows, I try to stay away from pillows with torn-up foam fill. In fact, I wouldn't have bought the two travel pillows had I known that they weren't solid-core.

However, I like my two travel pillows pretty well--so far the fill hasn't moved around. They are good quality pillows made with Tempur-Pedic memory foam that shapes to one's body. They work for me because the small size is very good for holding up an arm or leg in bed, or for giving spot support for back, neck, or shoulders in a chair.
words_common_s.amazon_reviews::18:
My workmate and I laughed when we found a link to this banana slicer on Amazon and asked each other "How hard can be it to slice a banana?" Well, about one week later I came across this exact slicer in a kitchen tool store and knew I had to order it. Now I'm not laughing any longer, because:

- A medium-size banana can be sliced in four passes through the tool.
- All slices are a perfect 1/4" wide.
- If you use a machine to dry your own fruits, this slicer makes sure all the banana pieces are even so that they dry at the same time.
- Same-sized banana slices on jello, cereal, or desserts make for great looks when serving food.

Cleaning is easy as long as you use a brush; otherwise it can be difficult to clean the blades well. Of course, use care when cleaning and do not leave this tool around children as they can put their fingers in the space and get hurt when pushing the handles together--but this is just common sense for any kitchen tool.

For a person who uses a drying machine or just wants good-looking banana slices, this is a must have. For others, it's a great talking point and clever tool. For those who slice one banana every so often, don't bake or use a drying machine or have no one to talk with, then this would be a wasteful purchase. It would be buying something you really don't need and won't use very much at all.

Personally, I love it!
words_common_s.amazon_reviews::19:
Pros:

1. Easy to set up - no tools needed. Just attach the stainless steel/aluminum mount to the tripod hole at the bottom of the camera and tighten the thumbscrew. (And check every so often that it's tightened)

2. Fits a lot more comfortably than a regular neck strap. All DSLRs should come with this type of strap. No neck burn or awkward carrying positions.

3. Can be tightened against the body by pulling on the turning ring and camera (in opposite directions) for when you need to go hands free across some difficult ground (or when your hands are otherwise busy)

4. Can be worn on either shoulder or even behind your back as needed.

5. There's a locking way to hold the strap in place when you're not shooting.

6. Strap adjusts itself and gets longer when you raise the camera to take a shot (when the locking way is released of course)

7. This strap is built for a man, (the women's strap has a small curve for the curvy photographer) but it's still comfortable (and strong enough) no matter what.

Cons:

1. Hanging an expensive camera and even more expensive lens
upside down,
from ONE screw,
in ONE spot,
on the bottom of the camera,
is a bit scary. (But regular straps can break also)

2. Strap could have been improved with a bit more soft cushioning on the shoulder area for better comfort during long periods of use.

3. Strap takes up quite a bit of space in a camera bag (but you can't have everything) For smaller bags you can remove the strap and put it back on when needed in a couple of seconds.

4. Of course you have to remove the strap when you want to use a tripod

5. No fault of the strap, but the people in the video on the product page need some teaching on how to hold a DSLR properly (LOL)

Overall, this has solved a big problem for me, as this is a much more comfortable way to carry around a heavy camera and lens for hours at a time.

Amanda Richards, January 8, 2013

Note: I recently bought the women's version of this strap. The only difference is that the strap is a little bit narrower at the top, and has a smart little bend for working around feminine curves.
words_common_s.amazon_reviews::20: I bought these to use with Brain.fm. I would have preferred wireless but Bluetooth models don't seem to be able to run all night (8 hours) on a charge. These are actually better than I expected in a couple ways - first, they sound surprisingly good for the price. The bass response is acceptable and the sound is well balanced across the hearable range. Second, the cable is a very bendable and strong mesh fabric. It doesn't bend sharply and tangle as easily as plastic and is strengthened at the plug end. The headband is a light fleece type material - it tends to be warm, but that would be a plus outdoors in cold weather. The speakers are fairly easy to move around by sticking your finger into the slots made for that purpose. That's really my only complaint - there's nothing to really keep them firmly in place. They tend to shift around easily when putting on or removing the headband. (This pulls on the cable where it enters the back of the headband.) It might be helpful to put a couple of stitches on either side of them to hold them in place. At first, the headband was a little tight on me but I was able to stretch it out a bit for better comfort - still snug enough to stay in position, but not enough to be uncomfortable or cause any problems. Overall, these work well for what I needed them for and the price was reasonable for the quality.
words_common_s.amazon_reviews::21:
I picked up this little beauty to replace both an old and difficult 5-disc CD Player and a single disc DVD player. I now have breathing room in the old entertainment center, so even my old turntable can take a noisy spin every now and again.

Seeing that I can't connect a toaster without help, I called on my trusty better half to solve the mystery of setting it up. In non-technical language, also known as plain English, this is what you need to know about this powerful machine:

1. The manual needs a lot of work. It's neither user-friendly nor idiot-proof. Same thing for the boxy silver remote.

2. It is easy to set up if you already know how to do that sort of thing. (We have component video connections to the TV and digital coaxial connections to the receiver.)

3. It gives excellent sound from both CDs and DVDs. With the benefit of 5.1 surround, movies like Master and Commander can really move you, and CDs have never sounded better.

4. It is as easy to use as a 5-disc CD changer as it is a 5-disc DVD player, except that when you're playing more than one CD you'll need to put it in "CD Mode" first.

5. It can easily play different types of media, such as audio CDs, MP3s, DVDs and those other mysterious formats - just put in the discs and play away.

6. The video quality is very good on a regular TV. You can set up different pre-set picture quality modes, or change things to suit your own taste if you're a technical person or a fan. If you have difficulty making up your mind, ignore this option.

7. The player is packed full of options, but you have to look around for yourself, which can be a bit confusing until you get the hang of it. Read the manual, you say? See Item 1 above.

8. There's on-screen information for MP3s and photo CDs, with different views available for the contents. (Groups or folders or entire playlists)

9. I can't comment on the forward scan feature, since I don't have an HD or HD-ready TV - yet. (Still waiting for that lottery win)

10. It is supposed to play DVD-Audio discs, but you need 6.1 channel inputs on your receiver to play them. Unfortunately, our receiver is lacking these inputs, but then again, I am also lacking any DVD-Audio discs.

Electronics fans will probably say that it needs a bit of "adjusting" to get it to look and sound just right, but it looks and sounds great to me. All in all a very good player, maybe even excellent when you think about the price and what you get for your money.

Amanda Richards, October 1, 2004
words_common_s.amazon_reviews::22: I have had a lot of printers over the years (IBM, Epson, HP, Canon, Lexmark, etc.), and had kind of gone away from HP a bit because of their software and driver problems (when they moved the work and help to other countries, the quality got quite a bit worse). However, when printing Christmas cards, my Canon died, and I had been impressed with this HP model when I was helping my sister sort out hers, so I bought one (MFP M479fdw). Software seems to work without problems so far, so I think HP has fixed that somewhat, even though it is a bit rough and simple in places, but it works. And it works from both Windows 10 and macOS 11 (Big Sur), as well as from mobile (iOS). The printer hardware seems to be very good, output arrives quite fast. One of the problems you run into with cheaper printers (including some lower end HPs) is that they do not put much power into the printer processors, and cut costs on the hardware to the point that they are slow and do not last long, but this version seems well designed and made. Reviews from PC Magazine, Wirecutter, etc. usually have this printer at or towards the top, I would say that is right. Print quality on text is wonderful, graphics from web pages and similar also wonderful, scans are very good (a separate flat-bed would be a little better, but this is for an all-in-one amongst the best I have seen). For printing high-quality pictures, you probably still want a Canon or Epson InkJet printer, but this one prints OK for a laser. HP does not ship this printer with full working life ink containers, but the ones they ship with will still do a good number of pages. Control screen is touch and good sized, gets the job done. Unit is fairly heavy and large, so if you are using this on a desk, check the measurements some. The printer is not cheap, but it has wonderful print quality and appears to be very well built, so HP has come back to where it once was, at the top of the market.

[[VIDEOID:5cb01b680d3ae41bbade0eaedaabfe62]] This is an absolutely beautiful kettle. It is well made, strongly built, and overall a dream to use.

POSITIVES
- It holds up to 2 quarts of water to the fill line.

- It is strongly built.

- It whistles lightly when the water has reached a rolling boil.

- The top fits tightly on the kettle but needs a little extra strength to seat and remove.

- It comes with a blue potholder.

- It comes in seven wonderful colors--gray, cream, navy, perracotta (like a salmon color), marigold (yellow), sage (deep green), and mist (a light green).

NEGATIVES
- The last bit of water in the kettle gets caught under the rim unless one can center the flow through the spout. This means that I have to dry the inside with a towel for storage.

- The kettle is heavy; almost like a cast iron pot.

- It needs a potholder to use (opening of the spout, pouring, etc.) because the entire kettle gets very hot and that includes the handle and spout lever. I also would have liked a mitt potholder the color of the kettle.

In summary, I love this kettle despite its negatives. At this high price, giving the user a mitt potholder instead of a flat one in the color of the kettle one purchases, would raise the purchase to the next level. Note that I never heard of the Caraway brand before and saw this kettle in blue on the Vine program. Since ordering this through Vine would not provide me with much savings at the list price, I decided to order this when the price came down for prime day in the color I wanted. The Caraway site was cheaper that day by $4 (that is $176) but sort of needed the purchase of insurance for $4.95. Therefore, I purchased this on Amazon for $180 plus tax, bringing this to $191.93. I still consider this expensive but this is the best made kettle I ever tried. It is right up there with Le Creuset Dutch Ovens and almost just as heavy too. This is a kettle that I expect to last my lifetime. There are many kettles on the market that are less than $40 that also could last a lifetime but they are not as nice. I do hope it continues to meet my hopes going forward. If it fails in any way, I will lower my rating, update my review, and will most likely regret my purchase. As of now, I love this and took off one star due to the negatives.

UPDATE - I've been using this regularly for days now and I noticed that this takes longer to boil water than my other kettle and keeps the water warmer a little longer. I also noticed that if I put this on my burner that has a lower flame, the handle does not get hot when the boil is complete, so that is nice and good.

You read that correctly - I installed this on the outside of my (1985) sliding glass door. Here's why: My kid is 23, by law, and 2 in his mind. He also has seizures. Oh, he's also medium to badly Autistic. All of my doors on this house have double cylinder (two keys needed to unlock, outside and in) deadbolts. The sliding glass doors have nothing. And it seems there is no way to key lock a sliding glass door. My son is just watching enough that all the usual sliding glass door 'locks' he figured out within about a week of our moving in; and given that 3 years ago he escaped on me for truly less than 60 SECONDS and in that 60 seconds or less he had a seizure, slammed backwards on the concrete, and got not only a bad cut on the back of his head but a near-life ending brain bleed on the front of his brain where his brain flew forward into his skull. I'm a solo parent... not a single parent that gets every other weekend or so free, no help from family or friends or government offices... and sometimes a girl's gotta get a bath. Or go to the bathroom. And I do not have the money for a set of French doors. So, after more looking into than I care to say, I figured I'd give this a try. I had already tried one of those track locks and for this old style sliding glass door it just didn't work at all. In our situation, when I need to use the bathroom or take a shower or just sleep without worry, I go out one of my locking doors, use the slide lock to stop the opening of the sliding glass door from the inside, come back in the house through the door I went out, lock everything up, and do what I gotta do. Then I can go back and open the slider from outside the house and it's just out of the way. No one comes in that sliding glass door - it opens onto a screened in porch with a concrete slab floor - so I'm not worried about how strange it looks that I have a lock outside - lol.

Anyway, my use for this item is unusual (they call that 'off label' in the medical field) but it sure makes my life easier and for that I am very happy and thankful for it:)

Here we have another case of buying an extra long warranty being asked to give a review but never having used (and hoping never to have to) the bought coverage. If they decided to replace the item it's completely their choice to either give a new or newest model of your device or give a rebuilt model of what you have. They promise quick turn-around and cover shipping in both directions. If you do not return the broken model within in a certain time period (I believe it's 30 days) of receiving your replacement your credit card (which you MUST have on file to file a claim) will be charged the full cost of the device when new.

This HAMILTON BEACH DIGITAL RICE COOKER (37518, Stainless Steel, 6-¾ cup yield for white rice) cooks perfect fluffy rice every time, and is a good family-sized rice cooker (enough rice for 4 persons). It has the same size as the [[ASIN:B071KPXVJ7 Hamilton Beach 37506 Model]], but has a lid with a hinge (with rubber seal, a special steam opening, an outside water collection cup, and a lid cover piece inside).

The special lid of this Model 37518 causes steamed foods to cook in one-third to one-half of the time needed by the simpler Model 37506, but the special lid has NO effect on rice or hot breakfast grain cooking times. The Model 37518 has a water collection cup that must be emptied, as needed, during cooking. The lid cover piece is a part that must be taken off each time for washing. (The directions don't explain how to take off the lid cover piece, but it pulls straight off the stick that holds it in place.)

The Model 37518 allows you to set your own cooking times for Hot Breakfast Grain or Steam. This isn't really needed, because the Model 37506 cooks both breakfast grain and rice by itself without watching, and steams food with the help of a cooking timer to tell you when it is done.

Most rice cookers do a good job of cooking rice--they have a heat sensor that touches the bottom of the cooking pot and turns the cooker off by itself when the water goes away and the pot heat level goes up. Some rice cookers--like this one--cook rice to greater perfection than others, but rice cookers mostly differ in their controls (going from simple on/off to extra-special many-button number displays), and in the amount of their cooked rice that comes out.

This rice cooker is sort of in the middle, regarding both controls and amount. It will cook different kinds of rice (there is a chart for correct amounts of rice and water for long grain brown or white, jasmine, basmati, and so on). It will cook different breakfast grains and grains (barley, oatmeal, Cream of Wheat, and so on). It will steam food (vegetables, chicken and other birds, fish and shellfish); and it will steam food and rice together at the same time.

The size of this cooker is good if you're making rice for a family of four, or if you're steaming foods for a family of two. I love it for the way it cooks fluffy rice and by itself keeps the rice warm for up to 12 hours. I also love it for cooking Cream of Wheat by itself without burning it on the bottom.

Cooking in a rice cooker takes longer than cooking on a stovetop or in a microwave oven. For example, 3 cups of raw white rice will take up to 45 minutes; 1-½ cups of Cream of Wheat, up to 37 minutes. But it's easy to start the rice cooker and let it work while you're making ready the rest of your meal.

*Washington D.C., USA*

*Day 0, 00:20*

~

"… there was an explosion right when I looked up…"

"… largest death toll in this country since…"

"… never seen before…"

Sirens blare from the TV. I sit on the floor. Dazed.

*What had just happened?*

The words "BREAKING NEWS" splash across the screen. Every pair of eyes in the country – no, the world – must be glued to their TVs. Clouds of smoke continue to rise from the side of the towers. Witnesses cry and scream about the terrible things they had witnessed. People are running everywhere, covered in dust and fear.

"Mommy," Emma stumbles into the living room. "It's time for school, Mommy."

"Oh honey," I say, on the edge of tears. "Come here." She walks to me and I hold her in my arms tightly, running my hands through her hair. "We won't be going to school today, dear."

News continues to pour in from the TV.

In the corner of the screen: Monday, 11 September 2001.


________

*Shanghai, China*

*Day 0, 01:00*

~

"Dr. Wu, you have to look at this."

"Not now, Lin. There're enough people freaking out about this! We need to focus on our research," I take off my thin, metal-rimmed glasses and look at my assistant. She has helped me so much in the past seven years. We're so close now. We can't afford to be distracted. "If we don't meet the deadline, all our efforts would have gone to waste."

Lin shakes her head. "No, doctor. I'm not talking about the attack. I… I…"

"What is it, then? Speak up."

"You… you should see this for yourself." Lin takes out a huge sheet of paper and lays it out on my table.

"This is the ocean temperature table today – why did you print it out? These changes are perfectly normal, and the –" Something at the end of the graph catches my eyes. A huge spike. "This… this…"

"Yes, doctor. You were right all along."

My heart skips a beat. I check the time of the spike. It matches perfectly.

"Lin,"

"Yes, doctor?"

"Get me the director of the Chinese Weather Administration. Now!"

*This is the end, isn't it?*

The thought hit Josh suddenly, almost by accident. It went through and broke apart his anger with the car that had let him break down so far from home; with the phone company that had failed to build towers by this empty desert road; with the sun that had boldly beaten him, sweaty and tired, to the ground.

*This is the end.*

This thought in particular stayed strong in his mind, even as he understood that he had already seen Heather for the last time. And... and Joey, who was still so proud about that geometry test. And Dale, and the business Dale would receive, the business that would serve as an unexpected gift passed down through the family.

*This is it.*

Dale, who had told him that this trip was a fool's task, and made a joke about what he would say at Josh's funeral; this memory, too, failed to shake the thought from Josh's head.

*The end of...*

The thought stayed there, still, for a time that Josh wasn't able to understand. Everything else in his mind seemed to disappear, from his edges, inward toward this single, alone idea.

*This is the end of me.*

When nothing else was left, Josh found it right that this idea of ending should itself be his final thought.

But it wasn't.

It disappeared as quickly as it came, and then --

Josh would have cried, if he was still able to do so with his body.

His regrets came rushing back all at once. And his anger, and his sadness and his hopelessness at his own lack of power. The calm peace of the "end" was over, replaced with the worry of a life not finished. A life that had failed to come to terms with itself.

And then Josh felt **fear**. Fear like he had never felt before. The terror of fate made real, of the great unknown for which he was completely not ready. The pure and total horror pushed aside his memory, and his pain, and all his other feelings.

That fear was the last thing Josh thought about.

"Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave. Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave. Citizens will not be allowed..." the Moral Officer shouted into his loudspeaker. I found it comforting. The ending being so near gave me the strength to push my weak and tired body to shovel faster, faster.

All around me my fellow citizens dug in the dust like dry broken dirt, scratching out the place where they would give their bodies back to the earth. In the distance other Moral Officers made their announcements into the same loudspeakers. At regular times throughout the field Compliance Officers stood, in perfect uniforms, waiting patiently to help us in our final duty to the Nation.

It had become clear that there was a food shortage well before the State announced it. Everyone had whispered about how the weekly food amounts they picked up from the handout station seemed to be smaller every week, though the center's Party workers would deny it if anyone asked. Then the whispers turned to fully voiced complaints when items began disappearing from the food amounts, never to come back again. Soon meat had almost become a memory and fully grown, healthy looking, vegetables were rare.

When the State News Agency, in a special broadcast, finally announced the hunger, nobody was surprised. We were told that we must, as always, stand united, strong and proud in the face of this Difficult Test. Everyone must do their part to bear this weight and our Perfect Society would clear this obstacle and come out winning. Even the Beloved Ruler was limiting his eating, we were told. It was clear, yes without doubt clear, that this was some trick by the rebels and the outsiders, trying to destroy our strength, to make us turn back from the ideas of the revolution. They had damaged our fields and killed our animals. But we would stay strong in our goodness and would come out, as ever, winning.

It was then that they announced the drawing. That a number of citizens would be randomly selected from the population to give glorious sacrifice of faith and goodness for the Nation, to help ease the weight of eating. Those who were selected were told the next day by a soldier showing up at their door to take them away from their families. I was one of the chosen.

A shout rang out across the fields, "May my body feed the soil to feed our glorious Nation. Long live the Beloved Ruler." A gunshot ended this statement. Someone had already finished their grave. A few others cheered their agreement, most were too tired and hungry to manage. The Compliance Officer put away his gun and pointed for the now dead man's two neighbors to fill in the grave he now occupied.

They had worked us hard after taking us away, shoveling out a roadway. We slept where we worked and the only food given to us was a broth so thin that they could hardly justify calling it more than hot water. And so the last of the strength of our bodies was taken.

My grave now looked deep enough. I paused before raising up my shovel to call over the Compliance Officer. If it was not deep enough for his liking I would have to wait until all others had finished, covering over their graves, before it would be my turn.

He came over and took out a tape measure. He checked the size and nodded his agreement. I let out a silent sigh of relief and went to stand at the foot of my grave. The time was here. The time for my glorious sacrifice for the sake of the Nation. The time for my final duty to my beloved land.

"Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave." The Moral Officer chanted into his loudspeaker.

I felt the cool metal of the Compliance Officer gun come to rest upon my forehead.

"Citizens will not be allowed..."

words_common_s.writingprompts::5:
"Happily ever afters doesn't exist for people like us," I said seriously. Clarissa looked up at me through her tears.
"Why not?" She asked quietly.
I gently wiped her tears away with the soft part of my thumb and smiled bitterly.
"Because, the world won't let us. Every time we try to be happy someone always knocks us down. Something always will."
"What if we run away?" She asked finally looking at me.
I swallowed, trying to hold back tears of my own.
"If we run away then we will always be running. I don't want that for us. I don't want that for you," I whispered.
Clarissa held back a sob.
"Will, please don't do this."
A tear ran down my face.
"I don't want to."
"Then why are you?"
"Because I'm no good for you Clarissa. I get into fights. I get arrested. You can find someone better who can make you so much happier. Who can give you want you want."
The words left a sour taste in my mouth but it had to be said. If we stayed together then there'd always be someone trying to break us apart.
Her parents.
My friends.
My enemies.
I gave her one last kiss.
"Maybe one day in the future, when things aren't hard and messy, we'll find each other again. Right now is not our time. Maybe tomorrow will be. Maybe someday we'll get our chance when everything is different and better for both of us."
words_common_s.writingprompts::6:
Daniel's wife stood at his side, completely falling apart at the edges, not that anyone else but him would be able to tell. Okay maybe that was a bit of an overstatement, but she was a touch worried. Nervous? Whatever she was something wasn't quite right, she was doing that little nose twitch that never happens when she's calm.

"Imani," he called out and her head tipped down to where he was seated in recognition "It's going to be fine." She gave him a weak smile that didn't quite reach her eyes before reaching out to press his hand. Of course he said it to comfort her, but he honestly felt like everything was going to be okay. They already crossed the worst bits. He survived the car crash, then he survived the operation to make sure the universe didn't decide to change its mind later, then later the leg removals, the artificial parts. With a roll of his eyes he pressed her hand back. "Honestly, this has been the easy part, we have plenty of time."

"The easy part? Since when do we ever get easy!" she reached out to hit his ears, her eyes wrinkling with fun "That's up there with 'What could possibly go wrong? Don't bring bad luck." she warned. He leaned in to tell her all that worrying could do nothing good when the door hit open, the solid bang bouncing through the large room.

"Oops," the tall man in the doorway looked embarrassed "I tripped into the door there. How are you two today?" he asked in a friendly way, walking into room and the sunlight from the windows poured over his thin form. "Ready to give it another go?" Daniel bent his legs, neat and held into his new running blades.

"Since the second I put these on Mason!" he replied truly and the easy going man gave him a thumbs up before reaching out his hands.

"That's what we like to hear! Alright lets get you up and moving then." With one last look as his wife, who was standing back with a worried look but held up crossed fingers, he reached for the other man's hands. These were the fourth pair of running blades he had tried. The other ones had problems, in spite of their so called custom fits. Too long. Too short. These hurt. Those felt like they were going to fall off. But as Daniel shook to his feet he knew these were it. It took a moment to steady himself. They had a different sort of balance and give to them than his normal artificial leg, and his fitness wasn't quite where he wanted it be. His heart raced as he moved his weight from one foot to the other, hearing the blades bend in response. Left. Right. Left. Right. Left right, left right, left right, bounce. They felt nothing like his old legs. But all the same... they felt right. Slowly Mason let go and then backed away to the other side of the room, his eyes never leaving Daniel's. When he hit the wall he called out to them.

"Great! Now start at a walk and work up to as fast as you feel comfortable doing." a sneaky tone crept into his voice "And remember, the room is padded and we're all friends here. Face plants are nothing to worry about." Daniel laughed at the suggestion. As if he'd let these things get the better of him. Sure of himself, he took a shaky step forward and his arms wheeled around a bit before he tightened his middle to keep balance. Then he took another. And another, and soon he had a slow bobbing jog going, carefully moving between his wife and physical therapist. He did this until finally, Mason signaled for him to stop. He ran down the room to the happy couple with a look of great excitement and happiness.

"It looks like we got it this time!" He stepped back and gave him one final look over "We just need to run a few more tests, make sure that everything is set correctly, but I think we found your golden pair here. So, how do you feel?"

His mind began to wander as he turned inward, trying to find the words that could even begin to describe what he was feeling. All he could think about were the things he thought he had lost forever when he hazily woke up from the operation that important day, looking down to see the sheet cave in where his lower legs had once been. The sound of the crowd screaming his name as he tore down the field. The strong feeling of running down a track, the world narrowing almost into blackness as he pushed himself to the limit. The lightness of a casual game of tag with his wife, catching thin air as she slipped by him with laughter dancing in her eyes. Bouncing on his new legs once more he felt weightless. Unable to be defeated. With a strength he hadn't felt in a long time he hugged Imani and spoke over her head, his face aching with a smile.

"Alive."

words_common_s.writingprompts::9:
"Yes, I remember it like yesterday. I was walking through the western mountains, just east of Markarth. The road curved below me, cutting a long path through the valley." A person dressed in animal skins caught my eye, moving slowly towards a wagon that had stopped before crossing the river. They pulled out a mean-looking sword as they came closer, clearly planning to kill the small group of travelers. I got on my horse and started down the hill, shouting at the top of my lungs to get their attention.

"The man who wanted to rob them right away looked at me with an angry face and let out a shout of his own. Right away, a dozen more men and women, dressed in the same torn clothes, were running down on the wagon with weapons out. I knew there were too many for me to fight, but I couldn't stand the thought of letting those poor people die to these thugs. As I reached the bottom of the hill, I remembered that my friend from Winterhold, he's a bit of a crazy one, had given me a magic paper before I set out on my trip." Let me say now that I'm no magic user. Sure, I tried to find some magic that would make me better looking, but none of that worked anyway. I was pretty sure that I only had to open the paper and read it, but I had no idea what it actually *did*. With any luck it would call up one of those big magical creatures my friend was always talking about. He made them out to be something close to like gods. Wouldn't mind having one of those on my side.

"Anyway, once I got to the bottom, I jumped off my horse and pulled the paper from my bag. I was shaking so badly, I almost couldn't read it, but I knew I had done it right when I started glowing. That should have been a good sign that something bad was about to happen, but I knew nothing about magic. Still don't. The glow was nice though, warm and easy. Suddenly, all the robbers were putting their weapons away and asking me what was happening to them. I had no idea, but I thought they couldn't do any more harm." Sadly, they were a little too amazed by me. They must have thought I was some sort of great magic user because they right away lifted me on their shoulders and carried me back to their camp for a big meal. I started out thinking they were people who ate other people or something when I saw them attacking, but I heard their story and understood they were really just trying to get by in the world. Their honey drink was wonderful, let me tell you. A little too wonderful, I guess, because I woke the next morning with an, I must admit, good-looking woman next to me and a camp full of these people cheering me with gifts and hugs.

"So, you see, I wish I was you. I miss the open fields and cold mountains, the gold and treasure, and the freedom to go wherever I please. I used to be young and without worries, I used to be strong and brave. You remind me a lot of myself, honestly. I used to be someone who went on adventures like *you*, until I took an arrow to the knee."

Note: "Taking an arrow to the knee" was seemingly a Norse saying about getting married.
words_common_s.writingprompts::12:
"You want to send in Nikon? You really think it's that bad?" The speaker was a large, wide chested man, well over six feet tall, with a long, neatly cut beard and a perfect suit. He was talking to a woman who had to have been in her sixties, the beauty she showed as a young person now a well-aged shine. Her sharp blue eyes looked at the wide chested man without blinking, staring through him.

"You have a problem, Lord Aerlman. A very particular type of problem. We can deal with this very particular problem, but it will need the services of an expert. Alex Nikon is that expert." Her tone was matter-of-fact, not excited or loud in any way.

"She's just a girl, a confused girl." The older woman lifted her shoulders and let them drop.

"Your girl, Lord Aerlman, has contacted the Outer Planes. She has let something through, and now it's inside her. However, until she does something public, I can't bring in the Circle without your request. If you don't want our help, that's fine. Just remember, terrible things strike first at the home." Her warning delivered, the woman turned and started to leave the fancy sitting room. As she reached the door, Lord Aerlman called to her.

"Laura! Ms. Cadswall. Wait. Please." She smiled to herself with confidence and then made her face blank, turning with a neutral look on her face.

"Yes?" The lord was twisting his hands together, walking back and forth in front of the fire.

"Your man, Nikon, I know his reputation. Will he... kill her?" Lord Aerlman looked upset and worried.

"Alexander Nikon will handle the emergency. That is what he does. How he handles it will remain at his choice. Be told though, Lord Aerlman, that contact with the Outer Planes ruins the very soul. Even death can't remove its mark."

Lord Aerlman looked crushed, and he slowly picked up a picture off the shelf of the fireplace, a family picture showing the lord and his wife, along with their daughter, a beautiful redhead in her late teens. He rubbed the picture with his thumb, before setting it back down. All of the energy left him and he bent over, turning towards the woman with a beaten look.

"Fine. Do it. Make the call." He sent her away with a wave and then dropped into one of the large leather chairs, pouring himself a large whiskey, which he right away drank down. As he poured another, Laura excused herself and closed the door quietly. She had a phone call to make.

-- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -

"Antonia. I know you're here." The same girl from the photo, now a fully-grown, and beautiful young woman, was hiding behind a large stack of wooden platforms, holding herself tight and trying not to scream. Her hands and body were covered in blood, some hers, and some her friends. They had been having a party, drinking in her London flat, when the man arrived.

The first sign of trouble was the door breaking inward, a large piece of it ripping through Pierce like a spear. He dropped with a choking sound and blood sprayed across the room. Screams came from the small group of young men and women, and before they could even understand the danger, a small man, barely five feet and six inches tall, was in their middle, a large curved sword in one hand and a handgun in the other. Glowing written symbols twisted across his skin, and his left eye was in an eyepatch. His right eye was the color of polished metal, and it quickly looked around the room. Everything after that was unclear, and Antonia couldn't recall any details, except the bodies, and the blood.

She remembered a voice in her head, then her friends all screaming, fire pouring from their eyes as they charged the sword-carrying man while shouting in some language Antonia had never heard. As her friends threw themselves at the man, she turned and jumped through the bay window, falling the three stories and landing with a sickening crunch. She remembered her legs feeling surprisingly good for such a fall, and then running. The voice in her head was louder, and she couldn't understand it, but it was hurting her.

As she ran through the streets, the voice was speaking in a rhythm, and every person she passed turned to stare at her, their eyes shooting out fire before they turned and charged the way she had come. She didn't understand what was happening, who the man was, or why he was after her. She didn't understand anything! Next thing she knew, she was hiding in the warehouse, where the man found her again, his curved sword and gun both covered in blood. As she curled up and tried not to let him find her, he kept talking.
words_common_s.writingprompts::13:
"Lamb, tell me a story…" said the Wolf, with a pleased voice and a smile on his face. "….Something sweet."

The Lamb shook with fear. He had heard stories of the wolf all throughout his childhood, but never thought that there was any truth to them.

"W-what would you like to hear?" The Lamb finally asked.

"You can decide that." The Wolf replied with a commanding voice.

The two of them were in a hidden area of the same field that the Lamb had been born and lived on, and he was currently pushed into the corner with a broken leg, while the Wolf walked a half circle around him, a mere two feet away. The Farmer was nowhere to be seen, and none of the other Lambs would dare try to save him, unless they felt like giving up their own lives.

He didn't have a story to tell. He had lived a short, boring life and with the understanding that his family wasn't coming to save him, he knew it was coming to an end. He felt a strange wave of calm rush over him as he accepted his fate at the mouth of the Wolf.

"If I had a story, it would be this one. But we've already reached the end." He said.

"I always liked the violent ones." The Wolf replied as he closed the gap between them, moving closer and closer until there was almost no space left between their bodies at all.

words_common_s.writingprompts::15:
Janice turned to me, her big blue eyes still full of childish innocence. Damn - I'd forgotten that she was watching the Presidential Inauguration for a school project. "Daddy," she began, "what does the President mean? What's 'gay'?"

"Well, honey..." I began, but trailed off as I tried to think of a way to explain it to a five year old. "Uh... Well, you know how Mommy and Daddy like to hold hands, and to hug, and kiss, and stuff?"

"Yeah! It's funny when Mommy pinches your butt when you're not looking, and makes you squeak!" she giggled. Kids, man - I'd forgotten what it was like to be so amused by the word "butt". Had I ever been that small, that innocent?

I waited for her giggles to quiet down before I carried on. "Well, sweetheart, 'gay' means that he - the President - he likes to do that stuff with a boy, not a girl like Mommy."

I could see the confusion in her eyes as she struggled to understand this new information. Damn you, McCain, for making me explain this to her! She's not old enough for this; she's not ready! I'M not ready!

Janice opened her mouth to speak. I knew what was coming; I'd opened the door to a lifetime of sexual wrongdoing. My sweet little girl was gone forever.

Suddenly I realized she'd said something, and in my worry, I'd completely missed it. "Sorry, sweetheart - what did you say?" I asked, fearing her response. What fresh hell have I opened up?

"I said, I'm hungry. Can I have a cookie? Please, Daddy?"

I was shocked, unable to respond at first.

"Uhm. Sure," I answered. "Get one for your brother, too."

Huh. I guess that maybe what two agreeing adults do behind closed doors isn't that big of a deal after all.

Even when they ARE public figures. Even when people know who they are and watch what they do. Even when everyone can see them and talk about them.
words_common_s.writingprompts::16:
"Why, hello, Ma'am," I said easily, standing up and offering her a chair with my usual grace. "Bertram Proudfoot at your service. Who do I have the pleasure of talking to?" 
 
 "I'd rather not say, if it's all the same to you," she said, sitting down. 
 
 "Alright," I said comfortably. "What can the Hobbiton Detective and Gossip Agency do for you?" 
 
 "Well," said the woman, rubbing her hands together nervously. "It's like this." She paused. 
 
 "Like what, Ma'am?" I said kindly, lighting my pipe and sitting back in my chair. 
 
 "My husband is dead," she said. 
 
 "Oh my dear, I am sorry!" I cried out, though I must admit there was part of me that was less than sorry. What can I say? I am only a Hobbit, and this woman had the most beautiful feet I had ever laid eyes on. "Tell me everything that happened." 
 
 "We were out boating on the Brandywine three nights ago," she said. "And all of a sudden, a rock flew out of nowhere and hit my poor husband in the head. He fell over in the water. I screamed for help, but he drowned." 
 
 Now of course I had already known it must have been something like this from the moment she walked in the door. I have an unusual sense for things like that. 
 
 I looked as serious as I could, given the circumstances. "I see," I said, blowing another perfect smoke ring up towards the ceiling. "And you would like me to find and charge the person who did this." 
 
 "Yes," said the woman. 
 
 "I will do my best, I can promise you that," I said, and I saw her clearly breathe out with relief. "May I offer you a cup of tea? Something stronger, perhaps?" 
 
 "No thank you," she said, and without another word she showed herself out. 
 
 I quickly made my way to the Brandywine River dock. My first line of questions would be to ask the man who rented out boats. An odd fellow, and an odd job -- not many sensible hobbits choose to be out in the middle of the water by their own free will. And indeed, this hobbit's boat-renting business was not doing well. 
 
 After a long look at his records he told me that he had rented out two boats on the evening in question, and only one of those was by a couple. The couple had been a one Drogo Baggins and a one Primula Brandybuck. Primula, that was the woman's name. But why had she not wanted to tell it to me? 
 
 Had this boat fellow heard any noise on the water, any cries for help? No he had not. Did he remember who returned the boat to him? It hadn't, he said. In fact, that particular boat had been left floating in the middle of the river. Strange. 
 
 Next I walked up and down the both banks of the river. Not much to gather here, except that whoever had thrown the rock must have been quite a shot. 
 
 Having carefully looked at the river, my next step was to find out about Priscilla and Drogo. After visiting several pubs in the areas of Buckland and Hobbiton, I had gathered this: Primula and Drogo were long married, though perhaps not happily. They had one son, now twelve years old, name Frodo Baggins. Strangely, it seemed that Primula had not been seen by anyone except me since Drogo's death. In fact, most of the gentleman hobbits that I spoke with seemed to be of the belief that both Drogo and Primula had died three nights ago. 
 
 Facts were not adding up. Before I could do anything else, I had to speak with my mysterious client again so as to make things clear. Though I had no way of reaching her, I knew she would return to my offices in short order. 
 
 The day following, she did just that. 
 
 "Good day, Primula," I said upon her coming in. 
 
 Her face showed surprise, but she did not deny the name. 
 
 "I have a few things I need to get straight with you about the case," I said, and went on to explain what I had discovered. "So I'm afraid I must ask again," I finished. "What happened that night?" 
 
 And without a word, the woman got up and left. Just like that. 
 
 I did not hear from her again, and two days later, her body was found floating down the Brandywine. I was saddened but not surprised. 
 
 My guess had been this: having been unhappily married for some time, Primula had pushed her husband into the water herself and boated back to the shore with the plan of disappearing forever. Everyone would think that they both were dead, and so would not think there was any wrong doing. However, upon listening in on the lawyer's meetings that quickly followed, she realized that care of her son would go to an extended cousin, none other than the famous crazy person Bilbo Baggins. 
 
 Understandably, Primula did not want her child to fall under the influence of said crazy person, and so she came to me in the hopes that I would believe her story and turn suspicion away from herself, all in a desperate attempt to keep care of her son. But I, having seen through her trick, stopped this fact. Seeing no other choice she then drowned herself in sadness. Shame -- I had just begun to think there may have been a very helpful choice for the both of us. 
 
 I sat back and began polishing my pipe thoughtfully. It was another case solved by the respected Bertram Proudfoot, but perhaps another opportunity lost. I had solved countless cases, but opportunities of the other sort came only but now and again. Like I said, it was a shame. 
 
 I blew another smoke ring to the ceiling as my thoughts turned to crazed old Mr. Baggins. I felt for the young Mr. Frodo, who was now cursed enough to fall into the old hobbit's care. Who knows what old Baggins would pass on to the easily influenced young fellow. As I'm sure you're all aware, Mr. Bilbo Baggins suddenly disappeared many years ago and then returned just as suddenly a year later with piles of gold and many tall tales. Having been a very respectable hobbit before he left, whatever he experienced on his journey seemed to have confused his mind. He came back a changed hobbit, and not for the better. 
 
 He was so changed, in fact, that it is my personal guess that the hobbit currently living in Bag End is not the real Bilbo Baggins at all, but rather a fake. There is plenty of evidence to suggest this: particularly the fact that "Mr. Baggins" appears much younger than a hobbit of his years has any right to look. 
 
 I shall have to look into that line of questions further some day.
words_common_s.writingprompts::17:
Lucifer stood in a large hall outside of space or time. It never changed, the dark stone walls forming into curved doorways to hell knows where. Within this huge room he and God would argue every several thousand years. God came out from the shadows of one of several doorways, an angry look on his face.

"Oh, it's you," he said. Lucifer looked at him calmly.

"Did I ever give you a sex drive, Lucy? I can't remember."

"No," Lucifer answered.

"Aw, why not? Feel like fucking? I'm kinda horny."

"Jesus Christ," Lucifer said quietly.

"Hey! Don't mention my son to me right now! That's fucked up!" God said.

Lucifer pressed his eyes shut. "I came here to talk to you about something," he said.

"Whaddya want, Lucy?"

"I don't want to rule hell anymore."

"Aw, why not?"

"I didn't do anything wrong! I showed your precious humans to sin and gave them self-awareness! Freedom! You would've kept them as sock puppets! I helped you make one of your greatest creations! I did it because I knew you needed it! I did it out of love for you!"

"So please," Lucifer said, falling down on one of the still stone thrones, "Let me come back to you. Let me serve you like I had before."

"Only if you kiss me, Lucy," God said unclearly. Lucifer made a face.

"Aww, don be like that, Luce, y'know why you have to be king of the shittiest place ever. You created the split, you got ta help me watch over one of its two places and I'm definitely not going down there, how fucked up would that be?"

"*You* created the split. You created everything."

"Ssssshhhh... here, have some soda."

"I don't - I don't want any fucking soda. That's - oh goddammit! You spilled it all over me!"

God laughed, "Don't say my name in vain, Luce."

Lucifer pulled his eyebrows together, God knew he was holding back tears, "I don't understand you."

"Of course you fucking don't! I am outside *space* and *time*! I exist in levels you have no fucking understanding of! I am all things at once! How could you possibly understand me?" God shouted.

"I... don't know. I thought, being your creation, I am part of you, and you are part of me."

God laughed meanly, "A *part* of me, Luce. You can never understand my whole self. You would break apart within a second. All creations in this straight line time frame would become a screaming smear of flesh."

A pause. Lucifer stared at his hands.

"Why did you create us then?"

"To forget, and then remember."

"I don't understand."

"I know," he said softly.

words_common_s.writingprompts::19:
* [ PI ] *

The Shine could have been salvation for humanity. Should have been, but we were never very good at avoiding conflict. Who knows how long ago it was, but in an age of wireless devices and everywhere information we lifted our look from our screens only to see the sky catch fire, eaten by a cold, many-colored fire. It lasted only a few hours, but took only a few minutes for the world to see. It didn't take much longer for people to want a closer look, to want a touch of the gentle flame.

And then they flew. They flew so far and so fast, and quickly they were joined by others; and then they fell, very slowly at first, but much like a boat in water they sank further the more that joined them. It didn't take long for people to work out that the sinking related directly to how many people flew, or to notice that flying wasn't the only *choice* available to us. Before the Shine had faded many such choices came and went; flight, strength, healing, being invisible, living forever, moving instantly from place to place, speed, and all the other common choices appeared and disappeared very quickly. At first some thought the powers only lasted a time, related to how long the Shine was present, but it quickly became clear that the strength of powers was backwards related to the number who picked that *choice*.

That's when the more unusual powers started showing up; at first it was just office workers who decided they wanted to shit gold, or kids who decided they wanted to control animals, but before a quarter day had passed things started getting weird. Fast drops in temperature, the ground shook often, clocks would stop and start and people died. Many people died. In half a day, an eight-billion-strong world-wide society of the most smart and tough kind on Earth broke down and cut in half in number; we broke into groups and sides just looking to survive, to get through the storm; those *without* powers were kings, and those with unusual powers that couldn't be worked out or copied were gods in flesh, right there to pray to when many needed them most.

A few days passed before things started to calm down - though in that time the sun only passed once. Weather was beyond wild and cities were almost completely empty, only able to live in for larger and more powerful sides. We went from chasing wealth and success to living rough in a day, if you could call it that. We went back to being like beasts, except a bit more smart, and sometimes having super-powers.

Much time has passed since the Shine touched our sky, and humanity has created many new places to live; but the most popular choices are still weak, so death is power, and attacks are common and never-ending. The largest places to live are the most powerful, but also the main target for smaller groups. Living with others is living in war, so the more peaceful of us left travel.

And that is what I have done. I have travelled, and looked for a way to end this craziness, and perhaps bring back the world to the somewhat normal state it once had. And I may well just have found it.

I stood at a crossing, looking towards the capitol building. I stared at this girl on fire. She sat calmly. Not moving a muscle, not making a sound. People stood and stared. There were other black marks on the stairs she sat on.

"Mommy, why is she on fire?"

"Oh, that's normal," my mother replied.

"So it is totally normal for people to burst into flames?" My six year old mind was confused.

"No son, that is not the normal part. We are in a war. People don't like the way the government controls things, so they complain by burning themselves."

"Will she be okay?" My young mind wanted her to be. No one should be so upset they hurt themselves like that.

"I don't know," came the scary response.

Years later, after the civil war was lost, I would read about all the people who burned themselves for their country. My country.

Through college, I would think of these people. The people with beliefs so strong they would actually kill themselves in such a way to make a powerful statement. They would not want to live in a country under the crushing rule that had been in control for many years. They wanted to be free, or they wanted to die.

It seems every generation, there is an uprising. The beaten down people realize that they're being beaten down, and they get a tool to help them get together and fight back. They gain power. Rarely does it happen in a short time. However, here I was, a beaten down 27 year old with completely no future.

I stood at that crossing that I stood at 21 years ago. The black marks were gone, but so was my youth. This government had to go. They had beaten down my mother's generation. They had beaten down the generation before them, and the generation after them. They weren't going to stop unless forced to. I calmly walked up to the steps and got ready to make the newest black mark, start the next revolution.

As the flames rose past my eyes, I wanted one last look as I burned. The pain was almost too much to bear, but I managed to see through the pain. The last thing I saw before the world faded was a young girl pointing at me, exactly where I had been 21 years before.

I walked downstairs and opened up the computer screen. A banker popped up on the screen.
"Hello Mrs. Roer. How may I help you?"

"I'd like to check my bank statement. I got a letter in the mail that I only have five credits?"

"Okay, one moment." The banker disappeared for a second and then came back up.

"Mrs. Roer. You right now have 10 credits."

"What? That's not even enough to buy food with this month?"

I looked outside and then let out a breath.

"Okay. Well thanks." I said.

The screen closed after the banker wished me a good day. How could I only have 10 credits of happiness? A bottle of milk is *1.21* credits. I couldn't even buy milk.

I walked outside this time. It was sunny and bright, birds were happy, I bet they have enough happiness credits to buy damn food. I looked around. My in-ground pool, my hot-tub, my outdoor deck complete with a pond further from the house. All of this was my life.

My husband and I had been married for ten years now. I was happy, he was happy. Right?

I went to look at my phone, I had a message from my husband.
'Want to have coffee?'
I sent back,'Yes.'

I went upstairs and took a shower. My husband was gone, as always. It was no secret we had been falling apart. We were so happy at one point though that we had more credits than anybody in the word. Like I said though, it was no secret that we had been falling apart. He had many affairs and I honestly, although I never cheated, found myself wanting for more.

I got myself ready for coffee. Nothing too fancy or too everyday. It was just coffee. I walked outside, got in one of our cars and drove to the airport. We owned a private airplane, my husband had already put gas in it.

"Just having coffee today Bill," I said.

I was walking off the airplane in 4 hours to see my husband.
"Hello Mrs. Roer," He said, kissing my cheek, as he always did.
I walked with him to our second home. A blonde woman with a tight shirt was leaving the house. I looked angrily at her, and she hurried from the front door to her car.

"We need to talk," I said.

"Exactly," He replied, looking pleased at my anger.

"Listen, Mr. Roer, I do love you, but there's so --."

"Elaine, I want a divorce."

"That was quick." I said.

He shrugged it off.

I left quickly after that. No coffee for me.

It wasn't long before I got home. I had a message from the bank again. My happiness points had hit zero.

A message from an old friend surprised me.
"Coffee?" It read.
"Sure." I answered.

At that moment my doorbell rang. I answered the door to him.
My old friend. He right away kissed me. I had missed that feeling. I felt my blood pressure rise.

"Good to see you."

"Listen Luke, I just-"

He kissed me again and broke my words.

"I paid your husband to let me marry you Elaine. He's wanted a divorce and he's not good to you. You know that."

I was surprised. He paid my husband to marry me? Why on Earth would he..

"Elaine. I know we didn't work out, but our son. He needs you."

I felt a tear hit my chest. I had given Luke, and our son up to be with my husband. My husband would not let me have a son in the house that was not his.

"Elaine. Marry me. Please?" He said. He walked inside towards me further. "Our sons in the car. He's 12 now," Luke said.

I had gotten to see our son, Reig, until he was four. Then I had to cut off talking to my husband being afraid it would make us look bad on the press.

I walked outside and my son ran from the car. He wrapped his arms around me. I felt my phone alert again and I checked it. In case it was my husband with an answer for why he'd'sold' my hand.

It was bank. My account had just been given 20,000 happiness credits.

"Yes. I'll marry you."

"Prisoner 778125-Sigma-8, you stand before this court today accused of crimes against galactic civilization, murder, four counts of xenocide, 70 counts of attempted xenocide, planetary dehabitation, planetary destruction, and attempting to overthrow the Pan-Galactic Alliance. How do you plead?"

The man before Councilwoman Asaarha met the gaze of her and her fellow Judges with cold blue eyes. Despite the 140 cycles of time-based isolation he had suffered before his trial, Sacha Markes stood tall and unbroken. He gave off power and command, even now, stripped of his rank, fleet, and army. The last of the humans was a perfect example of the species.

The silence before he spoke seemed louder to the Councilwoman than the crashing waves of her ocean home. The time it took for the human to speak seemed longer than the width of the galaxy.

"Guilty," he said with a simple finality.

The Judges nodded their heads seriously. None of them had expected this one to beg for mercy.

Asaarha typed the sentence into the computer before her. The other six Judges did the same. The blue lights of Markes's uniform and restraints changed to red. The screen on the mind-power blocker around his head changed to read GUILTY in Galactic Standard.

Though the trial room was empty except for the Court and Markes, Asaarha could hear the roars of revenge that were surely echoing throughout the galaxies. Each trial of the humans had been shown in its entirety. Each had ended in a guilty verdict.

"Sacha Markes, formal Admiral of the Seventh Human Expeditionary Fleet, High Captain of the Royal Guard, Commander-in-Chief of the Human Expeditionary Force, and Primarch of the Solar Empire, you are sentenced to Mind-Power Stripping and Execution by black hole. Do you have any last words before the sentence is carried out?"

The human threw his head back defiantly and turned his gaze on the camera nearest him. Addressing the billions of life forms throughout the galaxy, he began the last speech of the human race.

"We brought you up out of the mud we found you in. We gave you art, culture, and science. Our golden fleets created a civilization that will never be matched; not for 100,000 turns of the galaxy. We are responsible for all that you are.

I remember when the first of our race died after 100 centuries of living forever; killed trying to cure the sick of one of your backward planets. I remember when we decided to take our revenge on our children; to punish you for your ignorance. We burned that world. I watched our plasma cannons turn its surface to glass and its oceans to ash. One world for one human life. A fair trade.

But you did not accept our judgment. Like Icarus chasing the sun, you rose up against us. Did you expect us to just let you? Did you think we would not defend ourselves? I was the commander of the fleet that met yours on the first day of battle. My ten cruisers against the most powerful battleships of three galaxies and a hundred races.

Now, a hundred years later, you have finally defeated us. You have lost entire solar systems to us. You have given up huge numbers of lives and thousands of civilizations to bleed your gods dry and bind them in chains. Your worlds are broken. Your cities gone; wiped from history in an instant. Can you truly call that victory?

I am the last of my kind. I am Sacha Markes. Look upon my face, ye mighty, and despair. For when you kill me, you kill the last light left in this existence."

War Journal of P1C Henry Whiticker, First Divine Armored.

Entry:48

We finally reached the edge of the first circle today and heaven protect me the scout reports weren't lying, it's more huge than anything i could imagine. The spy photos we were given to prepare us are like a blind man trying to describe a sunrise, and by God the smell has actually somehow gotten Worse! Seeing the pit first hand i think the size of our task has finally hit home for some of the crew, they look shaken, i don't blame them, have we bitten off more than we can chew? I'm not sure but i have faith in our mission and our commanders.

The hugeness of the pit really can't be put into words but for the sake of this journal i'll try. The edge extends further than the human eye should be able to see and yet i can make out tiny details on the far cliff face, it looks big enough that you could fit the whole Earth in and knock it around like an ice cube in the bottom of a whiskey glass, even while sitting in the driver's seat of the rumbler i get dizzy looking down onto the levels below, if it wasn't for the special anti-crazy pills the doctors give us i'm sure what i see on the lower levels might have some lasting horrible effect on me. The crew and i wash down todays dose with a bottle of holy wine, and why not, today was a good day after all. Today we reached the edge of Limbo.

Entry:49

Not much to record today, some minor fights on the outer edge, just some low level demons taking a swipe at us otherwise nothing going on but general camp stuff. The builders are working double time to make sure the safety of Limbo Base, they say it'll be fully up in 2 days, i have my doubts. After their mess up at the river they've got a lot of face to save, 2 Rumblers, 4 groups of troops and a Screacher lost because of their damn boats. Bastards.

I Hate just sitting around like this with nothing to take my mind off the smell of rot and sulfur that somehow gets into the rumblers driver's seat despite the tech nerds promises that the driver's seat is perfectly air tight and sealed, it feels like the smell is inside my skull rotting tiny holes in my brain.

Entry:51

HOOAH! CONTACT BABY! Praise God i've been waiting for this moment since the first days of the war for the surface. Hell finally saw fit to send us some worthy enemies AND WE KICKED THEIR MUTHA FUCKING TEETH IN!! HAHAHAHAHAHA.

They came a few hours after my last entry like a great black tornado. A spinning column of harpies, skrieks and imps beyond counting rising up from the center of The Pit and came crashing down completely covering Limbo Base. The first few moments of fighting should've been chaos but by the grace of God we were ready.

All the Screachers had been on high alert since we came out from the maze of caves and onto the plains of Limbo proper 8 days ago and today that careful watching paid off. The sudden attack of the winged demon assault fell apart before the wall of sound our blessed Screachers blasted out. The word of God is poison to the residents of Hell, the word of God pumped out through a moving rig of high powered speakers driven by a faithful member of the clergy is down right weakening. The shocked and frozen Demons that twitched and twisted on the ground were easy targets, the rumblers blessed water guns burning away wide areas of the foul creatures as if the misted holy water were strong acid, huge piles of the creatures were turned to ash in seconds.

The larger Demon haridens proved more tough and i saw more than a few ground troops die on their claws, their blessed body armor little better than cardboard. We paid them back in kind and i'm proud to say our rumblers throwing spear guns sent a good lot of the giant buzzards screaming into death stuck on our gleaming silver spears. I should record so it doesn't seem like i'm making less of the ground troops efforts, their bravery and wildness in battle too, for they've got that in large amounts, despite the deadly danger they collected their fair share of kills, pinning the giant creatures with their silver long spears and finishing them off with their chain sickles. it was a wonderful bloody sight, like something out of a nature show on television.

The greatest test of the battle was yet to come though. After a full day and a half of fighting the black swarm began to thin out and we thought we might've finally broken their attack, but then they appeared. Three huge figures coming into focus through the cloud of ash and tiredness. Hell Dragons, nothing like what we'd seen in movies or our stories from childhood, these were great sick, foul things that stood over us. Flat nosed heads the size of a grand church covered in sharp points, long armored bodies like a bug's, their faces and joints slick with thick black tar that bubbled and made noise as it fell from them and stained the plains of Limbo.

Screachers focused their attack and stopped the giants from over running the base, the rumblers water tanks and throwing spear guns ran dry just trying to keep them away, our brave ground troops held back the black swarm, fighting without rest which allowed us time to pull back, get more supplies and come back into the fight. And so it went for hours on end and for all our hard work the Hell Dragons seemed to be none the worse.

Rescue finally came at the hands of the building team. Of all people! Through our hard work we had given them enough time to lock down and put together Limbo Bases major defenses, Blessed Big Guns and the Holy Rail Gun. The Rail Gun broke through the Dragons thick armor spraying fountains of tar onto the battlefield while the big guns smashed into the beasts weak exposed points pushing shells marked with holy writing deep in their bodies filling them with pain. The attack still went on for hours and we lost a great deal of our force but after nearly 2 months since we first went down into this place we finally have set up a forward base to launch our attack on Hell. One Circle down eight to go. This is the first day here that the smell doesn't bother me.

The planet Earth has changed a lot recently, 23 years ago- almost to the day, the storms on the surface ended. The same storms that had been going wild for roughly five thousand years, a few weeks passed whilst the cloud groups broke apart, and then we got our first clear view of our home.

I was five years old at the time and interested mostly by the colours, the beautiful blue and green were like nothing on the Ark. We had water- sure, but not pools large enough to give that blue colour. We had plants too, but the conditions were far from the best and made the plants a dirty green rather than rich. I wanted to see it closer- touch it- feel it.

That was probably when I decided to join the sign-up for the first journey. The first journey was- as the name suggests, the first trip back down to the planet. A lot of people wanted to go back down as soon as the storms ended, there were loud complaints- fighting even. People wanted the Ark to head straight back down- Idiots.

23 years may have been a long time to wait, but it was important... We were the last humans after all- if we landed and something went wrong? We couldn't risk it. Years of rock and earth checks, and low air searching gave us the perfect landing spot. Smallest damage to local surroundings, enough space to grow a community, plenty of food- water- and importantly a lot of natural safety taking the form of Disaster-formed mountain ranges, and deep holes filled with the darkest blue water.

Of course something as large as the Ark couldn't simply just land though... No- that was where the first journey came into the picture. We were the first guys to go planetside- and live there forever in over seven generations. Our goal was to build the dock, it'd be a long job- probably another five or six years even, but the dock would give us a much needed start- as well as drawing out local land and features much more clearly, learning about plants, animals. The truth of the situation is that we were going in blind- this "safe-zone" as the Corps had nicknamed it could very easily become a deathtrap. The problem with the safezone was that because of it's location once we went in, our shuttle wouldn't be able to make it out.

Part of the problem with the planet was the storms- even now 23 years after the main storm ended smaller groups continued to turn... The mountain ranges kept the area safe from the storms still going wild- not quite powerful enough to make it over the high peaks though.

Even in the air above there was a mean wind that always blew... It would tear a outgoing ship to pieces, only a ship as large as the Ark would be able to live through it- and the Ark needed a Dock in order to do a take off.

So that was the task, go down, face possible death, build a huge building, all in less than six years- and I was damn excited.

JESUS enters from the left carrying takeout coffee*

**JESUS** Sorry, there was a line. So, what have we got?

**MOSES** Dead body. Officer called it in, looks like another dead prostitute. Hey, Hazdrubul, do you have cause of death yet?

**JESUS** When did she die?

**HAZDRUBUL** Hard to give a time of death right now, but I'll go with some time last night and give you a better number when we get a body organ temperature reading.

*Jesus moves to get closer to the crime scene, trying to get a better look. He doesn't handle the dead body well and ducks behind a clay jar to throw up*

**MOSES** Jesus! Well, at least you didn't mess up the crime scene.

*JESUS comes back out wiping his mouth and looking pale*

**MOSES** OK, Officers are going to ask questions house to house. Let's go get you cleaned up and see if we can put a name to this poor girl.

**MOSES** What?

**JESUS** Of course! Stone throwing! Don't you see it?

**MOSES** Jesus, slow down will you? See what?

**JESUS** They thought they were *better than her*!

***

*Scene 832: Jerusalem, outside, night. MOSES is leaning on a police car as JESUS walks up with this week's BAD GUY in handcuffs. Moses watches as JESUS hands the BAD GUY off to uniformed cops.*

**JESUS** Couldn't have done it if you hadn't spotted the connection between the victims. How did you know?
