We found that VPD, rather than T a , better predicted rates of EWL in two of the three species that were considered in this investigation. Moreover, we found that T b , whole-animal EWL and whole-animal SMR increased with increasing T a , while T b , responding to body size variation, increased with increasing M b in A. delalandii and S. capensis but not in X. laevis . Whole-animal SMR, showing species-specific patterns, increased with increasing M b in S. capensis only. We did not find any significant effect of VPD, M b or sex on whole-animal EWL when examining variation within species. Lastly, M b did not influence T b , whole-animal SMR and EWL in the principally aquatic X. laevis , suggesting distinct physiological regulation. These results suggest that M b may not have the same effect on key physiological variables across all species, and that the influence of M b may also depend on the species ecological specialisation and lifestyle. Thus, the generality of M b as an important factor should be taken in the context of both physiology and species habitat specialisation, recognising ecological diversity.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::10: Chronotaraxis, which is an impairment of the perception of the sequencing of time, represents an alteration of temporality that has been described as being characteristically associated with thalamic involvement, specifically affecting the dorsomedial nucleus. We report the clinical cases of two patients who presented with acute ischaemic strokes located in said territory, demonstrating a clinical presentation that was based on this symptom, the recognition of which proved essential in determining the therapeutic approach that would be implemented. In both the first and second cases, it is described how the perception of temporality, being carefully evaluated and documented, was essential for establishing the diagnosis of the ischaemic condition affecting both patients who were examined. Awareness and dissemination of this association, linking chronotaraxis to thalamic pathology, may be vital in the management of patients presenting with thalamic disorders, this being due to the possibility of influencing and modifying the initial approach, since the recognition of a specific symptom, such as chronotaraxis, can prevent the spread of thalamic damage while simultaneously addressing the long-term sequelae that it causes, especially those of a cognitive nature that significantly impact patient outcomes. Cronotaraxis como síntoma guía de un infarto talámico medial. Introducción. La cronotaraxis, siendo una afectación de la percepción de la secuencia temporal, representa esta alteración de la temporalidad que se ha descrito asociada de forma característica a la afectación talámica, concretamente al núcleo dorsomediano que resulta comprometido. Casos clínicos. Presentamos los casos clínicos de dos pacientes que sufrieron ictus isquémicos agudos de localización en dicho territorio, con una clínica basada en este síntoma cuyo reconocimiento resultó esencial en el abordaje terapéutico que se implementó. Tanto en el primero como en el segundo caso se describe cómo la percepción de la temporalidad, siendo cuidadosamente evaluada, fue esencial para el diagnóstico de la patología isquémica de ambos pacientes examinados. Discusión. El conocimiento y la divulgación de esta asociación pueden resultar fundamentales en el manejo de los pacientes con alteraciones talámicas, esto debiendo a la posibilidad que surge de influir y modificar el abordaje inicial, puesto que el reconocimiento de un síntoma específico, como es la cronotaraxis, puede evitar la extensión del daño talámico, previniendo de esta manera las secuelas que ocasiona a largo plazo, sobre todo cognitivas.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::11: Some infectious diseases, such as influenza, tuberculosis, and SARS-CoV-2, may be transmitted when virus-laden particles that have been expelled from an infectious person are inhaled by someone else, a process which is known as the airborne transmission route. These virus-laden particles, being more concentrated in the expiratory jet of an infectious person than elsewhere in a well-mixed room, exhibit a near-field enhancement in virion exposure that has not been well quantified. Transmission of airborne viruses, depending on factors that are inherently variable and, in many cases, poorly constrained, requires large ensembles of model simulations spanning the variability in input parameters in order to quantify this uncertainty. However, models that are well-suited to simulate the near-field evolution of respiratory particles, being also computationally expensive, limit the exploration of parametric uncertainty. In order to perform many simulations spanning the wide variability in factors governing airborne transmission, we developed the Quadrature-based model of Respiratory Aerosol and Droplets (QuaRAD), which is an efficient framework for simulating the evolution of virus-laden particles after they are expelled from an infectious person, their deposition to the nasal cavity of a susceptible person, and the subsequent risk of initial infection. Having simulated 10 000 scenarios to quantify the risk of initial infection by a particular virus, SARS-CoV-2, we found that the predicted risk of infection was highly variable among scenarios and, in each scenario, was strongly enhanced near the infectious individual. In more than 50% of scenarios, the physical distancing needed to avoid near-field enhancements in airborne transmission was beyond the recommended safe distance of two meters (six feet) if the infectious person is not wearing a mask, though this distance defining the near-field extent was also highly variable among scenarios, with the variability in the near-field extent being explained predominantly by variability in expiration velocity. Our findings, suggesting that maintaining at least two meters of distance from an infectious person greatly reduces exposure to airborne virions, indicate that protections against airborne transmission, such as N95 respirators, should be available when distancing is not possible.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::12: Open fractures, being contaminated wounds that contain gram-positive and gram-negative organisms, require wide-spectrum antibiotic therapy to be incorporated into the treatment plan. Antibiotics should be initiated as soon after injury as possible, preferably within 3 hours of injury, after which time the rate of infection has been reported to increase. Time to surgical debridement within 12 hours of injury has not been reported to affect the rate of infection, given that a patient is being treated with antibiotics. An antibiotic bead pouch and vacuum-assisted wound closure may help reduce the risk for secondary and nosocomial contamination and subsequent infection. Open fractures, always being associated with a soft-tissue injury, can be considered a soft-tissue injury that involves a fracture. The management of the bone and the soft tissues in a patient with an open fracture is the major determinant of fracture healing and functional restoration of the injured extremity. The formulation of a soft-tissue treatment plan, which must occur during the initial wound assessment and the initial fixation of an open fracture, should not be considered a secondary or consecutive process. A soft-tissue surgeon should be consulted the night of the injury. Selection of fracture fixation depends on the fractured bone, the location of the fracture (whether intra-articular, metaphyseal, or diaphyseal), the extent of soft-tissue injury and contamination, and the physiologic status of the patient. More than one fixation method may be applicable for the management of a specific injury; therefore, a surgeon's expertise and the availability of implants also should be considered when making these decisions. Surgeons must understand bone healing biology to achieve successful outcomes in the management of open fractures. The cornerstones of these bone healing treatments include optimization of host biology, recognition of a patient's nutritional status, appropriate use of medications, and eradication of infection, all of which contribute to successful healing. Surgeons should consider bone grafting and/or the use of biologics to achieve bony union in patients with an acute open fracture and in the management of delayed union or nonunion that may develop subsequently.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::13: PURPOSE: Cyclical patterns of compliance, which have been observed with many health-related activities such as dieting and exercise, raise the question of whether such patterns of compliance exist among users of chronic medications. We sought to estimate the percentage of patients who restart osteoporosis therapy after experiencing a prolonged lapse in medication use and to identify the factors that are associated with a return to compliance. METHODS: We studied 26,636 new users of an osteoporosis medication (including alendronate, calcitonin, estrogen, raloxifene, or risedronate) who were age 65 or older and had experienced an extended lapse in refill compliance, which we defined as a period of at least 60 days after the completion of one prescription in which no refill for any osteoporosis medication was obtained. Using survival curves, we estimated the length of time until therapy is resumed. We estimated the association between patient characteristics and the rate of resuming treatment using Cox proportional hazards analysis, after which we conducted a case crossover analysis to examine whether certain events occurring during follow-up triggered a return to refill compliance. RESULTS: Of patients who stopped therapy for at least 60 days, an estimated 30% restarted treatment within 6 months, while 50% restarted within 2 years. Among patients who had experienced at least 6 months of continuous use before their interruption in treatment (n=5863), 42% restarted therapy within 6 months and 59% within 2 years. Younger patients, women, and those with a history of a fracture were more likely to return after experiencing a break in medication use. Recent hip fractures, discharges from nursing homes, and bone mineral density testing also predicted a return to treatment. CONCLUSION: Extended gaps in treatment, being common among users of osteoporosis medications, raise concerns because the effectiveness of these drugs when used in an interrupted way remains unknown; therefore, compliance interventions should emphasize the need for continuous medication use. Further research is needed to understand why patients often go for months without refilling prescriptions and also whether similar utilization patterns exist for other chronic medications.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::14: Imbalances in the gut microbial community (dysbiosis) of vertebrates, which have been associated with several gastrointestinal and autoimmune diseases, remain poorly understood in terms of which taxa are associated with gut dysbiosis and whether particular gut regions or specific time periods during ontogeny are more susceptible to these disruptions. We also know very little of this process in non-model organisms, despite an increasing realization of the general importance that gut microbiota holds for health across diverse species. Here, examining the changes that occur in the microbiome during dysbiosis in different parts of the gastrointestinal tract, we focus on a long-lived bird with high juvenile mortality, the ostrich (Struthio camelus), as our study system. We evaluated the 16S rRNA gene composition of the ileum, cecum, and colon of 68 individuals that died of suspected enterocolitis during the first 3 months of life (diseased individuals), comparing them with 50 healthy individuals that were euthanized as age-matched controls for this investigation. We combined these data with longitudinal environmental and fecal sampling, aiming to identify potential sources of pathogenic bacteria and to unravel at which stage of development dysbiosis-associated bacteria emerge within host populations. Diseased individuals, having drastically lower microbial alpha diversity, differed substantially in their microbial beta diversity from control individuals in all three regions of the gastrointestinal tract that were examined. The clear relationship between low diversity and disease, being consistent across all ages in the ileum, decreased with age in the cecum and colon as animals matured. Several taxa were associated with mortality (Enterobacteriaceae, Peptostreptococcaceae, Porphyromonadaceae, Clostridium), while others were associated with health (Lachnospiraceae, Ruminococcaceae, Erysipelotrichaceae, Turicibacter, Roseburia) in these populations. Environmental samples, showing no evidence of dysbiosis-associated bacteria being present in either the food, water, or soil substrate, suggested alternative origins. Instead, the repeated fecal sampling revealed that pathobionts were already present shortly after hatching and proliferated in individuals with low microbial diversity, resulting in high mortality several weeks later. Identifying the origins of pathobionts in neonates and the factors that subsequently influence the establishment of diverse gut microbiota may be key to understanding dysbiosis and host development. Video Abstract.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::15: We investigate the reason for the quantum speedup, which manifests when quantum algorithms require fewer computation steps than their classical counterparts, extending their representation to encompass the process of setting the problem. The initial measurement, selecting a setting at random, is followed by Bob (the problem setter) unitarily changing it into the desired one, yielding a representation that is accessible to Bob and any external observer while necessarily remaining inaccessible to Alice (the problem solver), since revealing it would tell her the function computed by the black box, which to her should remain hidden inside it. Resorting to relational quantum mechanics, we recognize that to Alice the projection of the quantum state due to the initial measurement is retarded until the end of her problem solving action, meaning that to her the algorithm input state remains one of complete ignorance of the setting. Through black box computations, she unitarily sends it into the output state that, for each possible setting, encodes the corresponding solution acquired by the final measurement. We show that we can ascribe to the final measurement the selection of any part—say the R-th part—of the random outcome produced by the initial measurement, thereby projecting the input state to Alice on a state of lower entropy where she knows a corresponding part of the problem setting. The quantum algorithm becomes a sum over classical histories in each of which Alice, knowing in advance one of the R-th parts of the setting, performs the black box computations still required to identify the solution. Given an oracle problem and a value of R, this retrocausality model provides the number of black box computations required to solve it, while conversely, given a known quantum algorithm, it yields the value of R that explains its speed up. R = 1/2 always yields the number of black box computations required by an existing quantum algorithm and the order of magnitude of the number required by optimal one.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::16: Cardiac disease and clinical intervention may both lead to an increased risk for thrombosis events due to modified blood flow in the heart, thereby creating a change in the mechanical stimuli experienced by blood cells as they pass through the chambers of the heart. The degree of platelet activation, specifically, is influenced by the level and type of mechanical stresses present in the blood flow. Here we analyze the blood flow occurring in the left ventricle of the heart through a computational model that has been constructed from patient-specific data. The blood flow in the ventricle is modeled by the Navier-Stokes equations, while the flow through the mitral valve is represented by a parameterized model which captures the projected opening of the valve. A finite element method is used to solve the equations, from which a simulation of the velocity and pressure of the blood flow is constructed, enabling detailed hemodynamic analysis. A triple decomposition of the velocity gradient tensor is then used to distinguish between rigid body rotational flow, irrotational straining flow, and shear flow, each representing fundamentally different mechanical environments. The triple decomposition enables the separation of three fundamentally different flow structures, with each one generating a distinct type of mechanical stimulus on the blood cells present in the flow. We compare the results to simulations where a mitral valve clip intervention is modelled, which leads to a significant modification of the ventricular flow patterns and hemodynamic characteristics. It was found that the shear in the simulation cases that had been treated with clips increased more compared to the untreated case than the rotation and strain did, demonstrating differential effects on flow components. A decrease in valve opening area of 64 % in one of the cases led to a 90 % increase in rotation and strain, but a 150 % increase in shear, indicating disproportionate mechanical effects. The computational analysis suggests a process for patient-specific simulation of clinical interventions in the heart with a detailed analysis of the resulting blood flow, which could support clinical risk assessment with respect to platelet activation and thrombosis events.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::17: The diffuse very high-energy (VHE, > 100 GeV) gamma-ray emission observed in the central 200 pc of the Milky Way by H.E.S.S. was found to follow the dense matter distribution in the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) up to a longitudinal distance of about 130 pc to the Galactic Centre (GC), where the flux rapidly decreases. Recent sensitive H.E.S.S. analysis revealed that the cosmic-ray (CR) density profile drops with the distance to the centre, thereby making data compatible with a steady cosmic PeVatron at the GC. In this paper, extending this analysis to obtain for the first time a detailed characterisation of the correlation with matter and to search for additional features and individual gamma-ray sources in the inner 200 pc, we take advantage of 250 hours of H.E.S.S. data and improved analysis techniques, performing a detailed morphology study of the diffuse VHE emission observed from the GC ridge and reconstructing its total spectrum. We show that the emission correlated with dense matter covers the full CMZ and that its flux is about half the total diffuse emission flux. We also detect some emission at higher latitude likely produced by hadronic collisions of CRs occurring in less dense regions of the GC interstellar medium. We detect an additional emission component centred on the GC and extending over about 15 pc that is consistent with the existence of a strong CR density gradient, thus confirming the presence of a CR accelerator at the very centre of our Galaxy. We show that the spectrum of the full ridge diffuse emission is compatible with the one previously derived from the central regions, suggesting that a single population of particles fills the entire CMZ, distributing itself throughout this vast molecular zone. Finally, we report the discovery of a VHE gamma-ray source near the GC radio arc and argue that it is produced by the pulsar wind nebula candidate G0.13-0.11, which represents a compelling astrophysical object warranting further investigation.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::18: These international clinical practice recommendations (CPR) for developmental coordination disorder (DCD), which were initiated by the European Academy of Childhood Disability (EACD), aim to address key questions on the definition, diagnosis, assessment, intervention, and psychosocial aspects of DCD that are relevant for clinical practice. Key questions in five areas were considered through literature reviews combined with formal expert consensus. For recommendations based on evidence, literature searches on 'mechanisms', 'assessment', and 'intervention' were updated since the last recommendations that had been published in 2012. New searches were conducted for 'psychosocial issues' and 'adolescents/adults', with evidence being rated according to the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine (level of evidence [LOE] 1-4) and transferred into recommendations. For recommendations based on formal consensus, two meetings of an international, multidisciplinary expert panel were conducted with a further five Delphi rounds being employed to develop good clinical practice (GCP) recommendations. Thirty-five recommendations were made, eight of which were based on the evidence derived from literature reviews (three on 'assessment', five on 'intervention'), while twenty-two were updated from the 2012 recommendations. New recommendations relate to diagnosis and assessment (two GCPs) and psychosocial issues (three GCPs), with one new recommendation (LOE) additionally reflecting active video games as adjuncts to more traditional activity-oriented and participation-oriented interventions, and two new recommendations (one GCP, one LOE) being made for adolescents and adults with DCD. The CPR-DCD is a comprehensive overview of DCD and current understanding based on research evidence combined with expert consensus, reflecting the state of the art for clinicians and scientists of varied disciplines. The international CPR-DCD may serve as a basis for national guidelines. Updated international clinical practice guidelines on developmental coordination disorder (DCD) are provided, offering refined and extended recommendations on clinical assessment and intervention for DCD, a critical synopsis of current research on mechanisms of DCD, a critical synopsis of psychosocial issues in DCD with implications for clinical practice, and the first international recommendations to consider adolescents and adults with DCD.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::19: Hypertension can lead to mood disorders that may worsen or ameliorate depending on the type of antihypertensive prescribed, with depression being associated with modifications in basal brain asymmetry, particularly that of the frontal cortex, which is involved in blood pressure control. Furthermore, different vasoactive drugs may change the brain's asymmetry in a manner that contributes to cognition status. We studied the bilateral activity of several neuropeptidases in frontal cortex as a reflect of the functional status of certain neuropeptides involved in mood. Using arylamide derivatives as substrates, we fluorometrically analysed the activity of these enzymes in the left and right frontal cortex of control untreated Wistar-Kyoto (WKY) and spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs), comparing their activities with WKY or SHR treated with the antihypertensive drugs captopril (CAP) and propranolol (PRO) or with the hypertensive N (G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester. SBP was also measured in all WKY and SHR groups. Untreated WKY, WKY treated with CAP or PRO and SHR treated with CAP exhibited normotensive values of SBP, whereas WKY treated with N (G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester as well as untreated SHR and SHR treated with PRO and N(G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester demonstrated hypertensive values of SBP. Changes in the bilateral distribution of neuropeptidases were depending on the strain, the enzyme analysed and the drug used. Normotensive WKY groups (WKY, CAP, PRO) revealed intrahemispheric correlations mainly in the left hemisphere, whereas, in contrast, WKY treated with N(G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester and SHR groups demonstrated intrahemispheric correlations mainly in the right hemisphere. Interhemispheric correlations were mostly observed in WKY as well as in SHR groups with antihypertensive treatments (CAP, PRO). Our results suggest specific brain bilateral patterns of neuropeptidase activities in WKY that change in SHR, an observation that may be related to the cognitive disorders that have been described in these animals and that change under antihypertensive or hypertensive drug's treatments.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::20: The purpose of this study, which evaluates the value and efficacy of rapid response teams (RRTs) for different triggering events in total hip arthroplasty (THA) patients, involved performing a retrospective review of all RRT events at a single, tertiary referral center from 2014 to 2016. Inclusion criteria, defined as patients >18 years old that underwent primary or revision THA, determined the study population. Information queried included demographics, primary reason for RRT, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), underlying etiology, whether any changes in management occurred, and whether the patient was uptriaged. In total, 168 RRTs were called on 153 hip arthroplasty patients, having a mean age of 65.2 ± 14.1 years, a mean body mass index of 32.3 ± 4.8, with 66% being female. Length of stay in RRT for primary and revision THA, measuring 3.4 and 6.2 days respectively, was significantly longer than the length of stay for primary THA patients (2.4 days, P < .001) and revision THA patients (4.6 days, P = .005) that did not require an RRT, with no mortalities occurring. RRTs for hypotension/presyncope (11%) and for syncope (11%) resulted in significantly fewer changes in management (P < .01) than those for tachycardia (77%), hypoxia (57%), AMS (79%), and other conditions (47%). RRTs for hypotension/presyncope (28%), syncope (15%), and hypoxia (30%) resulted in significantly fewer patients being uptriaged (P < .001) than tachycardia (81%). Hypotension/presyncope was found to be significantly more commonly due to volume depletion (67%) (P < .001) than other etiologies, while hypoxia was significantly more commonly due to atelectasis (57%) and opioids/oversedation (30.4%) (P = .037). AMS/delirium was also significantly more commonly caused by opioids/over-sedation (71%) (P < .001). In patients undergoing THA, RRTs for hypotension/presyncopal symptoms and syncope, when compared to tachycardia, were significantly less likely to result in changes in management or uptriaging, with the most common etiologies being potentially preventable, including volume depletion and opioid use.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::21: Emergency medical services, being an important part of acute stroke management, necessitate effective prehospital assessment tools. We devised a prehospital stroke scale, which we designated as the TOYOTA prehospital stroke scale for tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) intravenous therapy (TOPSPIN), for triaging patients with ischemic stroke who have especial indications for intravenous t-PA therapy in December 2006; this scale, comprising 5 items including consciousness, atrial fibrillation, language disorder, disturbance of the upper extremities, and disturbance of the lower extremities, represents a comprehensive assessment approach. The aim of this study was to analyze the results accumulated over 10 years of TOPSPIN implementation and to distinguish ischemic stroke from hemorrhagic stroke in the real world setting. We prospectively enrolled consecutive patients who, having been transferred to our hospital, were evaluated by Toyota city ambulance services using the TOPSPIN from December 2006 to January 2017. We examined definite diagnosis at the time of hospital discharge (categorized as ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, or stroke mimic), positive-predictive value of the stroke, the rate of the recanalization therapy, and clinical differentiation among patients presenting with hemorrhagic stroke, ischemic stroke, and stroke mimics. A total of 1,482 consecutive patients were enrolled; 1,134 (76.5%) were patients with stroke (628 ischemic-type, 34 transient ischemic attack-type, and 472 hemorrhagic-type) and 348 (23.5%) without stroke (80 with seizure, 42 with syncope, 27 with hypoglycemia, and 199 other conditions). Among 628 patients presenting with ischemic stroke, 130 (20.7%) received intravenous recombinant t-PA treatment, endovascular therapy, or both interventions. The presence of atrial fibrillation, combined with older age, lower blood pressure, and lower total TOPSPIN score, was more commonly associated with ischemic stroke than with hemorrhagic stroke. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, the presence of atrial fibrillation was independently associated with ischemic stroke (OR 2.33; 95% CI 1.61-3.40). The TOPSPIN, being a simple prehospital stroke scale that includes an assessment of atrial fibrillation, enables early detection. Detection of atrial fibrillation occurring in the prehospital stage may point to a higher probability of ischemic stroke.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::22: We aim to determine the redshift of GDS-1408, which is the most solid z~7 galaxy candidate lying in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field. We have used all the VLT spectra of GDS-1408 that were collected by us and two other groups with FORS2 at VLT in the last five years, achieving a total integration time of 52hr. The combined spectrum, being the deepest ever obtained of a galaxy in the Reionization epoch, does not show any emission line or continuum detection over the whole wavelength range, extending up to 10100A. Based on an accurate set of simulations that we performed, we are able to put a stringent upper limit of f(Lya)<3x10^(-18) erg/s/cm2 at 3-9 sigma in the explored wavelength range, which corresponds to a rest-frame equivalent width EW<9A. Combining this limit with the SED modelling, we refine the redshift to be z=6.82+/- 0.1 (1-sigma). The same SED fitting indicates that GDS-1408 is relatively extinct (A1600~1), having a dust corrected star formation rate of ~ 20 Msol/yr. The comparison between the un-attenuated equivalent width predicted by the case-B recombination theory and the observed upper limit provides a limit on the effective Lya escape fraction of f_(esc)^(eff)(Lya)<8%. Even though we cannot rule out a major contribution of the inter/circum galactic medium in damping the line, a plausible interpretation is that GDS-1408, being moderately evolved, contains sufficient gas and dust to attenuate the Lya emission before it reaches the intergalactic medium. The redshift confirmation of even the best z~7 candidates is very hard to achieve with the current generation of 8-10m class telescopes, unless the Lya or unusually strong rest-UV nebular emission lines are present. We show that both JWST and E-ELT will be necessary to make decisive progresses, while currently the increased redshift accuracy obtained with this kind of analysis makes ALMA an interesting option for the redshift confirmation.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::23: The survival of Salmonella spp., which served as pathogen indicator in composting, was studied using the inoculums technique that was employed to give the known amounts of Salmonella spp. involved in composting. The inoculums of Salmonella spp. solution, being added directly into the compost material, represented the direct inoculum that was compared with inoculums in vial technique, whereby the Salmonella spp. solution was placed into a vial and inserted into the middle of compost material before starting the composting process. The conventional method that is used for the enumeration of Salmonella spp., consisting of serial dilution followed by standard membrane filtration, is recommended in the compost quality standard method PAS 100 and the British Standard (BS EN ISO 6579:2002). This study, having been designed to investigate the relationship of temperature and contact material that may also be involved in pathogen activation specifically to Salmonella spp., maintained the exposure to an average temperature during composting of about 55-60°C for at least 3 days, which was reported as sufficiently killing the vast majority of enteric pathogen (Deportes et al., 1995). The amount of Salmonella spp. and temperature for both samples, being set as indicator, determined the survival of Salmonella spp. in direct and non-direct inoculums, with this study giving the figures of die-off rate for Salmonella spp. during composting while also revealing the differentiation between direct contact (Sample A) and non-contact of Salmonella spp. with compost material (Sample B) during composting. The results from laboratory scale of composting study showed that after 8 days, which included at least at 66°C, the numbers of Salmonella spp. in Sample A were below the limits in UK compost standard, known as PAS 100 (BSI, 2005), which required the compost to be free of Salmonella spp., whereas Sample B still gave high amount of Salmonella spp. even after composting for 20 days.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::24: BACKGROUND: Although race is associated with prostate cancer progression in early stage disease, once men have developed advanced disease, it remains unclear whether race continues to predict a poor outcome. The authors hypothesized that, in an equal-access setting among patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) and no known metastases (M0/Mx), black men would receive imaging tests at similar rates as nonblack men—meaning there would be an equal opportunity to detect metastases—but would nevertheless have a higher risk of metastatic disease. METHODS: In total, 837 men who were diagnosed with M0/Mx CRPC during 2000 through 2014 from 5 Veterans Affairs hospitals in the SEARCH (Shared Equal Access Regional Cancer Hospital) database were analyzed. Data on all imaging tests performed after CRPC diagnosis were collected, including date, type, and outcome. Multivariable Cox models, which were used to test associations between race and several outcomes, examined the time to first metastasis, first bone metastasis, first bone scan, second bone scan among men who had a negative first bone scan, and overall survival. RESULTS: Black men (n = 306), when compared with nonblack men (n = 531), were equally as likely to receive a first and second bone scan after receiving a diagnosis of CRPC. There were no significant differences observed in the risk of developing any metastases, bone metastases, time to bone scans, or overall survival between black men and nonblack men (all P > .2). CONCLUSIONS: The lack of racial differences in the development of metastases and scanning practices that was observed in this study suggests that, once men have received a diagnosis of M0/Mx CRPC, race may not be a prognostic factor. Efforts aimed at understanding prostate cancer racial disparities may derive greater benefit by focusing on the risk of developing prostate cancer and on the outcomes of men who have early stage disease. Cancer 2016;122:3848-3855. © 2016 American Cancer Society.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::25: We present deep Hubble Space Telescope single-star photometry of Leo A in B, V, and I, with our new field of view being offset from the centrally located field observed by Tolstoy et al. (1998) in order to expose the halo population of this galaxy. We report the detection of metal-poor red horizontal branch stars, which demonstrate that Leo A is not a young galaxy, being in fact at least as old as metal-poor Galactic Globular Clusters which exhibit red horizontal branches and are considered to have a minimum age of about 9 Gyr. We discuss the distance to Leo A while performing an extensive comparison of the data with stellar isochrones, finding that for a distance modulus of 24.5, the data are better than 50% complete down to absolute magnitudes of 2 or more. We can easily identify stars with metallicities between 0.0001 and 0.0004 and ages between about 5 and 10 Gyr in their post-main-sequence phases, but lack the detection of main-sequence turnoffs which would provide unambiguous proof of ancient (>10 Gyr) stellar generations. Blue horizontal branch stars, being above the detection limits, are difficult to distinguish from young stars with similar colors and magnitudes. Synthetic color-magnitude diagrams show it is possible to populate the blue horizontal branch in the halo of Leo A, with the models also suggesting ~50% of the total astrated mass in our pointing to be attributed to an ancient (>10 Gyr) stellar population. We conclude that Leo A started to form stars at least about 9 Gyr ago, while exhibiting an extremely low oxygen abundance of only 3% of Solar in its ionized interstellar medium. The existence of old stars in this very oxygen-deficient galaxy illustrates that a low oxygen abundance does not preclude a history of early star formation, demonstrating the complexity of galactic chemical evolution processes.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::26: One goal of neuromorphic engineering is to create 'realistic' robotic systems that interact with the physical world by adopting neuromechanical principles derived from biology. Critical to this is the methodology to implement the spinal circuitry responsible for the behavior of afferented muscles, which are muscles receiving sensory feedback. At its core, muscle afferentation represents the closed-loop behavior arising from the interactions among populations of muscle spindle afferents, alpha and gamma motoneurons, and muscle fibers, all working together to enable useful behaviors. Using programmable very-large-scale-circuit (VLSI) hardware, we implemented simple models of spiking neurons, skeletal muscles, muscle spindle proprioceptors, alpha-motoneuron recruitment, gamma motoneuron control of spindle sensitivity, and the monosynaptic circuitry connecting them. This multi-scale system of populations of spiking neurons, emulating the physiological properties of a pair of antagonistic afferented mammalian muscles, each simulated by 1024 alpha- and gamma-motoneurones acting on a joint via long tendons, proved highly capable. This integrated system was able to maintain a joint angle while reproducing stretch reflex responses even when driving the nonlinear biomechanics of an actual cadaveric finger. Moreover, this system allowed us to explore numerous values and combinations of gamma-static and gamma-dynamic gains when driving a robotic finger, some of which replicated certain human pathological conditions observed clinically. Lastly, we explored the behavioral consequences resulting from adopting three alternative models of isometric muscle force production. We found that the dynamic responses to rate-coded spike trains produce force ramps that can be very sensitive to tendon elasticity, particularly at high force output levels. Our methodology produced what is, to our knowledge, the first example of an autonomous, multi-scale, neuromorphic, neuromechanical system capable of creating realistic reflex behavior in cadaveric fingers. This research platform allows us to explore the mechanisms underlying both healthy and pathological sensorimotor function in the physical world by building them from first principles, serving as a precursor to neuromorphic robotic systems.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::27: Introduction and Objective: Patients presenting with a urinary tract infection accompanied by kidney or ureteral stones, which constitutes a urologic emergency, often achieve early clinical stability but remain hospitalized while awaiting results from urine antibiotic sensitivity analyses. We aimed to identify clinical predictors of antibiotic resistance in patients who underwent urgent urinary tract decompression for sepsis and obstructive urolithiasis, thereby facilitating early discharge on empiric oral antibiotics. Methods: Patients who underwent emergent urinary tract decompression for sepsis and an obstructing ureteral stone from 2014 to 2018 at two academic medical institutions were identified. Following emergent stent placement being performed, patients were treated with broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics. We assessed the association between clinical parameters at the time of presentation and resistance to at least one antibiotic from urine culture using the Wilcoxon test and Fisher exact test for continuous and categorical variables, respectively, before performing multivariate logistic regression using all significant variables from univariate analysis. Results: Out of 134 patients, 84 patients (62.7%) had urine cultures resistant to at least one antibiotic. On univariate analysis, patients with resistant cultures were significantly more likely to have had previous ureteroscopy, to require postoperative intensive care unit-level care, to have bacteremia, and to experience a longer length of stay. In multivariate analysis using significant variables identified from univariate analysis, only previous ureteroscopy was significantly associated with antibiotic resistance, demonstrating an increased odds of 6.95 (p = 0.011). Conclusions: In this study, we show that a history of ureteroscopy is significantly associated with antibiotic resistance in both univariate and multivariate analyses. Our findings suggest that patients with history of ureteroscopy should await urine culture results, while those without a history of ureteroscopy may be discharged early on empiric oral antibiotics, though future studies are necessary to determine the effectiveness of this predictor.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::28: Evidence details how cannabis can influence the use of other psychoactive substances, including prescription medications, alcohol, tobacco and illicit drugs, but very little research has examined the factors associated with these changes in substance use patterns. This paper explores the self-reported use of cannabis as a substitute for alcohol among a Canadian medical cannabis patient population. Data was derived from a survey of 2102 people enrolled in the Canadian medical cannabis program, from which we included 973 (44%) respondents who reported using alcohol on at least 10 occasions over a 12 month period prior to initiating medical cannabis, then using retrospective data on the frequency and amount of alcohol use pre-and post medical cannabis initiation to determine which participant characteristics and other variables were associated with reductions and/or cessation of alcohol use. Overall, 419 (44%) participants reported decreases in alcohol usage frequency over 30 days, while 323 (34%) decreased the number of standard drinks they had per week, and 76 (8%) reported no alcohol use at all in the 30 days prior to the survey. Being below 55 years of age and reporting higher rates of alcohol use in the pre-period were both associated with greater odds of reducing alcohol use, whereas an intention to use medical cannabis to reduce alcohol consumption was associated with significantly greater odds of both reducing and ceasing alcohol use altogether. Our findings suggest that medical cannabis initiation may be associated with self-reported reductions and cessation of alcohol use among medical cannabis patients, which is particularly significant given that alcohol is the most prevalent recreational substance in North America. Since its use results in significant rates of criminality, morbidity and mortality, these findings may result in improved health outcomes for medical cannabis patients, outcomes that could contribute to overall improvements in public health and safety across broader populations.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::29: The delicate balance between spin-orbit coupling, Coulomb repulsion and crystalline electric field interactions, which is observed in Ir-based oxides, is usually manifested as exotic magnetic behavior. Here we investigate the evolution of the exchange coupling between Co and Ir that occurs when La is partially substituted by Ca in La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$. A great advantage that arises from the use of Ca$^{2+}$ as replacement for La$^{3+}$ is the similarity of its ionic radii, meaning that the observed magnetic changes can more easily be associated to electronic variations. A thorough investigation of the structural, electronic and magnetic properties of the La$_{2-x}$Ca$_{x}$CoIrO$_6$ system was carried out by means of synchrotron x-ray powder diffraction, muon spin rotation and relaxation ($\mu$SR), AC and DC magnetization, XAS, XMCD, Raman spectroscopy, electrical resistivity and dielectric permittivity. Our XAS results show that up to 25% of Ca substitution at the La site results in the emergence of Co$^{3+}$, possibly existing in high spin state, while the introduction of larger amount of Ca leads to the increase of Ir valence. The competing magnetic interactions that result from the mixed valences lead to a coexistence of a magnetically ordered and an emerging spin glass (SG) state for the doped samples. Our $\mu$SR results indicate that for La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$ a nearly constant fraction of a paramagnetic (PM) phase persists down to low temperature, possibly being related to the presence of a small amount of Ir$^{3+}$ and to the anti-site disorder occurring at Co/Ir sites. For the doped compounds the PM phase freezes below 30 K, but there is still some dynamics that remains associated with the SG. The dielectric data obtained for the parent compound and the one with 25% of Ca-doping indicate a possible magnetodielectric effect, which is discussed in terms of the electron hopping between the TM ions, the anti-site disorder and the distorted crystalline structure that characterizes these materials.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::30: With the stringent requirements that have been introduced by the new sixth-generation (6G) internet-of-things (IoT) use cases, traditional approaches to multiple access control have started to show their limitations, prompting a new wave of grant-free (GF) approaches to be proposed as a viable alternative, although a definitive solution is still to be accomplished. In our work, we propose a new semi-GF coordinated random access (RA) protocol, denoted as partial-information multiple access (PIMA), designed to reduce packet loss and latency, particularly in the presence of sporadic activations that characterize modern wireless networks. We consider a machine-type communications (MTC) scenario, wherein devices need to transmit data packets in the uplink to a base station (BS) that coordinates the access procedure. When using PIMA, the BS can acquire partial information on the instantaneous traffic conditions and, using compute-over-the-air techniques, estimate the number of devices with packets waiting for transmission in their queue, thereby enabling informed scheduling decisions. Based on this knowledge, the BS assigns to each device a single slot for transmission, though since each slot may still be assigned to multiple users, collisions may occur despite the coordination effort. Both the total number of allocated slots and the user assignments are optimized, based on the estimated number of active users, to reduce collisions and improve the efficiency of the multiple access scheme being deployed. To prove the validity of our solution, we compare PIMA to time-division multiple-access (TDMA) and slotted ALOHA (SALOHA) schemes, which represent the ideal solutions for orthogonal multiple access (OMA) in the time domain in the case of low and high traffic conditions, respectively. We show that PIMA is able not only to adapt to different traffic conditions and to provide fewer packet drops regardless of the intensity of packet generations, but also able to merge the advantages of both TDMA and SALOHA schemes, thus providing performance improvements in terms of packet loss probability and latency.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::31: Background and purpose — Bone remodeling, occurring as a response to bone trauma, postoperative immobilization, and device-related bone reactions, can lead to loss of bone stock while increasing the risk of periprosthetic fracture and aseptic loosening. This study investigates the adaptive bone remodeling of the proximal tibia following uncemented total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Patients and methods — We performed a 2-year follow-up of 53 patients, having a mean age of 62 (38–70) years and including 27 men, who received an uncemented TKA in a randomized controlled trial utilizing bone mineral density (BMD) as a secondary endpoint. Patients were randomized to 2 groups receiving either monoblock (A) or modular (B) polyethylene design. The TKAs were performed using the uncemented Zimmer Nexgen trabecular metal, with measurements of BMD being done postoperatively and after 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. BMD was measured in 3 regions of interest (ROI). Results and interpretation — In group A, statistically significant changes in BMD were seen after 24 months in both the medial and lateral ROI, with BMD decreasing medially by 15% (p = 0.004) and laterally by 13% (p = 0.01). In group B the BMD changes, being limited, returned to the preoperative values after 24 months. The differences in BMD change between groups were statistically significant in both the medial (p = 0.03) and lateral (p = 0.02) ROI. In the distal ROI we found no significant change in BMD occurring in either group. A significantly different bone remodeling pattern of the proximal tibia was seen in the 2 groups, demonstrating a higher degree of bone loss in the knees that received the monoblock polyethylene design, thereby indicating that the flexible monoblock implant design, having been previously shown to improve fixation, does not decrease the bone loss of the proximal tibia.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::32: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs), which are bio-inspired models of neural computation that have proven highly effective, still lack a natural notion of time, with neural units in ANNs exchanging analog values in a frame-based manner, representing a computationally and energetically inefficient form of communication that contrasts sharply with biological neurons communicating sparingly and efficiently using binary spikes. While artificial Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) can be constructed by replacing the units of an ANN with spiking neurons, the current performance remains far from that of deep ANNs on hard benchmarks, and these SNNs use much higher firing rates compared to their biological counterparts, thereby limiting their efficiency. Here we show how spiking neurons employing an efficient form of neural coding can be used to construct SNNs that match high-performance ANNs and exceed state-of-the-art in SNNs on important benchmarks, while requiring much lower average firing rates. For this, we use spike-time coding based on the firing rate limiting adaptation phenomenon observed in biological spiking neurons, a phenomenon that can be captured in adapting spiking neuron models, for which we derive the effective transfer function. Neural units in ANNs trained with this transfer function can be substituted directly with adaptive spiking neurons, with the resulting Adaptive SNNs (AdSNNs) being capable of carrying out inference in deep neural networks using up to an order of magnitude fewer spikes compared to previous SNNs. Adaptive spike-time coding additionally allows for the dynamic control of neural coding precision, and we show how a simple model of arousal in AdSNNs further halves the average required firing rate, with this notion naturally extending to other forms of attention. AdSNNs thus hold promise as a novel and efficient model for neural computation that naturally fits to temporally continuous and asynchronous applications, offering substantial improvements in computational efficiency.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::33: Context. LQ Hya, being one of the most frequently studied young solar analogue stars, has recently been observed to show intriguing behaviour through analysing long-term photometry, whereby during 2003--2009 a coherent spot structure migrating in the rotational frame has been reported by various authors, though since that time the star has entered a chaotic state where coherent structures seem to have disappeared and rapid phase jumps of the photometric minima occur irregularly over time. Aims. LQ Hya, being one of the stars included in the SOFIN/FIES long-term monitoring campaign extending over 25 years, is the subject of this study where we publish new temperature maps for the star during 2006--2017, thereby covering the chaotic state of the star. Methods. We use a Doppler imaging technique to derive surface temperature maps from high-resolution spectra. Results. From the mean temperatures of the Doppler maps, which we have carefully analysed, we see a weak but systematic increase in the surface temperature of the star, this being consistent with the simultaneously increasing photometric magnitude. During nearly all observing seasons we see a high-latitude spot structure which is clearly nonaxisymmetric, the phase behaviour of this structure being very chaotic but agreeing reasonably well with the photometry. Equatorial spots are also frequently seen, but many of them we interpret to be artefacts due to the poor to moderate phase coverage that we obtained. Conclusions. Even during the chaotic phase of the star, the spot topology has remained very similar to the higher activity epochs with more coherent and long-lived spot structures, such that we see high-latitude and equatorial spot activity while the mid latitude range still remains most often void of spots. We interpret the erratic jumps and drifts in phase of the photometric minima to be caused by changes in the high-latitude spot structure rather than the equatorial spots.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::34: Context: Hydrogenation reactions, being among the most important surface reactions occurring on interstellar ices, are expected to play a crucial role in astrochemistry. However, solid state astrochemical laboratory data examining reactions of H-atoms with common interstellar ice constituents are largely lacking. Aims: The goal of our laboratory work is to determine whether and how carbon dioxide (CO2), formic acid (HCOOH) and acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) react with H-atoms in the solid state at low temperatures, while also deriving reaction rates and production yields. Methods: Pure CO2, HCOOH and CH3CHO interstellar ice analogues are bombarded by H-atoms in an ultra-high vacuum experiment, with the ices being monitored by reflection absorption infrared spectroscopy and the reaction products detected in the gas phase through temperature programmed desorption to determine the destruction and formation yields as well as the corresponding reaction rates. Results: Within the sensitivity of our set-up we conclude that H-atom bombardment of pure CO2 and HCOOH ice does not result in detectable reaction products, the upper limits on the reaction rates being less or equal to 7e(-17) cm^2/s, which make it unlikely that these species play a major role in the formation of more complex organics in interstellar ices due to reactions with H-atoms. In contrast, CH3CHO does react with H-atoms, with at most 20% being hydrogenated to ethanol (C2H5OH) while a second reaction route leads to the break-up of the C-C bond to form solid state CH4 (~20%) as well as H2CO and CH3OH (15-50%). The methane production yield, expected to be equal to the summed yield of H2CO and CH3OH, suggests that CH4 most likely evaporates partly after formation due to the high exothermicity of the reaction. The reaction rates for CH3CHO destruction depend on ice temperature and not on ice thickness.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::35: The methodology of funnel control, which was introduced in the early 2000s, has developed since then in many respects, achieving a level of mathematical maturity that is balanced by practical applications. Its fundamental tenet is the attainment of prescribed transient and asymptotic behaviour for continuous-time controlled dynamical processes, encompassing linear and nonlinear systems that are described by functional differential equations, differential-algebraic systems, and partial differential equations. Considered are classes of systems specified by structural properties—such as relative degree and stable internal dynamics—of the systems only, while the precise systems' data are in general unknown, the latter reflecting the property that in general any model of a dynamical process is not precise. Prespecified are: a funnel shaped through the choice of a smooth function and freely chosen by the designer, a fairly large class of smooth reference signals, and a system class satisfying certain structural properties. The aim is to design, based on the structural assumptions and the input and output information only, a single 'simple' control strategy—called the funnel controller—so that its application to any system of the given class and to any reference signal results in feasibility of the funnel control objective, meaning that solutions of the closed-loop system do not exhibit blow-up in finite time, all variables are bounded, and—most importantly—the evolution of the error between the system's output and the reference signal remains within the prespecified funnel. In the Introduction, we describe the genesis of funnel control, after which we investigate diverse system classes amenable to funnel control. Funnel control is shown for systems with arbitrary relative degree and systems described by partial differential equations, before finally discussing input constraints and applications.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::36: With the increasing diversity of Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks, which continue to evolve in sophistication, designing a fully protected network is becoming extremely challenging. For instance, Stealthy Link Flooding Attack (SLFA), being a variant of DDoS attacks that strives to block access to a target area by flooding a small set of links, has been shown to bypass traditional DDoS defense mechanisms that organizations typically deploy. One potential solution for tackling such SLFAs involves applying Moving Target Defense (MTD) techniques, wherein network settings are dynamically changed to confuse and deceive attackers, thus making it highly expensive to launch a successful attack against the protected infrastructure. However, since MTD comes with some overhead to the network, finding the best strategy—determining when and to what extent it should be applied—has been a major challenge facing network administrators. The strategy is significantly influenced by the attacker's behavior, which is often difficult to guess or predict accurately. In this work, we address the challenge of obtaining the optimal MTD strategy that effectively mitigates SLFAs while incurring minimal overhead to network operations. We design the problem as a signaling game, considering the network defender and the attacker as players engaged in strategic interaction. A belief function is established throughout the engagement between the attacker and the defender during this SLFA campaign, which is then utilized to pick the best response and action for each player participating in the game. We analyze the game model and derive a defense mechanism based on the equilibria that emerge from the game dynamics. We evaluate the technique on a Mininet-based network environment where an attacker is performing SLFAs while a defender applies MTD based on equilibria of the game. The results show that our signaling game-based dynamic defense mechanism can provide a similar level of protection against SLFAs like the extensive MTD solution, however, causing significantly reduced overhead.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::37: Multi-fidelity (MF) methods, which are gaining popularity for enhancing surrogate modeling and design optimization by incorporating data from various low-fidelity (LF) models, have traditionally assumed a fixed dataset, though adaptive sampling methods that dynamically allocate resources among fidelity models can achieve higher efficiency in exploring and exploiting the design space. However, most existing MF methods, relying on the hierarchical assumption of fidelity levels, fail to capture the intercorrelation between multiple fidelity levels and utilize it to quantify the value of future samples and navigate the adaptive sampling. To address this hurdle, we propose a framework that is hinged on a latent embedding for different fidelity models and the associated pre-posterior analysis to explicitly utilize their correlation for adaptive sampling. In this framework, each infill sampling iteration, including two steps, first identifies the location of interest with the greatest potential improvement using the high-fidelity (HF) model, then searches for the next sample across all fidelity levels that maximize the improvement per unit cost at the location identified in the first step. This is made possible by a single Latent Variable Gaussian Process (LVGP) model that maps different fidelity models into an interpretable latent space, capturing their correlations without assuming hierarchical fidelity levels. The LVGP, enabling us to assess how LF sampling candidates will affect HF response with pre-posterior analysis, determines the next sample with the best benefit-to-cost ratio. Through test cases, we demonstrate that the proposed method, outperforming the benchmark methods in both MF global fitting (GF) and Bayesian Optimization (BO) problems in convergence rate and robustness, offers the flexibility to switch between GF and BO by simply changing the acquisition function, thereby providing researchers with a versatile tool for optimization tasks.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::38: Cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum, being secondary lesions induced by significant increases in cytokine levels occurring in the brain, are associated with subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), although their clinical significance in SAH patients remains unclear. We retrospectively analyzed SAH patients who were treated in our hospital, evaluating between-group differences in the backgrounds, clinical findings, and outcomes between SAH patients who developed cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum and those who did not, further comparing patients who achieved good outcomes with those who had poor outcomes. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was used to identify risk factors for poor clinical outcomes. Having analyzed 159 SAH patients, we found that 17 patients (10.7%) had cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum. Patients with cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum were more likely to be in a severe condition (World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies grading IV-V: odds ratio [OR], 4.53; 95% confidence interval [95% CI]: 1.60-12.84; p = 0.0042) and have an intraventricular (OR, 5.98; 95% CI: 1.32-27.13; p = 0.0054) or an intraparenchymal hematoma (OR, 3.62; 95% CI: 1.25-10.45; p = 0.023). Patients with cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum had a greater propensity of a poor outcome 3 months after onset (modified Rankin Scale score 0-2: OR, 0.22; 95% CI: 0.07-0.66; p = 0.0043), while multivariate analysis confirmed that cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum increased the risk of a poor outcome (OR, 4.39; 95% CI: 1.06-18.1; p = 0.037). The development of cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum may be related to the extent of hematomas in SAH patients, and although they are usually reversible lesions, the development of cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum may be a predictor of poor outcomes in SAH patients.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::39: Information on appropriate protocols for sedation of Nordestino donkeys, being scarce, prompted an evaluation of the sedative and cardiorespiratory effects produced by low doses of intravenous (i.v.) xylazine administered with and without acepromazine in 'Nordestino' donkeys. Seven healthy female Nordestino donkeys (150 ± 18 kg) were included in this blinded, randomised, crossover experiment, during which four treatments were administered, consisting of two i.v. injections given at baseline (T0, 1st injection) and 15 min later (T15, 2nd injection). Treatments included acepromazine 0.05 mg/kg bwt + saline (AS), saline + xylazine 0.5 mg/kg bwt (SX0.5), acepromazine + xylazine 0.25 mg/kg bwt (AX0.25) or acepromazine + xylazine 0.5 mg/kg bwt (AX0.5), with sedative and cardiorespiratory parameters being evaluated before T0 and 15, 20, 30, 45, 60, 75 and 90 min after treatment. Degree [height of head above ground (HHAG)] and quality of sedation [ataxia, responses to stimuli and visual analogue scale (VAS) scoring] and respiratory rate were evaluated by the main investigator in situ, while heart rate was measured by an assistant investigator, and three experienced evaluators assessed videos for ataxia and responses to stimuli. Normal data were analysed by repeated measures ANOVA, and non-normal by Kruskal-Wallis (P<0.05). HHAG, being lower than baseline for 15 min after xylazine administration in AX0.25 and for 30 min in SX0.5 and AX0.5 groups, demonstrated dose-dependent effects. All treatments with xylazine increased VAS and ataxia scores in situ for 15 min after xylazine administration, showing no differences between groups, whereas ataxia scores in situ were higher in SX0.5 and AX0.5 groups than AS for 15 and 30 min after xylazine administration, respectively. The study, lacking a negative control group (saline-saline), nevertheless demonstrated that acepromazine added to xylazine at 0.25 mg/kg bwt produced briefer and milder sedation than xylazine at 0.5 mg/kg bwt.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::40: ALMA-IMF imaged 15 massive protoclusters down to a resolution of 2 kau scales, identifying about 1000 star-forming cores whose mass and luminosity, being fundamental physical characteristics, are difficult to determine, a problem that is greatly exacerbated at the distances >2 kpc of ALMA-IMF protoclusters. Having combined new datasets and radiative transfer modeling, we characterized these cores by estimating their mass-averaged temperature and the masses that these estimates imply. For 1/6 of the sample, we measured the bolometric luminosities, implementing deblending corrections when necessary, using spectral energy distribution (SED) analysis obtained with the PPMAP Bayesian procedure, which aims to preserve the best angular resolution of the input data. We extrapolated the luminosity and dust temperature images provided by PPMAP at 2.5" resolution to estimate those of individual cores, which were identified at higher angular resolution, applying approximate radiative transfer relationships between the luminosity of a protostar and the temperature of its surrounding envelope and between the external heating of prestellar cores and their temperatures. For the first time, we provide data-informed estimates of dust temperatures for 883 cores identified with ALMA-IMF: 17-31 K and 28-79 K (5th and 95th percentiles, up to 127 K) for the 617 prestellar and 266 protostellar cores, respectively, while also measuring protostellar luminosities spanning 20-80 000 Lsun. For hot cores, we estimated systematically lower temperatures than studies based on complex organic molecules, establishing a mass-luminosity evolutionary diagram for the first time at the core spatial resolution and for a large sample of high-mass protostellar cores. The ALMA-IMF data favor a scenario in which protostars accrete their mass from a larger mass reservoir than their host cores.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::41: The aim of the present study was to investigate the role of microRNA (miR)-27a-3p in osteoarthritis (OA), employing reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction and western blotting to determine the expression of miR-27a-3p and aggrecanase-2 (ADAMTS5) in cartilage tissues obtained from patients with OA and healthy controls, as well as in interleukin (IL)-1beta-treated primary human chondrocytes. Primary human chondrocytes, having been transfected with miR-27a-3p, were subjected to a luciferase reporter assay, which was used to validate the direct contact between miR-27a-3p and its putative binding site located in the 3'-untranslated region ADAMTS5 mRNA. Furthermore, the effects of IL-1beta-induced activation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and nuclear factor (NF)-kappaB on miR-27a-3p were evaluated using specific inhibitors. The results revealed that the level of miR-27a-3p was reduced in OA cartilage tissues compared with those of normal controls, while decreased miR-27a-3p and increased ADAMTS5 expression was observed in a time- and dose-dependent manner in chondrocytes treated with IL-1beta. Furthermore, overexpression of miR-27a-3p suppressed the expression of ADAMTS5 in human chondrocytes induced by IL-1beta, with miR-27a-3p overexpression also decreasing the luciferase activity of the wild-type ADAMTS5 reporter plasmid. Mutation of the miR-27a-3p binding site in the 3'-untranslated region of ADAMTS5 mRNA abolished the miR-27a-3p-mediated repression of reporter activity, while the use of specific inhibitors demonstrated that IL-1beta may regulate miR-27a-3p expression via NF-kappaB and MAPK signaling pathways in chondrocytes. The present study concluded that miR-27a-3p, being downregulated in human OA and suppressed by IL-1beta, functions as a crucial regulator of ADAMTS5 in OA chondrocytes, with IL-1beta-mediated suppression of miR-27a-3p activity possibly occurring via the MAPK and NF-kappaB pathways, thereby providing a novel strategy for clinical treatment of OA caused by upregulation of miR-27a-3p.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::42: Space weathering, which is a process that changes the surface of airless planetary bodies, involves prime agents including solar wind irradiation and micrometeoroid bombardment. These processes, altering planetary reflectance spectra, often modify their compositional diagnostic features. In this work, focusing on simulating and comparing the spectral changes caused by solar wind irradiation and by micrometeoroid bombardment, we aimed to gain a better understanding of these individual space weathering processes. We used olivine and pyroxene pellets, serving as proxies for planetary materials. To simulate solar wind irradiation, we used hydrogen, helium, and argon ions with energies ranging from 5 to 40 keV and fluences of up to $10^{18}$ particles/cm$^2$, while to simulate micrometeoroid bombardment we used individual femtosecond laser pulses. We analysed the corresponding evolution of different spectral parameters, which we determined by applying the Modified Gaussian Model, and we also conducted principal component analysis. The original mineralogy of the surface, as seen from the diverse evolution of the spectral slope of olivine and pyroxene upon irradiation, influences the spectral evolution more than the weathering agent does. The spectral slope changes seen in olivine, being consistent with observations of A-type asteroids, contrast with the moderate to no slope changes observed in pyroxene, which are consistent with asteroid (4) Vesta. We also observed some differences in the spectral effects induced by the two weathering agents. Ions simulating solar wind, having a smaller influence on longer wavelengths of the spectra than laser irradiation simulating micrometeoroid impacts, reflect what is most likely due to the different penetration depths of ions and laser pulses. Our results, suggesting that in some instances it might be possible to distinguish between the contributions of the two agents on a weathered surface, provide valuable insights.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::43: HEALPix, which was developed by Górski et al. in 2005, has become the de-facto standard for Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data storage and analysis, being widely used in current and upcoming CMB experiments that continue to generate increasingly large datasets. Almost all the datasets that are housed in the Legacy Archive for Microwave Background Data Analysis (LAMBDA) use HEALPix as their format of choice, reflecting its widespread adoption across the community. Visualizing the data plays an important role in research, leading to the development of several toolsets designed to work with HEALPix maps, most notably the original Fortran facilities and Python integration achieved through healpy. Given the current state of GPU performance, it has now become possible to visualize extremely large maps in real time on devices as portable as a laptop or a tablet. The HEALPix Viewer described here, having been developed specifically for macOS, takes full advantage of GPU acceleration to handle extremely large datasets in real time with remarkable efficiency. Compiling natively on both Intel and Arm64 architectures, it uses the Metal framework for high-performance GPU computations that maximize hardware capabilities. The aim of this project is to reduce the effort required for interactive data exploration while simultaneously minimizing the time overhead associated with producing publication-quality maps for dissemination. Drag and drop integration with presentation software such as Keynote and Powerpoint makes creating presentations easy and streamlined. The main codebase, written in Swift—a modern and efficient compiled language—delegates high-performance computing parts entirely to GPU, incorporating a few inserts in C that interface with the cfitsio library for input and output operations. The graphical user interface, written in SwiftUI, employs a new declarative UI framework based on Swift. Most common spherical projections and colormaps are supported out of the box, and the available source code makes customization easy. Overall performance improves on the current Python software stack by factors ranging from 3 to 180x depending on the specific task.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::44: To compare the cervical shear wave elastography (SWE), which was performed by using transvaginal ultrasound (TVS), between twin and singleton pregnant women, this prospective cohort study was conducted involving the twin and singleton pregnant women who attended the antenatal care at Ramathibodi Hospital, Bangkok, Thailand. The participants who met the inclusion criteria underwent serial measurements of the shear wave speed (SWS) by using TVS at early, mid-, and third trimester, allowing for evaluation of the changes in SWS with advancing gestational age between twin and singleton pregnancies. The gestational age at delivery and spontaneous preterm delivery rate, both being important clinical outcomes, were also analyzed. A total of 36 twin pregnancies and 38 singleton pregnancies were analyzed, revealing no significant difference in baseline characteristics, except the age of participants, with twin pregnancies showing 33.1±4.6 years and singleton pregnancies showing 29.9±5.4 years (p-value = 0.006). The cervical SWS, which decreased with advancing gestational age in both twin and singleton pregnancy, demonstrated a statistically significant difference of cervical SWS at the lower point in mid-trimester, with twin pregnancies measuring 2.27±0.4 and singleton pregnancies measuring 2.71±0.6 m/s (p-value = 0.001). However, no significant difference in cervical SWS at the upper point and the lower point in the early and third trimester was demonstrated. Even though the gestational age at delivery between both groups revealed a significant difference, with twin pregnancies delivering at 35.9±2.8 and singleton pregnancies at 37.6±2.9 wk. (p-value = 0.008), the spontaneous preterm delivery rate did not differ significantly, being 22.2% for twin pregnancies and 15.8% for singleton pregnancies (p-value = 0.483). The mid-trimester cervical SWS measurement at the lower point detects the difference in cervical softness between twin pregnancies and singleton pregnancies, suggesting that the cervical SWS might be an additional option for monitoring the change in cervical softness in twin pregnancies.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::45: Chromosome number, being a key feature of the higher-order organization of the genome, plays a fundamental role in evolution through changes that occur in chromosome number. Dysploid gains and losses in chromosome number, as well as polyploidization events, may drive reproductive isolation and lineage diversification. The recent development of probabilistic models of chromosome number evolution, which occurred in the groundbreaking work by Mayrose et al. (2010, ChromEvol), have enabled the inference of ancestral chromosome numbers over molecular phylogenies and generated new interest in studying the role that chromosome changes play in evolution. However, the ChromEvol approach, which assumes all changes occur anagenetically along branches, does not model events that are specifically cladogenetic. Cladogenetic changes may be expected if chromosome changes result in reproductive isolation. Here we present a new class of models of chromosome number evolution, called ChromoSSE, that incorporate both anagenetic and cladogenetic change. The ChromoSSE models, allowing us to determine the mode of chromosome number evolution, address whether chromosome evolution is occurring primarily within lineages, primarily at lineage splitting, or in clade-specific combinations of both. Furthermore, we can estimate the location and timing of possible chromosome speciation events over the phylogeny. We implemented ChromoSSE in a Bayesian statistical framework, specifically in the software RevBayes, to accommodate uncertainty in parameter estimates while leveraging the full power of likelihood based methods. We tested ChromoSSE's accuracy with simulations and re-examined chromosomal evolution in Aristolochia, Carex section Spirostachyae, Helianthus, Mimulus sensu lato (s.l.), and Primula section Aleuritia, finding evidence for clade-specific combinations of anagenetic and cladogenetic dysploid and polyploid modes of chromosome evolution. [Anagenetic; Bayes factors; chromosome evolution; chromosome speciation; chromoSSE; cladogenetic; dysploidy; phylogenetic models; polyploidy; reversible-jump Markov chain Monte Carlo; whole genome duplication.]
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::46: We present results of our time variability studies of Mg II and Al III absorption lines in a sample of 22 Low Ionization Broad Absorption Line QSOs (LoBAL QSOs) at 0.2 <= zem <= 2.1, using the 2m telescope at IUCAA Girawali Observatory over a time-scale ranging from 10 days to 7.69 years in the QSO's rest frame. The spectra, being analysed in conjunction with photometric light curves from Catalina Real-Time Transient Survey, reveal that long time-scale (i.e >= 1 year) absorption line variability is seen in 8 cases (36% systems), while only 4 of them (i.e 18% systems) show variability over short time-scales (i.e < 1 year). We notice a tendency of highly variable LoBAL QSOs to have high ejection velocity, low equivalent width and low redshift, noting that the detection rate of variability in LoBAL QSOs showing Fe fine-structure lines (FeLoBAL QSOs) is less than that seen in non-Fe LoBAL QSOs. Absorption line variability, being more frequently detected in QSOs having continuum dominated by Fe emission lines compared to rest of the QSOs, suggests that confirming these trends with a bigger sample will give vital clues for understanding the physical distinction between different BAL QSO sub-classes.
