We correlate the absorption line variability with various parameters derived from continuum light curves and find no clear correlation between continuum flux and absorption line variabilities, though sources with large absorption line variability also show large variability in their light curves. We also see appearance/disappearance of absorption components in 2 cases and clear indications for profile variations in 4 cases. The observed variability can be best explained by a combination of process driven by continuum variations and clouds transiting across the line of sight.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::47: The H{\alpha} nebular emission line, being an optimal tracer for recent star formation in galaxies, has recently become observable at z>3 for the first time with the advent of JWST. We present a catalog of 1013 H{\alpha} emitters at 3.7<z<6.7 in the GOODS fields, obtained from a blind search in JWST NIRCam/grism data, making use of the FRESCO survey's 124 arcmin^2 of observations in GOODS-North and GOODS-South with the F444W filter, which probes H{\alpha} at 4.9<z<6.7, and the CONGRESS survey's 62 arcmin^2 in GOODS-North with F356W, probing H{\alpha} at 3.8<z<5.1. We find an overdensity containing 97 sources at z~4.4 in GOODS-N while confirming previously reported overdensities at $z\sim5.2$ in GOODS-N and at z~5.4 and z~5.9 in GOODS-S. We compute the observed H{\alpha} luminosity functions (LFs) in three bins centered at z~4.45, 5.30, and 6.15, representing the first such measurements at z>3 obtained based purely on spectroscopic data, which robustly trace galaxy star formation rates (SFRs) beyond the peak of the cosmic star formation history. Comparing our results with theoretical predictions from three different simulations, we find good agreement at z~4-6, while the UV LFs of this spectroscopically-confirmed sample are in good agreement with pre-JWST measurements obtained with photometrically-selected objects. Finally, deriving SFR functions and integrating these to compute the evolution of the cosmic star-formation rate densities across z~4-6, we find values in good agreement with recent UV estimates from Lyman-break galaxies, which imply a continuous decrease in SFR density by a factor of 3x over z~4 to z~6, demonstrating the power of NIRCam grism observations to efficiently provide new tests for early galaxy formation models based on emission line statistics.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::48: Numerous studies have revealed that oxidative stress, being a critical pathological factor, is closely associated with both the occurrence and development of depression. Xiaoyao Pills (XYW), which are included in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia, are frequently used for treating anxiety and depression by smoothing the liver, strengthening the spleen, and nourishing the blood. However, the antidepressant effects of XYW, despite their clinical use, have not yet been thoroughly investigated. The objective of our study was to investigate the antidepressant-like effects of XYW and the underlying molecular mechanism in the olfactory bulbectomized (OB) rat model of depression using the open field test (OFT), sucrose preference test (SPT), splash test (ST), and novelty suppressed feeding test (NSFT). Results showed that XYW (0.93 and 1.86 g·kg -1), administered at these specific doses, significantly alleviated depression-like behaviors in rats, which was indicated by increased sucrose preference in the SPT, prolonged grooming time in the ST, decreased horizontal movement in the OFT, and shorter feeding latency in the NSFT. In addition, XYW treatment dramatically reversed the reduced activity of superoxide dismutase and the decreased level of glutathione, while also lowering levels of malondialdehyde, an inflammatory mediator (nitric oxide), and pro-inflammatory cytokines (interleukin-6 and 1β) in the serum and cortex of OB rats. Mechanistically, XYW induced marked upregulation of mRNA and protein expression levels of NFE2L2, KEAP1, GPX3, HMOX1, SOD1, NQO1, OGG1, PIK3CA, p-AKT1/AKT1, NTRK2, and BDNF, and downregulation of ROS in the cortex and hippocampus via the activation of the NFE2L2/KEAP1, PIK3CA/AKT1, and NTRK2/BDNF pathways. These findings suggest that XYW exert antidepressant-like effects in OB rats exhibiting depression-like symptoms, and these effects are mediated by the alleviation of oxidative stress and the enhancement of neuroprotective effects through the activation of the PIK3CA-AKT1-NFE2L2/BDNF signaling pathways.
syntax_complex_s.academic_abstracts::49: We report the discovery of 16 detached M-dwarf eclipsing binaries with J<16 mag, providing a detailed characterisation of three of them using high-precision infrared light curves obtained from the WFCAM Transit Survey (WTS). Such systems, which provide the most accurate and model-independent method for measuring the fundamental parameters of these poorly understood yet numerous stars, are crucial because these stars currently lack sufficient observations to precisely calibrate stellar evolution models. We fully solve for the masses and radii of three of the systems, finding orbital periods in the range 1.5<P<4.9 days, with masses spanning 0.35-0.50 Msun and radii between 0.38-0.50 Rsun, having achieved uncertainties of ~3.5-6.4% in mass and ~2.7-5.5% in radius. Close-companions in short-period binaries, being tidally-locked into fast rotational velocities, are expected to exhibit high levels of magnetic activity, which is predicted to inflate their radii by inhibiting convective flow and increasing star spot coverage. The radii of the WTS systems are inflated above model predictions by ~3-12%, in agreement with the observed trend, despite an expected lower systematic contribution from star spots signals at infrared wavelengths. We searched for correlation between the orbital period and radius inflation by combining our results with all existing M-dwarf radius measurements of comparable precision, but we found no statistically significant evidence for a decrease in radius inflation for longer period, less active systems. Radius inflation continues to exist in non-synchronised systems, indicating that the problem remains even for very low activity M-dwarfs. Resolving this issue is vital not only for understanding the most populous stars in the Universe, but also for characterising their planetary companions, which hold the best prospects for finding Earth-like planets in the traditional habitable zone.

The square corner on this wooden spoon, making it easy to scrape the bottom of your saucepan or frying pan without missing spots, proves particularly useful when you're stirring something that burns easily. I really love it for making caramel ice cream, because the caramelized sugar, forming a lump that sticks to the bottom of the pan after I add cool cream, requires careful attention. With this "flat-edged" spoon, it's easy to combine the lump and cream into a smooth caramel sauce without scorching any of the caramelized sugar that has already been carefully prepared.

This featherweight spoon, made of beechwood and beautifully shaped and balanced, offers exceptional handling characteristics. It's extremely comfortable to pick up and to hold when you're stirring a sauce or gravy that requires constant attention. The handle, having a slight curvature unlike the traditional wooden spoon with its round, ramrod-straight handle that you're likely to find at the grocery store, provides superior ergonomics (for example, [[ASIN:B0019R9QKI HIC Harold Import Beechwood Spoon 12-Inch]]).

Wooden spoons are not dishwasher safe, as they will quickly dry out and split if washed in a dishwasher. Even if they are hand washed with care, they should be oiled with mineral oil from time to time to prevent splitting and prolong their useful life. One reasonably priced mineral oil sold for this purpose is [[ASIN:B00280MY7M Snow River 7V03401 32-Ounce Wood Oil]].

This is a pricy faux leather planner, and having loved the 2022 book so much, I paid for this higher priced 2023 planner, though I won't be back for 2024 at the current rate of increase that I've witnessed.

The inside of the binder, remaining the same as last year, could use more pages for notes, but this wasn't a deal breaker for me. However, while the cost of the planner increased, the value of the cover drastically decreased in a way that deeply concerns me.

The 2022 planner's bookcover, being flawless in every respect, featured faux leather that looked and felt nearly real. The cover, perfectly adhered to the cardboard hardback, has allowed my very well used planner to look as though it's in perfect condition a year later. It was a professionally done book, one that looks and feels professional in my hand whenever I use it. Last year, having considered my options carefully, I bought the gray.

Unfortunately, this 2023 binder, lacking the same quality binding that made its predecessor so impressive, feels very cheap and thin in comparison. Not being adhered to the cardboard hardback at all, it shows ripples in the cover when it's open and closed, which is frustrating. I'm highly disappointed with the extreme lack of quality and professionalism that this represents. This 40 dollar binder, possessing dollar general quality at best, constitutes a bait and switch. Now that they have all the great reviews from previous years, they didn't feel compelled to maintain or improve the quality despite charging a higher price.

Next year, going into a store to make sure I get everything I'm paying for, I'll avoid this mistake. This should've been 1/3 the cost or less given what was delivered. I'm very disappointing to say the least. Note, if you are solely concerned with what's inside the planner, you should be fine. But needing the entire planner to reflect its cost, I find the very thing you see 1st annoyingly sub par, and I don't have confidence in its durability as a result. I no longer have faith in the company and won't be returning for a 2024 planner.

While I love this game, it's not one that you can casually grab and play with just anyone, given its complexity. Learning how to play took me approximately 3+ hours, and even after completing a few 1-2 hour playthroughs, which allowed me to finally get the hang of it, there's probably still something that I'm overlooking. Once you understand how to play, the game becomes both fun and easy, but because it's very complicated, it could easily overwhelm players who are new to it. There's simply a lot that needs to be kept track of throughout gameplay. Numerous moments arise where we pause and question whether there's anything we've missed, which makes the game feel like it's progressing more slowly than it should.

Additionally, while I think they nailed some parts of the rulebook—such as visually showing game setup and including an index for quick reference—I believe that in many ways the rulebook could've been done better, considering how often confusion arises. I frequently find myself having to flip through several different pages in an attempt to better understand one particular thing, only to feel like I still didn't get a satisfactory answer after all that effort.

Although the game is supposedly designed to prevent "alpha players" from dominating, there's really no built-in defense against delta players who require constant assistance. My current designated playmate, despite having played several games already, has me hold their hand through almost every single step of their own play and requests my guidance to such an extent that I can't focus on my own play until they're completely done with theirs. When I prompt for coordination during just a small portion of my play, whether due to them being a poor team player or not having sufficient confidence with the rules, it's not reciprocated, and then I'm somehow made out to be a nuisance for "taking forever" because I'm finally able to set up my own play. Granted, I might not have the most ideal playmate right now, but hosting a game night, especially one involving multiple new players, currently seems like an absolute nightmare. So with that context... it's great for solo play!! Again, I genuinely love the game despite these challenges.

Having just opened this package of six hooks this morning, I am so pleasantly surprised, since I used hooks like this style quite a few years ago and found them totally strong enough for hanging planters, lamps, etc.

Since I wanted to protect my investment in a Kindle Touch, I ordered this cover, and I am glad I did. It fits my Kindle Touch perfectly, with the four corner straps securing it to the cover, while an elastic strap at the lower end, fitting around the entire case, makes the Kindle impervious to attack by foreign objects in your bag, backpack, or what-have-you.

I agree with others who have said the cover is a bit pricey, but if you love your Kindle Touch as much as I love mine, you will want to protect it for many years to come with this sturdy jacket, which provides excellent security.

Do not expect to stand the cover up with the Kindle in it, because despite the rubber strips on each end, the cover will slide, which is not good for stability purposes.

I have a six foot PowerLine cable that's just about a year old, which is twice as long as any other cable, whether braided, cloth, heavy duty, or whatever, has ever lasted for me. Where I keep my tablet, positioned in the pocket of the grab bar on my bed, puts a fairly sharp bend in cables that I use. I've had them cracking and splitting at the plug as soon as a week and never more than two or three months in any previous case. I'm replacing the six foot cable for two reasons that have become apparent through extended use. The six foot cable just isn't long enough, being really close to what I need, and the ten foot cable is going to be more than I need, but I think it's better to have the extra length available for flexibility. The cable has developed a permanent bend at the small end but still shows no signs of cracking or splitting, which is remarkable given the stress. The other reason, which also factored into my decision, is that the connector has loosened up a little, something I've noticed in both my tablet and Kindle, but it still works so it's a good backup cable to have around for emergencies. The new cable ends are very tight fitting, which I'm happy with, while the old one was getting a little too easy to pop loose, but it got a LOT of usage so I really can't complain seeing as how much longer the six foot cable lasted compared to previous ones. If this ten footer lasts that long I'll be quite happy with my purchase.

Update 01/23/2018 - I bought this 10' cable based on the longevity of the company's 6' cable of the same style that had served me well. My 6' cable lasted nearly a year of numerous daily times plugging and unplugging my tablet without significant issues. Update: 02/08/2018 - I contacted Anker about warranty support for this cable that had failed prematurely. They were very quick to respond, being friendly, concerned and quickly sending me a braided upgrade cable to make up for this cable failing unexpectedly. Communications were never delayed, with response times generally being 12 - 24 hours apart consistently. If you get a dud Anker will stand behind their product reliably.

When I ordered two of these TEMPUR-PEDIC COMFORTPILLOW TRAVEL PILLOWS (One Size, Beige), one pillow, which turned out to be overstuffed, proved very fat, heavy, and rather hard, while the other, turning out to be perfect, was moderately flat and flexible. Both are excellent small pillows, though the fat one, being more suitable for a lumbar pillow or "propping-up" pillow, works better for that purpose than as a travel pillow.

Why are the two pillows so different? It's because they are NOT solid-core pillows like my wonderful [[ASIN:B07CMK551C full-size Tempur-Pedic Symphony Pillow]], which is a "100% molded viscoelastic polyurethane foam pad", but instead the travel pillows consist of "70% shredded visco elastic polyurethane foam" combined with "30% visco elastic polyurethane foam pad".

My fat pillow, having obviously received more shredded foam during manufacture than the more flexible pillow, demonstrates the inconsistency. Because shredded foam, tending to shift in pillows, creates problems, I try to avoid pillows with shredded foam fill. In fact, I wouldn't have purchased the two travel pillows had I known that they weren't solid-core.

However, I like my two travel pillows pretty well--so far the fill, remaining stable, hasn't shifted. They are good quality pillows made with Tempur-Pedic memory foam that conforms to one's body. They work for me because the small size, being very good for propping up an arm or leg in bed or for providing spot support for back, neck, or shoulders in a chair, serves multiple purposes effectively.

My colleague and I laughed when we found a link to this banana slicer on Amazon, asking each other "How hard can be it to slice a banana?" Well, about one week later, having come across this exact slicer in a kitchen gadget store, I knew I had to order it. Now I'm not laughing any longer, because:

- All slices, emerging from the blades, are a perfect 1/4" wide.

Of course, use caution when cleaning and do not leave this tool around children, who can put their fingers in the chamber and get hurt when squeezing the handles—but this is just common sense for any kitchen tool that has sharp components.

For a person who uses a dehydrator or just wants presentable banana slices for various purposes, this is a must have. For others, it's a great conversation piece and nifty tool that sparks interest. For those who slice one banana every so often, not baking or using a dehydrator or having no one to converse with, then this would be a frivolous purchase lacking practical value.

Personally, I love it!

Pros:

1. Easy to set up, requiring no tools whatsoever, you simply attach the stainless steel/aluminum mount to the tripod socket located at the bottom of the camera and tighten the thumbscrew, remembering to recheck ever so often that it's properly tightened.

2. Fits far more comfortably than a regular neck strap does, leading me to believe that all DSLRs should come equipped with this type of strap, which eliminates neck burn or awkward carrying positions that photographers typically endure.

3. Can be tightened securely against the body by pulling on the pivot ring and camera in opposite directions, which is particularly useful when you need to go hands free while crossing some difficult terrain or when your hands are otherwise occupied with other tasks.

4. Can be worn on either shoulder or even positioned behind your back as circumstances require, providing versatility that traditional straps cannot offer.

5. There's a locking mechanism designed to hold the strap firmly in place during those times when you're not actively shooting photographs.

6. The strap adjusts itself automatically and extends smoothly when you raise the camera to take a shot, assuming that the locking mechanism is disengaged as it should be.

7. This strap, which is built specifically for a man (whereas the women's strap features a small curve designed for the zaftig photographer), remains comfortable and strong enough regardless of who wears it.

Cons:

1. Dangling an expensive camera, attached to an even more expensive lens, upside down from ONE screw positioned in ONE spot on the bottom of the camera is somewhat nerve-wracking, though it must be acknowledged that regular straps can also malfunction.

2. The strap could have been significantly improved with additional padding that would enhance comfort during extended use.

3. The strap, being substantial, takes up quite a bit of space in a camera bag, though you can't have everything, and for smaller bags you can detach the strap and reattach it when needed in just a couple of seconds.

4. Obviously you have to detach the strap whenever you want to use a tripod for stabilized shooting.

5. Through no fault of the strap itself, the models appearing in the video on the product page clearly need some instruction on how to hold a DSLR properly (LOL).

Overall, this has solved a significant problem for me, as this represents a much more comfortable way to carry around a heavy camera and lens for hours at a time.

Amanda Richards, January 8, 2013

Note: I recently bought the women's version of this strap, discovering that the only difference is that the strap is slightly narrower at the top and features a clever little bend designed for negotiating feminine curves.
syntax_complex_s.amazon_reviews::20: I bought these to use with Brain.fm, and while I would have preferred wireless, Bluetooth enabled models don't seem to be able to run all night (8 hours) on a charge. These are actually better than I expected in a couple ways - first, they sound surprisingly good for the price, with the bass response being acceptable and the sound being well balanced across the audible spectrum. Second, the cable is a very flexible and durable mesh fabric that doesn't kink and tangle as easily as plastic and is reinforced at the plug end. The headband, being a light fleece type material, tends to be warm, though that would be a plus outdoors in cold weather. The transducers are relatively easy to reposition by sticking your finger into the slots made for that purpose, which is convenient for adjustment. That's really my only complaint - there's nothing to really keep them firmly positioned, meaning they tend to shift around easily when putting on or removing the headband, which tugs on the cable where it enters the back of the headband. It might be helpful to put a couple of stitches on either side of them to hold them in place, preventing this movement. Initially, the headband was a little tight on me, but I was able to stretch it out a bit for better comfort - still snug enough to stay in position while not being tight enough to be uncomfortable during extended wear sessions.

I picked up this little beauty to replace both an ancient and cranky 5-disc CD Player and a single disc DVD player, which means that I now have breathing room in the old entertainment center, so even my antique turntable can take a creaky spin every now and again.

Seeing that I can't connect a toaster without help, I called on my trusty better half to unravel the mystery of setting it up, and in non-technical language, a.k.a. plain English, this is what you need to know about this mighty machine:

1. The manual, being neither user-friendly nor idiot-proof, needs a lot of work, and the same criticism applies equally to the boxy silver remote that accompanies it.

2. It is easy to set up if you already know how to do that sort of thing, which in our case involved using component video connections to the TV and digital coaxial connections to the receiver.

3. It gives excellent sound from both CDs and DVDs, and with the benefit of 5.1 surround, movies like Master and Commander can literally move you, while CDs, having never sounded better, provide an equally impressive listening experience.

4. Being as convenient as a 5-disc CD changer as it is a 5-disc DVD player, it functions smoothly except that when you're playing more than one CD you'll need to put it in "CD Mode" first before proceeding.

5. It can easily play different types of media, such as audio CDs, MP3s, DVDs and those other mysterious formats, requiring nothing more than putting in the discs and playing away without complications.

6. The video quality, being very good on a regular TV, allows you to set up different pre-defined picture quality modes, or, if you're a techie or a buff, to customize settings to suit your own taste, though if you have difficulty making up your mind, you should simply ignore this option altogether.

7. The player, being chock full of options that you have to explore for yourself, can be a bit confusing until you get the hang of it, and while you might think to read the manual for guidance, I must refer you back to Item 1 above.

8. There's on-screen information for MP3s and photo CDs, with different views being available for the contents, whether you prefer groups and folders or entire playlists displayed before you.

9. I can't comment on the progressive scan feature, since I don't have an HD or HD-ready TV yet, still waiting as I am for that lottery win to materialize.

10. It is supposed to play DVD-Audio discs, but playing them requires having 6.1 channel inputs on your receiver, and unfortunately, our receiver is lacking these inputs, though I am also lacking any DVD-Audio discs to test with anyway.

Electronics buffs will probably say that it needs a bit of "tweaking" to get it to look and sound just right, but it looks and sounds great to me regardless. All in all a very good player, perhaps excellent when you factor in the price.

Amanda Richards, October 1, 2004
syntax_complex_s.amazon_reviews::22: Having had a lot of printers over the years (IBM, Epson, HP, Canon, Lexmark, etc.), I had kind of gone away from HP a bit due to their software and driver problems, which emerged when they off-shored the development and support, causing the quality to slip quite a bit. The software seems to work reliably so far, suggesting that HP has addressed that issue somewhat, and granted it is a bit rough and crude in places, it works, functioning well from both Windows 10 and macOS 11 (Big Sur), as well as from mobile devices running iOS. The printer hardware, which seems to be very good, delivers output quite fast. One of the problems you run into with cheaper printers, including some lower end HPs, is that they do not put much horsepower into the printer CPUs, cost-reducing the hardware to the point that they become slow and do not hold up, but this version seems well designed and made, demonstrating solid engineering throughout. Ratings from PC Magazine, Wirecutter, and similar publications generally have this printer at or towards the top, which I would say is accurate given my experience with it. Print quality on text is excellent, while graphics from web pages and similar sources are also excellent, and scans are very good (though a custom flat-bed would be a tad better, this is amongst the best I have seen for an all-in-one). For printing high-quality pictures, you probably still want a Canon or Epson InkJet printer, but this one prints acceptably well for a laser. HP does not ship this printer with full duty cycle cartridges, but the ones they ship with will still do a decent number of pages before requiring replacement. The control screen, being touch-enabled and good sized, gets the job done effectively. The unit is fairly heavy and large, so if you are using this on a desk, you should check the dimensions beforehand. The printer is not cheap, but having excellent print quality and appearing to be very well built, it shows that HP has come back to where it once was, at the top.

[[VIDEOID:5cb01b680d3ae41bbade0eaedaabfe62]] This is an absolutely gorgeous kettle that is well made, solidly built, and overall a dream to use.

POSITIVES
- Holding up to 2 quarts of water to the fill line, it provides ample capacity for most household needs.

- Being solidly built, it demonstrates exceptional construction quality throughout.

- Whistling lightly when the water has reached a rolling boil, it provides clear auditory notification of readiness.

- The top, which fits securely on the kettle, requires a little extra strength to seat and remove, ensuring a tight seal during heating.

- Coming with a blue potholder, it provides some protection for handling hot surfaces.

- Available in seven wonderful colors—including gray, cream, navy, perracotta (which resembles a salmon color), marigold (yellow), sage (deep green), and mist (a light green)—it offers excellent aesthetic variety.

NEGATIVES
- The last bit of water in the kettle gets caught under the rim unless one can center the flow through the spout, which means that I have to dry the inside with a towel for storage to prevent moisture accumulation.

- Being heavy, almost like a cast iron pot, the kettle requires significant strength to lift and pour when filled.

- Requiring a potholder to use for opening of the spout, pouring, and other handling tasks because the entire kettle gets very hot, including the handle and spout lever, it demands constant caution, and I also would have liked a mitt potholder matching the color of the kettle.

In summary, despite its negatives, I love this kettle. At this high price, supplying the user with a mitt potholder instead of a flat one in the color of the kettle one purchases would elevate the purchase to the next level. Note that, never having heard of the Caraway brand before, I saw this kettle in blue on the Vine program. Since ordering this through Vine would not provide me with much savings at the list price, I decided to order this when the price came down for prime day in the color I wanted. The Caraway site, which was cheaper that day by $4 (i.e. $176), sort of required the purchase of insurance for $4.95. Therefore, having purchased this on Amazon for $180 plus tax, bringing this to $191.93, I still consider this pricey, but this is the best made kettle I ever tried. Being right up there with Le Creuset Dutch Ovens and almost just as heavy too, this is a kettle that I expect to last my lifetime. There are many kettles on the market that are less than $40 that also could last a lifetime, but they are not as nice. I do hope it continues to meet my expectations going forward. If it fails in any way, I will lower my rating, update my review, and will most likely regret my purchase. As of now, loving this, I took off one star due to the negatives.

UPDATE - Having been using this regularly for days now, I noticed that this takes longer to boil water than my other kettle and keeps the water warmer a little longer. I also noticed that if I put this on my burner that has a lower flame, the handle does not get hot when the boil is complete, so that is nice.

You read that correctly - I installed this on the outside of my (1985) sliding glass door, and here's why: My kid, who is 23 legally but intellectually operates at a level of 2, also suffers from seizures and is, additionally, moderate to severely Autistic. All of my doors on this house, recognizing the security challenges I face, have double cylinder deadbolts, which are locks requiring two keys to unlock from both outside and inside, whereas the sliding glass doors, presenting a significant vulnerability, have nothing securing them. Apparently, there is no way to key lock a sliding glass door, which compounds the problem. My son, being just observant enough to notice mechanical operations, figured out all the typical sliding glass door 'locks' within about a week of our moving in; and given that 3 years ago he escaped on me for literally less than 60 SECONDS, during which time he had a seizure, slammed backwards on the concrete, and sustained not only a nasty gash on the back of his head but also a near-life threatening brain bleed on the front of his brain where his brain flew forward into his skull, I needed a solution. Being a solo parent—not a single parent who gets every other weekend or so free, receiving no help from family or friends or government agencies—I sometimes need to take a bath or use the potty, and I do not have the money for a set of French doors that might solve this dilemma. So, after conducting more investigating than I care to admit, spending countless hours researching options, I figured I'd give this a try, having already attempted one of those track locks which, for this old style sliding glass door, just didn't work. In our situation, when I need to use the restroom or take a shower or just sleep without constant worry consuming me, I go out one of my locking doors, use the slide lock to impede the opening of the sliding glass door from the inside, preventing any exit, come back in the house through the door I went out, lock everything up securely, and do what I gotta do. Then I can go back and unlatch the slider from outside the house, where it remains just out of the way. No one comes in that sliding glass door—which opens onto a screened in porch with a concrete slab floor—so I'm not worried about how weird it looks that I have a lock installed outside, an unconventional placement that works perfectly for my needs.

Anyway, my use for this item is unconventional, what they call 'off label' in the medical field, but it sure makes my life easier, and for that I am immensely happy:)

Here we have another case of purchasing an extended warranty, being asked to provide a review despite never having made use of (and hoping never to have to make use of) the coverage that was purchased. While the price was right, it was lower on SquareTrade's site, which I should have been made aware of since I'm signed up for the specials and such mailings that they send out, but since it's only a few dollars, it's no big loss that needs dwelling upon.

The plan, which covers up to three replacements of the covered item or the term of the warranty you purchased (two years in this case), works by having you first try to troubleshoot your device over the phone, after which they will make the decision to either repair or replace your item depending on what they determine. If they decide to replace the item, it's wholly their choice to either provide a new or newest model of your device or provide a refurbished model of what you currently have. They promise quick turn-around while covering shipping in both directions. If you do not return the defective model within a certain time frame (which I believe is 30 days) of receiving your replacement, your credit card, which you MUST have on file to file a claim, will be charged the full cost of the device when new.

Having heard nothing but good things about SquareTrade for years, I've noticed that almost all of the low-star reviews seem to be from users not understanding the plan or not making sure they would be covered for their purchases rather than anything to do with SquareTrade itself. This HAMILTON BEACH DIGITAL RICE COOKER (37518, Stainless Steel, 6-¾ cup yield for white rice), which cooks perfect fluffy rice every time, is a good family-sized rice cooker providing enough rice for 4 persons. Having the same capacity as the [[ASIN:B071KPXVJ7 Hamilton Beach 37506 Model]], it features a hinged lid equipped with a rubber gasket, a fancy steam vent, an exterior condensation cup, and a lid liner.

The fancy lid of this Model 37518, being more sophisticated in design, causes steamed foods to cook in one-third to one-half of the time required by the simpler Model 37506, though the fancy lid, despite its complexity, has NO effect on rice or cereal cooking times. The Model 37518, incorporating additional components, has a condensation cup that must be emptied, as needed, during cooking. The lid liner, serving as a removable component, is a part that must be removed each time for washing, though the instructions don't explain how to remove it—it simply pulls straight off the post that holds it.

The Model 37518, offering more control options, allows you to set custom cooking times for Hot Cereal or Steam, which isn't really necessary given that the Model 37506 cooks both cereal and rice automatically and steams food with the aid of a cooking timer.

Most rice cookers, employing similar technology, do a good job of cooking rice—they have a thermostat that contacts the underside of the cooking pot and turns the cooker off automatically when the water evaporates and the pot temperature rises. Some rice cookers—like this one—cook rice to greater perfection than others, but rice cookers, regardless of their cooking quality, mostly differ in their controls, which range from simple on/off switches to extra-fancy multi-button digital displays, and in the quantity of their cooked rice yield.

This rice cooker, positioned somewhere between basic and advanced models, is sort of in the middle regarding both controls and yield. It will cook different kinds of rice, with there being a chart for correct amounts of rice and water for long grain brown or white, jasmine, basmati, and other varieties. It will cook different cereals and grains, including barley, oatmeal, Cream of Wheat, and similar foods. It will steam food such as vegetables, poultry, and seafood; and it will steam food and rice together, combining both functions.

The size of this cooker, being appropriately proportioned, is good if you're making rice for a family of four or if you're steaming foods for a family of two. I love it for the way it cooks fluffy rice and automatically keeps the rice warm for up to 12 hours, maintaining perfect serving temperature. I also love it for cooking Cream of Wheat automatically without burning it on the bottom, which eliminates constant stirring.

Cooking in a rice cooker, requiring patience, takes longer than cooking on a stovetop or in a microwave, with 3 cups of uncooked white rice taking up to 45 minutes and 1-½ cups of Cream of Wheat taking up to 37 minutes. But it's easy to start the rice cooker and let it work while you're preparing the rest of your meal, making meal coordination simpler.

The rice cooker comes with a standard rice cup measure (about ¾ cup U.S.), a rice-rinsing/steamer insert, and a nylon spoon. The cooking pot, featuring superior coating, has an excellent nonstick surface, while the removable pieces are all hand washable in warm, soapy water, with handwashing being very easy.

In choosing between this Model 37518 and the Model 37506, I prefer the latter, which offers a simple, vented glass lid, no condensation cup, longer steaming times, and no ability to set custom cooking times. Both models are very good, but sometimes simpler is better.

This is my favorite roller pen of all time, despite having tried MUCH more expensive pens and refills — I still hold onto my LAMY's because I love the design — but nothing can touch the G2 0.5mm, neither the refill NOR the pen itself.

I scrape the logos off with a razor blade, which is enough to make me feel okay about using this pen.

I used to use fountain pens for everything, but having gotten back into cycling this year, I discovered that the activity shakes up the pen in my pocket like a paint mixer at a hardware store, forcing me to go back to roller pens for when I'm mobile. I tried really hard to find a "nice" pen, but the closest I came was LAMY pens that can be made to take the G2 0.5mm refills, and even then I still like the G2 pen better. I kinda hate the fact that my taste gravitated to the cheapest, most popular thing on the planet, but I have to either be honest and use the best thing for me, or risk becoming a hipster LOL.

I settled on the 0.5mm refill pretty early on, finding that it writes a great line and has the best feel for me on the paper I use. I generally buy just the refills and keep using the same pen, but having lost my last G2 on vacation, I figured a 12-pack is probably a lifetime supply for me. I feel really gross about buying disposable things, but I appeal to the case that I tried everything else before I resorted to this option.

I would recommend anyone to visit the local pen store and really try to find an elegant, suitable pen that will last for a lifetime — generations even. If that fails, don't feel too bad about using G2 0.5mm; it really is a great — all time great — pen that deserves its reputation despite being ubiquitous and inexpensive.

Although people don't write checks as much as they once did, we still have checking accounts and still have transactions, which makes the need for a check register as relevant as ever. The registers that are included when you order checks are far too few, and that is why a set of registers like these from Easy Read Register, offering multiple replacements, are a good idea to have on hand for future use.

With this set, you get ten registers, each containing 26 pages and a total of 416 lines, which is enough to last a long time even with frequent account activity. The individual pages, designed for comprehensive record-keeping, have the usual headers for date, description, payment, deposit, balance, and other essential categories. One extra feature appearing on these registers is a column for Fee, which is not something I have seen on most checkbook registers that I have examined previously.

The calendars printed on the back of each register show 2021, 2022, and 2023, which means that, with normal usage patterns, you should have the necessary calendars available as you use these registers over time. If you have very few checking account transactions occurring throughout the year, it is possible that 2024 might roll around and you will still be using these registers, and that means you won't have the correct calendar corresponding to the current year. With normal usage involving regular transactions, you should be fine without encountering this issue.

These check registers, being staple bound and made for the basic function for which they are designed, fit into a standard checkbook. They are exactly what you expect, and the price being low earns this product a high rating from me.
syntax_complex_s.amazon_reviews::43:
I already like Tiny Epic games, and this is probably my favorite among them. If you can imagine what a Jurassic Park game should be, this is more or less the one you want, offering a small package, great price, and endless fun that leaves you wondering what more you could possibly ask for.

You build parks and enclosures designed to house dinosaurs, which are perpetually hungry creatures requiring constant attention. If you can't feed them properly, they'll still eat—guess what they consume?—your other dinosaurs, creating a challenging survival dynamic! Being very well made and packed with entertainment, this game proves that if you don't like it, maybe board games simply aren't your thing.

I look at this game, which serves as an excellent example, to understand how designers make games well through careful balance and engaging mechanics. I think anyone who likes board games has to give at least one Tiny Epic game a try, and this is the one I would recommend most enthusiastically.

Do you have limited closet space while being desperate for something besides Monopoly, Risk, or Settlers of Catan? Do you like building games that feature dire consequences, or think dinosaurs are the least bit cool or interesting? Look no further than this gem.

My only minor criticism is that some might consider it complex, given the different special dinosaurs and some of the rules governing how and when to place dinos strategically. Any board game is going to have a learning curve, though this one remains relatively small.

All in all, I am very happy with my purchase and I would even buy at least one more of these for a friend if the price were a little bit more reasonable, thinking I read some reviews that said it used to be around $55, whereas I paid 50% more for mine, which doesn't make me so happy about that particular aspect of the purchase.

The table, being a little heavier than expected, probably wouldn't be as sturdy with thinner materials, which explains the weight to some degree and makes it understandable.

*This is the end, isn't it?*

The thought, striking Josh suddenly and almost by accident, pierced through and dissolved his frustration with the car that had allowed him to break down so far from home, with the phone company that had neglected to build towers by this barren desert road, with the sun that had audaciously beaten him, sweaty and tired, to the ground.

*This is the end.*

This thought in particular remained prominent in his mind, even as he realized that he had already seen Heather for the last time, and Joey too, who was still so proud about that geometry test, and Dale, along with the business Dale would inherit, the business that would serve as an unexpected legacy.

*This is it.*

Dale, who had told him that this trip was a fool's errand and made a joke about what he would say at Josh's funeral, this memory, too, failed to shake the thought from Josh's head, failing to dislodge what had embedded itself so deeply within his consciousness.

*The end of...*

The thought, lingering there in a state that could only be described as static, remained for a time that Josh wasn't able to comprehend, while everything else in his mind seemed to fade away, receding from his periphery inward toward this single, solitary idea that had taken root.

*This is the end of me.*

When nothing else was left, Josh found it fitting that this idea of finality should itself be his final thought, the ultimate conclusion to everything he had been.

But it wasn't.

It vanished as abruptly as it came, and then—

Josh would have cried, if he was still physically capable of producing tears.

His regrets came flooding back all at once, accompanied by his anger and his sorrow and his despondency at his own powerlessness, the tranquil peace of the "end" being over, replaced with the angst of a life incomplete, a life that had failed to come to terms with itself.

And then Josh felt **fear**, fear like he had never felt before, the terror of fate incarnate, of the great unknown for which he was utterly unprepared, the sheer and total horror overwhelming his memory and his pain and all his other emotions.

That fear was the last thing Josh thought about.

"Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave. Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave. Citizens will not be allowed..." the Moral Officer bellowed into his bullhorn, his voice echoing across the barren expanse. I found it heartening, the ending being so near that it gave me the strength to push my weak and weary body to shovel faster, faster, despite the exhaustion that threatened to overwhelm me.

All around me my fellow citizens dug in the dust like brittle dry dirt, scratching out the place where they would give their bodies back to the earth, their movements mechanical and resigned. In the distance other Moral Officers made their proclamations into identical bullhorns, creating a chorus of commands that reverberated throughout the vast field. At regular intervals throughout the field Compliance Officers stood in immaculate uniforms, waiting patiently to aid us in our final duty to the Nation, their expressions blank and unmoved by the scene unfolding before them.

It had become clear that there was a food shortage well before the State announced it, though no one dared speak openly of what everyone knew. Everyone had whispered about how the weekly rations they picked up from the distribution station seemed to be smaller every week, though the center's Party workers would deny it if anyone asked, their faces stern and unyielding. Then the whispers turned to fully voiced complaints when items began disappearing from the rations, never to reappear again, vanishing as though they had never existed. Soon meat had almost become a memory and fully grown, healthy looking vegetables were rare, appearing only occasionally in the dwindling supplies.

When the State News Agency, in a special broadcast that interrupted regular programming, finally announced the famine, nobody was surprised by the confirmation of what we had long suspected. We were instructed that we must, as always, stand united, strong and proud in the face of this Straining Test that would measure our devotion. Everyone must do their part to bear this burden and our Immaculate Society would clear this hurdle and emerge triumphant, stronger than before. Even the Beloved Ruler was rationing his consumption, we were told, sharing in our sacrifice. It was clear, yes undoubtably clear, that this was some ploy by the dissidents and the outsiders, attempting to destroy our resolve, to make us turn back from the ideals of the revolution that had shaped our lives. They had sabotaged our fields and murdered our animals, committing acts of treachery against the Nation. But we would stay strong in our virtue and would emerge, as ever, triumphant over adversity.

It was then that they announced the lottery, explaining that a number of citizens would be randomly selected from the population to give glorious sacrifice of faith and virtue for the Nation, to help ease the burden of consumption that threatened us all. Those who were selected were informed the next day by a soldier showing up at their door to take them away from their families, separating them forever from those they loved.

A shout rang out across the fields, cutting through the monotonous sound of shoveling: "May my body fertilize the soil to feed our glorious Nation. Long live the Beloved Ruler." A gunshot punctuated this declaration, sharp and final. Someone had already finished their grave, completing their duty. A few others cheered their assent, though most were too weary and hungry to manage even that small gesture. The Compliance Officer holstered his pistol and motioned for the now dead man's two neighbors to fill in the grave he now occupied, their faces expressionless.

They had worked us hard after taking us away, shoveling out a roadway that stretched endlessly before us. We slept where we worked and the only sustenance given to us was a broth so thin that they could hardly justify calling it more than hot water, barely enough to sustain life.

My grave now looked deep enough to satisfy requirements. I hesitated before raising up my shovel to call over the Compliance Officer, fearing his judgment. He came over and produced a tape measurer, checking the dimensions with practiced efficiency before nodding his assent. I let out an inaudible sigh of relief and went to stand at the foot of my grave, positioning myself for what came next.

"Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave," the Moral Officer chanted into his bullhorn, repeating the familiar refrain.

I felt the cool metal of the Compliance Officer's pistol come to rest upon my forehead.

"Citizens will not be allowed..."

"Happily ever afters doesn't exist for people like us," I said solemnly, watching as Clarissa peered up at me through her tears.

"Why not?" She asked quietly.

Gently wiping her tears away with the pad of my thumb, I smiled bitterly.

"Because the world won't let us, and every time we try to be happy someone always knocks us down, something always will."

"What if we run away?" She asked, finally looking at me.

Swallowing hard while trying to hold back tears of my own, I struggled to respond.

"If we run away then we will always be running, which is something I don't want for us, something I don't want for you," I whispered.

Clarissa held back a sob that threatened to escape.

"Will, please don't do this."

A tear ran down my face as I spoke.

"I don't want to."

"Then why are you?"

"Because I'm no good for you Clarissa, getting into fights and getting arrested, whereas you can find someone better who can make you so much happier, who can give you what you want."

The words left a sour taste in my mouth, but it had to be said, knowing that if we stayed together then there'd always be someone trying to break us apart—her parents, my friends, my enemies.

Giving her one last kiss, I murmured, "Maybe one day in the future, when things aren't complicated, we'll find each other again, though right now is not our time, but maybe tomorrow will be."
syntax_complex_s.writingprompts::6:
Daniel's wife, standing at his side, was absolutely coming apart at the edges, not that anyone else but him would be able to tell. Okay maybe that was a bit of an exaggeration, but she was a touch anxious. Nervous? Whatever she was, something wasn't quite right, given that she was doing that little nose twitch that never happens when she's calm, which he had learned to recognize over the years of their marriage.

"Imani," he called out, and her head tipped down to where he was seated in acknowledgement, her eyes meeting his with concern. "It's going to be fine." She gave him a weak smile that didn't quite reach her eyes before reaching out to squeeze his hand, her fingers trembling slightly. Of course he said it to comfort her, but he honestly felt like everything was going to be okay, considering that they had already crossed the worst bits. He survived the car accident, then he survived the surgery to make sure the universe didn't decide to change its mind later, then later the amputations, the implants, each milestone marking their journey forward. With a roll of his eyes, he squeezed her hand back, attempting to reassure her through touch. "Honestly, this has been the easy part, we have plenty of time."

"The easy part? Since when do we ever get easy!" she reached out to swat his ears, her eyes crinkling with mirth despite her anxiety. "That's up there with 'What could possibly go wrong? Don't jinx it,'" she scolded, wagging her finger at him playfully. He leaned in to tell her all that worrying could do nothing good when the door slammed open, the solid thump echoing through the large room, interrupting their moment.

"Oops," the tall man in the doorway looked sheepish, rubbing the back of his neck. "I tripped into the door there. How are you two today?" he inquired in a friendly manner, striding into the room while the sunlight from the windows poured over his lanky form, illuminating his features. "Ready to give it another go?" Daniel flexed his legs, which were neat and secured into his new running blades, feeling the carbon fiber respond beneath him.

"Since the second I put these on, Mason!" he replied earnestly, and the easy going man gave him a thumbs up before reaching out his hands, positioning himself to provide support.

"That's what we like to hear! Alright, let's get you up and moving then." With one last look at his wife, who was standing back with an apprehensive look but held up crossed fingers in a gesture of hope, he reached for the other man's hands, gripping them firmly. These were the fourth pair of running blades he had tried, having worked through several iterations. The other ones had issues, despite their so-called custom fits. Too long. Too short. These hurt. Those felt like they were going to fall off. But as Daniel wobbled to his feet, finding his center of gravity, he knew these were it. It took a moment to steady himself, his body adjusting to the new equipment. They had a different sort of balance and give to them than his normal prosthetic, and his fitness wasn't quite where he wanted it to be after months of recovery. His heart raced as he shifted his weight from one foot to the other, hearing the blades flex in response, the carbon fiber singing beneath him. Left. Right. Left. Right. Left right, left right, left right, bounce. They felt nothing like his old legs, those familiar limbs that had carried him through countless races. But all the same, despite their foreignness, they felt right. Slowly Mason let go and then backed away to the other side of the room, his eyes never leaving Daniel's, monitoring every movement for signs of instability. When he hit the wall, positioning himself at the far end, he called out to them.

"Great! Now start at a walk and work up to as fast as you feel comfortable doing," he instructed, and a sly tone crept into his voice as he added, "And remember, the room is padded and we're all friends here. Face plants are nothing to worry about." Daniel scoffed at the insinuation, bristling at the suggestion. As if he'd let these things get the better of him after everything he had endured. Confident despite his wobbling, he took a shaky step forward and his arms wheeled around a bit before he braced his core to maintain balance, engaging muscles he hadn't used in months. Then he took another. And another, and soon he had a slow bobbing jog going, carefully moving between his wife and physical therapist, finding his rhythm. He did this until finally, after several passes across the room, Mason signaled for him to stop. He sprinted down the room to the happy couple with a look of great excitement, his enthusiasm barely contained.

"It looks like we got it this time!" He stepped back and gave him one final look over, assessing the fit and movement. "We just need to run a few more tests, make sure that everything is adjusted correctly, but I think we found your golden pair here. So, how do you feel?"

His mind began to wander as he turned inward, trying to find the words that could even begin to describe what he was feeling in this momentous occasion. All he could think about were the things he thought he had lost forever when he hazily woke up from surgery that faithful day, looking down to see the sheet cave in where his lower legs had once been, the emptiness shocking him. The sound of the crowd screaming his name as he tore down the field, their voices creating a wall of sound. The heady feeling of sprinting down a track, the world narrowing almost into blackness as he pushed himself to the limit, chasing records. The lightness of a casual game of tag with his wife, catching thin air as she slipped by him with laughter dancing in her eyes, her joy infectious. Bouncing on his new legs once more, testing their spring, he felt weightless. Invincible. With a strength he hadn't felt in a long time, he hugged Imani and spoke over her head, his face aching with a smile that stretched wide.

"Alive."

"Aye, I remember it like yesterday, when I was wandering through the western mountains, just east of Markarth, where the road snaked below me, carving a long path through the valley." A figure dressed in animal skins caught my eye, creeping slowly towards a carriage that had stopped before crossing the river, drawing a cruel-looking sword as they approached closer, clearly intent on killing the small group of travellers who waited there. Mounting my horse, I started down the slope, yelling at the top of my lungs to get their attention before any violence could unfold.

"The would-be bandit immediately looked at me with a scowl, letting out a yell of his own, which caused a dozen more men and women, dressed in the same ragged fashion, to come bearing down on the carriage with weapons drawn, creating a scene of chaos. I knew there were too many for me to handle, but I couldn't bear the thought of letting those poor people die to these brutes who surrounded them. As I reached the bottom of the incline, I remembered that my friend from Winterhold, who's a bit of a nutty one, had given me a magic scroll before I set out on my journey, thinking it might prove useful." Let me say now that I'm no mage, though I tried to find some magics that would make me more handsome, none of which worked anyway. I was pretty sure that I merely had to open the scroll and read it, but I had no idea what it actually *did*, hoping it would summon one of those big Atronachs my friend was always talking about, making them out to be something near god-like. Wouldn't mind having one of those on my side during this confrontation.

"Anyway, once I got to the bottom, I jumped off my horse and yanked the scroll from my satchel, shaking so badly that I almost couldn't read it, though I knew I had done it correctly when I started glowing, which should have been a good sign that something bad was about to happen, but I knew nothing about magic and still don't. The glow was nice though, warm and comforting as it surrounded me. Suddenly, all the bandits were putting their weapons away and asking me what was happening to them, leaving me with no clue, but I figured they couldn't do any more harm in their confused state." Unfortunately, they were a little too impressed by me, apparently thinking I was some sort of grand wizard because they immediately propped me on their shoulders and carried me back to their camp for a feast, which surprised me greatly. I started out thinking they were cannibals or something when I saw them attacking, but I heard their story and realized they were really just trying to get by in the world, struggling as many do. Their mead was wonderful, let me tell you, though a little too wonderful, I guess, because I woke the next morning with an, admittedly, attractive woman next to me and a camp full of these people congratulating me with gifts and hugs, celebrating what they believed was my magical prowess.

"So, you see, I envy you because I miss the open fields and chilly mountains, the gold and treasure, and the freedom to go wherever I please without responsibilities weighing me down. I used to be young and carefree, I used to be strong and brave, possessing qualities that made adventure possible. You remind me a lot of myself, honestly, back when I used to be an adventurer like *you*, until I took an arrow to the knee."

Note: "Taking an arrow to the knee" was apparently a Norse saying about getting married.

"Lamb, tell me a story…" said the Wolf, his voice dripping with smugness and a smile spreading across his face, "….Something sweet."

The Lamb, trembling with fear that coursed through his entire body, recalled the stories of the wolf that he had heard all throughout his childhood, though he had never thought that there was any truth to them until this very moment.

"W-what would you like to hear?" the Lamb finally asked, his voice breaking.

"You can decide that," the Wolf replied, his voice carrying an authoritative tone that left no room for negotiation.

The two of them were positioned in a secluded area of the same pasture where the Lamb had been born and lived his entire life, and he was currently pressed into the corner with a broken leg throbbing in pain, while the Wolf, pacing a half circle around him and remaining a mere two feet away, seemed to savor the moment. The Farmer was nowhere to be seen, and none of the other Lambs, understanding the danger that awaited them, would dare try to save him unless they felt like sacrificing their own lives in the process.

He didn't have a story to tell, having lived a short, boring life, and with the realization that his family wasn't coming to save him washing over him, he knew it was coming to an end. He felt a strange wave of calm rush over him as he accepted his fate at the mouth of the Wolf.

"If I had a story, it would be this one, but we've already reached the end," he said.

"I always liked the violent ones," the Wolf replied as he closed the gap between them.

"You want to send in Nikon? You really think it's that bad?" The speaker, being a large, barrel-chested man who stood well over six feet tall, possessed both a long, neatly trimmed beard and an impeccable suit that spoke of his station. He was talking to a woman who, having to have been in her sixties, now displayed the beauty she had shown as a youth as a well-aged luster that time had refined rather than diminished. Her piercing blue eyes, looking at the barrel-chested man without blinking, were staring through him as though reading something written on his very soul.

"You have a problem, Lord Aerlman, a very specific type of problem that requires particular expertise. We can deal with this very specific problem, but doing so will require the services of a specialist who understands such matters. Alex Nikon is that specialist." Her tone, being matter-of-fact and neither excited nor loud in any way, conveyed absolute certainty.

"She's just a girl, a misguided girl." The older woman, hearing this dismissal, shrugged with evident indifference.

"Your girl, Lord Aerlman, has contacted the Outer Planes, opening channels that should have remained sealed. She has let something through, and now it's inside her, inhabiting her like a parasite. However, until she does something public that forces our hand, I can't involve the Circle without your request, which must be given freely. If you don't want our help, that's fine, though you should understand the consequences. Just remember that tragedy strikes first at the home, claiming those we hold most dear." Her warning having been delivered with appropriate gravity, the woman turned and started to leave the ornate sitting room that had witnessed their conversation. As she reached the door, preparing to depart, Lord Aerlman called to her with desperation evident in his voice.

"Laura! Ms. Cadswall. Wait. Please." She smirked confidently to herself, satisfied at this capitulation, and then composed her face before turning with a neutral expression that revealed nothing.

"Yes?" The lord was wringing his hands while pacing in front of the fire that crackled in the hearth.

"Your man, Nikon, whose reputation I know well—will he... kill her?" Lord Aerlman, looking distraught, awaited her answer with visible dread.

"Alexander Nikon will handle the crisis that has emerged, for that is what he does, what he was trained to accomplish. How he handles it will remain at his discretion, subject to his professional judgment. Be advised though, Lord Aerlman, that contact with the Outer Planes taints the very soul itself, corrupting it in ways that persist. Even death can't remove its stain, which remains forever."

Lord Aerlman, looking crestfallen upon hearing this pronouncement, idly picked up a picture off the mantle of the fireplace, this being a family portrait showing the lord and his wife along with their daughter, a striking redhead in her late teens whose smile radiated innocence. He caressed the picture with his thumb, tracing her features lovingly, before setting it back down with obvious reluctance. All of the energy drained from him and he sagged, his shoulders slumping as he turned towards the woman with a beaten look that spoke of surrender.

"Fine. Do it. Make the call." He dismissed her with a wave and then sank into one of the large leather chairs, pouring himself a large whiskey which he immediately downed in a single gulp. As he poured another, seeking oblivion, Laura excused herself and closed the door quietly, having business to conduct. She had a phone call to make.

-- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -

"Antonia. I know you're here." The same girl from the photo, now having become a fully-grown and beautiful young woman, was hiding behind a large stack of pallets while desperately clutching herself and trying not to scream. Her hands and torso were covered in blood, some being hers and some belonging to her friends who had died.

They had been partying, drinking in her London flat, when the man arrived without warning. The first indication of trouble was the door exploding inward, a large piece of it ripping through Pierce like a spear thrust by an invisible hand. He dropped with a gurgling sound and blood sprayed across the room in arterial spurts. Screams erupted from the small group of young men and women, and before they could even process the danger confronting them, a small man, barely measuring 5'6", was in their midst, wielding a large curved sword in one hand and a handgun in the other. Glowing runes twisted across his skin like living things, and his left eye was covered by an eyepatch. His right eye, being the color of polished metal, quickly scanned the room with mechanical precision. Everything after that became a blur, and Antonia couldn't recall any details except the bodies and the blood that pooled everywhere.

She remembered a voice speaking in her head, then her friends all screaming while fire poured from their eyes as they charged the sword-bearing man, shouting in some language Antonia had never heard before. As her friends threw themselves at the man with suicidal fury, she turned and leapt through the bay window, falling the three stories and landing with a sickening crunch that should have killed her. She remembered her legs feeling surprisingly good for such a fall, defying natural law, and then running without direction. The voice in her head was louder now, and though she couldn't understand it, it was hurting her with its insistent chanting.

As she ran through the streets in blind panic, the voice was chanting continuously, and every person she passed turned to stare at her, their eyes spewing fire before they turned and charged the way she had come, becoming unwilling soldiers. She didn't understand what was happening, who the man was, or why he was after her with such determination. She didn't understand anything! Next thing she knew, she was hiding in the warehouse, where the man found her again, his curved sword and gun both covered in blood that dripped steadily. As she curled up and tried not to let him find her, he kept talking.

It was a hell of a time to fall in love, a hell of a decision to make, considering that she had the prettiest eyes he had ever seen while he stood there sucking in his gut as she awaited the dose.

She had killed ten men and was about to be put to death by lethal injection, whereas he was just filling in because one of the guards had gotten sick, not even working there regularly, though he knew he was head over heels for her, seeing her not as a killer but as a beautiful angel as they stared at each other exchanging shy smiles.

"Do you have any last words?" asked the priest.

"What's his name?"

"Who?" asked the priest.

"That guard there," she indicated with her head.

"Me?! um ugh officer Jones," he stammered with excitement.

"Hi, I'm Rebecca."

The decision was made after that, with Officer Jones waiting until about five minutes before midnight, trying to argue with himself about the consequences but knowing in the end that consequences be damned since it was true love at first sight.

He pulled his side arm and shot everybody in the room except Rebecca, tremors shaking his arm as he dropped his gun and ran to her, embracing her desperately while his heart pounded with the realization of what he had done for love, making it a hell of a first kiss that sealed their fates together.
