The subway, which had been moving steadily through the tunnels beneath the city, stopped abruptly, causing Laurentius to awaken with a gasp that echoed in the confined space. Struggling to take in his surroundings while his mind cleared from the fog of sleep, he noted with certainty that it was cold, unmistakably so. Examining his armour with growing confusion, he observed that his hands were covered with gloves appearing to be made of cow hide, while his boots, which were black and fur-lined, provided welcome warmth. Underneath a thick black coat, which hung heavily on his shoulders, was a soft white shirt held together in the front by clasps, and a red strip of fabric that reached around his neck made its way down to just past his stomach. "*What is this,*" he thought, his mind racing with possibilities, "*Is that how I died? Do we wear tokens of our death?*" His eyes, searching for understanding, met those of a rotund darker-skinned woman who was reading a curious layered-parchment device resting on her lap. Looking around her neck, he spotted a cross hanging there, and he gazed at her sympathetically, thinking to himself, "*I suppose so.*"

Tubes of light, suspended from the ceiling, illuminated the metal chamber he found himself in, casting an artificial glow over everything. A smooth ding announced itself through the space, and the doors, sliding together with mechanical precision, closed shut. To Laurentius' surprise, which manifested as a slight widening of his eyes, the metal chamber began to move again, lurching forward with renewed purpose. Standing up and steadying himself against the movement, he made his way toward a man he assumed, based on his bearing and position, was in charge. The man, who was covered in what seemed to be traditional dress for the era, wore a large silver wig and glasses that read "2015" across the front, creating an incongruous appearance.

"*Salve*," Laurentius began, offering the traditional greeting he knew.

The man, turning his head slowly, returned a confused look before returning to gazing out the window, apparently dismissing the strange address. He smelled distinctly of wine, the scent wafting from him in waves.

"*Aut ubi sum? Quis hic locus?*" Laurentius pressed, seeking answers.

The metal chamber, continuing its journey through the underground passages, shook once again, slightly but enough to disrupt Laurentius' balance as he stood there waiting for a response. A voice, crackling with static, rang out over the loudspeaker, but Laurentius, unfamiliar with the language and accent, couldn't make out what it had said. When the metal chamber made another stop, arriving at what must have been a station, Laurentius wasn't prepared for the sudden deceleration. Falling onto the floor below as a wave of people, pressing forward with determination, exited through the opening doors, he got up quickly and followed the crowd, which weaved through tunnels that seemed to stretch endlessly. Struggling to take everything in while keeping pace with the moving mass of humanity, he noticed that musicians lined the enclosed street, and there were few vendors, from what he could understand of the scene. He continued walking until he reached a flight of stairs that led upward, which he ascended with growing anticipation, and he was astounded by what he saw upon reaching the surface.

Bright lights, flashing in patterns and colors he had never witnessed, surrounded him in all directions, creating a disorienting spectacle. What had been the steady hum of voices below, interrupted occasionally by an outburst or announcement, had now turned into an onslaught of voices and action that overwhelmed his senses. He was Marvolio IV, who had summoned demons the size of castles, who had created new rivers, who had figured out a charm that prevented you from getting nose itches when your hands were busy, and yet he wouldn't mistakenly summon a slug when he was looking for god, would he?

I knew I wouldn't be able to see immediately, understanding that it would take a lot of work, and I was even warned that I might feel overwhelmed by the experience that awaited me. I had vague memories of what sight was like, having been injured in a car accident that had left me blind in both eyes at the age of three. I do think it helped, though; being able to process light and color for three years before going blind may have made it a bit easier for my brain to remember rather than to learn anew what vision meant.

James helped me a lot during this difficult transition. Sometimes I would close my eyes to get around like I had before, and he would suddenly get in front of me and block my way, teasing me in his playful manner. It wasn't mean; if I protested, he'd raise his arms out and impede my movement until he closed them around me, hugging me tight while refusing to release me.

"I won't let go until you open your eyes," he'd say, expressing a devotion that no one had ever shown me before. I could hear it in his voice and feel it every time he hugged me, wrapping me in his protective embrace.

I practiced often, though sometimes I'd get headaches from trying to look at everything surrounding me. Blotches of dark smeared across the table as I tried to eat breakfast, confusing shapes that James told me were the shadows from the tree outside. That tree had never bothered me before, but now it was interrupting my breakfast, trying to make it even harder to simply eat a bowl of cereal without confusion. I still felt around to make sure I could trust what I was seeing, needing the confirmation of touch. I can't tell you how strange it was to see my own hands before me, two misshapen blurs fumbling with everything I tried to touch, moving clumsily through space. I used to love my hands before sight complicated everything.

After a while, the dark smears became shadows that I could recognize, and James's face became clear to me in a way that filled me with joy. I think that was the happiest moment in my life, waking up one morning as he turned over, allowing me to see his eyes for the first time with clarity. They shone bright, as if they themselves held light inside them, glowing with an inner radiance. He was beautiful in ways I never knew, having never understood how beautiful he really was during all those years of darkness.

The blotches no longer confused his face and I was able to see him clearly, but my problems began when I noticed that my own face wasn't clearing in the same way. The nasty blotches on my own face weren't tricks of the light or shadows that would eventually resolve. I had a slew of acne scars around my jawline, marks that my skin had hidden from my touch. My skin felt smooth to me, but I didn't know the dark marks were there, permanently etched into my complexion. I had a few wrinkles, which I had known about through touch, but the sickly green circles under my eyes contrasted poorly with my dark irises, creating an appearance that shocked me. My eyes didn't shine like James's eyes shone with their inner light. My eyes looked dead and sad, lacking any vitality.

I didn't want to ask James about it, confronting the reality that I never knew I was so ugly. Even if I was ugly, I assumed James must be just as ugly, reasoning that no handsome man would choose an ugly, blind girlfriend. I could finally see how women stared at him with obvious desire. Nobody ever looked at me that way, with that hunger in their eyes. A trip to the grocery store used to be a fun time for both of us, but now it was another opportunity to see every other bitch—who he could easily have if he wanted—stealing furtive glances at him, or smiling if he looked in their direction with any acknowledgment.

I have no idea what to think, trapped in this confusion. Sometimes I think he smiles back at them, returning their interest. I caught him looking at two women walking by us at a restaurant, his eyes following them. My stomach was in knots as I watched. I didn't say anything, just stared down at my pasta and tried not to lose my appetite while sitting there.

"Is something wrong?" James asked, noticing my silence.

"No, why?" I said, forcing my pockmarked face into an expression of amusement that I didn't feel.

"Just asking," he said before adding, "I love you," with a smile that seemed genuine.

I wish I could believe it.

*** 
 The Author 
 *** 
 
I can't shake the feeling, you know, that sensation which creeps along your spine while waiting to take up residence in the base of your skull like some kind of parasite that has burrowed its way into your consciousness. It's an indeterminable feeling, this sense that you're being watched by eyes you cannot see. I can't shake it off, no matter how hard I try to dismiss it as paranoia. I am sure I know what it is, but I'm not ready to admit that I know, not yet. The... *author*, let's call him, since naming him makes him somehow more real and less terrifying. He is watching, waiting, building something that I cannot yet comprehend. Even as I think this thought, forming these words in my mind, he is scratching it down in his chicken-scratch scrawl, touching the pen against his teeth in thought while contemplating my fate. I can feel it happening; I can see it in my mind's eye with a clarity that frightens me. He's trying to figure out how to kill me, weighing different scenarios and outcomes.
 
I suppose it is my own fault, considering how I brought this upon myself. See, I kept asking questions, pestering the universe with my inquiries because I needed to understand the fundamental nature of existence. I had to find out if there was some directing hand to life, some guiding force that shaped our destinies. If mankind had a purpose, a reason for existing beyond mere biological imperative, I needed to appreciate what purpose we worked toward, what grand design we served. There's a moment, one of particular realization, which caught me and held fast with an iron grip. Like my apprehension regarding an observer, this sensation of being monitored; only, this feeling was deeper, more primal, reaching into the very core of my being. I *knew*, I mean really *understood* with a certainty that defied logic; all of it is a narrative, every moment scripted. Life is a story, unfolding page by page. Which inevitably led me to the conclusion that haunts me now -- there needs to be an architect, an *author* who writes our fates.
 
The car narrowly missed me, its bumper passing within inches of my body. I had an inkling, a pressing sensation against my chest that was verging on the edge of panic, threatening to overwhelm me. I didn't cross when the green man displayed on the crossing signal, beckoning pedestrians forward; instead, I took a step back, heeding an instinct I couldn't explain. My *spidey-sense* tingled with warning. The taxi-cab driver never saw me standing there, and I hadn't seen him either as he barreled through the intersection. His drunken sprawling vehicle, weaving across lanes, slammed into the same traffic signal post I had been, until recently, standing beside like a lamb awaiting slaughter. Can I tell you how fucked up that is, having this realization about the nature of reality, followed immediately by a sudden sensation of fear that saves your life? If I hadn't heeded my gutless compulsion, that inexplicable urge to step backward, I might have been splattered between the cabbie's car and the hard place which was the traffic signal pole, my body crushed and broken. I turned my gaze upward, burning eyes and clenching jaw notwithstanding, and decried whoever worked at compiling this narrative, this story of my existence.
 
"What the actual fuck was that?" I said, my voice shaking with anger and fear.
 
Okay, so I realize my choice of words probably did not fall into the definition of circumspect or measured, but hell, we're talking about some kind of god-figure deciding on my time to die, playing with my life like it's entertainment.
 
*Are you sure?* My logical brain asked, trying to impose reason on the unreasonable.
 
I pondered my position, both in the physical and meta-physical sense, weighing the evidence before me.
 
*Yeah, I'm fucking sure,* I replied to myself internally, conducting this debate within my own mind. *How else do you explain the sudden epiphany and subsequently my almost immediate death, the timing too perfect to be coincidence? There's an* author, *a real one, and he doesn't want to be known, doesn't want his characters aware of his existence.*
 
I'm not sure how I knew the *author* didn't want to be known, or the fact that he was a man rather than a woman, but I figured it was something in my general make-up, some instinctive knowledge, granting me the understanding I needed. Oh, don't get all high and mighty and preach at me now about delusions or mental illness; I'm not talking religion or spirituality here, I want to live damnit, to survive this narrative. I stood, still staring up at the sky with defiant eyes, trying to impart my utter disgust and frustration when the signal pole creaked, unnaturally so, groaning with a sound that metal shouldn't make. I adjusted my head so my eyes were level with the pole, examining the damage.
 
The metal appeared warped, twisted by the impact, and I realized that the car had burst into flames, orange tongues licking upward.
 
*When had that happened?* I thought, confused by the gap in my perception. *Nevermind, run stupid, get away from here.*
 
My internal dialog is not always the most kind to myself; I'm a blunt sort who doesn't coddle. So, I ran, my feet pounding pavement. What I was running from, if Mr. Omniscient *author* was already in my head, reading my thoughts as I formed them, he could follow me anywhere I went. Hell, I could have an inopportune flashback, and he could hit me with a mack truck during my distraction. If this *author* decided I was going to die, why didn't he do it already, end it quickly?
 
*Fuck me,* I thought with sudden understanding. *It's about the drama; the story needs conflict and tension.*
 
"Sick fuck," I said aloud, knowing he'd hear me, or he'd write that in his juvenile scrawl, knowing I intended it for him specifically.
 
*What if I stop cooperating?*
 
I looked up again, addressing the sky, and said, "What are you going to do with a character who won't cooperate, huh?"
 
Naturally, he didn't respond with words. It wasn't like I expected a voice from the sky, some booming pronouncement, but I figured he might strike me down with lightning or something equally dramatic; I mean, potentially it's within his ability, right? He might decide my knowledge of the plan labeled me as a liability that needed eliminating.
 
*What the hell is the plan anyway?*
 
I don't know, I guess the plan is for me to die in some spectacular fashion. Perhaps, he's not into the mundane, the ordinary death. Maybe, just maybe, he wants my death to be something significant, something of a show worth writing about. I bet that's it, that's his motivation. I got the sense again, that warning; a gut punch to my stomach making my insides roil like they were leaking to the outside, and the rumbling in my stomach suggested I take a step back from where I stood. I did, moving instinctively. Something pierced the skin in my back, sliding between my ribs. It was a fluid, smooth motion that parted the skin like a knife through butter. I felt the warm blood mixing with my sweat as it soaked the back of my flannel shirt, spreading wetness.
 
A quiet voice whispered in my ear, breath hot against my skin. "Hello protagonist," she said softly. "I'm your antagonist, the *author* says hello."
 
That was all she said before vanishing. She didn't have a scent, like you would expect a person to have. She was a ghost from the shadows, insubstantial. I don't know who she was, or why her specifically, but she'd made it clear through her words... I was right about everything. Take that fucker. I didn't have the strength to say it aloud, but I know he heard me anyway.
 ***

Kai, who had been carefully sneaking back up the stairs from the kitchen, knew that getting caught by Mom and Dad would be bad, though getting caught with the leftover broccoli that Mom had been planning to serve for dinner tomorrow night would be considerably worse. Lucky for Kai, who had other plans for the vegetable, he wouldn't have to eat any of it.

After closing his bedroom door behind him, the six-year old, moving with determination, went straight to his closet, boldly opening it before beaming at the lump of eyes, hair and tentacles that he found waiting there.

"Here ya go, Blergh," Kai whispered as Blergh, accepting the open Tupperware container with one tentacle, emptied the entire thing into a mouth the size of a basketball hoop before swallowing it whole. Kai, who had been observing this ritual for months now, could never see if Blergh had teeth or not, but the monster, regardless of what he consumed, never chewed.

Beginning to lay a trail of crackers out to the middle of the floor, Kai watched as the monster, cajoled by the salty circles being offered, slowly left the closet where he had been hiding. Kai, moving quickly now, got a box out of his toy chest and dumped its contents on the floor in a scattered pile.

"We're playing army men tonight," Kai said while Blergh, who seemed content with any activity, merely grunted in agreement. Kai loved playing with Blergh because he could move lots of pieces at once and he was really good at pretending to be surprised when things, caught in imaginary explosions, "blew up."

***

Julia, who used to be annoyed when she woke up in the morning to find her son not only sleeping on the floor but also in the middle of a bunch of plastic men just waiting to be stepped on, had by now experienced this so many times that being annoyed wasn't worth the effort anymore.

"Wake up, sweetie," she said, softly shaking his shoulder while smiling down at him. "How's Blergh?"

As they walked toward the breakfast table together, Julia, who had heard countless variations of this tale, settled in for another story about how Kai and his imaginary friend had conquered some great evil, thinking that kids are so cute at that age.

***

Ten years later, Kai, who no longer had to sneak around like he once did, rationalized that all boys his age eat a lot in the middle of the night, right? Sitting in front of his X-Box, Kai passed one bag of Doritos and one bottle of Mountain Dew to his left.

**A wise man, making what was for him a rare attempt at humor, once said that "Heaven was eating pâté de foie gras to the sound of trumpets."**

Page of a journal of a Chef - Recently Deceased.

As a chef, being one who has dedicated his entire existence to the culinary arts, I wholly agree with the assessment regarding foie gras, though I must confess that I have never had much of an ear for trumpets, their brassy tones failing to move me as food does. Foie gras, for those who don't know—and do not worry, since many don't, their ignorance being no fault of their own—is a dish as old as the art of cooking itself, having survived through centuries of culinary evolution. Foie Gras, which is French for *fat liver*, represents the Pièce de résistance of any self respecting chef who takes pride in his craft. The process begins when you take a duck, though better still a goose, but more often a duck due to availability and cost. Having selected your bird, you cage it, giving it no room whatsoever, since movement, which would allow the muscles to develop, will ruin the texture that we seek. You take it by the neck, holding it firmly, and pump corn that has been boiled in fat down its gullet, forcing sustenance into its body. Doing this seven times a day, you pump it plump, watching as it swells with each feeding. After sufficient time has passed, you kill the bird, removing the liver with practiced precision, and a good chef, one who understands quality, would pay a wholesome price for it, knowing its value. Prepared with mustard, with honey, with diced onions and balsamic vinegar, never has anything been so delectable, so transcendent in its richness.

See, it is not the taste that repulses people, causing them to turn away in disgust, but rather it is the process, the means by which this delicacy is created. "Does the end justify the means?" is a question that philosophers and moralists often ask, debating ethics endlessly. The answer is no, if you are talentless, if you lack a palette capable of discerning true greatness. But yes, yes! Believe me when I say that anyone would scream "YES!" if they tried my Foie gras, experiencing what I have created. But then again, understanding that mine is different, mine is better than any other, makes all the difference.

See, they say, repeating the old cliché, that beauty is skin deep, existing only on the surface. It is, and taste, being even more superficial, is far shallower still. I am a chef, having devoted myself to this calling. A good chef, not claiming to be a good man but I reiterate with emphasis: A GOOD chef. If I had been born a painter, blessed with visual rather than gustatory talents, and my only source of red, the color of passion and life, was the blood of the innocent, do not doubt for even a moment that I would paint in red, creating masterpieces regardless of cost. Of-course I wasn't born a painter, having instead been born a chef, a GOOD chef who understands his purpose. Foie gras, as most chefs make it, following traditional cruel methods, is illegal in many countries: the UK, Germany, and Italy to name just a few among many. Needless to say, being one who pursues perfection above all else, that I do not get my recipes from law books, which concern themselves with morality rather than excellence. Foie gras as I make it, employing techniques that transcend conventional boundaries, is illegal in every country without exception. The pope, holding the highest moral authority in Christendom, once denounced Foie Gras as cruel, an abomination against God's creatures, but that was of-course before he tried mine, experiencing revelation. Mine is different, mine is better.

A cardinal, overwhelmed by what he had experienced, said to me that if god again came to earth, walking among mortals, he would make sure I cooked for the divine presence. Another, equally moved, said that "I once denounced your dish Chef, speaking against it from my pulpit. I am sorry Chef, filled with remorse. I owe you a thousand apologies Chef, for my ignorant condemnation. I have now sampled your dish Chef, and I now know, with absolute certainty, that the bliss derived from the supple marinated flesh on my tongue is greater than all the sufferance of all the geese and ducks that God has ever endeavored to make, throughout all of creation." They were in awe of me, unable to contain their wonder. Anyone who I convince to suspend their morals, setting aside their principles temporarily, will at the moment of contact with my Foie gras, transcending mere eating, be in awe of me. Mine is different, mine is better.

People would kill for a spoonful, committing murder without hesitation—good people, pious people, moral people who otherwise live righteously—they would kill for a spoonful of my Foie Grois. Believe me when I tell you that I would sell out completely if I charged a million per lb, such is the demand. But I don't, refusing wealth. I don't do it for power or riches, those corrupting forces, but rather I do it for the art, for the purity of creation. I am a chef, A GOOD chef, not claiming to be a good man but I reiterate with conviction: A GOOD chef whose work transcends morality. My recipe, representing the culmination of my life's work, is worth kingdoms, my dish having made kings, those who command nations, weak at the knees, so weak that they kneel before me, the Chef who has mastered his art.

My legacy, the only thing that will outlive my mortal body, will be my recipe. If you are reading this, having somehow obtained this journal, congratulations because you have inherited it. Here it is, revealed at last:

Take a baby, whether you abduct it, buy it, steal it, it makes no difference whatsoever. Any foundling or orphan will do, their origins being irrelevant. Boy or girl, it makes no difference to the final product. Black, White, Arab, Asian, it makes no difference in terms of quality. Though they must be newborn, untouched by the world! They must be innocent, pure, they must be succulent, their flesh tender.

Cage it, giving it no room whatsoever, since movement will ruin the texture we desire. Take it by the neck, holding firmly, and pump corn that has been boiled in fat down its gullet, forcing nutrition. As the ship reached the beacon, the pilot, having used the last of his jump fuel making it to this sector, nervously activated his directional scanning.

Glancing out his viewing port, the pilot felt an inexplicable chill that he figured was jump jitters, though he routed power to his security drone anyways. When sensors didn't find anything, he should have known it was a waste of time, particularly since he had more important things to focus on, like finding fuel that would allow him to continue his journey.

The directional scanner pinged and drew his attention to a large hull floating some distance from his vessel, its form partially obscured by a thick cloud of gas that drifted through the void. The ship, being powered-down, explained why the initial system scan had not detected its presence. He brought the impulse engines online and moved towards the derelict vessel while simultaneously hailing the ship, attempting to establish contact with anyone who might remain aboard.

No response came, which was curious, though abandoned vessels were not unheard of in these sectors. What proved more unusual was the pristine condition of the ship, which did not have so much as a dent marring its hull. Having found abandoned hulls before, he knew they were typically pocketed with scorch marks from a laser blast or short range teleporter, some sign of battle always being evident on their surfaces.

After briefly considering donning his EVA suit, he instead headed to the drone bay and took remote control of the security drone, a unit meant for boarding defense but one that could, in a pinch, be used as an exploration unit for situations exactly like this.

Moments later the drone, a sleek machine armed to the teeth with an assortment of lasers and close combat weapons that had saved the pilot's life more than once, slid through the airlock. Having schematics for this hull, he directed the drone to make a beeline for engineering, knowing that any remaining fuel would be found there.

The problem with remotely controlling the drone was that it demanded the full attention of the pilot, preventing him from noticing that the airlock had not sealed—had he been paying attention, he would have noticed his door system had malfunctioned.

His dying screams echoed as he was torn to pieces by creatures lurking in the shadows.

The pilot should have known that giant alien spiders are no joke.

Elwood and Shara, leaning against a concrete pillar in the courtyard of a high school, were watching Elwood's newest charge, an unassuming young man named Dale.

"So how did you get assigned to this one, Elwood?" Shara said while examining her claws, which gleamed in the afternoon light.

"I'm pretty sure this is a softball pitch from the management downstairs," Elwood said, his arms crossed against his chest in a posture suggesting both boredom and suspicion. A group of girls walked over to the pillar and leaned against it, occupying the same space as the two demons, who remained invisible to mortal eyes. A strong gust of wind, appearing from nowhere, blew the papers and binders out of the hands of the girls, who shrieked in surprise and ran after them, their voices echoing across the concrete expanse.

Shara, clearly annoyed by the proximity of the mortals, said, "I'll never get used to that, no matter how long we've been doing this work. I don't care if we *can* occupy the same space with these creatures." Turning to face the girls, who were gathering their scattered belongings, she held her arm out to them, her claws held behind her thumb, and flicked them outwards with a sharp snap, sending the books and papers flying out of the shrieking girls' hands once again. "Little wretches..." she muttered under her breath.

Dale, who was chewing on his bean and cheese burrito with methodical slowness, was looking at the scene across the courtyard with the expression of a placid cow chewing on grass, seemingly unbothered by the chaos unfolding before him.

"What's with that kid?" Shara asked, her curiosity piqued by his unusual demeanor.

"I don't know, to be perfectly honest. Maybe he's stupid?" Elwood chewed on his thumb for a bit, strategizing his next move with the concentration of a chess player. "Let's jump time forward to 6th period and see what opportunities present themselves there."

Shara gave Elwood a sideways glance and raised an eyebrow in skeptical amusement, "Sure, if you think that'll help...."

With a sound like tearing canvas, a noise that accompanied all their temporal movements, they were transported and came to rest on the ledge under the window in the back of Dale's 6th period class, which was already in session.

"So what's your plan, big boy?" Shara asked, settling into a comfortable position.

Elwood, pressing a long-clawed finger to his lips with theatrical deliberation, said, "Sssshhhh." As he did that, Dale's head hit the desk with a soft thud, having fallen asleep, and he was out cold, breathing deeply. Flinging his arms out wide in a dramatic gesture and then bringing them in together in a grand grouping motion, Elwood caused every student in the class to turn to face Dale without uttering a single word, their movements synchronized and eerie.

"That's cute," said Shara, observing the display with mild interest.

Elwood smiled with satisfaction and said, "It's time to wake up, Dale." As he said that, every single student in the class, speaking in a very flat tone that carried no emotion whatsoever, said the same thing in perfect unison with Elwood. Dale, his face half-slick with drool that had pooled on the desk, sat up and rubbed his eyes, looking around at the class that was staring back at him with blank expressions.

"Dale, it's time to wake up," all the students and Elwood said again, their voices merging into one unsettling chorus. No one blinked or moved. Dale glanced from side to side nervously, "I'm awake." Elwood flung his arms apart in a gesture of release, and the class resumed as normal, no one but Dale aware of what had just happened, the moment erased from everyone else's memory.

"That's your plan?" Shara asked, clearly unimpressed by what she considered a lackluster effort.

Dale, noticing that he was a little behind in taking notes due to his unexpected nap, began writing in a hurry, his pencil moving frantically across the page.

"You're kidding me, right? That's a daytime creep, which is far more unsettling than you're giving it credit for! It's not even 3 am, which is when everyone expects this sort of thing. That's some creepy shit, I don't care what you say," Elwood protested, defending his methodology.

"Uh huh," Shara said dismissively, watching Dale with narrowed eyes. "Look at him carefully. He's got no clue that was out of the ordinary at all. C'mon, lets go and try something else." She flexed a claw over her shoulder as she walked away, begging for Elwood to follow her lead.

As they were leaving through the wall, passing through solid matter as easily as air, Elwood spun around and made a bitch-slapping motion with his clawed hand. Dale grunted in pain and his head jerked forward violently, loose tangles of hair at the back of his head flying up, and his pencil shot out of his hand and bounced off the back of the muscular kid who sat in front of him. The girl next to Dale, wrinkling her nose in distaste, looked at him with plain disgust and said, "You're such a weirdo...", shifting in her small desk to be as far away as possible from him.

Shara laughed, genuinely amused for the first time.

The two demons, having positioned themselves strategically, waited outside the classroom for the end of period and for Dale to emerge. "You know this would be so much easier in the nighttime when people expect supernatural occurrences..." Shara said, clearly bored with the daylight approach.

"Yeah but that's not my style at all," Elwood said with conviction. "You get more *genuine* results during the day when people's guards are down. Anyone can be spooked at night and when the day comes, they're so quick to forget it and rationalize it away. No. No, what really freaks them out, what truly gets under their skin, is a daytime haunting that they can't explain away."

Shara didn't say anything in response, only yawned widely, showing her pointed teeth.

The bell sounded for the end of the period and Dale was the last one out of the classroom, walking slowly with his characteristic lack of urgency, looking down at his phone with focused attention. Elwood flapped his wings and dove into the phone, merging with its electronic circuitry. An alert popped up on Dale's screen, and Dale clicked on 'Read' which cued Elwood to jump into full-view on the screen and yell "DAAAAAAAAAAAALE" through the phone's speaker at maximum volume.

Dale hit the power button and put his phone back in his pocket without any visible distress. "Just great," he thought with mild annoyance, "One of my friends has been messing with my alerts again, probably thinking they're hilarious," and continued walking to his next class at the same unhurried pace.

Elwood stretched out of the phone like elastic with a 'pop' and took his place next to Shara, who was leaning against the wall with her arms crossed. "I don't get this kid at all," he said, watching Dale walk away down the corridor.

"Still insistent on the daytime approach?" Shara asked him with a knowing tone.

Elwood let out a heavy sigh of defeat. "Okay, let's try it your way and see if nighttime makes any difference," and they both vanished with a pop and sizzle that left a faint smell of sulfur.

The two demons burst into the space above Dale's bed and stared down at him, their wings gently flapping to keep them hovering. "So what do you do now?" Elwood asked Shara, who only gave a half smile and extended her index claw out in front of her and slowly curled it back into her palm. The bed sheet covering Dale was pulled off him in perfect sync with the flexing of Shara's finger, exposing him to the cool night air. Dale only scratched his stomach and rolled over onto his side.

"Wow... I'm.. I'm just at a loss for words, Shara. That's some scary stuff, right there," Elwood said with heavy sarcasm.

She narrowed her eyes at him and shot a hand out to grab something invisible in the air. Dale screamed in pain, a sound that tore through the silence of the night. Shara then yanked her arm back with tremendous force and Dale flew off the foot of the bed and crashed against the wall, knocking several books off the shelf which fell one after the other onto the top of his head with successive thuds.

Elwood's jaw dropped and he looked from Shara to Dale and back again in disbelief. "You have no subtlety at all, woman!"

"Just watch and learn..." she said confidently.

Dale stood up and picked up the books, putting them back on the shelf with care. The door to his room opened and his mom asked him if he was alright, concern evident in her voice. "Yeah, just had a really bad leg cramp and fell when I got up to stretch," he explained calmly.

"Oh for fuck's sake!" Shara said and threw her arms up in complete exasperation.

"Yeah, the hell with this kid..." Elwood said, shaking his head, and they both popped out of the air, disappearing back to wherever demons go when they admit defeat.

Dr. Kevin Bruin.. Log Entry E72 -- The Moment
-
To whoever is investigating my disappearance, in case I don't return from what I am about to undertake.

No one knows when their turn will come, although we quickly found ways to predict its movement and avoid it, understanding that there is no stopping it once it begins. The worst attempts, which came under Marshall Law when the isolation periods were implemented, were terrible—short, yes, but terrible in ways that still haunt those who remember. One of the iso-men once asked me, his voice trembling with philosophical weight, if it was worse that everyone lived, having to interact with the people we had selfishly isolated during those desperate days. "Would it have been best if the moment caused death instead?" he asked, his eyes locking into mine while mine were filled with panic and guilt, whereas his were peaceful, reflecting a serenity that came from knowing the moment had already passed him, though it hadn't yet passed me.

There are several rules we have identified corresponding to the moment, patterns emerging from careful observation. The first, which affects our understanding fundamentally, is that it only affects men—each and every man regardless of age or circumstance. The second, contradicting initial fears, is that its intent is not to kill, though deaths have occurred, usually among the very young or old, deaths that can be prevented through timely medical intervention. Third, operating on principles we still don't fully understand, it affects men on a singular basis, meaning only one man can experience the moment at a time, with no reported cases of simultaneous experiences ever documented. Four, following patterns that suggest intentionality, its movement is proximity based, so that the closer you are to someone experiencing the moment, the more likely you are to be next in its inexorable progression. Five, defying our attempts at containment, it can't be contained by any physical barrier, as the isolation of an infected area failed when the moment, having gone through the male population in the isolation area, simply advanced outwards. Sixth, offering our only hope of temporary escape, it is possible to outrun it since it moves at speeds comparable to an average human. Finally, according to all testimonies collected, the experience itself is said to be incredibly painful beyond description.

As to where I went and why I chose this path.

I was asked what I thought the moment could be when I first started investigating, and I claimed something explainable through scientific method! Observations, hypothesis, experiments, testing month after month for any rational explanation—a virus, bacterium, parasite, or even mass hysteria—none of it fit the data. There was no explanation that satisfied empirical scrutiny. When people talked about aliens or god's punishment, I laughed, exclaiming that science would find the answer eventually. Eventually though, it seemed no answer was coming despite our efforts. I doubted for a while, even started to believe the extremists whose theories I had dismissed. Few people know this about me, but there is one more rule that I choose to accept that others don't: it's sentient, and extinction is its end game. As a man of science, I can't be scared anymore but must test my hypothesis. You will now understand why I'm missing. Men my age are less likely to survive, but we can find the answer—science will prevail. I've performed an orchidectomy on myself, removing what might be the trigger. By the time you read this, I should be within the moment's current spread, walking deliberately into its path. I wonder what people will think when they see a naked old man walking into the fire—is he mad, a religious nut? No pun intended. If I succeed, which I believe I will, you will probably hear stories before I can make it back, hence this log entry. Stories of a crazy old man whose faith made him immune to the moment will circulate. Well, that will be so, but know that it was faith that triumphed—faith in science and empirical truth.

If I don't return, Dan, love always.

A small lamp burned steadily on the polished desk, where the human wore a pair of thin spectacles perched precariously on the edge of his nose. Stacks of parchment, arranged in teetering towers, occupied a far corner of the work surface, while he read through pages at a time, scribbling notes on another sheet as he worked. Empty ink bottles scattered across the floor suggested that the man was rather busy, having devoted considerable hours to his labors.

From the entrance, Ronn readied his flail, letting the heavy chains dangle menacingly, their echoes filling the room with metallic reverberations. But the man, seemingly absorbed in his work, refused to look up at the intruders who had burst into his sanctuary. Instead, holding up a finger in a gesture requesting patience, he continued reading through his documents with deliberate concentration. Ronn and the rest of his group, uncertain how to proceed, exchanged glances and shrugged shoulders in confusion. For a moment, standing still in awkward silence, they waited. With a disappointed smack of the tongue, the man finally replaced the parchment, pushed his glasses closer to his eyes to see them better, and called for his guests to approach. They did, moving forward cautiously.

"Apologies, my friends," he said, his voice cracking slightly as though it had gone unpracticed for some considerable time, unused to addressing living visitors. "Come. Come."

The adventurers, maintaining their vigilance, stepped forward slowly. Wilm's head darted around nervously as he scouted for suspicious stones concealed in the floor or another tripwire that might trigger some deadly mechanism. The cobbles, which had been gray stone, turned to green when the tasseled edge of the ornate rug stood before them, marking a boundary. The group stopped immediately, hesitating.

"Come," the man muttered again, any impatience in his tone defying detection despite the repetition of his invitation.

Firrel's boot, extended carefully forward, tested its weight against the rug to ensure there was no hidden danger. There was solid ground beneath, reassuringly firm. The rest followed suit, stepping onto the carpet one by one.

"Wait!" the man screamed suddenly, his voice sharp with alarm. The group, reacting with trained instincts, wasted no time assuming a defensive stance, their weapons and shields drawn and ready for combat. "I meant the carpet," he clarified, exasperated.

The adventurers, looking down towards their feet in confusion, observed that the jade fibers assumed a purplish hue as the blood from their persons, still fresh from recent battles, dripped freely onto the expensive fabric. Querth's face flushed with embarrassment at the destruction they had caused.

"Sorry," the wizard whispered apologetically, recognizing the value of what they had ruined.

The man rolled his eyes in resignation. "It's already ruined beyond repair. Nothing we can do now to salvage it. Let's just get this over with quickly."

The adventurers were finally within a pace of the desk when the open palm of the man, raised in a stopping gesture, begged their halt. The hordes of evil creatures that had led them through countless corridors to that chamber had promised epic confrontation. The supposed throne room of unspeakable villainy, which they had expected to contain some dark lord, was little more than a study occupied by what appeared to be a librarian.

"Well, then. I suppose congratulations are in order!" The man clapped his hands together with hollow enthusiasm. "Smashing job getting here. I'm Pollock and I'll be handling your processing from here onward."

"Processing?" Edmund echoed, confused by the bureaucratic terminology.

"Yes," replied Pollock matter-of-factly. "You're almost done in this dreadful castle and on your way back home to enjoy the spoils of your victory. All that's left is to handle the last odds and ends, the administrative matters."

The adventurers nodded in content, though they kept their weapons handy as a precaution. The legions they had been forced to cut through in order to reach that chamber began to feel concluded, their purpose fulfilled.

"Excellent! Let's get started with the accounting. In total you've slaughtered, according to my records, one hundred and fifty three goblins, twenty nine orcs, eighteen kobolds, and two dragons, which is quite impressive."

Edmund smirked and rolled the handle of his axe to catch the light, preening, much to the groans of Ronn and Dismal, who had enjoyed the chaos that had followed their arrival as it stopped their fellow warrior from gloating about his prowess.

"In addition, you broke down forty one doors, set off two fire traps, six spike snares, three boulders, and one acid spill that caused extensive damage. Plus, it says here you freed the dungeons of ten prisoners who were being lawfully detained."

"All in a day's work," Wilm interjected proudly, puffing out his chest.

"Quite," responded Pollock, not the least impressed by their boasting. "And adding up the costs of your little adventure, that comes to a total of eight million, eight hundred thirty seven thousand, two hundred and fifty one gold pieces owed."

Even Querth's mind, trained in complex calculations, could not comprehend such a staggering figure. They were used to generous spoils from their adventures, but several hundred was the most any had ever seen in one place.

"We couldn't possibly carry that much coin," Dismal remarked practically. "Or spend it in our lifetimes."

"That's quite expected," Pollock laughed without humor. "You can just pay in installments over time."

"Pay?" shouted Firrel, incredulous. "What do you mean pay?"

"Your fines. Your damages to property. You can't just go around killing things, damaging property, and setting off traps that require professional calibration without consequences."

"But we were on a quest," pleaded Ronn desperately. "We were trying to save the village from destruction."

"I see," sneered Pollock coldly. "Does that mean the village is going to pay the fines, rebuild the castle, reset the protections, mop the floors, rehire the guards, retrain dragons, and inform the families of those lost in your rampage?" The group stood in wide-eyed silence, unable to answer. "I didn't think so."

"B-but, it was a quest," Ronn repeated weakly.

"Do you have a license, a Writ of Pacification for this 'quest' of yours?" Ronn shook his head in admission. "No need to answer, I already know you don't have one. If you had bothered to apply for one properly, *this* castle would have been better protected and *I* wouldn't have been needed here. Just a little '[WP]' at the start would have been enough to save us all the mess of your unauthorized rampage."

"Who was supposed to file our WP?" Querth asked the group urgently. They considered the question for a moment before turning to face /u/dismaldreamer accusingly. "You've ruined us!"

"I'm sorry," cried Dismal, backing away. "I didn't know! I didn't know this would happen!"

The circle closed around him menacingly as the group looked to dispatch their greatest foe: the enemy within their own ranks.

-- -- -- -- --

*The moral is tag your posts or else your friends will murder you.*

He said if his son played for Rutgers or a coach like that, the coach would have some real explaining to do. He would still whoop on him afterwards. Athletic director Mr Pernetti apologised. He said this in a written statement. Rutgers had considered firing him at the time. Mr Pernetti added something. He thought it was in the best interest of everyone to rehabilitate. But he was wrong about that decision.

syntax_simple_s.xsum::26: The bill would pardon men only in specific cases. They must have had sex without force or threat. They must also marry the victim. Critics say it legitimises rape. It also legitimises child marriage. It lets off men who are aware of their crime. Violence against women in Turkey has increased in the past decade. Forty percent of women report sexual or physical abuse. Statistics also show the murder rate of women increased. It rose by 1,400% between 2003 and 2010. The bill was initially approved on Thursday evening. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's ruling Justice and Development Party brought it to parliament. The party is known as the AKP. On Tuesday, MPs will debate the bill a second time. They will then cast their final vote. It is a highly contentious bill. It has divided Turkey along its traditional fault line. This fault line is secular versus conservative. The government states an aim. The aim is not to excuse rape. The aim is to rehabilitate certain people. These people may not have realised their sexual relations were unlawful. The aim is also to prevent girls from feeling ostracised. These girls have sex under the age of 18. Their community might ostracise them. There is opposition to the bill on the streets of Istanbul. Many say it will encourage men to rape. But the government will get support among its pious voter base. This base is in poorer areas. Girls are married off young in these areas. The sexual abuse rate is higher there. Supporters say Mr Erdogan has liberated religious women. He repealed a ban on headscarves in public places. The vote on Tuesday could spark mass protests. The bill might pass. It will likely quash the convictions of some 3,000 men. These men are accused of assaulting an under-18-year-old. But critics say it would overlook statutory rape. Statutory rape is underage sex. It would legitimise child marriage as well. Ozgur Ozel is an MP for the opposition Republican People's Party. He spoke according to AFP news agency. He said sexual abuse is a crime. There is no consent in it. This is what the AKP fails to understand. Seeking the consent of a child is something universal law does not provide for. But Justice Minister Bekir Bozdag said it could help couples. These couples have engaged in consensual sex. They want to marry. When a child is then born from this non-official union, the doctor warns the prosecutor. The man is sent to prison. This puts the child and mother into financial difficulties.
syntax_simple_s.xsum::27: Andrew Apperley was 38 years old. He was from Eastbourne. People reported him missing. He did not return to his hotel. This happened four days after he went to the Full Moon party. Formal identification has not yet taken place. Mr Apperley's family have been informed. His family are from Gloucester. A Gloucestershire Police spokesperson made a statement. "The circumstances of the death are unknown at this time," the spokesperson said. Mr Apperley was staying at a hotel in Bophut. He went to the full moon party on 12 February. No one has heard from him since that time. He told his mother something important. He would be returning the following morning. The hotel reported him missing. This happened four days later. A spokesman for Gloucestershire Police made another statement. The spokesman said several things. They made inquiries with the Foreign and Commonwealth Office. The office is called the FCO. They can now confirm something. A body has been found. It was found in the search for Andrew Apperley. "Our thoughts are with Andrew's friends and family." Mr Apperley had flown into Ko Samui. He flew from Bangkok. He wanted to go to the party in Ko Phangan. His brother told the BBC this information. Richard Apperley is his brother. Richard said something about his brother. His brother checked in on the morning of the party. He left his passport with the hotel reception. He left his driving licence there too. Andrew did something before going out. He had a conversation with his mother Linda. They used the messaging app WhatsApp. He said he would be getting the boat back. This would happen the following morning. Staff at the Hotel ibis Samui Bophut confirmed something earlier. He had still not been seen. His documents were still in their possession. His bank told his family important information. His cards had not been used. This was true since going to the party. Mrs Apperley sent a message. She sent it to her son's mobile phone. She did not get a delivery report. The report would say he had received it.
syntax_simple_s.xsum::29: Philip Cullen is 57 years old. He was given a six-month suspended sentence. He captured two butterflies at reserves in Somerset and in Gloucestershire in 2015. The butterflies were an endangered species. He was convicted in March of six charges. The charges related to killing, capturing and possessing the endangered species. His case is believed to be the first prosecution in the UK. The prosecution involved offences related to the species. Bristol Magistrates' Court heard the case. Cullen was seen chasing a Large Blue. He used a child's net. This happened at Daneway Banks in Gloucestershire in June 2015. He was later spotted with a small net. This was at Collard Hill in Somerset. Someone reported it to police. Police raided his home. They found up to 30 trays of butterflies. The trays included Large Blues. Prosecutor Ian Jackson told the court something. The charges had been brought "on the grounds of endangering a species". Michael Hartnell was defending Cullen. He said something in mitigation. The 57-year-old had accepted the "enormity" of what he had done. He was "extremely remorseful". Cullen lives at The Grove, Warmley, Bristol. He was given a six-month prison sentence. The sentence was suspended for two years. He was ordered to carry out 250 hours of unpaid work. He was also given a five-year criminal behaviour order. The order bans him from three nature reserves. The Large Blue is popular at those reserves. He was ordered to pay £300 prosecution costs. He must pay an £80 victim surcharge. The Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust made a statement. It said this was the "first UK conviction for collecting a butterfly". It was a "breakthrough in the battle against wildlife crime". Source: Butterfly Conservation. The Large Blue is Maculinea arion. This species became extinct in Britain in 1979. It was reintroduced at sites in the 1980s. These sites included Collard Hill and Daneway Banks. In 2004 it was found at nine locations in the country. It has a wingspan of more than two inches. It can be identified by a row of black spots. These spots are on its upper forewing. A person collects and studies butterflies. That person is called a lepidopterist. The name comes from the branch of zoology. That branch deals with butterflies and moths.
syntax_simple_s.xsum::28:
Britain conquers Palestine from the Ottomans in 1917. Britain gives support to "national home for the Jewish people" in Palestine. Britain does this through the Balfour Declaration. The declaration includes an insistence. The insistence states that "nothing shall be done which may prejudice the civil and religious rights of existing non-Jewish communities". 

The first significant Palestinian Arab nationalist organisations emerge in 1918. These are the mainly cultural Muntada al-Adabi and the Damascus-based Nadi al-Arabi. 

The San Remo Allied Powers conference takes place in 1920. The conference grants Palestine to Britain as a mandate. The mandate is to prepare Palestine for self-rule. Jerusalem riots occur against the Balfour Declaration. The riots assert a distinct Palestinian Arab identity. 

Britain appoints Mohammed Amin al-Husseini in 1921. He is a member of a leading Palestinian Arab family. Britain makes him Grand Mufti of Jerusalem. Britain also makes him leader of the Muslim community. He rallies the Arabs and Muslims. He rallies them against any further concessions to the Jews. 

The Palestinian Arab delegation rejects a British proposal in 1922. The proposal is for a Legislative Council. The delegation says the inclusion of terms of the Balfour Declaration in the draft constitution is not acceptable. 

Arab rioters kill about 200 Jews in 1929. The killings happen in Jerusalem's Old City and Hebron. British troops kill 116 Arabs. They kill them in suppression of riots in Jerusalem. 

A British White Paper appears in 1930. A Royal Commission also appears. They recommend limiting Jewish immigration. 

The Black Hand Islamist group operates from 1930 to 1935. Sheikh Izz al-Din al-Qassam leads the group. The group launches a campaign of violence. The campaign targets the Jewish community and British rule. 

The Palestinian Arab leadership accepts a proposal in 1935. The proposal comes from the British High Commissioner. The proposal is for a Legislative Assembly. The British House of Commons rejects it the following year. 

The Arab revolt begins in 1936. It begins with a general strike in Jaffa. Britain declares martial law. Britain dissolves Grand Mufti Al-Husseini's Arab Higher Committee. The revolt continues until 1939. More than 5,000 Arabs are killed. 15,000 Arabs are injured in suppression of the revolt. Al-Husseini flees to French-run Syria. He flees to avoid arrest. 

The United Nations makes a recommendation in 1947. It recommends partition of Palestine. The partition would create separate Jewish and Arab states. Britain signals an end to the Mandate. The recommendation includes international control over Jerusalem and its environs. The Arab High Committee rejects the partition. 

Israel declares independence in 1948. The British mandate ends. More than four million Palestinians are thought to be living with refugee status. They live in Arab countries. Many are marginalised. Many are trapped in camps. 

Arab armies fail to defeat the new Jewish state of Israel. This happens after Britain withdraws. Jordan occupies the West Bank and East Jerusalem. Egypt occupies Gaza. Israel holds the rest of Mandate Palestine. Israel holds West Jerusalem too. At least 750,000 Palestinian Arabs either flee or are expelled. Disputes exist over the nature of their departure. These disputes endure to this day. The United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East is set up. People call it UNRWA. It caters to the educational and health needs of Palestinian refugees. It also caters to their descendants throughout the Middle East. 

Fedayeen Palestinian guerrillas operate from 1949 to the 1950s. They are based in Egypt and Gaza. They carry out raids into Israel. Egypt encourages these raids. This increases after pan-Arab officers seize power in Cairo. This happens in 1952. 

Israel colludes with Britain and France in 1956. They invade Egypt during the Suez Crisis. They do this partly to end Fedayeen incursions. A UN buffer force arrives in Sinai and Gaza. The raids are drastically reduced. This continues through 1957. 

Yasser Arafat forms Fatah fighting group in 1959. He forms it in Egypt. The group carries out raids into Israel. 

The Arab League sets up the Palestine Liberation Organisation in 1964. People call it the PLO. The Arab League also sets up the Palestine Liberation Army. Ahmad Shukeiri leads these organizations. 

The Six-Day War happens in June 1967. Israel occupies East Jerusalem after the war. Israel occupies all of the West Bank. Israel occupies Gaza. Israel occupies the Golan Heights and Sinai. Jewish settlements are set up in all of these areas. This happens in coming years. The government approves the settlements. 

Yasser Arafat takes over PLO leadership in 1969. He debuts as a military leader in clashes with Israeli forces in Jordan. This happens in 1968. He asserts the group's independence from Egyptian control. 

Tension increases over the strength of the PLO in Jordan in 1970. This leads to the Black September clashes. The clashes are with Jordanian forces. The clashes drive the PLO into exile. The PLO goes to southern Lebanon. 

The PLO and other armed Palestinian groups turn to airline hijackings in the 1970s and 1980s. They also turn to attacks on Israeli soldiers. They attack officials and civilians. They attack within Israel and abroad. They do this to highlight their cause. 

Palestinian "Black September" gunmen take the Israeli team hostage in 1972. This happens at the Munich Olympics. Two of the athletes are murdered at the site. Nine more are killed during a failed rescue attempt. The German authorities carry out the rescue attempt. Israel launches a series of reprisal assassinations. 

Israel raids PLO bases in Beirut and southern Lebanon in 1973. Israel does this before and during the October Yom Kippur/Ramadan War. 

Two hardline factions carry out raids into northern Israel in April and May 1974. These are the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine General Command and Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine. They kill 43 civilians. They kill many children. They kill people in a block of flats in Kiryat Shmona. They kill people in a school in Maalot. 

The PLO adopts the Ten-Point Programme in June 1974. This happens after the 1973 Yom Kippur/Ramadan war. The programme allows compromise with Israel. The compromise is on the way to establishing complete Palestinian control. The control would be over historic Palestine. This includes the territory of Israel. Some hardline factions split away. They form the Rejectionist Front. They step up attacks on Israeli soldiers and civilians. 

The Arab League recognises the PLO in October 1974. It recognises it as the "sole legitimate representative of the Palestinian people." The League admits it to full membership of the League. 

Yasser Arafat becomes the first non-state leader to address the United Nations General Assembly in November 1974. He delivers an "olive branch... and freedom fighter's gun" speech. 

The Rejectionist Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine hijacks an Air France plane in 1975. A German far-left armed group helps them. The plane is en route from Israel to France. They divert it to Entebbe in Uganda. Israeli commandos rescue most of the passengers and crew. They kill the hijackers. 

The right-wing Likud party wins a surprise election victory in Israel in May 1977. The party encourages the settlements policy on the West Bank and Gaza. 

A PLO attack kills 38 civilians on Israel's coastal road in March 1978. Israel carries out its first major incursion into southern Lebanon. Israel drives the PLO and other Palestinian groups out of the area. 

Israel pledges to expand Palestinian self-government in September 1978. This happens in the West Bank and Gaza. This is part of the Camp David Accords. The accords establish diplomatic relations with Egypt. 

Israel invades Lebanon again in June 1982. Israel wants to expel the PLO leadership from Beirut. A Palestinian faction attempts to assassinate the Israeli ambassador to London. The PLO leaders quit Lebanon. 

A massacre of Palestinians happens in September 1982. It happens in the Beirut Sabra and Shatila camps. Israel's Christian Phalangist allies carry out the massacre. The PLO leadership moves to Tunisia. It remains there until it moves to Gaza in 1994. 

The Israeli air force strikes PLO headquarters in Tunis in October 1985. A PLO group kills three Israeli tourists on a yacht. The Palestine Liberation Front PLO faction hijacks the Achille Lauro cruise ship. The hijackers demand the release of 50 Palestinians from Israeli prisons. The hijackers kill an elderly American wheelchair user. His name is Leon Klinghoffer. 

The First Palestinian Intifada uprising begins in December 1987. It begins in the Palestinian Territories. The Muslim Brotherhood in Gaza forms the Hamas movement. Hamas rapidly turns to violence against Israel. 

Jordan abandons its claim to the West Bank in 1988. Jordan cedes it to the PLO. The Palestinian National Council meeting takes place in Algiers. It proclaims the State of Palestine. 

The PLO backs Iraq in 1990. Iraq annexes Kuwait. Kuwait severs ties with the PLO. Kuwait subsequently expels about 400,000 Palestinians. 

A US-Soviet sponsored conference takes place in Madrid in October 1991. The conference brings Israeli and Palestinian representatives together. This is the first time since 1949. 

The Israeli Labour government of Yitzhak Rabin pledges to halt the settlement expansion programme in 1992. The government begins secret talks with the PLO. 

Yitzhak Rabin and Yasser Arafat sign the Oslo Declaration in September 1993. They plot Palestinian self-government. They formally end the First Intifada. The First Intifada had been running out of steam since the Madrid Conference. Violence continues. Various Palestinian groups carry out the violence. These groups reject the Oslo Declaration. 

Baruch Goldstein kills 29 Palestinians at prayer in February 1994. He is from the extremist Jewish Kach movement. The killings happen at the Cave of the Patriarchs shrine in Hebron. Hebron is on the West Bank. 

Israel withdraws from most of Gaza in May and July 1992. Israel also withdraws from the West Bank city of Jericho. This allows Yasser Arafat to move his PLO administration from Tunis. He sets up the Palestinian National Authority. 

Yasser Arafat receives the Nobel Peace Prize in December 1992. Yitzhak Rabin receives it too. Israeli Foreign Minister Shimon Peres also receives it. They are jointly awarded the prize. 

The Interim Agreement sets out a path in 1995. The path is for transfer of further power and territory to the Palestinian National Authority. The agreement forms the basis of the 1997 Hebron Protocol. It also forms the basis of the Wye River Memorandum of 1998. It forms the basis of the internationally-sponsored "Road Map for Peace" of 2003. 

Talks between Israeli Labour Prime Minister Ehud Barak and Yasser Arafat break down from 2000 to 2001. The talks are over the timing and extent of a proposed further Israeli withdrawal from the West Bank. Palestinian protests escalate into a new Intifada. 

Israel sends troops to encircle Ramallah in December 2001. This happens after a series of deadly Palestinian attacks inside Israel. Yasser Arafat is unable to leave his government compound. 

The Israeli army launches Operation Defensive Shield on the West Bank in March 2002. The army begins building a barrier there. The barrier is to stop armed Palestinians entering Israel. The route of the barrier is controversial. It frequently deviates from the pre-1967 ceasefire line. It deviates into the West Bank. 

The Arab League meeting takes place in Beirut in March 2002. The League offers to recognise Israel. The recognition is in return for its full withdrawal from all territories occupied since 1967. The League wants agreement to a Palestinian state. East Jerusalem would be its capital. The League wants a "fair solution" to the refugee question. People call this the "Arab League Peace Plan". 

Yasser Arafat establishes the post of prime minister in March 2003. He appoints Fatah veteran Mahmoud Abbas. Abbas leads contacts with the US and Israel. Both of these refuse to deal with Arafat. 

Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon says the occupation of Palestinian territories cannot continue indefinitely in May 2003. 

The Arab League meeting takes place in Egypt in June 2003. The meeting expresses support for the "road map." The US, European Union, Russia and UN propose the road map. The Palestinian National Authority accepts it. Israel accepts it. The road map posits an independent Palestinian state. It also posits a freeze on West Bank Jewish settlements. 

Mahmoud Abbas resigns as prime minister in September 2003. He cites US and Israeli intransigence. He also cites internal Palestinian opposition to his government. Fatah veteran Ahmed Qurei succeeds him. 

Israeli forces kill Sheikh Yassin in March 2004. He is the founder and leader of Hamas. Israeli forces kill his successor Abd al-Aziz al-Rantissi the following month. 

The International Court of Justice issues an advisory opinion in July 2004. The opinion states that the Israeli separation barrier violates international law. The barrier must be removed. 

Yasser Arafat dies in hospital in France in November 2004. He went there for urgent medical treatment in October. 

Mahmoud Abbas is elected Mr Arafat's successor in January 2005. He becomes head of the Palestinian National Authority. 

Israel withdraws all Jewish settlements and military personnel from Gaza in September 2005. Israel retains control over airspace. Israel retains control over ports and border crossings. 

The Hamas Islamist group's Ismail Haniyeh forms a government in March 2006. Hamas wins parliamentary elections in January. A struggle for primacy with Fatah begins. The United States and European Union suspend aid. Israel ends tax transfers. This happens because of Hamas's refusal to recognise Israel. Hamas refuses to renounce violence. Hamas refuses to accept previous peace accords. 

Hamas militants from Gaza seize Israeli soldier Gilad Shalit in June 2006. The seizure happens near a border crossing. They hold him hostage for five years. They demand the release of Palestinian prisoners. Major clashes between Israel and Hamas forces in Gaza follow. Israel imposes restrictions on Gaza. 

Clashes break out between Fatah and Hamas supporters in Gaza in September 2006. Various Arab states and Palestinian groups seek to mediate between them. This happens in coming months. They want to avert civil war. 

Fatah and Hamas form a national unity government in March 2007. This ends months of intermittent clashes in Gaza. 

The unity government founders in June 2007. Hamas ousts Fatah from Gaza. Hamas reinforces its control of the territory. Israel tightens the blockade. This happens after an increase in rocket attacks from Gaza. Egypt closes its border with Gaza. Mahmoud Abbas appoints Salam Fayyad as prime minister. Hamas refuses to recognise him. Two rival governments emerge. One is in the West Bank. One is in Gaza. The US and European Union resume aid to the Fayyad government. 

The US hosts the Annapolis Conference in November 2007. The conference establishes the "two-state solution" as the basis for future talks. The talks are between Israel and the Palestinian Authority. This is the first time this happens. 

Efforts at reconciliation between Fatah and Hamas begin in Yemen in March 2008. The next round takes place in Cairo in November. The round stalls. Hamas objects to Fatah arrest of its West Bank activists. 

Israel launches an incursion into Gaza in November 2008. Hamas sees this as a ceasefire violation. Hamas responds by launching rockets. 

Israel launches Operation Cast Lead in December 2008. This is a month-long invasion of Gaza. Israel wants to stop Hamas and other militant groups firing rockets into Israel. 

Fatah and Hamas resume talks on national reconciliation in February 2010. Direct talks resume between Israel and the Palestinian Authority. The talks falter over the question of settlements. 

Nine Turkish pro-Palestinian activists are killed in May 2010. They are killed in an Israeli capture of ships. The ships are attempting to break the maritime blockade of Gaza. 

Fatah and Hamas agree at talks in Cairo in April and May 2011. They agree to reform a unity government. They agree to hold fresh elections. No practical implementation follows. 

The Palestinian National Authority launches a campaign in 2011. The campaign is for UN membership of "State of Palestine." This is a means of highlighting stalled talks with Israel. The bid fails. The UNESCO cultural agency accepts Palestine as a member in October. 

Fatah and Hamas sign the Cairo Agreement in May 2012. This happens after preliminary talks in Qatar. They pledge to maintain non-violent resistance to Israeli occupation. They pursue an independent state within the 1967 ceasefire lines. 

Local elections take place on the West Bank in October 2012. The elections undermine Fatah's position. Fatah wins only two-fifths of the seats contested. The turnout is 55%. Lists led by Fatah rebels win four of the 11 major towns and cities. Independents and leftists take control of a fifth. Hamas boycotts the poll. Hamas allows no elections in Gaza. 

The UN upgrades Palestinian representation in November 2012. The representation becomes that of "non-member observer state." This allows Palestine to take part in General Assembly debates. This improves chances of joining UN agencies. 

Fatah allows a Hamas celebration rally on the West Bank in December 2012. The rally is over the UN status upgrade. Hamas reciprocates this gesture in Gaza the following month. 

Prime Minister Fayyad resigns in April 2013. He resigns after a long-standing dispute with Palestinian Authority Chairman Mahmoud Abbas. Academic Rami Hamdallah succeeds him in May. 

The newly appointed US Secretary of State launches a series of Israeli-Palestinian talks in 2013. The talks aim at reaching a framework peace deal by April 2014. Palestinian officials say continuing Israeli approval of Jewish housing in occupied East Jerusalem undermines progress. Israel accuses the Palestinians of incitement. 

The fall of the Morsi government in Egypt happens in July 2013. This dashes Palestinian hopes for lifting of the Egyptian blockade of the border with Gaza. This suspends Egyptian mediation in the Fatah-Hamas reconciliation process. 

Israel, Jordan and the Palestinian Authority sign a water-sharing pact in December 2013. The pact aims to halt and eventually reverse the drying-out of the Dead Sea. They will lay a pipeline to carry brine from a Red Sea desalination plant. The plant will provide drinking water to the region. 

Egypt bans Hamas activities in March 2014. Egypt seizes its assets. This happens because of links to Egypt's illegal Muslim Brotherhood. 

Fatah and Hamas agree to form a unity government in April 2014. The government takes office in June. Fatah complains that a separate Hamas cabinet continues to rule Gaza. 

Israel responds to the kidnapping and murder of three Jewish teenagers in the West Bank in June 2014. Israel arrests numerous Hamas members. Militants respond to the arrests and the killing of a Palestinian teenager by Jewish extremists. They respond by firing rockets from Gaza. 

Israel responds to attacks from armed groups in Gaza in July and August 2014. Israel launches a military campaign by air and land. The campaign aims to knock out missile launching sites. The campaign aims to attack tunnels. Clashes end in an uneasy Egyptian-brokered ceasefire in August. 

Minister Without Portfolio Ziad Abu Ein dies at a clash with Israeli troops at a West Bank protest in December 2014. 

The Vatican announces that it is to formally recognise Palestinian statehood in May 2015.
syntax_simple_s.xsum::30: David Sulman works for the UK Forest Products Association. He criticised the deal. He said there was a lack of "openness and transparency." Auditors had criticised the deal. NRW said the contracts were awarded in "extraordinary" circumstances. A company was awarded contracts in 2014. The contracts were worth £39m. They were for purchasing spruce timber. They were also for purchasing larch timber. The larch came from forests with a fungus disease. The disease was Phytophthora ramorum. It caused extensive damage. The contracts were part of action by NRW. NRW sells timber from publicly owned woodlands. NRW took action to deal with the disease. The disease had spread rapidly the previous year. A report was published in March. Auditor general Huw Vaughan Thomas wrote it. He expressed doubt about the decision. He questioned whether it met state aid rules. He said the decision-making process was not transparent. Mr Thomas revealed something about the deal. It was made without other companies being allowed to bid. NRW disputed his findings. The agreements were set to be pulled. The company had failed to meet a key promise. The promise was to build a new processing line. The line was for cutting timber. Mr Sulman is executive director of the UK Forest Products Association. The association represents the domestic timber industry. He said the situation was very serious. He said it was disturbing. He said it was worrying for businesses. These businesses are across the forestry sector. They are in the forest public sector in Wales. They are also in areas further afield. He explained their principal concern. Businesses had dealt with Natural Resources Wales historically. They had always been assured of fair dealings. They expected dealings with NRW would be fair. They expected openness. They expected transparency. He said this case appeared different. There seemed to be a considerable lack of fairness. There seemed to be a lack of openness. There seemed to be a lack of transparency. This was giving rise to serious concern. The concern was across the sector at the moment. He said there probably were businesses out there. These businesses felt they were denied opportunities. Fears existed at the time of the deal. The market for larch was on the brink of collapse. This was given as one reason. NRW went ahead with the deal for this reason. Mr Sulman has questioned whether this was the case. Chief executive Emyr Roberts gave evidence. He spoke at a meeting. The meeting was of the assembly's public accounts committee. This happened in March. He said they had a real crisis on their hands at the time of the deal. He said there was a danger. The timber market could collapse at that time. Mr Sulman said the statement was "wildly inaccurate." He said it was "misleading." Events have proved something in the intervening period. The period ran from 2014 through today. The diseased larch was harvested. It has been processed equally well. It has been sold in the market place. He said a full investigation was probably warranted. The public accounts committee should conduct it. The seriousness of the situation warranted this. Mr Sulman will give evidence to the assembly's public accounts committee. The committee is calling NRW in again. They will re-examine the issue. This happens on Monday. Emyr Roberts is chief executive of Natural Resources Wales. He said something in a statement. The contracts were awarded at a point in time. They were dealing with extraordinary circumstances then. Their prime objective at the time was clear. It was to secure a market for the diseased larch. They succeeded in doing so. They followed their agreed processes. They are confident about the evidence. They gave evidence to the previous public accounts committee. The evidence was accurate. It was valid. NRW has not revealed the name of the firm. The firm was awarded the contracts. The Wales Audit Office has not revealed it either.
syntax_simple_s.xsum::31: Denbighshire council wanted to create a new bilingual school. They planned to shut Ysgol Pentrecelyn and Ysgol Llanfair Dyffryn Clwyd in Ruthin. They would open a new site.
