syntax_simple_s.xsum::43: The so-called Egtved Girl was discovered in 1921. She was found in a burial mound in the Jutland Peninsula. The cremated bones of a young child were also found with her. She was estimated to have been between 16 and 18 when she died. People assumed she was Danish. This research has challenged that view. The study has been published in the journal Scientific Reports. A team led by Dr Karin Margarita Frei from the National Museum of Denmark analysed the girl's teeth. They looked for levels of the radioactive element strontium. Strontium exists in the Earth's crust. It is absorbed by humans, animals, and plants through water and food. Natural levels of strontium vary from region to region. Researchers found a certain amount in one of the girl's first teeth. This indicated she grew up in the Black Forest area of southwestern Germany. This location is 800km (500 miles) to the south of her burial place. It was already known that the Egtved Girl was born on a summer's day in 1370 BC. There were few clues in her coffin to where she spent her life. Her clothes pointed to a person of high standing. The girl's bones had been dissolved by the acidic water in the coffin. Her blond hair, teeth, nails and parts of her brain and skin were extraordinarily well preserved. Dr Frei's team traced the final two years of the girl's life. They did this by analysing the elements in her 23-cm-long hair. Their groundbreaking chemical sleuthing showed something important. She had been on a long journey shortly before she died. Dr Frei made a statement about the last two years of the girl's life. She said they could see certain patterns. The girl stayed in a place 13 to 15 months before her death. This place had a strontium isotope signature. The signature was very similar to the one that characterises the area where she was born. Then she moved to an area. This area may well have been Jutland. She spent a period of nine to 10 months there. After that she went back to the region she originally came from. She stayed there for four to six months. Then she travelled to her final resting place, Egtved. That timeline represents something significant. It represents the first time researchers have been able to so accurately track a pre-historic person's movements. Prof Kristian Kristiansen from the University of Gothenburg made a statement. He said the discovery confirmed that Bronze Age Denmark shared close ties with southern Germany. He said the girl was likely given in marriage. This was done to cement ties between two families. He explained more about Bronze Age western Europe. Southern Germany and Denmark were the two dominant centres of power. They were very similar to kingdoms. Many direct connections between the two appear in the archaeological evidence. His guess is that the Egtved Girl was a southern German girl. She was given in marriage to a man in Jutland. This was done to forge an alliance between two powerful families. Parts of Sweden and Norway were also identified as possible locations for her birth. The geologically old Danish island of Bornholm was also identified as a possible location. Southwestern Germany was by far the most likely location. This was according to the research team. Dr Frei and Prof Kristiansen said they now planned to analyse strontium levels in other human remains found in Denmark. They want to piece together the stories of more prehistoric lives.

Some senior figures worry about something. They have spent years trying to persuade constituents. They want constituents to understand something. Many are worried about immigration. Dr Fatoumata Nafo-Traoré heads the Roll Back Malaria Partnership. She is known as RBM. She visited west Africa. She said something after her visit. She said health workers focus all their attention on Ebola. This is understandable. Children's wards used to be full of malaria patients. These wards were becoming ghost areas. She added this observation.

Malaria killed 7,000 people in 2012. This happened in the three countries worst hit by Ebola. Most of these people were young children. Malaria is curable. The disease caused almost 4,000 deaths in Sierra Leone in 2012. It caused around 2,000 deaths in Liberia. It caused approximately 1,000 deaths in Guinea.

The three countries are wrestling with the Ebola virus now. Dr Nafo-Traoré said something. She feared something. Recent gains in preventing malaria could be threatened by the crisis. She said these countries have been really hit by malaria previously. Five years ago it was even worse. The deaths were double then.

Everyone agrees on something. No child should die from malaria. We have the tools to prevent it. We have the tools to treat it. But now all the health workers' attention is on Ebola. This is understandable. Hospital beds used to have three children in them at a time. There was not enough space. Those paediatric wards are becoming ghost areas now. There is a lack of manpower there. We don't know who has malaria. We don't know who is dying from it.

The situation might be at the same level as last year. That was still very bad in those countries. Ebola will cause a setback to the efforts on malaria. This is a real concern. There is a lack of trust in health workers. There is a lack of confidence in health workers. People still have a feeling. They feel health workers are bringing the virus to people.

RBM is a partnership. It includes more than 500 organisations. It was formed 16 years ago. Its purpose is to coordinate global efforts against malaria. Guinea and Sierra Leone met key targets last year. They distributed bed nets. Bed nets are a crucial weapon. They protect children from mosquitoes. Mosquitoes spread malaria. The situation in Liberia was less positive. Officials there are trying to work out something. They want to boost their distribution efforts. They are trying to contain Ebola too.

One problem exists. The early symptoms of Ebola and malaria can be similar. Dr Nafo-Traoré travelled by road. She went from Conakry in Guinea to Sierra Leone. This happened earlier this month. She told me something. The Ebola treatment centres have a protocol. They treat cases of fever with anti-malarial drugs too. The patient might be suffering from both diseases.

People have fevers at the moment. They are often afraid to go to healthcare facilities. They want to avoid being held in the Ebola treatment centres. We are working with the countries. We want to ensure something. People need to be tested for malaria. They need to get the drugs.

It's important to have an approach. The approach must be coordinated. A key aim exists. The aim is to decrease cases of malaria-related fever. The Ebola centres must not get overwhelmed. She is worried. The health systems are weak. Communication is so easy. It happens between all 15 of the West African countries.

Ebola occurred in remote bush areas in the past. Today it's happening in capital cities. People are getting organised now. She travelled by road there. She saw checkpoints. People were having their temperature taken there. They were washing their hands. The world has received something fortunately. It received a wake-up call. But the response was slow at the beginning.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::0: Regulatory testing schemes for genetic damage have been standardized for several decades. The tests being utilized examined mutations. They also examined structural chromosomal damage. They examined numerical chromosomal damage too. This has served the genetic toxicity community well. Most of the substances being tested were amenable to such assays. The outcome from this testing is usually a dichotomous evaluation of test results. It provides a yes or no answer. In many instances, the information is only used for one purpose. That purpose is to determine whether a substance has carcinogenic potential or not. Over the same time period, mechanisms have been recognized. Modes of action have been recognized too. These modes of action are called MOAs. They elucidate a wider range of genomic damage. This genomic damage is involved in many adverse health outcomes. In addition, a paradigm shift in applied genetic toxicology is moving the field. It moves the field toward a more quantitative dose-response analysis. It also moves toward point-of-departure determination. This is called PoD determination. There is a focus on risks to exposed humans. This is directing emphasis on genomic damage. This genomic damage is likely to induce changes. These changes are associated with a variety of adverse health outcomes. This paradigm shift is moving the testing emphasis for genetic damage. It moves from a hazard identification only evaluation. It moves to a more comprehensive risk assessment approach. This approach provides more insightful information for decision makers. The information regards the potential risk of genetic damage to exposed humans. A next generation testing strategy needs to take into account a broader approach. This approach must be more flexible. It applies to testing. It ultimately applies to modeling of genomic damage too. This genomic damage relates to human exposure. This enables a broader context for examining genetic damage. This is consistent with the larger risk assessment context. This context is being used in regulatory decision making. This flexible approach for examining genomic damage is presented here. It focuses on testing for relevant genomic effects. These effects can be associated with an adverse health effect. This association should be as good as possible. The most desired linkage for risk to humans would be changes in loci. These loci are associated with human diseases. This applies whether in somatic cells or in germ cells. The outline of a flexible approach is presented. Associated considerations are presented too. They are presented in a series of nine steps. Some of these steps can occur in parallel. This was developed through a collaborative effort. Leading genetic toxicologists participated. They came from academia. They came from government. They came from industry. They worked through the International Life Sciences Institute. This is called ILSI. They worked through the Health and Environmental Sciences Institute. This is called HESI. They worked through the Genetic Toxicology Technical Committee. This is called GTTC. The ultimate goal is to provide quantitative data. This data can model the potential risk levels of substances. These substances induce genomic damage. This genomic damage contributes to human adverse health outcomes. Any good risk assessment begins with a specific action. It begins with asking the appropriate risk management questions. This happens in a planning effort. This happens in a scoping effort. This step sets up the problem. The problem needs to be addressed. For example, broadly, does genomic damage need to be addressed? And if so, how to proceed? The next two steps assemble what is known about the problem. They do this by building a knowledge base. This knowledge base is about the substance of concern. They also develop a rational biological argument. This argument explains why testing for genomic damage is needed or not. The focus is on the risk management problem. The focus is also on potential genomic damage of concern. The next step of assay selection takes place. The work-up of the problem during the earlier steps provides the insight. This insight shows which assays would most likely produce the most meaningful data. This discussion does not detail the wide range of genomic damage tests available. But it points to types of testing systems. These testing systems can be very useful. Once the assays are performed, they are analyzed. The relevant data sets are selected for modeling potential risk. From this point on, the data are evaluated. They are modeled as they are for any other toxicology endpoint. Any observed genomic damage can be modeled. Any observed effects can be modeled. Any genetic events can be modeled. They can be modeled via a dose-response analysis. They can be modeled via determination of an estimated PoD. When a quantitative risk analysis is needed for decision making, something happens. A parallel exposure assessment effort is performed. Exposure assessment is not detailed here. This is not the focus of this discussion. Guidelines for this assessment exist elsewhere. Then the PoD for genomic damage is used. It is used with the exposure information. They develop risk estimations together. These use reference dose, which is called RfD. These use margin of exposure approaches. These are called MOE approaches. This happens in a risk characterization. It is presented to risk managers. It informs decision making. This approach is applicable now. It incorporates genomic damage results into the decision-making process. This process assesses potential adverse outcomes in chemically exposed humans. It is consistent with the ILSI HESI Risk Assessment in the 21st Century roadmap. This is called RISK21 roadmap. This applies to any substance. Humans are exposed to these substances. This includes pharmaceuticals. This includes agricultural products. This includes food additives. This includes other chemicals. It is time for regulatory bodies to do something. They need to incorporate the broader knowledge. They need to incorporate the insights provided by genomic damage results. These results go into the assessments of risk. This helps to more fully understand the potential of adverse outcomes. These outcomes happen in chemically exposed humans. Thus this improves the assessment of risk. This risk is due to genomic damage. The historical use of genomic damage data has been too narrowly focused. It has been used as a yes or no gateway. This gateway was for possible cancer risk. It has been too narrowly focused in risk assessment. The recent advances in assaying for genomic damage add information. The recent advances in understanding genomic damage add information too. This includes eventually epigenetic alterations. Obviously these add a greater wealth of information. This information determines potential risk to humans. Regulatory bodies need to embrace this paradigm shift. The shift moves from hazard identification to quantitative analysis. They need to incorporate the wider range of genomic damage. This goes in their assessments of risk to humans. The quantitative analyses discussed here can be readily applied. The methodologies discussed here can be readily applied too. They apply to genomic damage testing results now.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::1: Nutritional supplements may improve development of infants born small. These are preterm infants or infants small for gestational age (SGA). The supplements may increase the risk of later metabolic disease. We conducted a systematic review. We also conducted a meta-analysis. We wanted to assess the effects of macronutrient supplements for infants born small. We looked at later development. We looked at metabolism. We searched OvidMedline. We searched Embase. We searched Cochrane CENTRAL. We searched Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. We searched from inception to April 1, 2019. We also searched controlled-trials.com. We searched clinicaltrials.gov. We searched anzctr.org.au. We included randomised trials. We included quasirandomised trials. The trials had to meet certain criteria. The intention was to increase macronutrient intake. The goal was to improve growth or development of infants born small. The trials assessed post-discharge outcomes. Co-primary outcomes were cognitive impairment and metabolic risk. We evaluated these in toddlers. Toddlers are under 3 years old. We evaluated these in childhood. Childhood is 3 to 8 years. We evaluated these in adolescence. Adolescence is 9 to 18 years. Two reviewers independently extracted data. We assessed quality. We used the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. We pooled data. We used random-effect models. Twenty-one randomised trials were included. One quasirandomised trial was included. The trials had variable methodological quality. The trials involved 3,680 infants. We looked at toddlers born small. Supplementation did not alter cognitive impairment. The relative risk (RR) was 1.00. The 95% confidence interval (CI) was 0.67 to 1.49. P equaled 0.99. There were no differences in cognitive scores. The mean difference (MD) was 0.57. The 95% CI was -0.71 to 1.84. P equaled 0.38. There were no differences in motor scores. The MD was 1.16. The 95% CI was -0.32 to 2.65. P equaled 0.12. We compared supplemented groups to unsupplemented groups. However, fewer supplemented children had motor impairment. The RR was 0.76. The 95% CI was 0.62 to 0.94. P equaled 0.01. We did subgroup analyses. Supplementation improved cognitive scores in boys. The MD was 5.60. The 95% CI was 1.07 to 10.14. P equaled 0.02. Supplementation did not improve cognitive scores in girls born small. The MD was -2.04. The 95% CI was -7.04 to 2.95. P equaled 0.42. Supplementation did not alter cognitive scores in children born SGA. It did not alter motor scores in this subgroup either. We looked at childhood. There was no difference in cognitive impairment. The RR was 0.81. The 95% CI was 0.26 to 2.57. P equaled 0.72. There was no difference in cognitive scores. The MD was 1.02. The 95% CI was -1.91 to 3.95. P equaled 0.50. We compared supplemented groups to unsupplemented groups. There were no differences in blood pressure. There were no differences in triglyceride concentrations. There were no differences in low-density lipoprotein (LDL) concentrations. All P values were greater than 0.05. However, supplemented children had lower fasting glucose. The MD in mmol/L was -0.20. The 95% CI was -0.34 to -0.06. P equaled 0.005. They had higher high-density lipoprotein (HDL) concentrations. The MD in mmol/L was 0.11. The 95% CI was 0.02 to 0.19. P equaled 0.02. We did subgroup analyses. There was no evidence of differences in blood pressure. We compared supplemented groups to unsupplemented groups. This applied to boys born small. This applied to girls born small. This applied to SGA children. We looked at adolescence. There was no difference in blood pressure. There was no difference in triglycerides. There was no difference in LDL concentrations. There was no difference in HDL concentrations. There was no difference in fasting blood glucose. There was no difference in insulin resistance. There was no difference in fasting insulin concentrations. We compared supplemented groups to unsupplemented groups. All P values were greater than 0.05. Limitations include considerable unexplained heterogeneity. The evidence had low to very low quality. There was limited data beyond early childhood. This was a systematic review. This was a meta-analysis of randomised trials. We found no evidence. Early
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::2: Objectives Recently, two point-of-care (PoC) feline immunodeficiency virus (FIV) antibody test kits were reported. These kits were Witness and Anigen Rapid. syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::3: Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) is a rare monogenic disorder. It is characterized by benign tumors in multiple organs. syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::4: Silica nanoparticles (nanoSiO 2 ) are promising systems. They can deliver biologically active compounds to tissues. They can deliver them to the heart. syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::5: Return to play (RTP) of National Football League (NFL) athletes after isolated anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tears has been reported. syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::6: Pulmonary hypertension in response to exercise is a marker of the hemodynamic severity of mitral stenosis. This condition is called MS. syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::7: The impact of chronic liver disease on outcomes in patients with COVID-19 is uncertain. We aimed to explore this association. syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::9: Temperature and water availability are two of the most important variables. They affect all aspects of an anuran's key physiological processes. syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::11: Some infectious diseases may be transmitted through the air. These diseases include influenza, tuberculosis, and SARS-CoV-2. An infectious person expels virus-laden particles. Someone else inhales these particles. This process is known as the airborne transmission route. The virus-laden particles are more concentrated in the expiratory jet of an infectious person. They are less concentrated elsewhere in a well-mixed room. This is called near-field enhancement in virion exposure. Scientists have not quantified this enhancement well. Transmission of airborne viruses depends on many factors. These factors are inherently variable. In many cases, these factors are poorly constrained. Scientists need large ensembles of model simulations to quantify this uncertainty. These simulations must span the variability in input parameters. Some models can simulate the near-field evolution of respiratory particles well. However, these models are also computationally expensive. This expense limits the exploration of parametric uncertainty. Scientists wanted to perform many simulations. These simulations needed to span the wide variability in factors. These factors govern airborne transmission. Scientists developed a new model. The model is called the Quadrature-based model of Respiratory Aerosol and Droplets. The abbreviation is QuaRAD. QuaRAD is an efficient framework. It simulates the evolution of virus-laden particles. An infectious person expels these particles. The particles then deposit to the nasal cavity of a susceptible person. QuaRAD also simulates the subsequent risk of initial infection. Scientists simulated 10,000 scenarios. They wanted to quantify the risk of initial infection by a particular virus. That virus was SARS-CoV-2. The predicted risk of infection was highly variable among scenarios. The risk was strongly enhanced near the infectious individual in each scenario. Scientists examined more than 50% of scenarios. The physical distancing needed to avoid near-field enhancements was beyond two meters. Two meters equals six feet. This was true if the infectious person is not wearing a mask. The distance defining the near-field extent was also highly variable among scenarios. Variability in expiration velocity explained the variability in near-field extent predominantly. The findings suggest something important. Maintaining at least two meters of distance from an infectious person greatly reduces exposure to airborne virions. Protections against airborne transmission should be available. These protections include N95 respirators. They are necessary when distancing is not possible.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::12: Open fractures are contaminated wounds. They contain gram-positive organisms. They contain gram-negative organisms. syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::13: PURPOSE: Cyclical patterns of compliance have been observed with many health-related activities. These activities include dieting and exercise. It is not known whether such patterns of compliance exist among users of chronic medications. We sought to estimate the percentage of patients who restart osteoporosis therapy after a prolonged lapse in medication use. We also wanted to identify the factors associated with a return to compliance. METHODS: We studied 26,636 new users of an osteoporosis medication. These medications included alendronate, calcitonin, estrogen, raloxifene, or risedronate. The patients were age 65 or older. They had an extended lapse in refill compliance. We defined this lapse as a period of at least 60 days after the completion of one prescription. During this period no refill for any osteoporosis medication was obtained. Survival curves were used to estimate the length of time until therapy is resumed. We estimated the association between patient characteristics and the rate of resuming treatment. We used Cox proportional hazards analysis for this estimation. We then conducted a case crossover analysis. This analysis examined whether certain events occurring during follow-up triggered a return to refill compliance. RESULTS: Patients stopped therapy for at least 60 days. An estimated 30% restarted treatment within 6 months. An estimated 50% restarted within 2 years. Some patients had at least 6 months of continuous use before their interruption in treatment. There were 5863 such patients. Among these patients, 42% restarted therapy within 6 months. Among these patients, 59% restarted within 2 years. Younger patients were more likely to return after a break in medication use. Women were more likely to return. Those with a history of a fracture were more likely to return. Recent hip fractures predicted a return to treatment. Discharges from nursing homes predicted a return to treatment. Bone mineral density testing also predicted a return to treatment. CONCLUSION: Extended gaps in treatment are common among users of osteoporosis medications. The effectiveness of these drugs used in an interrupted way is unknown. Compliance interventions should emphasize the need for continuous medication use. Further research is needed. We must understand why patients often go for months without refilling prescriptions. We must also determine whether similar utilization patterns exist for other chronic medications.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::14: Imbalances in the gut microbial community (dysbiosis) of vertebrates have been associated with several gastrointestinal and autoimmune diseases. syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::15: We investigate the reason for the quantum speedup. Quantum algorithms require fewer computation steps than their classical counterparts. It would tell her the function computed by the black box. The function should be hidden inside the box to her. We resort to relational quantum mechanics. This retrocausality model provides useful information. Given an oracle problem and a value of R, it provides the number of black box computations required to solve it. Given a known quantum algorithm, it yields the value of R. This value of R explains its speed up. R equals one half always yields the number of black box computations required by an existing quantum algorithm. It also yields the order of magnitude of the number required by optimal one.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::16: Cardiac disease can increase the risk for thrombosis events. Clinical intervention can also increase this risk. syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::17: The diffuse very high-energy (VHE, > 100 GeV) gamma-ray emission was observed in the central 200 pc of the Milky Way. H.E.S.S. made this observation. syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::18: These international clinical practice recommendations (CPR) for developmental coordination disorder (DCD) were initiated by the European Academy of Childhood Disability (EACD). syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::19: Hypertension can lead to mood disorders. These disorders may worsen or ameliorate. This depends on the type of antihypertensive prescribed. syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::20: This study evaluates rapid response teams (RRTs) for different triggering events in total hip arthroplasty (THA) patients. These patients underwent primary or revision THA. We queried information about demographics. We also queried the primary reason for RRT. We examined the Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI). Mean age was 65.2 ± 14.1 years. Mean body mass index was 32.3 ± 4.8. Sixty-six percent were female. Length of stay in RRT for primary THA was 3.4 days. Length of stay for revision THA was 6.2 days. There were no mortalities. RRTs for hypotension/presyncope (11%) resulted in significantly fewer changes in management (P < .01). RRTs for syncope (11%) also resulted in fewer changes. Tachycardia (77%), hypoxia (57%), AMS (79%), and other (47%) resulted in more changes. RRTs for hypotension/presyncope (28%) resulted in significantly fewer patients being uptriaged (P < .001). Syncope (15%) and hypoxia (30%) also resulted in fewer uptriages. Tachycardia resulted in more uptriages (81%). AMS/delirium was significantly more commonly caused by opioids/over-sedation (71%) (P < .001). syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::21: Emergency medical services are an important part of acute stroke management. We devised a prehospital stroke scale in December 2006. We call it the TOYOTA prehospital stroke scale for tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) intravenous therapy (TOPSPIN). It triages patients with ischemic stroke. They include disturbance of the upper extremities. They include disturbance of the lower extremities. The aim of this study was to analyze the results. We analyzed 10 years of TOPSPIN implementation. We wanted to distinguish ischemic stroke from hemorrhagic stroke in the real world. We prospectively enrolled consecutive patients. These patients were transferred to our hospital. Toyota city ambulance services evaluated them. The services used the TOPSPIN. This occurred from December 2006 to January 2017. We examined definite diagnosis at the time of hospital discharge. We looked at ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, or stroke mimic. We examined positive-predictive value of the stroke. We examined the rate of the recanalization therapy. We examined clinical differentiation among patients. These patients had hemorrhagic stroke, ischemic stroke, and stroke mimics. A total of 1,482 consecutive patients were enrolled. 1,134 patients (76.5%) were patients with stroke. This included 628 ischemic-type. This included 34 transient ischemic attack-type. This included 472 hemorrhagic-type. 348 patients (23.5%) were without stroke. This included 80 with seizure, 42 with syncope, 27 with hypoglycemia, and 199 other. Several factors were more commonly associated with ischemic stroke than with hemorrhagic stroke. These factors included the presence of atrial fibrillation, older age, lower blood pressure, and lower total TOPSPIN score. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, the presence of atrial fibrillation was independently associated with ischemic stroke. The odds ratio was 2.33. syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::22: We aim to determine the redshift of GDS-1408. GDS-1408 is the most solid z~7 galaxy candidate. It lies in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field. syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::23: The survival of Salmonella spp. as pathogen indicator in composting was studied. The inoculums technique was used. syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::24: BACKGROUND: Race is associated with prostate cancer progression in early stage disease. Men have advanced disease. syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::25: We present deep Hubble Space Telescope single-star photometry of Leo A in B, V, and I. Our new field of view is offset from the centrally located field. syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::26: One goal of neuromorphic engineering is to create 'realistic' robotic systems. These systems interact with the physical world. We build them from first principles. It is a precursor to neuromorphic robotic systems.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::27: Introduction and Objective: Patients present with a urinary tract infection. They have kidney stones. They have ureteral stones. This is a urologic emergency. They were more likely to require postoperative intensive care unit-level care. They were more likely to have bacteremia. They had a longer length of stay. In multivariate analysis we used significant variables from univariate analysis. Only previous ureteroscopy was significantly associated with antibiotic resistance. It had an increased odds of 6.95. The p value was 0.011. Conclusions: In this study, we show one thing. A history of ureteroscopy is significantly associated with antibiotic resistance. This was true in both univariate analyses. This was true in multivariate analyses. Our findings suggest something. Patients with history of ureteroscopy should await urine culture results. Those without a history of ureteroscopy may be discharged early on empiric oral antibiotics. However, future studies are necessary. They must determine the effectiveness of this predictor.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::28: Evidence details something. Cannabis can influence the use of other psychoactive substances. These substances include prescription medications. Data came from a survey. The survey included 2102 people. These people were enrolled in the Canadian medical cannabis program. We included 973 respondents. This number represents 44 percent. These respondents reported using alcohol. They used it on at least 10 occasions. This happened over a 12 month period. This period came before they started medical cannabis. We then used retrospective data. This data concerned the frequency of alcohol use. It concerned the amount of alcohol use. We examined use before medical cannabis. They reported decreases in alcohol usage frequency. This frequency was measured over 30 days. Another 323 participants decreased something. This number represents 34 percent. They decreased the number of standard drinks. These were drinks they had per week. Additionally, 76 participants reported something. This number represents 8 percent. They reported no alcohol use at all. This was in the 30 days before the survey. Being below 55 years of age mattered. Reporting higher rates of alcohol use in the earlier period mattered too. Both factors were associated with greater odds. These were odds of reducing alcohol use. An intention to use medical cannabis mattered. This intention was to reduce alcohol consumption. syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::29: The delicate balance between spin-orbit coupling, Coulomb repulsion and crystalline electric field interactions is observed in Ir-based oxides. This balance is usually manifested as exotic magnetic behavior. Here we investigate the evolution of the exchange coupling between Co and Ir. We do this for partial La substitution by Ca in La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$. The use of Ca$^{2+}$ as replacement for La$^{3+}$ has a great advantage. The advantage is the similarity of its ionic radii. Thus, the observed magnetic changes can more easily be associated to electronic variations. We carried out a thorough investigation of the structural, electronic and magnetic properties of the La$_{2-x}$Ca$_{x}$CoIrO$_6$ system. We did this by means of synchrotron x-ray powder diffraction, muon spin rotation and relaxation ($\mu$SR), AC and DC magnetization, XAS, XMCD, Raman spectroscopy, electrical resistivity and dielectric permittivity. Our XAS results show something important. Up to 25% of Ca substitution at the La site results in the emergence of Co$^{3+}$. This is possibly in high spin state. The introduction of larger amount of Ca leads to the increase of Ir valence. The competing magnetic interactions result from the mixed valences. These interactions lead to a coexistence of a magnetically ordered state and an emerging spin glass (SG) state for the doped samples. Our $\mu$SR results indicate something for La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$. A nearly constant fraction of a paramagnetic (PM) phase persists down to low temperature. This is possibly related to the presence of a small amount of Ir$^{3+}$. It is also related to the anti-site disorder at Co/Ir sites. For the doped compounds the PM phase freezes below 30 K. But there is still some dynamics associated with the SG. We obtained dielectric data for the parent compound and the one with 25% of Ca-doping. These data indicate a possible magnetodielectric effect. This effect is discussed in terms of the electron hopping between the TM ions. It is also discussed in terms of the anti-site disorder and the distorted crystalline structure.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::30: The new sixth-generation (6G) internet-of-things (IoT) use cases have stringent requirements. Traditional approaches to multiple access control have started to show their limitations. A new wave of grant-free (GF) approaches have been proposed. They offer a viable alternative. However, a definitive solution is still to be accomplished. We propose a new semi-GF coordinated random access (RA) protocol in our work. We denote it as partial-information multiple access (PIMA). It reduces packet loss and latency. This happens particularly in the presence of sporadic activations. We consider a machine-type communications (MTC) scenario. Devices need to transmit data packets in the uplink to a base station (BS) in this scenario. The BS can acquire partial information on the instantaneous traffic conditions when using PIMA. The BS uses compute-over-the-air techniques. It estimates the number of devices with packets waiting for transmission in their queue. The BS assigns to each device a single slot for transmission. This assignment is based on this knowledge. However, each slot may still be assigned to multiple users. Collisions may occur. Both the total number of allocated slots and the user assignments are optimized. This optimization is based on the estimated number of active users. It reduces collisions. It improves the efficiency of the multiple access scheme. We compare PIMA to time-division multiple-access (TDMA) and slotted ALOHA (SALOHA) schemes. We do this to prove the validity of our solution. These schemes are the ideal solutions for orthogonal multiple access (OMA) in the time domain. They apply in the case of low and high traffic conditions, respectively. We show that PIMA is able to adapt to different traffic conditions. It provides fewer packet drops regardless of the intensity of packet generations. PIMA merges the advantages of both TDMA and SALOHA schemes. It provides performance improvements in terms of packet loss probability and latency.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::31: Background and purpose â?? Bone remodeling occurs as a response to bone trauma. It also occurs with postoperative immobilization. Device-related bone reactions cause it too. This remodeling can lead to loss of bone stock. It can increase the risk of periprosthetic fracture. It can increase the risk of aseptic loosening. This study investigates the adaptive bone remodeling of the proximal tibia. The remodeling occurs after uncemented total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Patients and methods â?? We performed a 2-year follow up of 53 patients. The patients had a mean age of 62 years. The range was 38â??70 years. 27 of them were men. They received an uncemented TKA in a randomized controlled trial. Bone mineral density (BMD) was the secondary endpoint. We randomized patients to 2 groups. Group A received monoblock polyethylene design. Group B received modular polyethylene design. We performed the TKAs using the uncemented Zimmer Nexgen trabecular metal. We did measurements of BMD postoperatively. We repeated them after 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. We measured BMD in 3 regions of interest (ROI). Results and interpretation â?? Group A showed statistically significant changes in BMD after 24 months. These changes occurred in both the medial and lateral ROI. BMD decreased medially by 15%. The p value was 0.004. It decreased laterally by 13%. The p value was 0.01. Group B showed limited BMD changes. The values returned to the preoperative values after 24 months. The differences in BMD change between groups were statistically significant. The medial ROI showed significance at p equals 0.03. The lateral ROI showed significance at p equals 0.02. We found no significant change in BMD in the distal ROI. Neither group showed this change. The 2 groups showed a significantly different bone remodeling pattern of the proximal tibia. The knees that received the monoblock polyethylene design showed a higher degree of bone loss. The flexible monoblock implant design had previously shown improvement in fixation. It does not decrease the bone loss of the proximal tibia.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::32: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) are bio-inspired models of neural computation. They have proven highly effective. Still, ANNs lack a natural notion of time. Neural units in ANNs exchange analog values in a frame-based manner. This is a computationally and energetically inefficient form of communication. This contrasts sharply with biological neurons. Biological neurons communicate sparingly and efficiently. They use binary spikes. Artificial Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) can be constructed. One replaces the units of an ANN with spiking neurons. The current performance is far from that of deep ANNs on hard benchmarks. These SNNs use much higher firing rates compared to their biological counterparts. This limits their efficiency. Here we show something important. Spiking neurons employ an efficient form of neural coding. They can be used to construct SNNs. These SNNs match high-performance ANNs. They exceed state-of-the-art in SNNs on important benchmarks. They require much lower average firing rates. For this, we use spike-time coding. It is based on the firing rate limiting adaptation phenomenon. This phenomenon is observed in biological spiking neurons. This phenomenon can be captured in adapting spiking neuron models. We derive the effective transfer function for these models. Neural units in ANNs are trained with this transfer function. They can be substituted directly with adaptive spiking neurons. The resulting Adaptive SNNs (AdSNNs) can carry out inference in deep neural networks. They use up to an order of magnitude fewer spikes compared to previous SNNs. Adaptive spike-time coding additionally allows for the dynamic control of neural coding precision. We show how a simple model of arousal in AdSNNs further halves the average required firing rate. This notion naturally extends to other forms of attention. AdSNNs thus hold promise as a novel and efficient model for neural computation. They naturally fit to temporally continuous and asynchronous applications.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::33:
Context. LQ Hya is one of the most frequently studied young solar analogue stars. It has been observed recently. Long-term photometry shows intriguing behaviour. Various authors have reported a coherent spot structure during 2003--2009. This structure migrated in the rotational frame. Since that time the star has entered a chaotic state. Coherent structures seem to have disappeared. Rapid phase jumps of the photometric minima occur irregularly over time.

Aims. LQ Hya is one of the stars included in the SOFIN/FIES long-term monitoring campaign. This campaign extends over 25 years. Here we publish new temperature maps for the star during 2006--2017. These maps cover the chaotic state of the star.

Methods. We use a Doppler imaging technique. This technique derives surface temperature maps from high-resolution spectra.

Results. We examine the mean temperatures of the Doppler maps. We see a weak but systematic increase in the surface temperature of the star. This is consistent with the simultaneously increasing photometric magnitude. We see a high-latitude spot structure during nearly all observing seasons. This structure is clearly nonaxisymmetric. The phase behaviour of this structure is very chaotic. It agrees reasonably well with the photometry. Equatorial spots are also frequently seen. We interpret many of them to be artefacts. This is due to the poor to moderate phase coverage.

Conclusions. The spot topology has remained very similar even during the chaotic phase of the star. It resembles the higher activity epochs with more coherent and long-lived spot structures. We see high-latitude and equatorial spot activity. The mid latitude range is still most often void of spots. We interpret the erratic jumps and drifts in phase of the photometric minima. They are caused by changes in the high-latitude spot structure. The equatorial spots do not cause them.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::34: Context: Hydrogenation reactions are expected to be among the most important surface reactions on interstellar ices. Solid state astrochemical laboratory data on reactions of H-atoms with common interstellar ice constituents are largely lacking. These data are needed. Aims: The goal of our laboratory work is to determine whether carbon dioxide (CO2), formic acid (HCOOH) and acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) react with H-atoms in the solid state at low temperatures. We want to know how they react. We also want to derive reaction rates and production yields. Methods: Pure CO2, HCOOH and CH3CHO interstellar ice analogues are bombarded by H-atoms in an ultra-high vacuum experiment. The ices are monitored by reflection absorption infrared spectroscopy. The reaction products are detected in the gas phase through temperature programmed desorption. This determines the destruction and formation yields. It also determines the corresponding reaction rates. Results: We conclude that H-atom bombardment of pure CO2 and HCOOH ice does not result in detectable reaction products. This is within the sensitivity of our set-up. The upper limits on the reaction rates are less or equal to 7e(-17) cm^2/s. This makes it unlikely that these species play a major role in the formation of more complex organics in interstellar ices due to reactions with H-atoms. CH3CHO does react with H-atoms. This is in contrast to the other species. At most 20% is hydrogenated to ethanol (C2H5OH). A second reaction route leads to the break-up of the C-C bond. This forms solid state CH4 (~20%). It also forms H2CO and CH3OH (15-50%). The methane production yield is expected to be equal to the summed yield of H2CO and CH3OH. CH4 most likely evaporates partly after formation. This happens due to the high exothermicity of the reaction. The reaction rates for CH3CHO destruction depend on ice temperature. They do not depend on ice thickness.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::35: The methodology of funnel control was introduced in the early 2000s. It has developed since then in many respects. It has achieved a level of mathematical maturity. This maturity is balanced by practical applications. Its fundamental tenet is the attainment of prescribed transient behaviour. It also aims for prescribed asymptotic behaviour. These apply to continuous-time controlled dynamical processes. The processes encompass linear systems. They also encompass nonlinear systems. These systems are described by functional differential equations. They include differential-algebraic systems. They include partial differential equations. We consider classes of systems. These classes are specified by structural properties. The properties include relative degree. They include stable internal dynamics. These are properties of the systems only. The precise systems' data are in general unknown. The latter reflects a property. Any model of a dynamical process is not precise in general. Several things are prespecified. A funnel is shaped through the choice of a smooth function. The designer freely chooses this. A fairly large class of smooth reference signals is given. A system class is provided. This class satisfies certain structural properties. The aim is to design a control strategy. The design is based on the structural assumptions. It uses the input information only. It uses the output information only. We design a single simple control strategy. This is called the funnel controller. Its application goes to any system of the given class. It goes to any reference signal. This results in feasibility of the funnel control objective. Solutions of the closed-loop system do not exhibit blow-up in finite time. All variables are bounded. Most importantly, the evolution of the error remains within the prespecified funnel. This error is between the system's output and the reference signal. In the Introduction, we describe the genesis of funnel control. After that, we investigate diverse system classes. These classes are amenable to funnel control. Funnel control is shown for systems with arbitrary relative degree. It is shown for systems described by partial differential equations. Finally, we discuss input constraints. We discuss applications.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::36: Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks are becoming more diverse. This makes it extremely challenging to design a fully protected network. Stealthy Link Flooding Attack (SLFA) is a variant of DDoS attacks. It strives to block access to a target area. It does this by flooding a small set of links. It can bypass traditional DDoS defense mechanisms. This has been shown in research. One potential solution exists to tackle such SLFAs. The solution is to apply Moving Target Defense (MTD) techniques. In MTD, network settings are dynamically changed. This confuses attackers. It deceives attackers. This makes it highly expensive to launch a successful attack. However, MTD comes with some overhead to the network. Finding the best strategy of applying it has been a major challenge. We need to know when to apply it. We need to know to what extent to apply it. The strategy is significantly influenced by the attacker's behavior. This behavior is often difficult to guess. In this work, we address the challenge. We want to obtain the optimal MTD strategy. This strategy effectively mitigates SLFAs. It also incurs a minimal overhead. We design the problem as a signaling game. We consider the network defender and the attacker as players. A belief function is established throughout the engagement. The attacker and the defender engage during this SLFA campaign. The belief function is utilized to pick the best response for each player. It picks the best action for each player. We analyze the game model. We derive a defense mechanism. This mechanism is based on the equilibria of the game. We evaluate the technique on a Mininet-based network environment. An attacker is performing SLFAs in this environment. A defender applies MTD based on equilibria of the game. The results show something important. Our signaling game-based dynamic defense mechanism can provide a similar level of protection against SLFAs. It works like the extensive MTD solution. However, it causes a significantly reduced overhead.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::37: Multi-fidelity (MF) methods are gaining popularity. They enhance surrogate modeling and design optimization. They incorporate data from various low-fidelity (LF) models. Most existing MF methods assume a fixed dataset. Adaptive sampling methods dynamically allocate resources among fidelity models. These methods can achieve higher efficiency. They explore and exploit the design space more effectively. However, most existing MF methods have limitations. They rely on the hierarchical assumption of fidelity levels. They fail to capture the intercorrelation between multiple fidelity levels. They do not utilize this intercorrelation properly. They cannot quantify the value of future samples accurately. They cannot navigate adaptive sampling effectively. We address this hurdle. We propose a framework. The framework is hinged on a latent embedding. This embedding represents different fidelity models. The framework uses pre-posterior analysis. This analysis explicitly utilizes their correlation for adaptive sampling. Each infill sampling iteration includes two steps in this framework. We first identify the location of interest. This location has the greatest potential improvement. We use the high-fidelity (HF) model for this identification. Then we search for the next sample. We search across all fidelity levels. We maximize the improvement per unit cost. We focus on the location identified in the first step. A single Latent Variable Gaussian Process (LVGP) model makes this possible. The LVGP model maps different fidelity models into an interpretable latent space. It captures their correlations. It does not assume hierarchical fidelity levels. The LVGP enables us to assess something important. We can determine how LF sampling candidates will affect HF response. We use pre-posterior analysis for this assessment. We determine the next sample. We select the sample with the best benefit-to-cost ratio. We demonstrate results through test cases. The proposed method outperforms the benchmark methods. It excels in both MF global fitting (GF) and Bayesian Optimization (BO) problems. It shows better convergence rate and robustness. Moreover, the method offers flexibility. Users can switch between GF and BO. They simply change the acquisition function.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::38: Cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum are secondary lesions. Significant increases in cytokine levels in the brain induce them. They are associated with subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). However, their clinical significance in SAH patients remains unclear. We retrospectively analyzed SAH patients. Our hospital treated these patients. We evaluated between-group differences in the backgrounds, clinical findings, and outcomes. We compared SAH patients who developed cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum with those who did not. We further compared patients who achieved good outcomes with those who had poor outcomes. We used multivariate logistic regression analysis. This analysis identified risk factors for poor clinical outcomes. We analyzed 159 SAH patients. 17 patients (10.7%) had cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum. Patients with cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum were more likely to be in a severe condition. World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies grading IV-V showed this: odds ratio [OR], 4.53; 95% confidence interval [95% CI]: 1.60-12.84; p = 0.0042. They had an intraventricular hematoma more often (OR, 5.98; 95% CI: 1.32-27.13; p = 0.0054). They also had an intraparenchymal hematoma more often (OR, 3.62; 95% CI: 1.25-10.45; p = 0.023). Patients with cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum had a greater propensity of a poor outcome 3 months after onset. Modified Rankin Scale score 0-2 showed this: OR, 0.22; 95% CI: 0.07-0.66; p = 0.0043. Multivariate analysis confirmed this finding. Cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum increased the risk of a poor outcome (OR, 4.39; 95% CI: 1.06-18.1; p = 0.037). The development of cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum may be related to the extent of hematomas in SAH patients. These lesions are usually reversible lesions. However, the development of cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum may be a predictor of poor outcomes in SAH patients.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::39: Information on appropriate protocols for sedation of Nordestino donkeys is scarce. This study evaluated the sedative and cardiorespiratory effects of low doses of intravenous (i.v.) xylazine. The study tested xylazine with and without acepromazine in 'Nordestino' donkeys. Seven healthy female Nordestino donkeys were included in this blinded, randomised, crossover experiment. The donkeys weighed 150 ± 18 kg. Four treatments were administered. Each treatment consisted of two i.v. injections. The first injection was given at baseline (T0). The second injection was given 15 min later (T15). Treatments included acepromazine 0.05 mg/kg bwt plus saline (AS). Other treatments were saline plus xylazine 0.5 mg/kg bwt (SX0.5). Another treatment was acepromazine plus xylazine 0.25 mg/kg bwt (AX0.25). The final treatment was acepromazine plus xylazine 0.5 mg/kg bwt (AX0.5). Sedative and cardiorespiratory parameters were evaluated before T0. They were also evaluated at 15, 20, 30, 45, 60, 75 and 90 min after treatment. Degree and quality of sedation were measured. Degree was measured by height of head above ground (HHAG). Quality was measured by ataxia, responses to stimuli and visual analogue scale (VAS) scoring. Respiratory rate was evaluated by the main investigator in situ. Heart rate was measured by an assistant investigator. Three experienced evaluators assessed videos for ataxia and responses to stimuli. Normal data were analysed by repeated measures ANOVA. Non-normal data were analysed by Kruskal-Wallis (P<0.05). HHAG was lower than baseline for 15 min after xylazine administration in AX0.25. It was lower for 30 min in SX0.5 and AX0.5 groups. All treatments with xylazine increased VAS and ataxia scores in situ for 15 min after xylazine administration. No differences existed between groups. Ataxia scores in situ were higher in SX0.5 and AX0.5 groups than AS. This occurred for 15 and 30 min after xylazine administration, respectively. The study lacked a negative control group (saline-saline). Acepromazine added to xylazine at 0.25 mg/kg bwt produced briefer and milder sedation. This sedation was briefer and milder than xylazine at 0.5 mg/kg bwt alone.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::40: ALMA-IMF imaged 15 massive protoclusters down to a resolution of 2 kau scales. The survey identified about 1000 star-forming cores. Mass and luminosity are fundamental physical characteristics of these cores. They are difficult to determine. The problem becomes greatly worse at the distances >2 kpc of ALMA-IMF protoclusters. We combined new datasets and radiative transfer modeling. We wanted to characterize these cores. We estimated their mass-averaged temperature. We also estimated the masses these estimates imply. We measured the bolometric luminosities for 1/6 of the sample. We implemented deblending corrections when necessary. We used spectral energy distribution (SED) analysis. We obtained it with the PPMAP Bayesian procedure. This procedure aims to preserve the best angular resolution of the input data. PPMAP provided luminosity and dust temperature images at 2.5" resolution. We extrapolated these images. We wanted to estimate those of individual cores. The cores were identified at higher angular resolution. We applied approximate radiative transfer relationships. One relationship connects the luminosity of a protostar and the temperature of its surrounding envelope. Another relationship connects the external heating of prestellar cores and their temperatures. We provide data-informed estimates of dust temperatures for 883 cores for the first time. ALMA-IMF identified these cores. The 617 prestellar cores have temperatures of 17-31 K. The 266 protostellar cores have temperatures of 28-79 K. These are 5th and 95th percentiles. Temperatures reach up to 127 K. We also measured protostellar luminosities. They span 20-80 000 Lsun. We estimated systematically lower temperatures for hot cores. Other studies based on complex organic molecules found higher temperatures. We established a mass-luminosity evolutionary diagram. This is the first time at the core spatial resolution. It is also the first time for a large sample of high-mass protostellar cores. The ALMA-IMF data favor a scenario. Protostars accrete their mass from a larger mass reservoir. This reservoir is larger than their host cores.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::41: The present study had an aim. The aim was to investigate the role of microRNA (miR)-27a-3p in osteoarthritis (OA). Researchers performed reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction and western blotting. They wanted to determine the expression of miR-27a-3p and aggrecanase-2 (ADAMTS5). They examined cartilage tissues from patients with OA and healthy controls. They also examined interleukin (IL)-1beta-treated primary human chondrocytes. Researchers transfected primary human chondrocytes with miR-27a-3p. They used a luciferase reporter assay. This assay validated the direct contact between miR-27a-3p and its putative binding site in the 3'-untranslated region ADAMTS5 mRNA. Researchers evaluated the effects of IL-1beta-induced activation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and nuclear factor (NF)-kappaB on miR-27a-3p. They used specific inhibitors for this evaluation. The results revealed findings. The level of miR-27a-3p was reduced in OA cartilage tissues. Researchers compared these tissues with those of normal controls. Researchers observed decreased miR-27a-3p and increased ADAMTS5 expression in chondrocytes treated with IL-1beta. This occurred in a time- and dose-dependent manner. Overexpression of miR-27a-3p suppressed the expression of ADAMTS5 in human chondrocytes induced by IL-1beta. miR-27a-3p overexpression also decreased the luciferase activity of the wild-type ADAMTS5 reporter plasmid. Mutation of the miR-27a-3p binding site in the 3'-untranslated region of ADAMTS5 mRNA abolished the miR-27a-3p-mediated repression of reporter activity. Specific inhibitors demonstrated findings. IL-1beta may regulate miR-27a-3p expression via NF-kappaB and MAPK signaling pathways in chondrocytes. The present study concluded findings. miR-27a-3p was downregulated in human OA. IL-1beta suppressed it. It functions as a crucial regulator of ADAMTS5 in OA chondrocytes. IL-1beta-mediated suppression of miR-27a-3p activity may occur via the MAPK and NF-kappaB pathways. The present study may provide a novel strategy for clinical treatment of OA. This treatment is caused by upregulation of miR-27a-3p.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::42: Space weathering is a process. This process changes the surface of airless planetary bodies. Prime space weathering agents are solar wind irradiation and micrometeoroid bombardment. These processes alter planetary reflectance spectra. They often modify their compositional diagnostic features. In this work we focused on simulating the spectral changes. We also compared them. Solar wind irradiation causes these changes. Micrometeoroid bombardment causes them too. We wanted to gain a better understanding of these individual space weathering processes. We used olivine pellets as proxies for planetary materials. We used pyroxene pellets as proxies for planetary materials. We used hydrogen ions to simulate solar wind irradiation. We used helium ions too. We used argon ions as well. These ions had energies from 5 to 40 keV. They had fluences of up to $10^{18}$ particles/cm$^2$. We used individual femtosecond laser pulses. These pulses simulated micrometeoroid bombardment. We analysed the corresponding evolution of different spectral parameters. We determined these parameters by applying the Modified Gaussian Model. We also conducted principal component analysis. The original mineralogy of the surface influences the spectral evolution. It does so more than the weathering agent. We saw this from the diverse evolution of the spectral slope of olivine. We saw it from the diverse evolution of the spectral slope of pyroxene upon irradiation. The spectral slope changes seen in olivine are consistent with observations of A-type asteroids. The moderate slope changes observed in pyroxene are consistent with asteroid (4) Vesta. The no slope changes observed in pyroxene are consistent with asteroid (4) Vesta. We also observed some differences in the spectral effects. The two weathering agents induced these effects. Ions simulate solar wind. They have a smaller influence on longer wavelengths of the spectra. Laser irradiation simulates micrometeoroid impacts. This is most likely due to the different penetration depths of ions. It is also due to the different penetration depths of laser pulses. Our results suggest something. In some instances it might be possible to distinguish between the contributions of the two agents. These agents act on a weathered surface.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::43: HEALPix by Górski et al. (2005) is the de-facto standard for Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data storage and analysis. Current and upcoming CMB experiments use it widely. Almost all datasets in Legacy Archive for Microwave Background Data Analysis (LAMBDA) use HEALPix as their format of choice. Visualizing the data plays an important role in research. Several toolsets were developed to do that with HEALPix maps. The most notable ones are the original Fortran facilities and Python integration with healpy. GPU performance has reached a current state. It is now possible to visualize extremely large maps in real time on a laptop or a tablet. HEALPix Viewer is described here. It is developed for macOS. It takes full advantage of GPU acceleration to handle extremely large datasets in real time. It compiles natively on Intel and Arm64 architectures. It uses Metal framework for high-performance GPU computations. This project aims to reduce the effort required for interactive data exploration. It also reduces the time overhead for producing publication-quality maps. Drag and drop integration with Keynote and Powerpoint makes creating presentations easy. The main codebase is written in Swift. Swift is a modern and efficient compiled language. High-performance computing parts are delegated entirely to GPU. A few inserts in C interface to cfitsio library for I/O. The graphical user interface is written in SwiftUI. SwiftUI is a new declarative UI framework based on Swift. Most common spherical projections and colormaps are supported out of the box. The available source code makes it easy to customize the application. Users can add new features if desired. Overall performance improves on the current Python software stack by a factor of 3-180x. The improvement depends on the task at hand.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::44: We wanted to compare cervical shear wave elastography (SWE) by using transvaginal ultrasound (TVS). We compared twin and singleton pregnant women. This was a prospective cohort study. It involved twin and singleton pregnant women. They attended antenatal care at Ramathibodi Hospital, Bangkok, Thailand. The participants met the inclusion criteria. We serially measured the shear wave speed (SWS). We used TVS at early, mid-, and third trimester. We evaluated the changes in SWS with advancing gestational age. We compared twin and singleton pregnancies. We also analyzed the gestational age at delivery. We analyzed spontaneous preterm delivery rate. We analyzed a total of 36 twin pregnancies and 38 singleton pregnancies. We observed no significant difference in baseline characteristics. There was one exception. The age of participants was different. Twin pregnancies were 33.1±4.6 years. Singleton pregnancies were 29.9±5.4 years. The p-value was 0.006. The cervical SWS decreased with advancing gestational age. This occurred in both twin and singleton pregnancy. There was a statistically significant difference of cervical SWS at the lower point in mid-trimester. Twin pregnancies showed 2.27±0.4. Singleton pregnancies showed 2.71±0.6 m/s. The p-value was 0.001. However, no significant difference in cervical SWS at the upper point and the lower point in the early and third trimester was demonstrated. The gestational age at delivery between both groups revealed a significant difference. Twin pregnancies delivered at 35.9±2.8 weeks. Singleton pregnancies delivered at 37.6±2.9 weeks. The p-value was 0.008. But the spontaneous preterm delivery rate did not differ significantly. Twin pregnancies showed 22.2%. Singleton pregnancies showed 15.8%. The p-value was 0.483. The mid-trimester cervical SWS measurement at the lower point detects the difference in cervical softness. It detects the difference between twin pregnancies and singleton pregnancies. The cervical SWS might be an additional option. It can monitor the change in cervical softness in twin pregnancies.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::45: Chromosome number is a key feature of the higher-order organization of the genome. Changes in chromosome number play a fundamental role in evolution. Dysploid gains and losses in chromosome number may drive reproductive isolation and lineage diversification. Polyploidization events may also drive reproductive isolation and lineage diversification. The recent development of probabilistic models of chromosome number evolution occurred in the groundbreaking work by Mayrose et al. (2010, ChromEvol). These models have enabled the inference of ancestral chromosome numbers over molecular phylogenies. They have generated new interest in studying the role of chromosome changes in evolution. However, the ChromEvol approach assumes all changes occur anagenetically. These changes occur along branches. The approach does not model events that are specifically cladogenetic. Cladogenetic changes may be expected if chromosome changes result in reproductive isolation. Here we present a new class of models of chromosome number evolution. We call these models ChromoSSE. They incorporate both anagenetic and cladogenetic change. The ChromoSSE models allow us to determine the mode of chromosome number evolution. Is chromosome evolution occurring primarily within lineages? Is it occurring primarily at lineage splitting? Or is it occurring in clade-specific combinations of both? Furthermore, we can estimate the location and timing of possible chromosome speciation events over the phylogeny. We implemented ChromoSSE in a Bayesian statistical framework. We implemented it specifically in the software RevBayes. This accommodates uncertainty in parameter estimates. It leverages the full power of likelihood based methods. We tested ChromoSSE's accuracy with simulations. We re-examined chromosomal evolution in Aristolochia, Carex section Spirostachyae, Helianthus, Mimulus sensu lato (s.l.), and Primula section Aleuritia. We found evidence for clade-specific combinations of anagenetic and cladogenetic dysploid and polyploid modes of chromosome evolution. [Anagenetic; Bayes factors; chromosome evolution; chromosome speciation; chromoSSE; cladogenetic; dysploidy; phylogenetic models; polyploidy; reversible-jump Markov chain Monte Carlo; whole genome duplication.].
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::46: We present results of our time variability studies of Mg II and Al III absorption lines. We studied a sample of 22 Low Ionization Broad Absorption Line QSOs. These are LoBAL QSOs. They are at 0.2 <= zem <= 2.1. We used the 2m telescope at IUCAA Girawali Observatory. The time-scale was 10 days to 7.69 years in the QSO's rest frame. We analysed spectra. We used photometric light curves from Catalina Real-Time Transient Survey with them. Long time-scale absorption line variability is seen in 8 cases. This means >= 1 year. This is 36% of systems. Only 4 of them show variability over short time-scales. This means < 1 year. This is 18% of systems. We notice a tendency. Highly variable LoBAL QSOs have high ejection velocity. They have low equivalent width. They have low redshift. The detection rate of variability in LoBAL QSOs showing Fe fine-structure lines is less. These are FeLoBAL QSOs. It is less than that seen in non-Fe LoBAL QSOs. Absorption line variability is more frequently detected in QSOs. These QSOs have continuum dominated by Fe emission lines. We compare them to rest of the QSOs. Confirming these trends with a bigger sample will give vital clues. These clues are for understanding the physical distinction between different BAL QSO sub-classes. We correlate the absorption line variability with various parameters. These parameters are derived from continuum light curves. We find no clear correlation between continuum flux and absorption line variabilities. However, sources with large absorption line variability also show large variability in their light curves. We also see appearance and disappearance of absorption components in 2 cases. We see clear indications for profile variations in 4 cases. The observed variability can be best explained by a combination of process. This process is driven by continuum variations and clouds. These clouds transit across the line of sight.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::47: The H{\alpha} nebular emission line is an optimal tracer for recent star formation in galaxies. JWST has arrived. This line has recently become observable at z>3 for the first time. We present a catalog of 1013 H{\alpha} emitters at 3.7<z<6.7 in the GOODS fields. We obtained these from a blind search in JWST NIRCam/grism data. We make use of the FRESCO survey's 124 arcmin^2 of observations in GOODS-North and GOODS-South with the F444W filter. This probes H{\alpha} at 4.9<z<6.7. We also use the CONGRESS survey's 62 arcmin^2 in GOODS-North with F356W. This probes H{\alpha} at 3.8<z<5.1. We find an overdensity with 97 sources at z~4.4 in GOODS-N. We confirm previously reported overdensities at z~5.2 in GOODS-N. We also confirm overdensities at z~5.4 and z~5.9 in GOODS-S. We compute the observed H{\alpha} luminosity functions (LFs) in three bins. These bins center at z~4.45, 5.30, and 6.15. These are the first such measurements at z>3. We obtained them based purely on spectroscopic data. They robustly trace galaxy star formation rates (SFRs) beyond the peak of the cosmic star formation history. We compare our results with theoretical predictions from three different simulations. We find good agreement at z~4-6. The UV LFs of this spectroscopically-confirmed sample are in good agreement with pre-JWST measurements. Those measurements were obtained with photometrically-selected objects. We derive SFR functions. We integrate these to compute the evolution of the cosmic star-formation rate densities across z~4-6. We find values in good agreement with recent UV estimates from Lyman-break galaxies. These imply a continuous decrease in SFR density by a factor of 3x over z~4 to z~6. Our work shows the power of NIRCam grism observations. They efficiently provide new tests for early galaxy formation models. These tests are based on emission line statistics.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::48: Numerous studies have revealed something important. Oxidative stress is closely associated with the occurrence and development of depression. Xiaoyao Pills (XYW) are included in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia. They are frequently used for treating anxiety and depression. They work by smoothing the liver, strengthening the spleen, and nourishing the blood. However, the antidepressant effects of XYW have not yet been thoroughly investigated. The objective of our study was to investigate the antidepressant-like effects of XYW. We also wanted to investigate the underlying molecular mechanism. We used the olfactory bulbectomized (OB) rat model of depression. We employed the open field test (OFT), sucrose preference test (SPT), splash test (ST), and novelty suppressed feeding test (NSFT). Results showed that XYW (0.93 and 1.86 g·kg-1) significantly alleviated depression-like behaviors in rats. The SPT indicated increased sucrose preference. The ST showed prolonged grooming time. The OFT revealed decreased horizontal movement. The NSFT demonstrated shorter feeding latency. In addition, XYW treatment dramatically reversed the reduced activity of superoxide dismutase. It also reversed the decreased level of glutathione. It lowered levels of malondialdehyde. It reduced an inflammatory mediator (nitric oxide). It decreased pro-inflammatory cytokines (interleukin-6 and 1β) in the serum and cortex of OB rats. Mechanistically, XYW induced marked upregulation of mRNA and protein expression levels. These included NFE2L2, KEAP1, GPX3, HMOX1, SOD1, NQO1, OGG1, PIK3CA, p-AKT1/AKT1, NTRK2, and BDNF. It caused downregulation of ROS in the cortex and hippocampus. This occurred via the activation of the NFE2L2/KEAP1, PIK3CA/AKT1, and NTRK2/BDNF pathways. These findings suggest that XYW exert antidepressant-like effects in OB rats with depression-like symptoms. These effects are mediated by the alleviation of oxidative stress. They also involve the enhancement of neuroprotective effects. This happens through the activation of the PIK3CA-AKT1-NFE2L2/BDNF signaling pathways.
syntax_simple_s.academic_abstracts::49: We report the discovery of 16 detached M-dwarf eclipsing binaries with J<16 mag. We provide a detailed characterisation of three of them. 1. This strap is easy to set up. You need no tools. You attach the stainless steel/aluminum mount to the tripod socket. The socket is at the bottom of the camera. You tighten the thumbscrew. You should recheck it every so often. You want to make sure it stays tightened.

2. This strap fits a lot more comfortably than a regular neck strap does. All DSLRs should come with this type of strap. You get no neck burn. You get no awkward carrying positions.

3. You can tighten the strap against the body. You pull on the pivot ring and camera. You pull them in opposite directions. You do this when you need to go hands free across some difficult terrain. You also do this when your hands are otherwise occupied.

4. You can wear the strap on either shoulder. You can even wear it behind your back as needed.

5. The strap has a locking mechanism. This mechanism holds the strap in place. It works when you're not shooting.

6. The strap adjusts itself. It extends when you raise the camera to take a shot. This happens when the locking mechanism is disengaged of course.

7. This strap is built for a man. The women's strap has a small curve. That curve is for the zaftig photographer. But this strap is still comfortable. It is strong enough regardless.

Cons:

1. You dangle an expensive camera and even more expensive lens upside down. You dangle it from ONE screw. The screw is in ONE spot. The spot is on the bottom of the camera. This is a bit nerve-wracking. But regular straps can malfunction also.

2. The strap could have been improved with a bit more padding.

3. The strap takes up quite a bit of space in a camera bag. But you can't have everything. For smaller bags you can detach the strap. You can reattach it when needed. This takes only a couple of seconds.

4. Obviously you have to detach the strap when you want to use a tripod.

5. The strap itself has no fault here. But the models in the video on the product page need some instruction. They need to learn how to hold a DSLR properly. LOL.

Overall, this has solved a big problem for me. This is a much more comfortable way to carry around a heavy camera and lens. You can carry them for hours at a time.

Amanda Richards, January 8, 2013

Note: I recently bought the women's version of this strap. The only difference is that the strap is a little bit narrower at the top. It has a clever little bend. The bend is for negotiating feminine curves.
